It will be ​livestreamed. ⁠Details will follow," a Pentagon official told Reuters.US President Donald Trump this week ordered the use of a firing squad ⁠to execute Hasan.Hasan, a former US Army major, later described his shooting spree as retaliation for US wars in the ⁠Muslim world.Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said on X that Mr Trump had approved putting Hasan to death by an Army firing squad at the recommendation of Mr Hegseth.Mr Parnell said Hasan shouted "Allahu Akbar" during the attack, in which 12 unarmed active-duty soldiers and a retired serviceman were killed, and 32 others ​wounded.Death by firing squad was ​one of several forms of capital punishment the Trump administration recently added to permissible forms of execution for the gravest of federal crimes, along with electrocution and gas asphyxiation.Thom Tillis, a Republican senator who voted to confirm Mr Hegseth, said Hasan should face the death penalty, but that making his execution public and streaming it was "beyond disgusting"."Public executions are what oppressive dictatorships like Iran and Afghanistan do. It should not be happening in America," he wrote on X. Hasan should face the death penalty, but making his execution public and streaming it? Beyond disgusting. Public executions are what oppressive dictatorships like Iran and Afghanistan do. It should not be happening in America. https://t.co/qpl6KQj4Wb— Senator Thom Tillis (@SenThomTillis) October 9, 2026The number of federal execution options was expanded in part because of increasing difficulties in obtaining drugs for lethal injections, which have also proved challenging to carry out for other reasons at times.Plans by the state of Tennessee to execute a woman for the first time in more than 200 years went awry last week when prison personnel botched an attempt to administer a lethal injection, leaving the death-row inmate, Christa Pike, alive but unconscious and in hospital on life support. She regained consciousness on Tuesday.Pike's lawyers had previously urged the Tennessee Department of Correction to consider an alternative to lethal injection, such as hanging or firing squad, because of the trouble executioners faced in establishing a sound intravenous line.A military jury sentenced Hasan to death in August 2013, after finding him guilty of 45 counts of premeditated murder ​and attempted premeditated murder for opening fire with a laser-sighted handgun in a medical centre at the sprawling central Texas military base.The shooting ⁠came weeks before Hasan, now 56, was scheduled to be ​sent to Afghanistan. He was left partially paralysed and confined to a wheelchair from being shot ​by police upon ‌his arrest.In a statement responding to Mr Trump's decision, the group Death Penalty Action, which opposes capital punishment, said: "There is nothing Donald Trump ⁠loves more than the power to kill."Military executions are rare, and under the Uniform Code of Military Justice ⁠a death sentence imposed by court-martial may not be carried out "until approved by the president".If Hasan is put to death, it would mark the first military execution since 1961, the group said. According to the Death Penalty Information Centre, the 1961 execution was carried out by hanging. The apparent last known execution by a US military firing squad ​was one carried out "by musketry" in November 1945, the centre reported.At least five states have firing squads on the books, according to the Death Penalty Information Centre. In 2025, South Carolina carried out the first such execution in the United States in 15 years.

headline: Making e-scooters safe requires more than fines and enforcement
summary: Dubai Police said this week it had seized hundreds of e-scooters and e-bikes for a variety of traffic offences during a road safety drive in one of the emirate’s neighbourhoods. It is the latest action taken to tackle unsafe use of so-called last-mile vehicles.The same authority said last month that it had confiscated more than 13,000 e-scooters since the beginning of the year for dangerous riding, such as speeding. The authorities noted that accidents, incidents and injuries have risen. Abu Dhabi has this year also issued warnings about improper use of such vehicles, as well as disseminating public safety information videos.There has not been a nationwide “census” conducted regarding the volume of e-scooters in active use in the country – nor does there need to be one – but e-bikes and e-scooters are now a ubiquitous presence on neighbourhood roads and cycle path networks, helping reduce congestion and pollution in the process. What is becoming obvious is that more scooters and more journeys means, in all likelihood, the potential for more accidents and incidents.The National reported earlier this year that Ministry of Interior data showed significant e-scooter accidents had increased by 97 per cent last year, from 61 cases to 120. Despite the rapid rise in the headline number, the overall figure is still low. That, of course, provides no comfort to anyone or any family that has been affected by one of those serious accidents. It is in all of our interests to reduce the number of significant incidents to zero, while also recognising we are not sat in the middle of a contagion-level event.Statistical models produced elsewhere in the world suggest every 100,000 e-scooter rides might result in between 10 and 20 accidents requiring medical support or intervention. A significant contributory factor to that global modelling is alcohol intoxication by the e-scooter user, which may be less of a determinant in this region. World Health Organisation figures also report that road traffic injuries of all forms tend to disproportionately affect young people. Globally, unintentional injury, such as that resulting from vehicle collision, is the leading cause of death for people under 30.The rules for e-scooters say riders must be at least 16 years old and wear a helmet when using one. The maximum speed permitted by one of those vehicles is 20 kph. Riders are also required to keep a safe distance from pedestrians, are not allowed to carry passengers or use mobile phones while using them. Reflective clothing is also advised, and any vehicle is meant to be equipped with front and rear lights.The drip-drip of persistent messaging does increase the likelihood of bringing about behavioural changeAuthorities have said they would take action against riders who cross roads dangerously, weave between lanes or ride outside demarcated or approved zones. Improper use leads to confiscation and fines.Anecdotally, if it is not controversial to say that most road users will have seen an e-scooter rider breach at least one of those rules in day-to-day life. A counter-argument would also say that most drivers break road rules on their daily drives, whether that is speeding, distracted driving, tailgating or another form of anti-social or potentially reckless behaviour.Few drivers are the paragons of road-using virtue that we may think we are and only a small number of drivers willingly identify themselves as “bad” even if their fellow road users might absolutely attest that they are. It is down to every road user to take a higher level of personal responsibility to keep the roads safe.So, how can we realistically reach a state of accident-free nirvana?Education and awareness are key to beating back the rising tide rather than enforcement with last-mile vehicles.Only the utterly rules-driven among us would advocate for round-the-clock and always-visible enforcement of regulations regarding e-scooters, which would be a drain on resources that could not be justified by the thankfully low volume of incidents and accidents.Each time authorities share video footage of e-scooter misuse, however, it will help subtly change behaviour and attitudes towards risk.Road safety campaigns elsewhere in the world on the dangers of driving while intoxicated or failing to use seat belts or child seats have helped change habits and save lives over a prolonged period. Campaigns by Abu Dhabi Police to highlight the dangers of rubber-necking, tailgating and speeding have garnered widespread attention and, inevitably, offer pause for individual reflection and thought. Dubai has set up a unit in relation to e-scooter use to help education and improve safety. All of these things will help.There is also the question of performance-limiters. E-bikes are typically able to achieve limits far in excess of the permitted maximums for the path network, much in the same way as performance cars have the potential to be driven at more than double the speed permitted on the nation’s motorways. While speed limiters are also common in both performance cars and e-bikes, software has the potential to be overridden. Awareness campaigns about the dangers of speeding and the increased risk of injury to the e-scooter user or pedestrians are the best defence in such circumstances.The drip-drip of persistent messaging does increase the likelihood of bringing about behavioural change and keeping our path and road network safe.

headline: Saudi-led coalition vows to 'punish' Houthis after attacks on airports and civilian facilities
summary: The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen has vowed to “punish” Houthi rebels after deadly attacks hit airports in Riyadh and Saudi Arabia's southern region, and debris from an intercepted ballistic missile damaged civilian facilities in the capital.“The brutal attacks by the terrorist Houthi militia on civilians and civilian objects in the kingdom … will not go unpunished,” said coalition spokesman Maj Gen Turki Al Malki. He said the coalition’s joint forces had destroyed dozens of military Houthi targets across Yemen.Authorities at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh urged passengers to check with their airlines and confirm their flight status before heading to the hub, as flights continued to be affected.The Saudi Civil Defence said debris from the missile caused damage to a nursery and a medical clinic on Thursday, and two Riyadh residents reported hearing explosions.Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree claimed the Iran-backed group had attacked the airport in Riyadh repeatedly.The UAE's Ministry of Foreign Affairs “condemned in the strongest terms” the attacks, adding that they “constitute a flagrant violation of the sovereignty of the kingdom of Saudi Arabia and a threat to its security and stability”.The ministry, in a statement, reaffirmed the UAE’s “full solidarity” with the kingdom and its support for “all measures” taken in response. It also expressed its “solidarity and sincere condolences and sympathy to the families of the victims, as well as its wishes for a speedy recovery for all the injured”. Drone and missile strikes on King Khalid airport and Abha International Airport in the south killed three people and injured 36 others, the kingdom's General Authority of Civil Aviation announced late on Wednesday.Attacks by Houthi rebels against Saudi Arabia come amid renewed fighting after the rebels made advances along Yemen's Red Sea coast and a Yemeni government counter-offensive supported by coalition air strikes.“The targeting of civilian infrastructure is completely unacceptable,” the Indian Foreign Ministry said in a statement, expressing condolences to the families of those killed and wishing a speedy recovery to those injured. It also expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia and said it stood with the kingdom’s people and government.France also condemned the Houthis’ repeated attacks on Saudi Arabia and expressed its “full solidarity” with the kingdom's defence of its territory and infrastructure, the Foreign Ministry in Paris said.Last month, Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan called for a comprehensive political solution in Yemen and condemned Houthi missile and drone attacks against his country and commercial vessels, as well as threats to navigation in the Red Sea. He told the UN General Assembly that a comprehensive agreement was needed to bring stability to Yemen and called for diplomacy over the bigger conflict between the US and Iran.Communication channels between the two countries remain open, with new messages exchanged through mediators, diplomats and sources have told The National, as efforts to reach a lasting agreement to end the nearly seven-month-old war remain elusive.The push to establish a fresh diplomatic path following the failure to achieve a breakthrough in New York during the UN General Assembly last month comes amid growing signs that both sides are preparing for a major confrontation.Last week, a source in Tehran told The National that Iran was preparing for a “major round of fighting”. Days later, US media reports suggested that US President Donald Trump's administration was considering renewed strikes on Iran before the November 3 midterm elections and that the Pentagon had ordered preparations for possible major combat operations.Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said his country was reviewing Washington's response to its proposal, under which the Strait of Hormuz could be reopened within seven days, and could reply within days. “The ⁠diplomatic process is still continuing,” he said.

headline: Premier League predictions as Arsenal host Leeds and Man United face Spurs
summary: The Premier League returns on Saturday after one of the longest international breaks in memory. Below we try and pick the results from what looks like being a pivotal weekend of action. Saturday: Arsenal v Leeds United (3.30pm)Arsenal saw their perfect start to the season end before the break as they fell to a 3-0 loss at Brighton, leaving the Gunners three points behind leaders Manchester City. Kai Havertz is an injury doubt after picking up a hamstring problem on international duty with Germany.Leeds go into the match unbeaten with two wins and three draws, the last of which was a stalemate at home to Crystal Palace. The Yorkshiremen are three points and three places shy of Arsenal in the table.Prediction: Arsenal 2 Leeds 0Aston Villa v Brentford (6pm)Villa dragged themselves out of the bottom three when they defeated Spurs 3-2 in what was their first league win of the campaign, with Johan Manzambi, Nicolas Jackson and Emiliano Buendia scoring the goals.Brentford are one of five teams yet to lose a league game this season and were convincing 3-0 winners over Chelsea last time out – which saw Igor Thiago open his league account for the season – lifting the Bees to fourth in the table.Prediction: Villa 2 Brentford 1Chelsea v Bournemouth (6pm)Chelsea have dropped down to 10th place after taking one point from three matches and have the worst defensive record in the top flight, conceding 12 goals.Marco Rose has yet to win a game as Bournemouth manager, with the Cherries having drawn three and lost two so far. They will also be without key midfielder Alex Scott for two months after he picked up a thigh injury on his England debut.Prediction: Chelsea 3 Bournemouth 1Ipswich Town v Fulham (6pm)Ipswich have lost three of their past four matches, the last of which was a 1-0 defeat at Everton. The Tractor Boys still have six points on the board, though, and are in 11th place.Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa is still waiting for his first league win, but the Spaniard's side has shown signs of improvement after starting with three successive losses, as they drew with Liverpool and then Manchester United. The Black Cats are on four points, one place above the bottom three.Brighton are flying high in third place following wins over Coventry and Arsenal that saw Fabian Hurzeler's side score eight and concede none.Prediction: Sunderland 2 Brighton 2Manchester United v Tottenham Hotspur (8.30pm)United needed a last-minute deflected Matheus Cunha strike to avoid defeat at Fulham last time out, and the Red Devils have won only once in five league games.Spurs are rock bottom, without a win, and have scored just twice in five games, with those proving to be late consolations in the defeat at home to Villa.Prediction: Man United 2 Spurs 1Sunday: Crystal Palace Nottingham Forest (5pm)Palace have just one win so far, having drawn at Leeds before the break, leaving the Eagles one point and three places outside the bottom three.Forest are one point and two places above Palace, and have one win from five games, but fell to a surprise home loss to Coventry last time out.Prediction: Palace 1 Forest 1Hull City v Everton (5pm)Hull's fine unbeaten start was ended by a narrow loss at Newcastle, but the Tigers remain in the top half with eight points on the board.Everton are one point above Hull, with Thierno Barry's goal earning them a home win over Ipswich, their first victory since the opening weekend of the season, following three successive draws.Prediction: Hull 1 Everton 1Liverpool v Manchester City (7.30pm)Liverpool are sixth in the table with three draws and two wins after Alexander Isak's goal earned manager Andoni Iraola a victory at his former club Bournemouth. Manchester City have won all seven games since losing to Arsenal in the Community Shield and top the table, but are back in action for the first time since being found guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules. Top scorer Erling Haaland is also an injury concern. headline: UAE investigation to determine if flydubai incident was linked to 'terrorist activity'
summary: The UAE's attorney general has ordered an investigation into the mid-flight altercation aboard a flydubai aircraft that forced the plane to divert to Saudi Arabia.Dr Hamad Saif Al Shamsi directed a specialist team to examine flydubai flight FZ1073, which was travelling from Dubai airport to Tel Aviv on Wednesday. The probe will look at whether the mid-air drama involved "any terrorist activity or purpose or involved prior planning or direction", news agency Wam said.Saudi Arabia announced initial findings from its own investigation late on Thursday. The Interior Ministry said the pilot was "assaulted by his co-pilot, resulting in both sustaining various injuries". An official ministry source said both pilots had left for Abu Dhabi on Thursday after their conditions improved. They said a UAE security team had assisted the Saudi investigation. The pilot attacked on board has been identified as Smit Machchhar from India. The co-pilot's identity has not been revealed, although Israeli authorities have claimed he was Omani. Details of what happened on the flight on Wednesday morning remain unclear, but the Boeing 737 plunged 14,000ft during a cockpit altercation before it diverted to Saudi Arabia. Crew members and passengers intervened to help land the plane safely at Saudi Arabia’s Tabuk Airport.UAE probeThe UAE team has begun work in co-ordination with the General Civil Aviation Authority and other UAE authorities, Wam said. The attorney general urged the public to refrain from circulating unverified information. Early reports of the mid-air drama, including the nationalities of the pilots and other details, were strewn with inaccuracies.Under UAE law, crimes committed aboard aircraft registered in the country fall within the jurisdiction of UAE courts, regardless of where the incident occurs, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs reiterated on Thursday."The UAE also expressed its appreciation to the Saudi authorities for their cooperation and handling of the incident", it added.Hero pilotMeanwhile, the flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar, hailed as a hero for averting a potential disaster on the flight, is recovering in a UAE hospital.Dr Deepak Mittal, India's Ambassador to the UAE, visited the captain at the hospital and said he was recovering rapidly. "He was speaking openly, smiling and laughing, which was a great relief for us and, above all, for his family," said Mr Mittal. He added that the pilot's morale was high and that he was being well cared for by the hospital team.The Israeli Prime Minister publicly named the Indian aviator and recognised him for his actions. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said, Mr Machchhar "has shown the world the highest form of courage. Without fearing for his own life, he fought valiantly."Speaking on Wednesday night, US President Donald Trump called the captain a hero, while saying he was "pretty banged up" in the cockpit assault.Disaster averted on Israel flight – in picturesIsraeli leaders claim attack was 'terrorism'Israeli leaders have alleged the attack on the flydubai plane was 'terrorism', even as an investigation is yet to be completed.Defence Minister Israel Katz has called it an "attempted jihadist terror attack".US President Donald Trump said he had spoken with Mr Netanyahu, saying it seemed as though the attacker was "perhaps a terrorist" or there were other reasons behind it.Speaking on BBC Radio 4 on Thursday, Israeli President Isaac Herzog was asked whether he thought there was an Iranian link to the incident, but said: "It's too early to say". He did refer to the co-pilot as a "terrorist".Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu claimed in an interview with Fox News that the co-pilot had undergone "radical Islamist indoctrination" and was clearly "suicidal".Mid-air dramaNarrating events in the cockpit, Mr Herzog claimed: "He was fighting, the co-pilot was stabbing him ... with an axe or a knife ... screaming and screaming and wanting to bring the plane down."They pulled out the terrorist, they handcuffed him, they pulled out the pilot, they took care of him with a doctor - [he] was actually a dentist who took care of him and saved his life ... the life of the Indian hero."Mr Herzog alleged that the co-pilot is Omani - though there was no confirmation of that from Oman, the UAE or flydubai.He claimed he is an "Omani citizen, although that does not mean anything. They're all peaceful nations".Mr Herzog thanked the people of Saudi Arabia for their help and suggested the drama could improve relations between Saudi Arabia and Israel. He further highlighted that the UAE and other Gulf states are "all partners in fighting terror together".

headline: LIXIL’s 1967 shower toilet technology receives IEEE Milestone recognition
summary: LIXIL Corporation (TSE: 5938) announced that its “Sanitarina 61” — Japan’s first domestic shower toilet launched in 1967 — has been recognised with an IEEE Milestone designation by the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers. The designation, which acknowledges global breakthroughs such as the compact disc and Wi-Fi, also jointly recognises Toyo Toki (now TOTO Ltd.) and Matsushita Electric Industrial Co., Ltd. (now Panasonic Housing Solutions Co., Ltd.) for their contributions to electric bidet toilet technology in Japan. “The IEEE Milestone recognition is an immense honor for LIXIL and a testament to an ongoing commitment to innovation, which has been driven not only by our own journey since ‘Sanitarina 61’ in 1967, but by the collective achievements of Japan’s sanitaryware industry,” said Hiroyuki Onishi, Executive Officer of LIXIL Water Technology Japan. “From the outset, our focus was never merely on creating a convenient sanitary fixture, but on delivering meaningful value that nurtures personal well-being and enriches the bathroom space. What began as a Japanese innovation is now redefining daily wellness and hygiene practices around the world. As a pioneer, LIXIL remains dedicated to advancing this technology to make better homes a reality for everyone, everywhere.” LIXIL’s development of shower toilets began in 1964 at Ina Seito, one of its core heritage companies. Without existing anatomical or behavioural data, engineers conducted thousands of practical evaluations using clay and plaster. The team established an optimal nozzle location, water pressure, and a spray angle of approximately 75 degrees to balance cleansing with nozzle cleanliness, while also devising multi-layer thermal controls to eliminate burn risks. The technology continues to evolve in modern products, including the company’s “SATIS X” series. The company introduced Japan’s first dedicated feminine-wash function in 1981 based on female user feedback. LIXIL later incorporated a dual-nozzle system, separating rear-wash and feminine-wash nozzles to address cross-contamination concerns. The company’s products also feature accessibility functions such as automated lids to reduce physical strain for seniors and users with mobility challenges. Additionally, LIXIL utilises its proprietary Aqua Ceramic technology, which features a super-hydrophilic performance designed to prevent waste and limescale buildup on the bowl to maintain cleanliness. The company has expanded its shower toilet technology internationally through its global brand portfolio, which includes INAX, GROHE, and American Standard. This includes products such as the GROHE Sensia Series, which combines INAX’s Japanese technology with GROHE’s German design and engineering to adapt to regional cultures, preferences, and infrastructure needs.

headline: AAIB obtains updated PCI DSS v4.0.1 cybersecurity certification
summary: Arab African International Bank (AAIB) has obtained the latest version of the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS v4.0.1) certification, a move aimed at protecting customer payment data and strengthening the security of card transactions, the bank announced. Securing the PCI DSS v4.0.1 certification required the implementation of a comprehensive set of security controls and practices, the bank said in a statement. These measures include the protection of customers’ payment data, the strengthening of security across relevant stages of digital payment processes, and the enhancement of security controls related to payment services. The certification process also involved applying security governance practices and continuous monitoring, aligning the bank’s operations with international security requirements and standards, according to AAIB. The bank stated that obtaining the certification reflects its ongoing commitments to strengthen its cybersecurity capabilities and security controls, supporting safe and trusted card payment experiences for its customers. The move additionally reinforces AAIB’s focus on advancing information security practices to keep pace with evolving risks, the lender said.

headline: Banque du Caire to list 30% stake in upcoming Egyptian Exchange IPO
summary: Egypt’s Banque du Caire announced on Sunday its intention to float 30% of its issued share capital on the Egyptian Exchange (EGX), in an initial public offering (IPO) expected to conclude in November. The offering will comprise a secondary sale of 4.575 billion existing ordinary shares currently held by the state-owned Banque Misr, the bank said in a statement. The transaction includes a private placement directed at qualified institutional investors globally—including in the United States under Rule 144A and outside the US under Regulation S—alongside a public offering for retail investors in Egypt. The bank is in the process of securing regulatory clearances, including from the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) and the EGX. Subject to these approvals, the subscription period is scheduled for late October, with trading anticipated to begin in November. “We are pleased to announce our intention to float Banque du Caire on the Egyptian Exchange, marking an important milestone in the Bank’s long-standing history,” said Hussein Abaza, Banque du Caire’s Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer. “As one of Egypt’s largest banks, Banque du Caire has built a well-established and diversified franchise across retail, corporate, SME and microfinance banking, supported by a differentiated approach focused on delivering profitable margins, disciplined risk and portfolio management, and maintaining a solid balance sheet. We look forward to welcoming new investors to Banque du Caire and to engaging with the market as we embark on the next phase of the Bank’s development as a publicly listed institution.” CI Capital Investment Banking is acting as lead global coordinator and joint bookrunner, with EFG Hermes Promoting & Underwriting serving as joint global coordinator and joint bookrunner. Baker McKenzie LLP is acting as legal counsel for US and English law, while its member firm Helmy, Hamza & Partners is advising on Egyptian law. The lender reported robust financial results for the first half of 2026, generating a net profit after tax of EGP 8.94bn, net interest income of EGP 18.79bn, and net fee and commission income of EGP 3.42bn. The bank’s total assets reached EGP 561.22bn as of 30 June 2026, supported by gross loans of EGP 280.25bn and total deposits of EGP 443.87bn. Total equity stood at EGP 66.82bn. Banque du Caire recorded an annualised net interest margin of 7.4% and a return on average equity of 27.6% in the first half of the year. The bank maintained a total capital adequacy ratio of 22.1%. Its liquidity coverage ratio and net stable funding ratio were reported at 841% and 172%, respectively, as of 30 June 2026. The planned listing follows a multi-year transformation programme launched in 2018. Over this period, the bank increased its current account savings account (CASA) ratio from 35.2% in 2017 to 53.4% of total deposits by mid-2026. The cost-to-income ratio improved from 48.7% in 2017 to 35.9% in the first half of 2026. Asset quality also strengthened, with the non-performing loan ratio dropping from 5.0% in 2017 to 3.7% in mid-2026, or 2.5% when excluding legacy loans. Established over 70 years ago, Banque du Caire currently operates a network of 242 branches—factoring in planned openings for late 2026 and 2027—and 2,205 ATMs across all 27 governorates, serving approximately 3.2m customers. The bank has expanded its digital footprint, growing its mobile banking customer base to 1m users, with transaction volumes reaching EGP 24.5bn in the first half of 2026. Point-of-sale terminals increased from 571 in 2022 to 13,410 by mid-2026, processing EGP 13.8bn in transactions, while QaheraCash mobile wallet users reached 471,000. In July 2026, the bank migrated its core banking system to Temenos Transact (T24) R22. As of 30 June 2026, the bank’s corporate direct loans amounted to EGP 115bn, while retail loans, excluding microfinance, totalled EGP 98.1bn. SME loans reached EGP 20.9bn across 10,585 customers. Microfinance loans stood at EGP 8.8bn, encompassing approximately 145,000 customers and capturing a 14.0% market share as of May 2026, according to I-Score. The Financial Institutions division held total assets of EGP 69bn, while the Treasury and Capital Markets division managed EGP 212.2bn in assets. The IPO announcement noted Egypt’s broader macroeconomic reform momentum, citing the country’s nominal GDP at $365bn in 2025 and an IMF forecast of a 4.9% compound annual growth rate from 2026 to 2030. Despite net international reserves reaching $56.3bn in July 2026 and improving credit default swap rates, the Egyptian banking sector remains underpenetrated, with only 43% of the population over 15 holding bank accounts in 2024. Banque du Caire’s operations are led by CEO Hussein Abaza, a former banking executive who joined in 2024. The leadership team includes Deputy CEOs Bahaa El-Shafie, Hisham M. Abdelaal, and Ahmed Effat, alongside Chief Risk Officer Hala El Kasar, Chief Treasury Officer Mohamed Aly, and Chief Financial Officer Mohamed Ibrahim. Looking ahead, the bank intends to drive cross-selling initiatives and grow its non-interest banking income, which accounted for 17.8% of net banking income in 2025. BdC also aims to monetise its non-borrowing customer base and expand tailored solutions for mid-cap customers to further increase its market share.

headline: Egypt condemns strikes on Riyadh airport as fresh explosion triggers evacuation and flight grounding
summary: Egypt has strongly condemned recent attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh that targeted the facility and a Saudia Airlines aircraft, killing three Saudi citizens and injuring several civilians. The official statement coincided with reports of a fresh explosion at the hub on Saturday that forced its evacuation and grounded flights. In a press statement issued on Saturday, Egypt’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigration denounced the strikes in the strongest terms. Egypt emphasized its total rejection of the attacks as a flagrant violation of international law, expressing full solidarity with Saudi Arabia in all measures taken to preserve its security, sovereignty, and citizen safety. Cairo warned that targeting air navigation undermines regional and international stability, while offering condolences to the Saudi government and wishing a speedy recovery to the injured. The Egyptian statement came as reports emerged of a new attack on the Saudi capital’s main international hub. King Khalid International Airport was evacuated on Saturday after a loud blast was heard, according to Reuters and AFP reports. More than a dozen ambulances were seen rushing to the airport, according to an eyewitness cited by Reuters. Casualty figures from Saturday’s incident remain unconfirmed, and Saudi authorities have not publicly commented on the blast. The explosion follows claims by Yemen’s Houthi rebels days earlier regarding two successful attacks on the hub. The airport instructed passengers to check flight statuses with their airlines prior to travelling, without providing an explanation for the directive. Arrivals at King Khalid International Airport were cancelled or delayed across the board Saturday afternoon, according to flight tracking platform Flightradar24. One passenger reported that his flight to Riyadh was diverted to Dammam, forcing him to complete his journey to the capital by taxi. Regional carriers suspended service to the hub due to security concerns. Kuwait Airways cancelled all flights to and from Riyadh, citing the airport’s closure over the “security situation”. Etihad Airways and Qatar Airways also cancelled multiple flights between their respective hubs and Riyadh, with some cancellations extending into Monday.

headline: Egypt’s annual urban inflation eases to 13.9% in September
summary: Egypt’s annual urban inflation rate fell to 13.9% in September, down from 14.5% in August 2026, according to the Central Agency for Public Mobilisation and Statistics (CAPMAS). However, monthly inflation accelerated to 1.3% in September, compared with 0.1% in August, driven primarily by higher vegetable and food prices. In a statement issued on Saturday, CAPMAS attributed the monthly increase primarily to a 15.1% rise in vegetable prices. Prices also increased by 0.4% for grains and bread, 2.5% for meat and poultry, 1.2% for fish and seafood, 0.4% for dairy products, cheese and eggs, 0.3% for oils and fats, 2.6% for fruit, 0.2% for sugar and sugary foods, 0.3% for coffee, tea and cocoa, 0.5% for mineral and carbonated water and natural juices, and 0.1% for tobacco. Prices also rose by 1.7% for fabrics, 0.6% for ready-made clothing, 1.8% for clothing cleaning, repair and rental services, and 1.2% for footwear. Actual rentals for housing increased by 0.9%, while housing maintenance and repair costs recorded a similar rise. Water and miscellaneous housing-related services rose by 0.1%, while electricity, gas and other fuels increased by 0.5%. Prices of furnishings, household equipment, carpets and other floor coverings rose by 1.1%, while household textiles increased by 0.6%. Household appliances rose by 0.4%, glassware, tableware and household utensils by 0.8%, tools and equipment for homes and gardens by 0.8%, and goods and services for routine household maintenance by 1.5%. In the healthcare sector, prices increased by 1.2% for outpatient services and 0.7% for hospital services. Vehicle prices rose by 0.3%, while telephone and fax equipment increased by 0.4%. Cultural and recreational services rose by 0.4%, newspapers, books and stationery by 1%, ready-made meals by 0.3%, personal care by 0.7%, and personal effects by 1.2%. By contrast, prices fell by 1.1% for audio-visual, photographic and information-processing equipment and by 0.6% for package holidays. Annual headline inflation across Egypt as a whole reached 12.8% in September, compared with 12.7% in August, according to CAPMAS. The Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) has revised down its inflation outlook, expecting annual headline inflation to remain stable in the third quarter of 2026 before declining gradually towards its target of 7%, plus or minus 2 percentage points, in the second half of 2027. The revised outlook reflects recent inflation developments that have been more favourable than previously expected. In a statement issued by its Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) on 24 September, the CBE said the downward revision to its inflation forecasts would reinforce the prevailing monetary conditions, which it described as sufficiently restrictive, providing further support for the expected disinflationary path. However, the bank warned that the balance of risks surrounding the inflation outlook remained tilted to the upside, reflecting renewed regional hostilities. These risks could affect domestic inflation through the pass-through of fiscal consolidation measures and global food price increases exceeding expectations, particularly if international energy prices remain elevated for an extended period. On the same day, the MPC decided to keep its key interest rates unchanged at 19% for overnight deposits, 20% for overnight lending, and 19.5% for the credit and discount rate and the main operation rate. The decision marked the fifth consecutive meeting at which the CBE had maintained rates, following similar decisions on 20 August, 9 July, 21 May and 2 April. The CBE’s key interest rates serve as the main indicator of the short-term direction of Egyptian pound interest rates. The MPC said its decision reflected its assessment of the latest inflation developments and outlook, alongside changes in the risks surrounding inflation. It reaffirmed that it would continue to assess monetary conditions in light of economic developments affecting the expected inflation path and the associated risks, adding that it would not hesitate to use the tools at its disposal to safeguard price stability.

headline: Egypt, ICARDA seek to scale up solar irrigation, desalination projects
summary: Egypt’s Water Resources and Irrigation Minister Hani Sewilam and International Center for Agricultural Research in the Dry Areas (ICARDA) Director General Nizar Haddad discussed expanding cooperation on water conservation, solar-powered irrigation, desalination and soil salinity management under a joint programme running through 2027. The two sides reviewed implementation of their 2025-2027 joint work programme, which aims to translate areas of cooperation outlined in a memorandum of understanding signed during the seventh Cairo Water Week in 2024 into practical projects and activities. The programme includes a pilot desalination unit at the National Water Research Center’s Wadi El Natrun research station under the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organization’s Water Scarcity Initiative, in which ICARDA participates. Other activities include establishing farmer field schools in Qena and Kafr El-Sheikh and introducing integrated systems for managing soil salinity alongside agricultural production and aquaculture. The meeting also reviewed the “Enhancing Food Security in Egypt” project, implemented in cooperation with the Japanese government, which aims to strengthen climate resilience, improve agricultural and water productivity, and support sustainable rural livelihoods. The project includes deploying solar energy for irrigation, managing soil salinity, improving agricultural extension services, building technical capacity and introducing digital tools. Sewilam called for successful practices in water productivity, solar-powered irrigation, salinity management, agricultural extension and digital irrigation to be expanded to additional areas. He said cooperation with ICARDA aimed to improve water-use efficiency while strengthening the long-term sustainability and productivity of Egypt’s agricultural sector.

headline: Cornerstone laid for date-processing complex in New Valley’s Shorbagy Oasis
summary: Manal Awad, Minister of Local Development and Environment, and Hanan Magdy, Governor of New Valley, laid the cornerstone for a date-processing complex in the Shorbagy Oasis area, marking a key step towards shifting from agricultural production to agro-processing and maximising added value. The ceremony was attended by Amr Abdel-Moneim, Head of the Upper Egypt Development Authority; Mohamed Kegk, Deputy Governor of New Valley; several members of the Senate; and the governorate’s executive and popular leaders. Awad and Magdy received a briefing on the project, which covers approximately 64,000 square metres and has reached around 30% completion. The complex will feature an integrated system for handling date crops and production inputs, including lines for receiving, sorting, grading and preparing dates, alongside automated processing and manufacturing lines equipped with imported machinery and production systems. It will also include packaging lines, handling and transportation equipment, and storage and refrigeration facilities with a capacity of approximately 20,000 tonnes. The project’s infrastructure will rely on modern irrigation systems and solar energy, alongside efforts to diversify crops and introduce varieties offering higher economic returns. The wider project includes more than 650,000 palm trees at different stages of growth and fruit production, including approximately 300,000 fruit-bearing trees. It aims to increase the total number of palms to one million, producing a range of date varieties, alongside strategic crops, fruit, olives, and medicinal and aromatic plants. The complex is expected to create around 1,500 jobs across the agricultural and industrial value chains, helping strengthen the competitiveness of Egyptian products and expand date production, processing and exports to domestic and international markets. Awad said the government sought to bring about a qualitative leap in agro-processing in New Valley Governorate to strengthen the competitiveness of Egyptian products in global markets and generate greater economic returns from the governorate’s leading strategic crop. She added that the complex aimed to integrate post-harvest activities, processing, packaging, storage, market preparation and export operations, linking agricultural production with industry and date-related logistics services. Awad noted that the complex would serve as the processing and value-addition hub within the agricultural production system at Shorbagy Oasis, covering the entire value chain, from cultivation and harvesting to sorting and grading, handling and cold storage, packaging and processing, marketing and exports. For her part, Magdy said the project would also include a weighbridge to facilitate the receipt, handling and shipment of dates, as well as industrial facilities for producing baraneek packaging crates, zamat sacks and white bags used to cover date bunches. She added that the project formed part of the governorate’s efforts to maximise the economic value of its date crop, strengthen the competitiveness of Egyptian products and increase local added value by encouraging date-based industries and improving product quality to meet export market requirements.

headline: Egypt, AUDA-NEPAD agree framework to expand African drug, vaccine production
summary: Egypt has agreed with the African Union Development Agency – New Partnership for Africa’s Development (AUDA-NEPAD) programme to develop a long-term cooperation framework to expand local production of medicines, vaccines and medical technologies across Africa and identify priority healthcare projects for financing and implementation. The agreement was discussed during a meeting between Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar and AUDA-NEPAD Chief Executive Nardos Bekele-Thomas on the sidelines of the World Health Summit in Berlin, according to Egypt’s Health Ministry. The proposed framework would identify priority initiatives, focal points and implementation and follow-up mechanisms, with a focus on strengthening local production and improving access to essential medicines, vaccines and medical technologies across the continent. Discussions covered pharmaceutical regulation, drug and vaccine manufacturing, technology transfer and the development of more resilient medical supply chains to reduce Africa’s dependence on external sources. The two sides also discussed mobilising investment and development financing for priority healthcare infrastructure and pharmaceutical manufacturing projects. The ministry did not announce specific projects, funding commitments or an implementation timetable. Egypt expressed its readiness to draw on its pharmaceutical manufacturing capacity, regulatory experience and healthcare expertise to support African health systems and expand access to medical products and services. The proposed cooperation would also cover professional training and regulatory capacity building, alongside disease surveillance, pandemic preparedness, laboratory capabilities and emergency response. The meeting also addressed primary healthcare, universal health coverage and health insurance, with both sides discussing ways to strengthen healthcare systems across the continent. Egypt and AUDA-NEPAD further agreed to identify potential joint health projects that could be developed in cooperation with African financing institutions and international development partners.

headline: Egypt, Saudi Arabia discuss expanding tourism ties during WTTC summit
summary: Egyptian Tourism and Antiquities Minister Sherif Fathy held a series ofmeetings on the sidelines of the World Travel and Tourism Council’s (WTTC) 26th Global Summit in Valletta, Malta, to discuss expanding tourism cooperation, boosting arrivals to Egypt, and attracting more cruise and yacht tourism. Fathy met with Saudi Deputy Minister of Tourism Abdul Mohsen Al Mazid to discuss strengthening tourism ties and increasing travel between the two countries. Both sides highlighted the close relations between Egypt and Saudi Arabia and reviewed developments in their respective tourism sectors. The Egyptian minister outlined trends in tourist arrivals to Egypt and the ministry’s plans to expand the use of modern technology and artificial intelligence (AI) in promoting the country as a tourism destination. Discussions also covered the growing appeal of Egypt’s North Coast among Saudi tourists and opportunities to develop yacht tourism in the Red Sea. On the industry front, Fathy met with Neal Jones, president of Europe, Middle East and Africa at Marriott International, and Chris Nassetta, president and CEO of Hilton, to discuss the groups’ expansion plans in Egypt in line with the country’s targets for increasing tourist arrivals. The meetings also explored cooperation in training and skills development for Egyptian tourism and hospitality workers, opportunities for Egyptian talent to gain international experience at the groups’ hotels worldwide, and ways to leverage their global networks to promote Egypt and attract new segments of visitors. Jones outlined Marriott’s expansion plans in Egypt, while Nassetta reaffirmed the importance of the Egyptian market to Hilton. He highlighted the group’s expansion across several Egyptian destinations, including the North Coast, as well as its activities in Nile cruises and dahabiya sailing trips. Fathy also met with representatives of a Saudi company specialising in cruise tourism to discuss increasing the number of its cruises calling at Egyptian ports and tourist destinations as part of its Mediterranean itineraries, particularly along the North Coast and in El Alamein. The minister welcomed expanded cooperation in the sector. Both sides agreed to coordinate with the Egyptian Tourism Federation to explore ways to activate the partnership and increase tourist arrivals through cruise tourism. During his visit, Fathy also gave several media interviews to Maltese outlets to outline the ministry’s vision and strategy and highlight the latest developments in Egypt’s tourism sector. The meetings were attended by Ahmed Youssef, CEO of the Egyptian Tourism Authority; Rana Gohar, adviser to the tourism minister for communications and foreign relations and supervisor of the ministry’s international relations and agreements department; Ahmed Nabil, assistant minister for aviation and follow-up; and Suzanne Mostafa, head of the tourism marketing central administration at the Egyptian Tourism Promotion Authority.

headline: Egypt’s net international reserves rise by $5.9bn in 9M 2026
summary: The Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) has revealed that its net international reserves increased by $5.896bn during the first nine months of 2026, reaching $57.348bn in September, compared with $51.452bn in December 2025. According to renowned banking expert Mohamed Abdel Aal, Egypt’s foreign exchange reserves comprise a diversified basket of major international currencies, including the US dollar, euro, pound sterling, Japanese yen, and Chinese yuan. These currencies are allocated in line with the CBE’s strategy for managing liquidity and maintaining a balance between exchange rates and stability in global markets. He noted that net reserves continued their upward trajectory for the 49th consecutive month, reaching $57.350bn in September 2026, compared with approximately $57.214bn in August, an increase of $136m and monthly growth of around 0.24%. Although this monthly increase may appear modest in numerical terms, Abdel Aal said a closer examination reveals implications that extend beyond the size of reserves to their quality. He stressed that the strength of the Egyptian economy’s external position no longer depends solely on the level of reserves, but is increasingly supported by an integrated set of positive indicators. He explained that improvements in funding sources reflect a structural development in the Egyptian economy’s external position, which international institutions and credit rating agencies monitor as a more accurate measure of economic resilience and the ability to absorb shocks. Mohamed Abdel Aal In August 2026, the banking sector’s net foreign assets rose to $31.2bn, their highest level since January 2020, supported by an increase in commercial banks’ net foreign assets to $12.4bn, alongside a rise in the CBE’s net foreign assets to $18.8bn. According to Abdel Aal, these figures carry significant implications, indicating that the improvement in international reserves is no longer confined to the CBE’s balance sheet, but is also supported by the banking system as a whole, with foreign assets exceeding external liabilities, making the improvement more sustainable. He added that the recovery was not limited to banking assets, but extended to actual sources of foreign currency. Remittances from Egyptians working abroad recorded notable growth of 28.1% during the first seven months of 2026, reaching $29.7bn, compared with $23.2bn during the same period last year. At the same time, the tourism sector maintained its performance, generating revenues of $12bn during the first eight months of the year, an increase of approximately 1.7%. In foreign trade, Egyptian exports continued to grow, reaching $31.9bn during the first seven months of 2026, exceeding the $29.9bn recorded during the corresponding period last year. Suez Canal revenues also recorded a noticeable improvement in the second quarter of the year, reaching $1.26bn, compared with around $1.1bn in the first quarter, representing growth of 13%. Abdel Aal said the continued accumulation of reserves over 49 consecutive months represents more than a financial figure. It constitutes a cumulative line of defence that strengthens the economy’s ability to withstand financial and geopolitical shocks and fluctuations in energy markets, gives monetary policymakers greater flexibility, and reinforces the confidence of international institutions. He noted that a particularly striking development was the growth in reserves despite a decline in the dollar value of their gold component, which stood at $17.46bn in September 2026, down by $1.6bn as global gold prices fell by more than $270 per ounce. However, the increase in the liquid foreign-currency component fully offset this decline, highlighting the flexibility of the reserve composition as an additional strength in managing the reserve portfolio. Addressing recurring questions about the adequacy of reserves, Abdel Aal said the modern professional approach goes beyond identifying a safe level of reserves to determining the optimal level, assessed according to import coverage, short-term external debt, and the nature of capital flows. He noted that the real challenge is not to maximise reserves without limit, but to strike a careful balance between security, liquidity, and investment returns. Looking ahead to the final quarter of 2026, Abdel Aal said that, with foreign currency inflows continuing and the foreign exchange market remaining stable, there appeared to be scope for reserves to maintain their upward trend, although the pace of growth would remain dependent on geopolitical developments and global energy prices. Abdel Aal stressed that foreign exchange reserves are more than figures recorded on the Central Bank’s books. They serve as a safety valve that is reshaping market confidence in the Egyptian economy. He said the continued upward trend was undoubtedly the result of carefully considered monetary and fiscal policies that strengthen the country’s economic security.

headline: Yemen's Houthis renew warning over Saudi airports after deadly Riyadh attack
summary: By Jana Choukeir, Maha El Dahan and Timour AzhariDUBAI/RIYADH, Oct 11 (Reuters) - Yemen's Houthis warned airlines, travellers and airport workers on Sunday to stay away from Saudi airports, a day after an attack on Riyadh's international airport killed 12 people and wounded more than 300 others.It was the deadliest such attack in the kingdom in more than a decade and comes amid an escalation of fighting between the Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces.
body_text:
By Jana Choukeir, Maha El Dahan and Timour Azhari

DUBAI/RIYADH, Oct 11 (Reuters) - Yemen's Houthis warned airlines, travellers and airport workers on Sunday to stay away from Saudi airports, a day after an attack on Riyadh's international airport killed 12 people and wounded more than 300 others.

It was the deadliest such attack in the kingdom in more than a decade and comes amid an escalation of fighting between the Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces.

"We renew our warning to all airlines, experts, employees, workers and travellers against using Saudi airports and airspace, as they are vulnerable to attack and have become a theatre of operations for our forces, with the exception of the airports in (the holy cities of) Mecca and Medina," the Houthis said in a post on X.

"We urge everyone to take our warnings seriously, and Saudi Arabia bears responsibility for any failed interceptions."

Saudi Arabia has stepped up its military involvement in Yemen in recent weeks, launching strikes against theHouthis and backing a Yemeni government counteroffensive after the group seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month.

President Donald Trump said on Saturday the United States was considering joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis in the conflict, a spillover from the wider war on Iran that the US and Israel launched in February.

The Saudi-led coalition said on Saturday that a projectile had also fallen near King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, in the kingdom's Eastern Province. The coalition also reported intercepting a drone in the region on Sunday.

INTERNATIONAL ENERGY CONFERENCE STILL GOING AHEAD IN RIYADH

Saturday's attack has forced the temporary closure of King Khalid International Airport but the Saudi energy ministry said a long-planned international energy conference was still going ahead in Riyadh on Sunday.

The five-day WPC Energy Congress is taking place at a conventioncentre some 10 km (6 miles) from the airport. State TV said more than 70 ministers, 300 company executives and representatives of over 25 international energy organisations have confirmed their attendance.

It was not immediately clear whether the participants would attend in person or virtually.

A ministerial meeting of the International Energy Forum is also set to go ahead on Sunday, with its plenary session to be held behind closed doors, according to a media advisory. No further details were immediately available.

Separately, Saudi authorities notified parents that in-person classes would be suspended and shifted to remote learning from Sunday until Thursday for all students, teachers and administrative staff.

In Saturday's attack, the third on Riyadh's airport in a week, the 12 dead included 4 Saudis, 2 Bangladeshis and nationals of the United States, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt, Saudi authorities said.

Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said airport operations were temporarily suspended pending damage and safety assessments, without specifying when flights would resume.

Two previous attacks on Riyadh's international airport earlier in the week had killed four people and caused heavy damage to a Saudi commercial plane parked on the tarmac.

(Reporting by Jana Choukeir, writing by Andrew Mills Editing by Gareth Jones)

headline: Imran Khan's provincial government suspended by Pakistan president over militancy fight
summary: By Asif Shahzad and Ariba ShahidISLAMABAD, Oct 11 (Reuters) - Pakistan's president declared a state of emergency and suspended the provincial government of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan on Sunday, the president's office said, following allegations it has failed to tackle Islamist militancy.The constitution allows the federal government to take over some or all provincial government functions during an emergency.
body_text:
By Asif Shahzad and Ariba Shahid

ISLAMABAD, Oct 11 (Reuters) - Pakistan's president declared a state of emergency and suspended the provincial government of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan on Sunday, the president's office said, following allegations it has failed to tackle Islamist militancy.

The constitution allows the federal government to take over some or all provincial government functions during an emergency.

The provincial governor will take charge with an advisory council, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar told a news conference in Islamabad, adding that the arrangement will initially be in place for six months.

The move comes after Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party rallied for several days to pressure the government for his release, threatening to march on the capital Islamabad in coming days amid deepening political instability.

The federal government and the military have accused Khan's party of failing to curb Islamist militants in the northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province bordering Afghanistan, which has suffered an increasing number of militant attacks in recent months.

Khan's party rejects the allegation, saying the federal government failed to provide the provincial government with funding and equipment to combat the militancy.

"The situation is so grave that you wouldn't see any residents coming out of their houses after evening in some of the districts," said Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi.

Islamabad accuses neighbouring Afghanistan of harboring Islamist militants who launch attacks inside Pakistan, and says that Khan's party had been sympathizing with both the Taliban in Kabul and their affiliates at home.

Both the Afghan Taliban and Khan's party have denied the accusation.

President Asif Ali Zardari declared an emergency on the advice of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif following a federal cabinet decision, the president's office said.

"This is more of a coup disguised as emergency," said Zulfikar Bukhari, Khan's aide and his party's spokesperson.

Bukhari said it was a "ridiculous decision" that would only lead to further bloodshed and instability.

The country's powerful military is widely seen as the ultimate power broker to decide who will rule the South Asian nation of 240 million. Khan's supporters say the military rigged the 2024 election against the 74-year-old former cricket star, an allegation the military denies.

KHAN'S PARTY CHIEF MINISTER'S MOVEMENT BLOCKED

Ahead of the planned march, authorities detained three of Khan's sisters and hundreds of party activists in recent days.

Restrictions have been placed on Chief Minister, Sohail Afridi of Khan's party in the northwestern province, one of his close aides told Reuters. All roads leading to his office had been blocked with shipping containers, with hundreds of police deployed, said witnesses.

The PTI's last large-scale protest two years ago ended in deadly clashes with security forces.

The government has cut access to the capital, Islamabad, to bar the protesters from reaching parliament, blocking major highways with shipping containers and deploying tens of thousands of security forces, interior ministry officials said.

STANDOFF OVER KHAN'S HEALTH

The standoff comes more than a month after the government defied a court order and refused to allow Khan's treatment in a private hospital, despite mounting concerns over his health.

The protest also coincides with public discontent over inflation and rising fuel prices that has spread beyond Khan's core supporters.

Khan's 2023 arrest sparked nationwide riots that threatened the standing of the Pakistani military. He says he is a political prisoner and the military is making up charges to keep him out of the country's politics, a charge the army denies.

Cases against Khan have ranged from concerns over state gifts to instigating violent attacks on military and state installations, and an accusation of an unlawful marriage.

All convictions but one have since been suspended or overturned, with appeals pending. He ⁠denies wrongdoing.

(Reporting by Asif Shahzad and Ariba Shahid in Islamabad; Additional reporting by Mubasher Bukhari in Lahore; Editing by Jamie Freed and Elaine Hardcastle)

Oct 10 (Reuters) - The US militarysaid on Saturday it had disabled a commercial cargo vessel in the Gulf of Oman after the ship's crew ignored warnings and attempted to run a naval blockade against Iran.

"AU.S. military fighter jet struck the stern of Panama-flagged M/V Ocean Molica (also known as the “Arika Sun”) with a precision munition, fully disabling the ship’s propulsion without harming the crew," the US Central Commandposted on X.

CENTCOM said the cargo vessel had attempted to transit regional waters after leaving an Iranian port.

Reuters was not immediately able to reach the bulk carrier's operator for comment.

CENTCOM warned mariners in the Gulf of Oman and the approaches to the Strait of Hormuz to heed blockade warnings, monitor notice-to-mariners broadcasts and contact US naval forces.

The number of vessels transiting the vital strait fell to the lowest in more than two months after attacks on tankers reached their highest level last week since the US and Israel launched the war on Iran in February, raising concerns over shipping disruptions and supporting crude prices.

Before the war, the Strait of Hormuz carried 20% of the world's oil consumption.

(Reporting by Rishabh Jaiswal and Abu Sultan in Bengaluru; Editing by William Mallard)

headline: Abbas postpones Palestinian legislative elections to September 2027
summary: Palestinian president Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday postponed legislative elections to September next year, official media said, confirming widespread speculation that they would be delayed once again. The first legislative elections since 2006, which the international community has strongly advocated for, had been scheduled for November 28, with a presidential election expected in early 2027.
body_text:
Palestinian president Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday postponed legislative elections to September next year, official media said, confirming widespread speculation that they would be delayed once again.

The first legislative elections since 2006, which the international community has strongly advocated for, had been scheduled for November 28, with a presidential election expected in early 2027.

But both elections will now be held on September 11, 2027, Abbas said in a decree, blaming Israeli "obstacles", according to the Palestinian official news agency Wafa.

Israel, which will hold its own elections on October 27, had blasted Abbas as a "corrupt dictator" over the postponement.

Abbas's office, in a statement published by Wafa, blamed the delay on "obstacles imposed by Israeli measures... as well as the need to create appropriate political, security and on-the-ground conditions".

Abu Amin Joudeh, a displaced man living in the central Gaza city of Deir el-Balah, said Palestinians wanted to vote for their representatives.

"We know things are difficult here because of the war and all the destruction, but how long will the elections continue to be postponed?" said the 40-year-old.

This week, the Ramallah-based Palestinian Authority said Israel refused to allow Palestinian election officials access to east Jerusalem or Gaza ahead of the legislative elections.

Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar on Friday had denied Israel was obstructing the process.

"(Abbas's) attempt to drag Israel into this, falsely claiming that Israel imposed obstacles to holding elections, is yet another ridiculous lie designed to evade responsibility and accountability," Saar said on X.

Palestinian factions including Abbas's Fatah party and its longtime Islamist rival Hamas had agreed to recommend the elections be postponed at a meeting in Cairo on Wednesday, a source who was present told AFP.

Mohammed Dahlan, head of a splinter group from Abbas's Fatah party, called the delay a "crime against democracy".

"Abbas and the circle of self-serving beneficiaries around him have turned the institutions of the Palestinian Authority into a private fiefdom," Dahlan, a Gaza native based in the United Arab Emirates, said in a statement.

Esmat Mansour, a journalist and former official for the Democratic Front for the Liberation of Palestine (DFLP), a leftist party, suggested that Israeli restrictions had been known at the time the elections were initially scheduled and were not the only explanation for the delay.

"The only thing that could explain this delay is your fear of elections. You are afraid of holding elections. You do not want people to have a say," Mansour said in a Facebook video addressing other Palestinian factions.

But Palestinian analyst Ghassan al-Khatib disagreed, telling AFP he never expected there to be a vote because "Israel is making conditions that are not conducive to elections".

"I don't think that the internal Palestinian politics are the reason for the postponement," the former Palestinian Authority minister said, pointing to the devastation and ongoing bloodshed in Gaza, as well as Israeli military operations and settler violence in the West Bank.

East Jerusalem, which Israel occupied in 1967 before annexing it, also hosts a large Palestinian population that the PA says should vote in elections, but it accuses Israel of refusing to allow them to organise it.

Holding polls is part of the reforms demanded by the international community, including the European Union, for the Palestinian Authority.

The last legislative elections in the Palestinian territories were in 2006, when Islamist movement Hamas defeated Fatah, which dominates the Palestinian Authority.

The ensuing rift set off a round of factional fighting with Hamas later seizing power in the Gaza Strip, creating a divide with Fatah in the West Bank.

As a result, the Palestinian Legislative Council, which is the PA's parliament, has not met since 2007.

Abbas won the last Palestinian presidential election in 2005, and his term should have expired in 2009, but he has since ruled by decree.

headline: Thousands join pro-Palestinian marches in several European cities
summary: Thousands of people on Saturday joined pro-Palestinian marches in London, Berlin and Dublin calling for an end to Israeli strikes on Gaza, three years
body_text:
Thousands of people on Saturday joined pro-Palestinian marches in London, Berlin and Dublin calling for an end to Israeli strikes on Gaza, three years after Hamas's October 7 attack.

Several thousand marchers in London carried placards reading "End the genocide" and "Free Palestine" as they made their way along the route near the British parliament.

"We are here today to mark three years of the ongoing genocide in Gaza," Aimee Shalan, director of the Palestine Solidarity Campaign, told AFP.

Western sanctions over settler violence did not go far enough, she said, calling for "full sanctions on Israel".

A ceasefire began a year ago and although Israel has reduced its level of attacks it has kept striking Gaza on a near-daily basis.

Strikes have killed some 1,450 Palestinians since the ceasefire, according to Gaza's health ministry.

London police said they had arrested 20 people including a man and a woman with placards supporting the organisation Palestine Action, banned under UK law.

Recent graduate Hibo Hassan, 23, said she was there to show her solidarity.

"Although it is happening in the Middle East, it affects us here now," she said.

"It's extremely dystopian and that is something we should be all scared about," she added.

Another protester, a 32-year-old Kosovar immigrant who gave his name as Kobe, said his own experience of war made him want to "stand up today and not let history repeat" itself.

A small counter-demonstration was organised by Stop The Hate UK, a Jewish-led, pro-Israel campaign group.

Ahead of the protest, organised by the Palestine Coalition, London's Metropolitan Police said it would be using powers under public order legislation to require anyone wearing a face covering to hide their identity to remove it.

"We will take a zero-tolerance approach to hate crime and other offending," said senior Met officer Carl Galvin.

In Berlin, a similar march organised by the group United for Palestine drew around 3,500 people as it set off from a square between the chancellery and parliament, said police.

Many denounced Germany's arms exports to Israel, carrying banners and placards condemning Berlin's military support.

For decades, Germany has seen resolute support for Israel as a fundamental duty largely because of Nazi Germany's responsibility for the genocide of millions of European Jews during the Holocaust.

"I find it really terrible that Germany finds it so difficult to criticise Israel," a student told AFP, who asked not to be named.

In Dublin, protesters took part in a march organised by the Irish Palestine Solidarity Campaign.

Saturday's protests came three days after the third anniversary of the October 7, 2023 attack.

The attack was the deadliest in Israel's history, resulting in the deaths of 1,221 people, according to an AFP tally based on official Israeli figures.

Militants also dragged 251 hostages into Gaza, 44 of them already dead.

In response, Israel launched a military offensive that has left most of Gaza in ruins and killed more than 74,200 people, according to Gaza's health ministry.

headline: Houthi strike on Saudi airport kills 12, worst attack on kingdom in a decade
summary: By Timour Azhari and Enas AlashrayRIYADH, Oct 10 (Reuters) - At least 12 people were killed and more than 300 wounded in an attack on Riyadh's international airport on Saturday, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade, as the Iran-backed Houthis escalate a campaign they launched this summer.The dead from the third attack this week on the airport included four Saudis, two people from Bangladesh and one person each from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt, the Saudi civil aviation authority said. At the latest count, 309 were wounded, officials said.
body_text:
By Timour Azhari and Enas Alashray

RIYADH, Oct 10 (Reuters) - At least 12 people were killed and more than 300 wounded in an attack on Riyadh's international airport on Saturday, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade, as the Iran-backed Houthis escalate a campaign they launched this summer.

The dead from the third attack this week on the airport included four Saudis, two people from Bangladesh and one person each from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt, the Saudi civil aviation authority said. At the latest count, 309 were wounded, officials said.

President Donald Trump said Washington was considering joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis in the conflict, a spillover from the war on Iran that the US and Israel launched in February.

Hospitals were flooded with wounded brought by ambulance and helicopter, some in critical condition after the attack, which occurred without warning.

CONFLICT ESCALATES AFTER YEMEN WAR CEASEFIRE UNRAVELS

The two previous attacks on King Khalid International Airport this week killed four and caused heavy damage to a Saudi commercial plane parked on the tarmac.The strikes have exposed vulnerabilities in Saudi defence capabilities as it wages an air campaign against the Houthis to support a ground war by the Yemeni government against the Iran-backed group.

The Houthis have not claimed responsibility for the attack, but a Saudi-led military coalition vowed to respond.

Trump, asked whether the US planned to join Saudi strikes on the Houthis, told reporters: "We may. We're going to look at it. We just found out about the recent attack, so we'll make a decision. We move very quickly."

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio condemned the attacks on the airport, saying they "demonstrate a blatant disregard for innocent civilian life". UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres also condemned Saturday's strike, reiterating that attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure violate international law and must cease immediately.

Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government have claimed hundreds of strikes on targets in Houthi-held territory. The Houthis have said these killed civilians including women and children. Reuters could not independently verify those claims.

The Saudis entered the Yemen war in 2015 at the head of an Arab coalition to try to force the Houthis out of the Yemeni capital Sanaa. The war became a bloody stalemate, with hundreds of thousands of Yemenis killed by fighting and famine.

A 2022 ceasefire reached by the Saudis and the Houthis unravelled this summer, culminating in a lightning Houthi advance that took the Red Sea chokepoint of Bab el-Mandeb from Saudi-backed government forces.

EXPLOSION, PEOPLE ON GROUND, AMBULANCES RUSHING

The Saudi-backed Yemeni government began an offensive this week to try to retake that territory, but it has made only slow gains, even as the Houthis put the country's third-largest city, Taiz, under siege.

On Saturday, all flights were diverted from Riyadh and operations at the airport that serves a city of 8 million people were suspended, the Saudi civil aviation authority said.

The head of the Houthi media office posted on X that the group had "shut down Riyadh international airport". The Houthis have said airliners should avoid Saudi airspace, declaring it a zone of military operations.

The Houthis have warned international airlines against operating flights through Saudi airspace, saying it has become a theatre of their military operations, with the exception of airspace over the holy cities of Mecca and Medina.

An eyewitness at the airport reported seeing an explosion and then multiple people lying injured on the ground inside. More than a dozen ambulances were seen rushing towards the facility. A video verified by Reuters showed ambulances at the airport.

An injuredtraveller told Reuters they saw something fly across the sky outside the airport before part of the ceiling near a departure gate collapsed.

The US embassy in Riyadh said it "strongly recommends all US citizens avoid this airport and surrounding areas."

Earlier Houthi attacks had prompted a number of carriers to suspend or cancel services to the Saudi capital, shortly before Riyadh is due to host major energy and investment conferences. Organizers of those conferences said ahead of the strikes on Saturday they would go ahead as planned.

(Reporting by Timour Azhari in Riyadh; Additional reporting by Steve Holland in Washington; Writing by Enas Alashray, Maya Gebeily and Ann Saphir; Editing by Gareth Jones, Joe Bavier, David Gregorio and William Mallard)
