headline: Egypt’s annual urban inflation eases to 13.9% in September
summary: Egypt’s annual urban inflation rate fell to 13.9% in September, down from 14.5% in August 2026, according to the Central Agency for Public Mobilisation and Statistics (CAPMAS). However, monthly inflation accelerated to 1.3% in September, compared with 0.1% in August, driven primarily by higher vegetable and food prices. In a statement issued on Saturday, CAPMAS attributed the monthly increase primarily to a 15.1% rise in vegetable prices. Prices also increased by 0.4% for grains and bread, 2.5% for meat and poultry, 1.2% for fish and seafood, 0.4% for dairy products, cheese and eggs, 0.3% for oils and fats, 2.6% for fruit, 0.2% for sugar and sugary foods, 0.3% for coffee, tea and cocoa, 0.5% for mineral and carbonated water and natural juices, and 0.1% for tobacco. Prices also rose by 1.7% for fabrics, 0.6% for ready-made clothing, 1.8% for clothing cleaning, repair and rental services, and 1.2% for footwear. Actual rentals for housing increased by 0.9%, while housing maintenance and repair costs recorded a similar rise. Water and miscellaneous housing-related services rose by 0.1%, while electricity, gas and other fuels increased by 0.5%. Prices of furnishings, household equipment, carpets and other floor coverings rose by 1.1%, while household textiles increased by 0.6%. Household appliances rose by 0.4%, glassware, tableware and household utensils by 0.8%, tools and equipment for homes and gardens by 0.8%, and goods and services for routine household maintenance by 1.5%. In the healthcare sector, prices increased by 1.2% for outpatient services and 0.7% for hospital services. Vehicle prices rose by 0.3%, while telephone and fax equipment increased by 0.4%. Cultural and recreational services rose by 0.4%, newspapers, books and stationery by 1%, ready-made meals by 0.3%, personal care by 0.7%, and personal effects by 1.2%. By contrast, prices fell by 1.1% for audio-visual, photographic and information-processing equipment and by 0.6% for package holidays. Annual headline inflation across Egypt as a whole reached 12.8% in September, compared with 12.7% in August, according to CAPMAS. The Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) has revised down its inflation outlook, expecting annual headline inflation to remain stable in the third quarter of 2026 before declining gradually towards its target of 7%, plus or minus 2 percentage points, in the second half of 2027. The revised outlook reflects recent inflation developments that have been more favourable than previously expected. In a statement issued by its Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) on 24 September, the CBE said the downward revision to its inflation forecasts would reinforce the prevailing monetary conditions, which it described as sufficiently restrictive, providing further support for the expected disinflationary path. However, the bank warned that the balance of risks surrounding the inflation outlook remained tilted to the upside, reflecting renewed regional hostilities. These risks could affect domestic inflation through the pass-through of fiscal consolidation measures and global food price increases exceeding expectations, particularly if international energy prices remain elevated for an extended period. On the same day, the MPC decided to keep its key interest rates unchanged at 19% for overnight deposits, 20% for overnight lending, and 19.5% for the credit and discount rate and the main operation rate. The decision marked the fifth consecutive meeting at which the CBE had maintained rates, following similar decisions on 20 August, 9 July, 21 May and 2 April. The CBE’s key interest rates serve as the main indicator of the short-term direction of Egyptian pound interest rates. The MPC said its decision reflected its assessment of the latest inflation developments and outlook, alongside changes in the risks surrounding inflation. It reaffirmed that it would continue to assess monetary conditions in light of economic developments affecting the expected inflation path and the associated risks, adding that it would not hesitate to use the tools at its disposal to safeguard price stability.

headline: Egypt, ICARDA seek to scale up solar irrigation, desalination projects
summary: Egypt’s Water Resources and Irrigation Minister Hani Sewilam and International Center for Agricultural Research in the Dry Areas (ICARDA) Director General Nizar Haddad discussed expanding cooperation on water conservation, solar-powered irrigation, desalination and soil salinity management under a joint programme running through 2027. The two sides reviewed implementation of their 2025-2027 joint work programme, which aims to translate areas of cooperation outlined in a memorandum of understanding signed during the seventh Cairo Water Week in 2024 into practical projects and activities. The programme includes a pilot desalination unit at the National Water Research Center’s Wadi El Natrun research station under the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organization’s Water Scarcity Initiative, in which ICARDA participates. Other activities include establishing farmer field schools in Qena and Kafr El-Sheikh and introducing integrated systems for managing soil salinity alongside agricultural production and aquaculture. The meeting also reviewed the “Enhancing Food Security in Egypt” project, implemented in cooperation with the Japanese government, which aims to strengthen climate resilience, improve agricultural and water productivity, and support sustainable rural livelihoods. The project includes deploying solar energy for irrigation, managing soil salinity, improving agricultural extension services, building technical capacity and introducing digital tools. Sewilam called for successful practices in water productivity, solar-powered irrigation, salinity management, agricultural extension and digital irrigation to be expanded to additional areas. He said cooperation with ICARDA aimed to improve water-use efficiency while strengthening the long-term sustainability and productivity of Egypt’s agricultural sector.

headline: Cornerstone laid for date-processing complex in New Valley’s Shorbagy Oasis
summary: Manal Awad, Minister of Local Development and Environment, and Hanan Magdy, Governor of New Valley, laid the cornerstone for a date-processing complex in the Shorbagy Oasis area, marking a key step towards shifting from agricultural production to agro-processing and maximising added value. The ceremony was attended by Amr Abdel-Moneim, Head of the Upper Egypt Development Authority; Mohamed Kegk, Deputy Governor of New Valley; several members of the Senate; and the governorate’s executive and popular leaders. Awad and Magdy received a briefing on the project, which covers approximately 64,000 square metres and has reached around 30% completion. The complex will feature an integrated system for handling date crops and production inputs, including lines for receiving, sorting, grading and preparing dates, alongside automated processing and manufacturing lines equipped with imported machinery and production systems. It will also include packaging lines, handling and transportation equipment, and storage and refrigeration facilities with a capacity of approximately 20,000 tonnes. The project’s infrastructure will rely on modern irrigation systems and solar energy, alongside efforts to diversify crops and introduce varieties offering higher economic returns. The wider project includes more than 650,000 palm trees at different stages of growth and fruit production, including approximately 300,000 fruit-bearing trees. It aims to increase the total number of palms to one million, producing a range of date varieties, alongside strategic crops, fruit, olives, and medicinal and aromatic plants. The complex is expected to create around 1,500 jobs across the agricultural and industrial value chains, helping strengthen the competitiveness of Egyptian products and expand date production, processing and exports to domestic and international markets. Awad said the government sought to bring about a qualitative leap in agro-processing in New Valley Governorate to strengthen the competitiveness of Egyptian products in global markets and generate greater economic returns from the governorate’s leading strategic crop. She added that the complex aimed to integrate post-harvest activities, processing, packaging, storage, market preparation and export operations, linking agricultural production with industry and date-related logistics services. Awad noted that the complex would serve as the processing and value-addition hub within the agricultural production system at Shorbagy Oasis, covering the entire value chain, from cultivation and harvesting to sorting and grading, handling and cold storage, packaging and processing, marketing and exports. For her part, Magdy said the project would also include a weighbridge to facilitate the receipt, handling and shipment of dates, as well as industrial facilities for producing baraneek packaging crates, zamat sacks and white bags used to cover date bunches. She added that the project formed part of the governorate’s efforts to maximise the economic value of its date crop, strengthen the competitiveness of Egyptian products and increase local added value by encouraging date-based industries and improving product quality to meet export market requirements.

headline: Egypt, AUDA-NEPAD agree framework to expand African drug, vaccine production
summary: Egypt has agreed with the African Union Development Agency – New Partnership for Africa’s Development (AUDA-NEPAD) programme to develop a long-term cooperation framework to expand local production of medicines, vaccines and medical technologies across Africa and identify priority healthcare projects for financing and implementation. The agreement was discussed during a meeting between Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar and AUDA-NEPAD Chief Executive Nardos Bekele-Thomas on the sidelines of the World Health Summit in Berlin, according to Egypt’s Health Ministry. The proposed framework would identify priority initiatives, focal points and implementation and follow-up mechanisms, with a focus on strengthening local production and improving access to essential medicines, vaccines and medical technologies across the continent. Discussions covered pharmaceutical regulation, drug and vaccine manufacturing, technology transfer and the development of more resilient medical supply chains to reduce Africa’s dependence on external sources. The two sides also discussed mobilising investment and development financing for priority healthcare infrastructure and pharmaceutical manufacturing projects. The ministry did not announce specific projects, funding commitments or an implementation timetable. Egypt expressed its readiness to draw on its pharmaceutical manufacturing capacity, regulatory experience and healthcare expertise to support African health systems and expand access to medical products and services. The proposed cooperation would also cover professional training and regulatory capacity building, alongside disease surveillance, pandemic preparedness, laboratory capabilities and emergency response. The meeting also addressed primary healthcare, universal health coverage and health insurance, with both sides discussing ways to strengthen healthcare systems across the continent. Egypt and AUDA-NEPAD further agreed to identify potential joint health projects that could be developed in cooperation with African financing institutions and international development partners.

headline: Egypt, Saudi Arabia discuss expanding tourism ties during WTTC summit
summary: Egyptian Tourism and Antiquities Minister Sherif Fathy held a series ofmeetings on the sidelines of the World Travel and Tourism Council’s (WTTC) 26th Global Summit in Valletta, Malta, to discuss expanding tourism cooperation, boosting arrivals to Egypt, and attracting more cruise and yacht tourism. Fathy met with Saudi Deputy Minister of Tourism Abdul Mohsen Al Mazid to discuss strengthening tourism ties and increasing travel between the two countries. Both sides highlighted the close relations between Egypt and Saudi Arabia and reviewed developments in their respective tourism sectors. The Egyptian minister outlined trends in tourist arrivals to Egypt and the ministry’s plans to expand the use of modern technology and artificial intelligence (AI) in promoting the country as a tourism destination. Discussions also covered the growing appeal of Egypt’s North Coast among Saudi tourists and opportunities to develop yacht tourism in the Red Sea. On the industry front, Fathy met with Neal Jones, president of Europe, Middle East and Africa at Marriott International, and Chris Nassetta, president and CEO of Hilton, to discuss the groups’ expansion plans in Egypt in line with the country’s targets for increasing tourist arrivals. The meetings also explored cooperation in training and skills development for Egyptian tourism and hospitality workers, opportunities for Egyptian talent to gain international experience at the groups’ hotels worldwide, and ways to leverage their global networks to promote Egypt and attract new segments of visitors. Jones outlined Marriott’s expansion plans in Egypt, while Nassetta reaffirmed the importance of the Egyptian market to Hilton. He highlighted the group’s expansion across several Egyptian destinations, including the North Coast, as well as its activities in Nile cruises and dahabiya sailing trips. Fathy also met with representatives of a Saudi company specialising in cruise tourism to discuss increasing the number of its cruises calling at Egyptian ports and tourist destinations as part of its Mediterranean itineraries, particularly along the North Coast and in El Alamein. The minister welcomed expanded cooperation in the sector. Both sides agreed to coordinate with the Egyptian Tourism Federation to explore ways to activate the partnership and increase tourist arrivals through cruise tourism. During his visit, Fathy also gave several media interviews to Maltese outlets to outline the ministry’s vision and strategy and highlight the latest developments in Egypt’s tourism sector. The meetings were attended by Ahmed Youssef, CEO of the Egyptian Tourism Authority; Rana Gohar, adviser to the tourism minister for communications and foreign relations and supervisor of the ministry’s international relations and agreements department; Ahmed Nabil, assistant minister for aviation and follow-up; and Suzanne Mostafa, head of the tourism marketing central administration at the Egyptian Tourism Promotion Authority.

headline: Egypt’s net international reserves rise by $5.9bn in 9M 2026
summary: The Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) has revealed that its net international reserves increased by $5.896bn during the first nine months of 2026, reaching $57.348bn in September, compared with $51.452bn in December 2025. According to renowned banking expert Mohamed Abdel Aal, Egypt’s foreign exchange reserves comprise a diversified basket of major international currencies, including the US dollar, euro, pound sterling, Japanese yen, and Chinese yuan. These currencies are allocated in line with the CBE’s strategy for managing liquidity and maintaining a balance between exchange rates and stability in global markets. He noted that net reserves continued their upward trajectory for the 49th consecutive month, reaching $57.350bn in September 2026, compared with approximately $57.214bn in August, an increase of $136m and monthly growth of around 0.24%. Although this monthly increase may appear modest in numerical terms, Abdel Aal said a closer examination reveals implications that extend beyond the size of reserves to their quality. He stressed that the strength of the Egyptian economy’s external position no longer depends solely on the level of reserves, but is increasingly supported by an integrated set of positive indicators. He explained that improvements in funding sources reflect a structural development in the Egyptian economy’s external position, which international institutions and credit rating agencies monitor as a more accurate measure of economic resilience and the ability to absorb shocks. Mohamed Abdel Aal In August 2026, the banking sector’s net foreign assets rose to $31.2bn, their highest level since January 2020, supported by an increase in commercial banks’ net foreign assets to $12.4bn, alongside a rise in the CBE’s net foreign assets to $18.8bn. According to Abdel Aal, these figures carry significant implications, indicating that the improvement in international reserves is no longer confined to the CBE’s balance sheet, but is also supported by the banking system as a whole, with foreign assets exceeding external liabilities, making the improvement more sustainable. He added that the recovery was not limited to banking assets, but extended to actual sources of foreign currency. Remittances from Egyptians working abroad recorded notable growth of 28.1% during the first seven months of 2026, reaching $29.7bn, compared with $23.2bn during the same period last year. At the same time, the tourism sector maintained its performance, generating revenues of $12bn during the first eight months of the year, an increase of approximately 1.7%. In foreign trade, Egyptian exports continued to grow, reaching $31.9bn during the first seven months of 2026, exceeding the $29.9bn recorded during the corresponding period last year. Suez Canal revenues also recorded a noticeable improvement in the second quarter of the year, reaching $1.26bn, compared with around $1.1bn in the first quarter, representing growth of 13%. Abdel Aal said the continued accumulation of reserves over 49 consecutive months represents more than a financial figure. It constitutes a cumulative line of defence that strengthens the economy’s ability to withstand financial and geopolitical shocks and fluctuations in energy markets, gives monetary policymakers greater flexibility, and reinforces the confidence of international institutions. He noted that a particularly striking development was the growth in reserves despite a decline in the dollar value of their gold component, which stood at $17.46bn in September 2026, down by $1.6bn as global gold prices fell by more than $270 per ounce. However, the increase in the liquid foreign-currency component fully offset this decline, highlighting the flexibility of the reserve composition as an additional strength in managing the reserve portfolio. Addressing recurring questions about the adequacy of reserves, Abdel Aal said the modern professional approach goes beyond identifying a safe level of reserves to determining the optimal level, assessed according to import coverage, short-term external debt, and the nature of capital flows. He noted that the real challenge is not to maximise reserves without limit, but to strike a careful balance between security, liquidity, and investment returns. Looking ahead to the final quarter of 2026, Abdel Aal said that, with foreign currency inflows continuing and the foreign exchange market remaining stable, there appeared to be scope for reserves to maintain their upward trend, although the pace of growth would remain dependent on geopolitical developments and global energy prices. Abdel Aal stressed that foreign exchange reserves are more than figures recorded on the Central Bank’s books. They serve as a safety valve that is reshaping market confidence in the Egyptian economy. He said the continued upward trend was undoubtedly the result of carefully considered monetary and fiscal policies that strengthen the country’s economic security.

headline: UN secretary-general condemns attack on airport in Riyadh
summary: Antonio Guterres urged to cease attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure immediately
body_text:
UN, October 11. /TASS/. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has strongly condemned an attack on the international airport in the capital of Saudi Arabia, he said in a statement.

"I am deeply shocked by and strongly condemn Saturday’s lethal attack by the Houthis on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, which reportedly killed 12 people and injured hundreds of civilians," the statement reads.

"Attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure are a violation of international law. These attacks must cease immediately."

According to the General Authority of Civil Aviation of Saudi Arabia, at least 12 people were killed and another 309 were injured as a result of the attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh.

analysis.framing: The article frames the event through the UN Secretary-General's condemnation of a Houthi attack on a Saudi airport, emphasizing international law and civilian casualties.

loaded_language.explanation: Emotionally charged diplomatic language that conveys moral outrage rather than neutral reporting.
Expresses a strong emotional reaction, adding subjective intensity.
The adjective 'lethal' emphasizes the deadly outcome, which is already stated by the casualty figures.
A legal characterization that frames the act as unlawful, which is an evaluative judgment.

omissions: Houthi perspective or statement
Context on the conflict in Yemen
Saudi-led coalition airstrikes in Yemen
Details about the type of attack or munitions used
International reactions beyond the UN

headline: Zelensky does not want to agree to settlement deal in Ukraine — Trump
summary: The US president separately said he thinks that "Russia would like to make a deal," when asked about plans to send his representatives to Moscow for negotiations on Ukraine
body_text:
WASHINGTON, October 11. /TASS/. Vladimir Zelensky, for various reasons, does not want to pursue a peaceful settlement in Ukraine, said US President Donald Trump.

"This is something that could have been solved many times, but for whatever reason, Zelensky does not want to make a deal," he told journalists at Andrews Air Force Base near Washington, returning from Tennessee to the White House.

"I think it would have been smart if he would have made a deal two years ago. He would have been a lot better off. He would have made a much better deal two years ago."

When asked about plans to send his representatives, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, to Moscow for negotiations on Ukraine, the president said: "I think that Russia would like to make a deal."

analysis.framing: The article frames the Ukraine settlement solely through Trump's assertion that Zelensky is the obstacle to peace, while noting Trump's claim that Russia wants a deal, without including any Ukrainian or European response.

loaded_language.quote: does not want to make a deal
loaded_language.explanation: Attributed to Trump, this phrase casts Zelensky as the sole obstructionist to peace, implying blame without addressing Ukraine's stated conditions or security concerns.
loaded_language.neutral_alternative: has not agreed to the proposed terms

loaded_language.explanation: Vague attribution dismisses any specific Ukrainian rationale for not accepting a deal, making the refusal appear arbitrary.
loaded_language.neutral_alternative: for reasons that have not been specified

loaded_language.quote: would have been a lot better off
loaded_language.explanation: Counterfactual claim presented without evidence, suggesting Ukraine's current situation is a direct result of not making a deal earlier.

omissions: Ukraine's stated conditions for any settlement, such as security guarantees or territorial integrity
European allies' positions on negotiations
Context about previous failed negotiations or the Istanbul talks
Any response from Zelensky or Ukrainian officials to Trump's remarks

headline: Abu Dhabi plans major road upgrades in Mussaffah to ease congestion and improve links
summary: Abu Dhabi is set to overhaul key roads in Mussaffah, with upgrades spanning 13 kilometres designed to cut congestion and improve safety.The Department of Municipalities and Transport (DMT) has announced plans to upgrade roads along the E30 and 8th Street corridors in Mussaffah, improving connections between the industrial area, Mohamed Bin Zayed City and Zayed City. The project aims to ease congestion, reduce travel time and improve road safety across the district.Central to the scheme is a new free-flowing motorway at 8th Street, featuring three lanes in each direction and three additional service lanes on each side to maintain access to shops and businesses. The upgraded street is expected to accommodate up to 4,000 vehicles per hour.The wider project includes upgrades to four interchanges along E30, improved connections with 8th Street and E20, and modifications to nine key junctions. Two new bridges linking Musaffah with Mohamed Bin Zayed City are also planned, along with a dedicated pedestrian bridge. Separate enhancement works will cover about 8km along 8th Street. Eisa Mubarak Al Mazrouei, Director General of Infrastructure Development at DMT, said the upgrades were designed to serve the varied demands placed on Mussaffah's road network. “By separating traffic passing through the area from local access and improving connections with surrounding communities, we can support economic activity while making everyday journeys easier and safer,” Mr Al Mazrouei said.The Mussaffah project forms part of broader efforts to strengthen connectivity across Abu Dhabi emirate. Among the wider initiatives is a planned two-tunnel undersea link running from the eastern tip of Abu Dhabi Island to Mussaffah, passing beneath Khor Al Maqta and the Al Hudayriyat Island channel. Officials said the decisions being made now are intended to support the emirate's long-term development needs.

headline: RTA wins Dubai-it Award for delivering projects at record speed
summary: The first Dubai-it Award for Institutions in the Field of Government has been given to the emirate's Roads and Transport Authority in recognition of its record-breaking delivery of infrastructure.Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister, Minister of Defence and Chairman of the Dubai Executive Council, presented the award to the RTA, citing its ability to deliver major roads, bridges and tunnels at twice the global benchmark for speed and efficiency. “Dubai-it means achieving something extraordinary with excellence in record time,” Sheikh Hamdan said.Dubai Metro has achieved a punctuality rate of 99.7 per cent, while the authority has completed more than 250 traffic improvements that reduced travel times by up to 60 per cent. It also executed major infrastructure projects, including the Infinity Bridge, at costs below the global average, while maintaining high-quality standards. The authority implemented 117 quick-win improvements within two years and made 82 services available with no waiting time. The RTA also developed AI-powered autonomous taxis and an air-taxi station, advancing Dubai's future mobility programme. Road feedback is now monitored and addressed within 24 hours, while cycle tracks have been expanded at pace.Mohammad Al Gergawi, Minister of Cabinet Affairs and Chairman of the Executive Office of Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid, said the award highlighted an institutional model built on sustained achievement and rapid response. “RTA's approach clearly reflected this philosophy on the ground by combining quality, speed and continuity, turning challenges into opportunities for development and service improvement,” Mr Al Gergawi said.The Dubai-it initiative was launched by Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid, Vice President and Ruler of Dubai, to embed a culture of bold ambition and excellent execution across public and private institutions. The annual Dubai-it Award recognises people, projects, companies and institutions that deliver extraordinary results, setting the standard continued development in the emirate.

headline: Pope Leo XIV to undergo lung surgery this week
summary: Pope Leo XIV said he would undergo surgery after doctors found a "localized nodule" in his lung.(Image credit: Gregorio Borgia)
body_text:
Pope Leo XIV delivers the Angelus prayer in St. Peter's Square at the Vatican, Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026. Gregorio Borgia/AP hide caption

Pope Leo XIV announced Sunday that he would have surgery this week to remove a "localized nodule" in his lung.

Leo said the nodule was found at a "very early stage" with doctors recommending surgery.

"Following their advice, I have therefore decided to undergo an operation to remove it," Leo said during his weekly Sunday noon blessing in St. Peter's Square.

The surgery is due to occur at Rome's Gemelli Hospital, which is the primary location for popes to receive medical attention.

Leo has had no known previous health problems.

"I thank you for your spiritual closeness and entrust myself to your prayers," Leo said to the crowds on Sunday.

According to the American Cancer Society, a lung nodule is a small abnormal area, less than or equal to 3 cm, found during a CT scan of the chest or abdomen. These tests are often conducted as routine screenings for "trauma, heart disease, non-cancer related lung disease, or lung infection."

Vatican spokesperson Matteo Bruni said in a statement that "the operation is scheduled for the first days of this week and the estimated post-operative recovery time will be about one week."

Leo's next major international trip is scheduled for early November to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. It's unclear if the surgery would affect his travels.

During his papacy, Leo has been outspoken about peace throughout the world. He spent part of his Sunday address renewing calls for peace in Ukraine.

"I make a heartfelt appeal to the parties to the conflict to allow the safe transport of grain across the Black Sea," Leo said. "The daily bread of millions of people cannot be held hostage by war."

On Saturday, the Pope also called for the death penalty to be abolished, saying on X that it is "inadmissible because it is an attack on the inviolability and dignity of the person."

"The common good can be safeguarded and the requirements of justice can be met without recourse to capital punishment: effective systems of detention have been developed that protect citizens while at the same time do not completely deprive those who are guilty of the possibility of redemption," Leo said.

headline: Pakistan imposes emergency rule over Imran Khan's provincial government
summary: By Asif Shahzad and Ariba ShahidISLAMABAD, Oct 11 (Reuters) - Pakistan's president declared a state of emergency and suspended the provincial government of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan on Sunday, following allegations by the federal government that it has failed to tackle Islamist militancy.The constitution allows the federal government to take over some or all provincial government functions during an emergency.
body_text:
By Asif Shahzad and Ariba Shahid

ISLAMABAD, Oct 11 (Reuters) - Pakistan's president declared a state of emergency and suspended the provincial government of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan on Sunday, following allegations by the federal government that it has failed to tackle Islamist militancy.

The constitution allows the federal government to take over some or all provincial government functions during an emergency.

A provincial governor will take charge with an advisory council, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar told a news conference in Islamabad, adding that the arrangement will initially be in place for six months.

The interior ministry said it would be deploying troops in the northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province bordering Afghanistan, which has suffered an increasing number of militant attacks in recent months.

"The situation is so grave that you wouldn't see any residents coming out of their houses after evening in some of the districts," said Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi.

The federal government and the military have accused Khan's party of failing to curb the militants, while Khan's party has rejected the accusation and says the federal government has failed to provide it with the funding and equipment needed.

Islamabad accuses neighbouring Afghanistan of harboring Islamist militants who launch attacks inside Pakistan, and says that Khan's party had been sympathizing with both the Taliban in Kabul and their affiliates at home.

Both the Afghan Taliban and Khan's party have denied the accusation.

President Asif Ali Zardari declared an emergency on the advice of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif following a federal cabinet decision, the president's office said.

The security forces and citizens had been under attack for the last two years, Sharif told the Cabinet. "We can't just act a silent spectator."

`COUP DISGUISED AS EMERGENCY`

The move comes after Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party rallied for several days to pressure the government for his release, threatening to march on the capital Islamabad in coming days amid deepening political instability.

Khan's supporters say the military rigged the 2024 election against the 74-year-old former cricket star, an allegation the military denies.

"This is more of a coup disguised as emergency," said Zulfikar Bukhari, Khan's aide and his party's spokesperson, adding that it risks leading to further bloodshed and instability.

Ahead of the planned march, authorities detained three of Khan's sisters and hundreds of party activists. Restrictions have been placed on the movements of Chief Minister, Sohail Afridi of Khan's party, one of his close aides told Reuters.

The government has cut access to the capital, Islamabad, to bar the protesters from reaching parliament, blocking major highways with shipping containers and deploying tens of thousands of security forces, interior ministry officials said.

The party's last large-scale protest two years ago ended in deadly clashes with security forces.

Khan's 2023 arrest sparked nationwide riots that threatened the standing of the Pakistani military. Cases against Khan have ranged from concerns over state gifts to instigating violence and an accusation of an unlawful marriage.

All convictions but one have since been suspended or overturned, with appeals pending. He ⁠denies wrongdoing.

The latest protest coincides with public discontent over inflation and rising fuel prices that has spread beyond Khan's core supporters.

(Reporting by Asif Shahzad and Ariba Shahid in Islamabad; Additional reporting by Mubasher Bukhari in Lahore; Editing by Jamie Freed and Elaine Hardcastle)

headline: Carrie season 2: Mike Flanagan on Stephen King's ideas for what comes next
summary: When creator Mike Flanagan brought his plans for a new adaptation of Carrie to Stephen King, he had more in mind than another retelling of the author's 1974 horror novel.His eight-part Prime Video series follows Carrie White (Summer H. Howell), a bullied teenager discovering her telekinetic powers, but also expands on something King had only hinted at: the existence of others like her.Flanagan, who previously adapted King's Gerald's Game and Doctor Sleep, was uncertain how the author would receive his proposed changes.“I was very nervous to bring it to him because the pitch was loaded with changes, and my feeling was that if he didn't like them, I wasn't going to do the show,” he tells The National.But Stephen King embraced the approach, even contributing ideas to one of the new characters. His involvement could prove important to the series' future, with Flanagan having previously discussed the possibility of telling the story over three seasons.Prime Video has yet to announce a second, although the first season leaves several storylines unresolved.Warning: spoilers for all eight episodes of Carrie follow.Why Flanagan changed Carrie's endingThe most significant departure from King's novel comes in the finale. The original story ends with Carrie dying after the destruction of her school and much of her hometown. Flanagan instead allows her to survive, escaping Chamberlain alongside Emaline (Thalia Dudek), another young woman with psychic abilities.“We decided very early that we really believed this version of Carrie deserved to survive the story, regardless of whether we were talking about future seasons or anything else,” Flanagan says.Her survival raises a question the novel never had to address: how Carrie might come to terms with the violence she has committed.Flanagan has also changed the circumstances of the prom massacre. The series preserves the humiliation that sets it in motion, when a bucket of blood is dumped on Carrie after she is crowned prom queen, but distributes responsibility for the deaths among several characters.Emaline, who has been secretly observing Carrie, takes control of her body during the disaster, with her permission. Other women with supernatural abilities are involved in the violence that follows.“I think the tragedy hasn't changed whatsoever. The scope of the tragedy is exactly the same,” Flanagan says. “But I do think tragedies have many authors.”There are three deaths, however, that he was determined to leave in Carrie's hands.The first is Tommy Ross (Joel Oulette), her prom date, whom she accidentally kills before Emaline takes control. Later, she confronts Chris Hargensen (Alison Thornton) and Billy Nolan (Arthur Conti), the teenagers responsible for humiliating her. Chris attempts to stop Billy from running Carrie over, causing their car to crash. Both survive, only for Carrie to kill them herself.Flanagan describes Carrie confronting Chris and Billy “eye to eye, and not in a moment of reactivity, but in a moment of clear and conscious sober decision”.“I do think it was important to me if she was going to live that she also be able to live with what happened,” he says.Chris's final attempt to stop Billy adds another complication. Having spent much of the series tormenting Carrie, she ultimately tries to save her life, only to be killed by the girl she has bullied.Flanagan is conscious of how audiences might respond to that moment, describing the satisfaction of “wanting that wish fulfilment of seeing people get their comeuppance”, alongside the discomfort of “realising we're kind of celebrating the death of teenagers and kids”.For Carrie, those conflicting feelings could become a central part of her story. She has escaped Chamberlain and the people who made her life miserable, but must now reckon with having killed two of them deliberately.“There's plenty for her to have to wrestle with what she did and why, and for her to deal with the complex feelings that she'll have,” Flanagan says.How Stephen King's ideas could shape season twoCarrie's escape also leaves her with an uncertain ally in Emaline, whose actions have put them both at odds with Adelaide (Kate Siegel), the powerful woman who sent her to observe Carrie.Throughout the series, Adelaide interviews survivors of the prom disaster, manipulating their memories to conceal her group's involvement. Emaline eventually defies her and helps Carrie leave Chamberlain, although Adelaide's interest in the teenager remains unresolved.Their escape provides another possible direction for a second season, with Carrie now connected to a group of women whose abilities resemble her own. Adelaide's intentions, Emaline's relationship with her former allies and the extent of their powers all remain to be explored.The foundation for this storyline comes from King's novel, which suggests Carrie is not the only person capable of telekinesis. The new characters, however, allowed Flanagan to develop that idea far beyond the original story.King himself played an active role in that process. “Most of his direct ideas and suggestions came to bear with the character of Emaline,” Flanagan says.That involvement is especially significant given Emaline's influence over the finale. Her intervention changes Carrie's responsibility for the massacre, and her decision to help her escape creates the opportunity for their story to continue.Flanagan expects some resistance to the character from readers familiar with King's novel, making the author's contribution all the more interesting.“That's a character I think that people who love the books have an initial resistance to, and that's the character that Stephen King had the most input into,” he says.Emaline also holds knowledge of Adelaide's group that Carrie has only begun to discover. Having turned against the woman who sent her to Chamberlain, she could become Carrie's guide to this unfamiliar world, although the full extent of her loyalties and motivations has yet to be established.Flanagan says King was particularly engaged by the direction these characters could take the story, and their potential influence on Carrie's life beyond the events of the first season.“He had a lot to say about that other world of powerful women and how it could impact Carrie's story and where it could go moving forward,” Flanagan says. “And he was very excited about the possibilities there.”All eight episodes of Carrie are streaming on Prime Video

The government has cut access to the capital, Islamabad, to bar the protesters from reaching parliament, blocking major highways with shipping containers and deploying tens of thousands of security forces, interior ministry officials said.

The party's last large-scale protest two years ago ended in deadly clashes with security forces.

Khan's 2023 arrest sparked nationwide riots that threatened the standing of the Pakistani military. Cases against Khan have ranged from concerns over state gifts to instigating violence and an accusation of an unlawful marriage.

All convictions but one have since been suspended or overturned, with appeals pending. He ⁠denies wrongdoing.

The latest protest coincides with public discontent over inflation and rising fuel prices that has spread beyond Khan's core supporters.

(Reporting by Asif Shahzad and Ariba Shahid in Islamabad; Additional reporting by Mubasher Bukhari in Lahore; Editing by Jamie Freed and Elaine Hardcastle)

headline: Carrie season 2: Mike Flanagan on Stephen King's ideas for what comes next
summary: When creator Mike Flanagan brought his plans for a new adaptation of Carrie to Stephen King, he had more in mind than another retelling of the author's 1974 horror novel.His eight-part Prime Video series follows Carrie White (Summer H. Howell), a bullied teenager discovering her telekinetic powers, but also expands on something King had only hinted at: the existence of others like her.Flanagan, who previously adapted King's Gerald's Game and Doctor Sleep, was uncertain how the author would receive his proposed changes.“I was very nervous to bring it to him because the pitch was loaded with changes, and my feeling was that if he didn't like them, I wasn't going to do the show,” he tells The National.But Stephen King embraced the approach, even contributing ideas to one of the new characters. His involvement could prove important to the series' future, with Flanagan having previously discussed the possibility of telling the story over three seasons.Prime Video has yet to announce a second, although the first season leaves several storylines unresolved.Warning: spoilers for all eight episodes of Carrie follow.Why Flanagan changed Carrie's endingThe most significant departure from King's novel comes in the finale. The original story ends with Carrie dying after the destruction of her school and much of her hometown. Flanagan instead allows her to survive, escaping Chamberlain alongside Emaline (Thalia Dudek), another young woman with psychic abilities.“We decided very early that we really believed this version of Carrie deserved to survive the story, regardless of whether we were talking about future seasons or anything else,” Flanagan says.Her survival raises a question the novel never had to address: how Carrie might come to terms with the violence she has committed.Flanagan has also changed the circumstances of the prom massacre. The series preserves the humiliation that sets it in motion, when a bucket of blood is dumped on Carrie after she is crowned prom queen, but distributes responsibility for the deaths among several characters.Emaline, who has been secretly observing Carrie, takes control of her body during the disaster, with her permission. Other women with supernatural abilities are involved in the violence that follows.“I think the tragedy hasn't changed whatsoever. The scope of the tragedy is exactly the same,” Flanagan says. “But I do think tragedies have many authors.”There are three deaths, however, that he was determined to leave in Carrie's hands.The first is Tommy Ross (Joel Oulette), her prom date, whom she accidentally kills before Emaline takes control. Later, she confronts Chris Hargensen (Alison Thornton) and Billy Nolan (Arthur Conti), the teenagers responsible for humiliating her. Chris attempts to stop Billy from running Carrie over, causing their car to crash. Both survive, only for Carrie to kill them herself.Flanagan describes Carrie confronting Chris and Billy “eye to eye, and not in a moment of reactivity, but in a moment of clear and conscious sober decision”.“I do think it was important to me if she was going to live that she also be able to live with what happened,” he says.Chris's final attempt to stop Billy adds another complication. Having spent much of the series tormenting Carrie, she ultimately tries to save her life, only to be killed by the girl she has bullied.Flanagan is conscious of how audiences might respond to that moment, describing the satisfaction of “wanting that wish fulfilment of seeing people get their comeuppance”, alongside the discomfort of “realising we're kind of celebrating the death of teenagers and kids”.For Carrie, those conflicting feelings could become a central part of her story. She has escaped Chamberlain and the people who made her life miserable, but must now reckon with having killed two of them deliberately.“There's plenty for her to have to wrestle with what she did and why, and for her to deal with the complex feelings that she'll have,” Flanagan says.How Stephen King's ideas could shape season twoCarrie's escape also leaves her with an uncertain ally in Emaline, whose actions have put them both at odds with Adelaide (Kate Siegel), the powerful woman who sent her to observe Carrie.Throughout the series, Adelaide interviews survivors of the prom disaster, manipulating their memories to conceal her group's involvement. Emaline eventually defies her and helps Carrie leave Chamberlain, although Adelaide's interest in the teenager remains unresolved.Their escape provides another possible direction for a second season, with Carrie now connected to a group of women whose abilities resemble her own. Adelaide's intentions, Emaline's relationship with her former allies and the extent of their powers all remain to be explored.The foundation for this storyline comes from King's novel, which suggests Carrie is not the only person capable of telekinesis. The new characters, however, allowed Flanagan to develop that idea far beyond the original story.King himself played an active role in that process. “Most of his direct ideas and suggestions came to bear with the character of Emaline,” Flanagan says.That involvement is especially significant given Emaline's influence over the finale. Her intervention changes Carrie's responsibility for the massacre, and her decision to help her escape creates the opportunity for their story to continue.Flanagan expects some resistance to the character from readers familiar with King's novel, making the author's contribution all the more interesting.“That's a character I think that people who love the books have an initial resistance to, and that's the character that Stephen King had the most input into,” he says.Emaline also holds knowledge of Adelaide's group that Carrie has only begun to discover. Having turned against the woman who sent her to Chamberlain, she could become Carrie's guide to this unfamiliar world, although the full extent of her loyalties and motivations has yet to be established.Flanagan says King was particularly engaged by the direction these characters could take the story, and their potential influence on Carrie's life beyond the events of the first season.“He had a lot to say about that other world of powerful women and how it could impact Carrie's story and where it could go moving forward,” Flanagan says. “And he was very excited about the possibilities there.”All eight episodes of Carrie are streaming on Prime Video

headline: Boat capsizes off Djibouti leaving 139 dead and scores missing
summary: At least 139 migrants, including ​15 children, ​have died ​and more than 80 are ⁠missing after a boat carrying about 305 people ⁠capsized while sailing from Djibouti to Yemen, ​the UN's migration agency said on Sunday.The boat overturned ⁠near Guhere, north of Djibouti's port town of Obock, during the night of October 8 into October 9, the International Organisation for Migration said, citing survivor accounts.More than 80 people survived ⁠the shipwreck, all Ethiopian citizens, the agency said. The ⁠Ethiopian government did not immediately ‌respond to requests for comment from Reuters.The IOM raised its initial death toll of 109 released earlier on Sunday after 30 more bodies were recovered. Out of the 109 bodies recovered earlier, 52 were men, 42 women and 15 children, the agency said."Our teams are on the ground alongside local authorities to provide emergency assistance," said IOM chief of mission in Djibouti, Alexandre Coissac."This tragedy is a stark reminder of the dangers faced by migrants along this migration corridor as they seek economic opportunities," he added.Djiboutian authorities are continuing search and rescue operations, the IOM said, also providing medical care to survivors and arranging burials.The tragedy follows renewed fighting in Ethiopia's Tigray region, nearly four years after a peace agreement ended a devastating two-year civil war there. The IOM's Displacement Tracking Matrix shows more than 20,000 incoming movements to Djibouti from Ethiopia since September 10.Each year, tens of thousands of migrants from the Horn of Africa travel through Djibouti and cross the Bab Al Mandeb strait to Yemen, from where they hope to reach Gulf countries. The crossings continue despite fighting on Yemen's Red Sea coast between government forces and Iran-backed Houthi rebels since early September. At the same time, more than 3,700 people fled the fighting and made the crossing from Yemen to Djibouti, according to ​the IOM.With reporting from agencies

headline: Major road upgrades planned in Abu Dhabi's Mussaffah
summary: Abu Dhabi is set to overhaul key roads in Mussaffah, with upgrades spanning 13 kilometres designed to cut congestion and improve safety.The Department of Municipalities and Transport has announced plans to upgrade roads along the E30 and 8th Street corridors in Mussaffah, improving connections between the industrial area, Mohamed Bin Zayed City and Zayed City. The project aims to ease congestion, reduce travel time and improve road safety across the district.Central to the scheme is a new free-flowing motorway at 8th Street, featuring three lanes in each direction and three additional service lanes on each side to maintain access to shops and businesses. The upgraded street is expected to accommodate up to 4,000 vehicles per hour.The wider project includes upgrades to four interchanges along E30, improved connections with 8th Street and E20, and modifications to nine key junctions. The project also plans two new bridges linking Musaffah with Mohamed Bin Zayed City, along with a dedicated pedestrian bridge. Separate enhancement works will cover about 8km along 8th Street. Eisa Mubarak Al Mazrouei, Director General of Infrastructure Development at DMT, said the upgrades were designed to serve the varied demands placed on Mussaffah's road network. “By separating traffic passing through the area from local access and improving connections with surrounding communities, we can support economic activity while making everyday journeys easier and safer,” Mr Al Mazrouei said.The Mussaffah project forms part of broader efforts to strengthen connectivity across Abu Dhabi emirate. Among the wider initiatives is a planned two-tunnel undersea link running from the eastern tip of Abu Dhabi Island to Mussaffah, passing beneath Khor Al Maqta and the Al Hudayriyat Island channel. Officials said the decisions being made now are intended to support the emirate's long-term development needs.

US President Donald Trump said in a brief statement Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to halt strikes on each other's energy infrastructure.

Read moreUkraine says ready to halt refinery strikes if Moscow stops energy attacks

"Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!" he wrote on his Truth Social network, without adding further details.

Zelensky quickly responded to Trump's announcement, stating during an interview with news outlet Axios that the ceasefire was "news for me".

"The ceasefire ‌announcement was news for ​me. But if Russians agree to an energy ceasefire Ukraine ​will agree. If ​president Trump negotiated it ​with Putin – please tell us ​when the ceasefire begins – we are ready and we will accept ⁠it," Zelensky was quoted as saying ⁠by ​Axios.

As yet, no comments have been made by Russia.

Earlier Sunday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky reiterated that his country would be ready to stop targeting Russian oil refineries if Russia curbed its attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure.

Zelensky's comment came amid a spat between Trump and the Ukrainian leader, who had denounced a US move to temporarily ease sanctions on Russian diesel.

headline: Iran to pursue national interests through diplomacy, battle
summary: TEHRAN, Oct. 11 (MNA) – Spokesperson for the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran (AEOI) Behrouz Kamalvandi has said that Iran will pursue its national interests through diplomacy if possible, but will use force if necessary.
body_text:
TEHRAN, Oct. 11 (MNA) – Spokesperson for the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran (AEOI) Behrouz Kamalvandi has said that Iran will pursue its national interests through diplomacy if possible, but will use force if necessary.

Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the international conference “Ecocide: The Silent War Crime” in Tehran on Sunday, Kamalvandi said Iranian authorities had stressed that the country was pursuing negotiations and resistance simultaneously.

Iran would pursue its national interests with determination, he said, adding that securing them through diplomacy would be preferable. Otherwise, the country would seek to achieve them on the battlefield.

The conference was held at the Department of Environment’s conference hall to examine the legal, humanitarian and environmental dimensions of war crimes and environmental devastation committed by the United States and the Israeli regime in Iran and the Gaza Strip.

Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and AEOI chief Mohammad Eslami also addressed the gathering, which focused on the consequences of environmental destruction during the recent conflicts.

headline: Max Verstappen wins Singapore GP as Kimi Antonelli moves closer to title
summary: ​Red ⁠Bull's Max ⁠Verstappen dominated the Singapore ⁠Grand Prix as he won from pole at the ⁠Marina Bay Street ​Circuit ⁠on ‌Sunday for ​his second straight victory of the season.⁠Verstappen had a few complaints about the circuit, lamenting the lack of overtaking opportunities, but enjoyed a near perfect weekend as he also won the Sprint race. It was a memorable way for the four-time world champion to celebrate his 250th grand prix weekend.Ferrari's Charles Leclerc finished ​second ‌while ⁠Mercedes driver ​Kimi Antonelli ​was ‌third to ⁠extend his championship ⁠lead over teammate George Russell.Verstappen was in control of the race from the start, overcoming an early challenge from ⁠Leclerc.The Dutchman, who won ‌the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia last weekend, had never ​won in Singapore before and he had come into the race weekend stating he had “unfinished business”.“It's taken a while but I think this race was very good. We had pace when we needed to have it on the soft tyre, even though I think the medium tyre for everyone was more of a struggle,” Verstappen said.Closing in on history Kimi has a mathematical chance of winning the world title at the next race in Austin 🇺🇸#F1 #SingaporeGP pic.twitter.com/VZLZ13BtQV— Formula 1 (@F1) October 11, 2026“But it worked out, so of course very happy to win here … The last two races have been really positive for us and it's just great to ​see.“We have a lot of motivation in the team to try and deliver even more results. It is a really good group of people, I really enjoy working with them and hopefully we can have a bit more fun until the end of the year.”Antonelli extended his championship lead over teammate ‌Russell to 102 ⁠points. The young Italian can ​win the title in the next round in ​Austin.“Can ‌I? Really?” Antonelli said when he was told after ⁠his 14th podium of the season.“Well, let's not worry about ⁠that. Let's try to do the best weekend as possible and finish the job.“It was a very tough race [in Singapore] but really happy with a podium at the end. I managed to take advantage of the fight of Lando and Lewis and to make a move on both and to bring home P3 is a great result for the team.”Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton had qualified third on the grid but endured a forgettable evening. The Briton slipped to ​sixth behind Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri after the two McLaren drivers overtook him in the dying stages as he struggled with his tyres.Hamilton spoke to his team over the radio and said the result was due to his call.“Sorry, boys. headline: At least 139 migrants dead, including some children, after boat from Djibouti to Yemen capsizes, UN agency says
summary: NAIROBI, Oct 11 (Reuters) - At least 139 migrants, including at least 15 children, have died and around 84 are missing after a boat carrying more than 300 people capsized while sailing from Djibouti to Yemen, the United Nations' International Organization for Migration said on Sunday.The boat, carrying 305 people, capsized near Guhere, north of Obock — a port town in Djibouti — during the night of October 8-9, the IOM said, citing survivor accounts.
body_text:
NAIROBI, Oct 11 (Reuters) - At least 139 migrants, including at least 15 children, have died and around 84 are missing after a boat carrying more than 300 people capsized while sailing from Djibouti to Yemen, the United Nations' International Organization for Migration said on Sunday.

The boat, carrying 305 people, capsized near Guhere, north of Obock — a port town in Djibouti — during the night of October 8-9, the IOM said, citing survivor accounts.

Around 82 people survived the shipwreck, the statement said. A spokesperson for the Ethiopian government did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Photographs shared by the UN agency showed worn-out sandals and sneakers washed up on the shore.

"Our teams are on the ground alongside local authorities to provide emergency assistance," saidIOM Chief of Mission in Djibouti Alexandre Coissac.

"This tragedy is a stark reminder of the dangers faced by migrants along this migration corridor as they seek economic opportunities," Coissac said.

Djiboutian authorities are continuing search and rescue operations, the IOM statement said, adding that local authorities are also providing medical care to survivors and arranging burials for the deceased.

The Djibouti government could not be immediately reached for comment.

The migrants were heading toYemen, with the hope of eventually making it to wealthier Gulf nations, even as Yemeni nationals themselves flee their country, which is experiencing the most serious escalation in fighting between Saudi Arabia-backed government forces and theIran-backed Houthis since a UN-brokered truce in 2022. ​

"Despite the violence in Yemen, migrants are still making the perilous journeys hoping to make it to the Gulf countries," the IOM statement said.

Fighting has also broken out in Ethiopia since last month in the biggest escalation of violence since ​the 2020-2022Tigray war.

An IOM official told Reuters that the UN agency had documented heavy migrant traffic along the so-called Eastern Route through Djibouti for several years.

"People continue to use the route amid changing conditions in Ethiopia and Yemen, although the volume and direction of movement can shift over time," the official said.

Ethiopian migrants interviewed as part of the agency's most recent situation report on Djibouti from September 20 to September 30 said they had left their countrydue to difficult living conditions, including the impact of drought.

"Some migrants also reported that they were fleeing conflict and forced recruitment by armed forces," the report said.

Multiple residents ofTigray, where fighting erupted on September 23, have told Reuters that they had seen Tigrayan rebels forcibly recruit young men into the defence forces. The rebels havedenied conducting forced recruitment.

The conflict has sparked fears of a return to all-out war with Ethiopia and Eritrea severing relations over allegedEritrean support for the rebel alliance seeking to overthrow Ethiopia's government. Eritrea has denied backing the alliance.

The so-called Eastern Route presents many dangers, including accidents at sea, trafficking and arbitrary arrests once on land.In 2025, more than 900 migrants died or went missing along the route, according to IOM’s Missing Migrants Project, as the number of people undertaking the journey increased by 18%.

IOM has described the crisis sparked by the fighting in Yemen as alarming, with displacement figures surging to 200,000 from 76,000 in mid-September, according to data released by the agency last week.

More than 3,700 people have fled Yemen by sea to Djibouti as of last week, it said.

(Reporting by Nethra Sailesh and Anusha Shah in Bengaluru and Ammu Kannampillyin Nairobi; Editing by Tomasz Janowski, Alexandra Hudson and Susan Fenton)

headline: Saudi-led coalition says new attack at Riyadh airport causes fire, day after strike kills 12
summary: By Jana Choukeir, Maha El Dahan and Timour AzhariDUBAI/RIYADH, Oct 11 (Reuters) - The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said an "unidentified projectile" had targeted Riyadh's international airport on Sunday, causing a fire, hours after the Iran-backed Houthis warned airlines and travellers to stay away from Saudi airports.The coalition also said Saudi air defences had intercepted a cruise missile in the vicinity of King Khalid International Airport. No further details were immediately available.
body_text:
By Jana Choukeir, Maha El Dahan and Timour Azhari

DUBAI/RIYADH, Oct 11 (Reuters) - The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said an "unidentified projectile" had targeted Riyadh's international airport on Sunday, causing a fire, hours after the Iran-backed Houthis warned airlines and travellers to stay away from Saudi airports.

The coalition also said Saudi air defences had intercepted a cruise missile in the vicinity of King Khalid International Airport. No further details were immediately available.

The airport remains closed after an attack there on Saturday killed 12 people and wounded more than 300 others, the deadliest such strike on the kingdom in over a decade, amid an escalation of fighting between the Houthis and Yemeni government forces.

Despite the airport's temporary closure, the Saudi Energy Ministry said a long-planned international energy conference was still going ahead in Riyadh on Sunday.

The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said Sunday's projectile had targeted Terminal 4 of the airport, without elaborating.

Earlier, the Houthis had said in a statement on X:

"We renew our warning to all airlines, experts, employees, workers and travellers against using Saudi airports and airspace, as they are vulnerable to attack and have become a theatre of operations for our forces, with the exception of the airports in (the holy cities of) Mecca and Medina."

"We urge everyone to take our warnings seriously, and Saudi Arabia bears responsibility for any failed interceptions."

'WORSE IS YET TO COME,' HOUTHIS WARN

Saudi Arabia has stepped up its military involvement in Yemen in recent weeks, launching strikes against theHouthis and backing a Yemeni government counteroffensive after the group seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month.

Yemen's Houthi-run foreign ministry said later on Sunday that further Saudi military action in Yemen would trigger a stronger response, adding that its actions would be guided by the principle of reciprocity.

"Unless the Saudi enemy stops its aggression and interference in Yemen, worse is yet to come, God willing," the ministry said in statements carried by Houthi-run Al Masirah television.

President Donald Trump said on Saturday the United States was considering joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis in the conflict, a spillover from the wider war on Iran that the US and Israel launched in February.

INTERNATIONAL ENERGY CONFERENCE STILL GOING AHEAD

A five-day WPC Energy Congress is taking place this week at a conventioncentre some 10 km (6 miles) from the airport. State TV said more than 70 ministers, 300 company executives and representatives of over 25 international energy organisations had confirmed their attendance.

It was not immediately clear whether the participants would attend in person or virtually.

A ministerial meeting of the International Energy Forum is also set to go ahead on Sunday, with its plenary session to be held behind closed doors, according to a media advisory. No further details were immediately available.

Separately, Saudi authorities notified parents that in-person classes would be suspended and shifted to remote learning from Sunday until Thursday for all students, teachers and administrative staff.

In Saturday's attack, the third on Riyadh's airport in a week, the 12 dead included 4 Saudis, 2 Bangladeshis and nationals of the United States, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt, Saudi authorities said.

Four people were killed in the two previous attacks on the airport earlier in the week. One of the attacks also caused heavy damage to a Saudi commercial plane parked on the tarmac.

(Reporting by Jana Choukeir and Maha El Dahan in Dubai, Timour Azhari Riyadh, Menna Alaa El-Din and Yasmine Ghania in Cairo; Editing by Andrew Mills and Gareth Jones)

body_text:
Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari suspended the government of northwest Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Sunday, the last province ruled by jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party, and declared a state of emergency over the deteriorating law-and-order situation.

During an emergency, Pakistan’s constitution allows the federal government to take over some or all of the provincial government functions, including executive and legislative powers. President Zardari proclaimed Articles 232(1) and 234(1) of the Constitution, citing rising terrorist attacks and a breakdown of constitutional machinery in the northwestern province.

During a press briefing in Islamabad on Sunday, Pakistan’s Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said the provincial governor will take charge of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province with an advisory council, adding that the arrangement is poised to be in place for the next six months.

Pakistan’s Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said, “The situation is so grave that you wouldn’t see any residents coming out of their houses after evening in some of the districts.”

The development comes as Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, who has long been demanding the release of PTI chief Imran Khan and access to medical assistance, led a protest march in Lakki Marwat last week and passed through several districts of the province.

Afridi, along with PTI supporters, has been pressuring Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s government to release Khan, threatening to lead the march to Islamabad in the coming days, Reuters reported.

However, the Pakistan government and military have accused the Afridi-led government in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa of failing to restrict Islamist militants in the province that borders Afghanistan, which has seen several militant attacks in the recent past. But PTI has rejected the allegations, saying the government has failed to provide the province with funding and equipment to combat the ​militancy.

According to the presidential declaration issued on Sunday, the emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa was imposed in view of rising terrorist incidents and the grave law and order situation in the province. “The extraordinary intensity of terrorist incidents poses serious threats to the lives and property of the public.”

US President Donald Trump said on Sunday Russia and Ukraine agreed to stop attacks on each other’s energy infrastructure, and announced an immediate halt after an escalation in deadly strikes.

“Effective immediately, there is an energy ceasefire in the war between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it,” Mr Trump wrote on social media.

He provided no details on its duration, how it would be enforced or which sites would be covered.

Ukrainian ⁠President Volodymyr Zelenskyy ​said in an ​interview with the news outlet Axios that he was ​not ‌aware of ⁠any ceasefire but added that if ​Moscow agreed to ‌it, Kyiv would accept it.

“The ceasefire ‌announcement was news for ​me. But if Russians agree to an energy ceasefire Ukraine ​will agree. If ​President Trump negotiated it ​with [Russian President Vladimir] Putin – please tell us ​when the ceasefire begins – we are ready and we will accept ⁠it,” Mr Zelenskyy said.

The announcement followed a dispute between Mr Trump and Mr Zelenskyy over attacks on Russian oil refineries.

Mr Trump criticised the strikes on Saturday, a day after Washington temporarily lifted sanctions on Russian fuel that were intended to limit Moscow’s revenue for its war.

“I think it’s time for Ukraine to get a new president,” Donald Trump told reporters at the White House.

Mr Zelenskyy responded on Sunday by offering to organise elections if Mr Putin agreed to a 60-day halt in fighting.

“Please tell Putin, give us two months, 60 days of total ceasefire, 60 days, and we will organise elections,” Mr Zelenskyy told ABC News.

He also challenged suggestions that Ukraine’s attacks were responsible for rising fuel costs, saying it was easy to blame Kyiv “when everybody in the world understands (that) because of the war in (the) Middle East, the prices are rising”.

EU chief Ursula von der Leyen voiced backing for Mr Zelenskyy amid his row with Mr Trump, and backed Kyiv's calls for an energy ceasefire with Russia.

"Fully supported the call of President Zelenskyy for a ceasefire that would protect global food supplies and energy infrastructure in Ukraine and Russia," Ms von der Leyen wrote online after talking to Mr Zelenskyy.

"And my full support for President Zelenskyy as he leads the fight for his people's freedom," she added.

headline: Prominent Republican senator says Trump's Russian diesel deal may be illegal
summary: By Jan WolfeOct 11 (Reuters) - Republican US Senator Thom Tillis on Sunday said President Donald Trump's diesel supply ​deal with Russia may be illegal and will put American lives at risk, adding to bipartisan criticism of the arrangement announced by the president on Friday.Trump saidthat Russia had agreed to supply ​diesel to global markets, and his administration temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel that were designed to deprive Moscow of revenue for its ‌war on Ukraine.
body_text:
Oct 11 (Reuters) - Republican US Senator Thom Tillis on Sunday said President Donald Trump's diesel supply ​deal with Russia may be illegal and will put American lives at risk, adding to bipartisan criticism of the arrangement announced by the president on Friday.

Trump saidthat Russia had agreed to supply ​diesel to global markets, and his administration temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel that were designed to deprive Moscow of revenue for its ‌war on Ukraine.

“I do believe there’s a legitimate case for saying the president’s not following the law,” said Tillis, an influential Republican from North Carolina who is retiring from the Senate at the end of his term in January.

Prices for diesel — used for agriculture, heating homes and trucking — are near record highs and could hurt Trump's fellow Republicans in next month's congressional elections that will determine whether they maintain their thin majorities in Congress.

Analysts have said Trump's agreement with Moscow was unlikely to lead to sustained lower fuel prices.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News on Sunday that the Trump administration will follow through with the deal using existing legal authority, adding that the agreement was good for the American people and would bring prices down.

"We're going to do it with all the legal authorities we have. So, you know, anyone in Congress who says whether it's an old bill or the current Lindsey Graham bill (that) prohibits us from doing it is wrong," Bessent told the "Fox & Friends" program.

Trump last month signed a sweeping Russia ​sanctions bill into law, ​called the "Lindsey ⁠O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026," to honor ​the South Carolina Republican who died in ​July. Graham, a ⁠longtime ​Russia hawk, was a staunch ​backer of the legislation.

Tillis is not the first Republican to criticize the deal. Retiring Representative Don Bacon of Nebraska said on X on Friday that "propping up Putin’s war economy is morally wrong as he uses that money to bomb cities."

Mike Pence, Trump's former vicepresident,called his decision to lift sanctions on Russian oil a "betrayal" of Graham’s legacy and urged the president to "rescind" it.

"The president's actions and his comments over the last 24 hours are the exact opposite of the intent of that bill," Tillis said, adding, "I will guarantee you at the first opportunity (Russian President Vladimir) Putin has to embarrass or undermine President Trump, he will."

As Trump's poll numbers have cratered, congressional Republicans have increasingly distanced themselves from the president, on matters ranging from the conflict in Iran to the trade war with Canada.

The Senate's No. 2 Republican, John Barrasso of Wyoming, defended the diesel deal on Sunday, telling CBS' "Face the Nation" that Trump is focused on bringing costs down for consumers, ranchers, farmers and truckers.

"The president is balancing and has to make tough decisions," Barrasso said.

(Reporting by Jan Wolfe and Ismail Shakil; Editing by Jesse Mesner-Hage, Susan Fenton and Bill Berkrot)

headline: Greater power than US previously failed in battle with Iran
summary: TEHRAN, Oct. 11 (MNA) – Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, Major General Mohsen Rezaei, says powers greater than the US have tried to conquer Iran but ultimately ended up in the “dustbin of history.”
body_text:
TEHRAN, Oct. 11 (MNA) – Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, Major General Mohsen Rezaei, says powers greater than the US have tried to conquer Iran but ultimately ended up in the “dustbin of history.”

During an interview with Press TV on Saturday, Rezaei said the “US suffered repeated defeats in its confrontation with Iran and has consequently turned to economic warfare out of desperation.”

Iran, rather than the US, would determine when the confrontation ends, he said, stressing that Tehran would continue its resistance until its rightful demands are met.

Addressing the presence of US forces in the region, Rezaei told Press TV that the withdrawal of US forces from Iraq reflected Washington’s failure to impose its military agenda on the region, describing it as a vindication of Iran’s resistance to American military presence in West Asia.

Rezaei further said that more than “30 million Iranians have registered in ‘Janfada’ (Sacrifice for Iran) Campaign to take up arms in the event of US aggression.”

On diplomacy, the official said “Tehran would not return to its previous diplomatic norms,” while stressing that “Iran would never abandon diplomacy altogether.”

The senior official warned that, if Washington launched another act of aggression against Iran, American assets could be targeted, including key data systems and artificial intelligence sensors.

Rezaei also identified Washington and its regional allies as the root of the problem surrounding the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz in response to the latest round of US-Israeli aggression, preventing US and allied ships from navigating the strategic waterway.

The move resulted in a significant increase in oil and energy prices across the globe, especially in the US, forcing Washington and the International Energy Agency (IEA) to release their strategic resources several times.

Following the signing of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between Iran and the US in June, Tehran opened the Strait of Hormuz, but after the US violated the MoU by blockading Iranian ports, Iran’s Armed Forces closed the maritime corridor once again.

loaded_language.neutral_alternative: have ultimately failed or been defeated
