headline: UK PM Burnham warns French voters of Russian political influence on back of Brexit vote
summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Sunday warned French and German voters of potential for Russian influence in upcoming elections, on the back of "clear" interference in Britain's referendum on European Union membership in 2016. Russia has previously denied meddling in the Brexit vote, while former British leader Boris Johnson 2020 also said there was no evidence of interference. Burnham made the comments in an interview with The Rest is Politics podcast, released on Sunday.

headline: Egypt, Indonesia target $5bn in bilateral trade by 2030
summary: President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi said Egypt and Indonesia aim to increase bilateral trade to $5bn by 2030, while expanding joint manufacturing projects and attracting more Indonesian investment to the Egyptian market. Al-Sisi made the remarks following talks with Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto at the Merdeka Presidential Palace in Jakarta during an official visit on October 10-11, focused on advancing the two countries’ strategic partnership and coordinating positions on regional and international issues. The two presidents witnessed the signing of four memorandums of understanding covering maritime affairs and fisheries, statistical cooperation, an action plan for the strategic partnership, and visa exemptions for holders of diplomatic, service and special passports. Al-Sisi said the two countries had agreed to prioritise trade growth and work to remove obstacles to achieving the $5bn target. They also agreed to expand joint manufacturing in priority sectors and strengthen Egypt’s role as a production and export hub serving Arab, African and international markets. A joint statement issued during the visit welcomed progress in cooperation between Indonesia’s Danantara and Egypt’s Future of Egypt for Sustainable Development Authority, particularly in the production and distribution of crude palm oil and its derivatives, as well as phosphate fertilisers and related raw materials. The two leaders encouraged the institutions to broaden cooperation into infrastructure, energy, logistics and agribusiness, while promoting market access, investment and joint manufacturing. Egypt and Indonesia also agreed to deepen defence and security cooperation and strengthen political coordination through regular high-level visits and existing bilateral mechanisms, including the joint committee. On Nile water, Al-Sisi described the river as an existential issue for Egypt, reiterating Cairo’s commitment to safeguarding its water rights and rejecting unilateral measures that could undermine its water security. Prabowo expressed regret over any violations of international law or attempts to diminish states’ water rights, and voiced support for Egypt’s efforts to protect its interests. The joint statement also emphasised adherence to international law governing transboundary waterways, including the principle of avoiding significant harm. The presidents also discussed the Palestinian Cause, reaffirming their support for an independent, sovereign and viable Palestinian state along the June 4, 1967 lines, with East Jerusalem as its capital. They rejected any attempts to forcibly displace Palestinians and condemned continued Israeli military operations in Gaza and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, as well as settlement policies and activities. Both sides called for full, safe and sustained humanitarian access to Gaza. The talks also addressed escalating tensions in the Gulf. Both leaders called for immediate de-escalation and restraint, stressing the importance of respecting state sovereignty and territorial integrity, safeguarding freedom of navigation and maintaining energy security. In education, culture and youth, the two presidents agreed to expand cooperation. Prabowo welcomed Al-Azhar University’s November 2025 decision to introduce Indonesian language studies at its Faculty of Languages and Translation. Al-Sisi said Egypt continued to receive thousands of Indonesian students each year at Al-Azhar and other Egyptian universities, describing educational and cultural ties as a central pillar of relations between the two countries.

headline: World Bank Group mobilises $6.7bn in private capital for Egypt since FY2022
summary: The World Bank Group has mobilised nearly $6.7bn in private capital for Egypt since fiscal year (FY) 2022, supporting investments in renewable energy, port infrastructure, affordable housing and entrepreneurship, according to the group. Private capital mobilisation involves attracting funding from private-sector investors to finance development projects, helping bridge the gap between governments’ development priorities and the limitations of public financing. The World Bank Group uses financing, guarantees, partnerships and risk-mitigation mechanisms to attract additional investment alongside its own resources. One of the key examples is the group’s partnership with AMEA Power, which supports several renewable energy and battery storage projects in Egypt. The International Finance Corporation (IFC) provided approximately $289.9m in financing and blended finance resources, mobilising more than $1bn from private-sector investors and partners for four projects: the Abydos 1 and Abydos 2 solar power plants, the Amunet wind power project, and Egypt’s first utility-scale battery energy storage system. The projects are expected to expand Egypt’s supply of clean and reliable electricity. headline: Semak Pharma to double investments in 2027, expand Fayoum production
summary: Semak Pharmaceutical Group plans to double its current investment volume in 2027, with an expansion strategy focused on increasing production capacity, broadening its personal care portfolio and expanding distribution across Egyptian pharmacies. headline: Egypt explores expanding health economics research with WifOR, Roche
summary: Health and Population Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar discussed expanding the use of economic and social research in health policymaking with Germany’s WifOR Institute, focusing on how improved health outcomes affect productivity, labour-force participation and human-capital development. Both sides discussed research methodologies, data requirements and ways to strengthen co-ordination among relevant institutions to increase the use of scientific evidence in health policymaking and decision-making. headline: Egypt’s chemical exports to Saudi Arabia surge 98% to $356m in 8M 2026
summary: Egypt’s exports of chemicals and fertilisers to Saudi Arabia surged 98% year on year to approximately $356m in the first eight months of 2026, up from $180m in the same period last year, making the Kingdom the sector’s sixth-largest export market, according to the Export Council for Chemical Industries and Fertilisers. The strong growth underscores Saudi Arabia’s importance as a key destination for Egyptian chemical products and fertilisers, supported by a diverse export base serving a range of industries. Petrochemicals led exports to Saudi Arabia, reaching approximately $102m between January and August 2026. Fertilisers and pesticides ranked second at $51m, followed by plastics at $44m. Exports of detergents totalled around $41m, while inks and paints reached $31m. Dry cells and batteries, as well as oils and extracts, each generated approximately $22m in exports. Other exported products included miscellaneous chemicals valued at $16m and inorganic chemicals at $14m, alongside rubber products, organic chemicals, glass products and adhesives. The council is seeking to build on this growth by intensifying promotional activities in Saudi Arabia and aligning its participation in international trade fairs with market performance and demand indicators. As part of these efforts, the council is preparing to participate in Saudi Agriculture, scheduled for October 19-22, 2026, with a joint Egyptian pavilion showcasing products from participating companies and specialised sectors. The participation aims to connect Egyptian exporters with Saudi buyers and importers, identify market requirements and explore commercial partnerships, particularly in fertilisers, pesticides and agricultural-related products. The council plans to participate in four international exhibitions in Saudi Arabia in 2026, increasing its target to five exhibitions in 2027. The planned events will cover fertilisers and agricultural supplies, chemicals, plastics, tableware, glass products and the hospitality sector. Khaled Abou El Makarem, Chairperson of the Export Council for Chemical Industries and Fertilisers, said the 98% increase in exports during the first eight months of 2026 highlighted the opportunities available for Egyptian companies to expand their presence and increase their market share in Saudi Arabia. He added that the diversity of Egyptian exports, particularly petrochemicals, fertilisers, plastics, detergents, inks and paints, offered scope for further growth and expansion into additional product categories. Abou El Makarem said the council would continue participating in international exhibitions and specialised events to strengthen direct engagement with importers, understand market needs and establish sustainable commercial relationships. Mohamed Mageed, the council’s Executive Director, said the strategy extended beyond increasing participation in exhibitions to maximising their commercial returns through direct engagement with importers, bilateral meetings and follow-up on business opportunities after each event. The council also supports member companies in addressing barriers to entering the Saudi market and provides market research and product-related information to help exporters identify opportunities and develop expansion plans. Mageed added that the five exhibitions planned for 2027 would help broaden the range of Egyptian products available in Saudi Arabia and strengthen the sector’s presence across additional industries. He concluded that the increase in exports should serve as a starting point for further expansion, with the council using trade data to guide promotional activities and translate market opportunities into actual exports and sustained growth.

headline: Youth Ministry, FRA sign MoU to promote entrepreneurship, fintech innovation
summary: Minister of Youth and Sports Gohar Nabil and Islam Azzam, Chairperson of the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA), witnessed the signing of a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to empower young Egyptians and develop their capabilities in entrepreneurship, innovation, financial technology (fintech) and non-banking financial services. The agreement aims to help transform promising ideas into viable, scalable businesses through the FRA’s FinTech Regulatory Sandbox. The MoU was signed by Mohamed Saeed Mazen, Permanent Undersecretary of the Ministry of Youth and Sports, and Ahmed Khalifa, Executive Director of the FRA’s Regulatory Sandbox. The agreement seeks to strengthen co-operation between the two parties to promote entrepreneurship and innovation among young people. It also provides for training and awareness programmes, workshops and introductory sessions across Egypt’s governorates, focusing on fintech, non-banking financial services, financial literacy and awareness, and business model development. These initiatives aim to equip young people with the skills needed to establish and expand their projects in line with market requirements. Co-operation will also support the implementation and development of innovative youth-led ideas and projects through the FRA’s regulatory sandbox. Planned activities include events, competitions and innovation challenges, as well as guidance and mentorship for entrepreneurs with promising ideas. The agreement also provides for connecting entrepreneurs with business incubators, accelerators and capacity-building programmes, while facilitating access for eligible projects to investors, venture capital funds and relevant funding networks in accordance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements. The agreed areas of co-operation include promoting innovation across non-banking financial services, including insurance, non-banking finance, financial leasing, factoring and capital markets. The two parties will also raise awareness of the FRA’s regulatory sandbox, which provides a supervised testing environment for eligible projects and technology-based solutions to develop and test their business models and products in line with applicable rules and procedures. Gohar Nabil, Minister of Youth and Sports, said that supporting young people, empowering them economically and creating new opportunities for their ideas and projects were key pillars of the Egyptian state’s efforts to develop human capital and achieve sustainable development. He stressed the importance of strengthening co-operation between the ministry and the FRA to create an enabling environment for innovation and entrepreneurship. For his part, Azzam said the MoU marked an important step towards expanding co-operation with national institutions to empower young people and encourage innovation and entrepreneurship. He stressed that fostering an environment conducive to new ideas required co-ordinated efforts, the exchange of expertise and stronger links between innovators and the organisations, knowledge and opportunities needed to turn their ideas into viable, sustainable businesses. Azzam noted that around 75 companies in Egypt currently provide non-banking financial services using fintech, reflecting the sector’s adaptation to evolving requirements and the transformation of financial services and operating mechanisms at both local and international levels. He also underscored the importance of extending co-operation to young people across all governorates rather than concentrating efforts in Greater Cairo. He pointed to the growing share of investors aged between 18 and 40 in the non-banking financial sector, noting that they accounted for 80% of new stock market investors last year and more than 70% of investors in precious metals investment funds. It aims to increase the contribution of entrepreneurs to the non-banking financial sector and the national economy by supporting innovative ideas and startups and helping them maximise their value and returns.

headline: Madbouly reviews 2026/2027 development plan targeting 5.4% growth
summary: Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly met Ahmed Rostom, Minister of Planning and Economic Development, on Sunday to review the ministry’s key priorities, including the main features of the economic and social development plan for fiscal year 2026/2027, which targets economic growth of 5.4% and total investments of EGP 3.7trn. During the meeting, the two sides reviewed macroeconomic developments and current economic performance indicators. Rostom said the private sector is expected to account for around 59% of planned investments, reflecting the government’s commitment to expanding private-sector participation, strengthening productive capacities and supporting manufacturing industries. Rostom also outlined the main features of the National Economic Transformation Programme for 2027-2030, which was developed based on existing sectoral strategies, the Industrial Development Strategy and the National Employment Strategy. The programme sets out a series of priorities aimed at strengthening the national economy’s resilience to crises, enhancing mechanisms for private-sector participation and enabling businesses to compete more effectively. It also seeks to raise employment and productivity levels and create jobs that improve citizens’ living standards. Other priorities include improving the efficiency of public and private investment allocation across governorates, strengthening public financial management, increasing energy production and efficiency, expanding domestic utilisation and exports, and establishing an effective coordination framework between the Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) and the ministries of Finance and Planning and Economic Development. Rostom also reviewed the ministry’s efforts to develop legal and legislative frameworks aimed at improving the investment climate and protecting investors’ rights. He highlighted initiatives to support entrepreneurship, startups and high-growth businesses, with the aim of strengthening their competitiveness. These efforts are being pursued alongside structural reforms outlined in the State Ownership Policy Document and the government’s initial public offering (IPO) programme, which seek to create greater scope for the private sector to drive economic growth. The ministry is also working to expand innovative long-term financing instruments, diversify funding sources and improve liquidity to facilitate the expansion of national projects and private-sector investments. In parallel, it is pursuing efforts to broaden the tax base through digitalisation. On human capital development, Rostom highlighted the government’s efforts to better align workforce skills with labour market needs. He referred to his recent meeting with LinkedIn officials to explore ways to strengthen cooperation in using big data to identify the skills most in demand, helping decision-makers plan workforce development more effectively. He also pointed to an expanded meeting with a delegation from ESLSCA University to discuss renewing and broadening the scientific and training partnership between the government and the university. The partnership focuses on qualifying and training leaders and employees of state administrative bodies. The discussions build on the results of the existing partnership, which has provided 1,500 scholarships for young government leaders to pursue a Master of Government Business Administration degree. The initiative has also helped attract new talent to the state’s administrative apparatus. At the conclusion of the meeting, Rostom stressed that developing human capabilities, leadership and management skills remains central to improving government performance and supporting institutional development.

Egypt, Indonesia target $5bn in bilateral trade by 2030
summary: President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi said Egypt and Indonesia aim to increase bilateral trade to $5bn by 2030, while expanding joint manufacturing projects and attracting more Indonesian investment to the Egyptian market. Al-Sisi made the remarks following talks with Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto at the Merdeka Presidential Palace in Jakarta during an official visit on October 10-11, focused on advancing the two countries’ strategic partnership and coordinating positions on regional and international issues. The two presidents witnessed the signing of four memorandums of understanding covering maritime affairs and fisheries, statistical cooperation, an action plan for the strategic partnership, and visa exemptions for holders of diplomatic, service and special passports. Al-Sisi said the two countries had agreed to prioritise trade growth and work to remove obstacles to achieving the $5bn target. They also agreed to expand joint manufacturing in priority sectors and strengthen Egypt’s role as a production and export hub serving Arab, African and international markets. In education, culture and youth, the two presidents agreed to expand cooperation. Prabowo welcomed Al-Azhar University’s November 2025 decision to introduce Indonesian language studies at its Faculty of Languages and Translation. Al-Sisi said Egypt continued to receive thousands of Indonesian students each year at Al-Azhar and other Egyptian universities, describing educational and cultural ties as a central pillar of relations between the two countries.

The ministry is also working to expand innovative long-term financing instruments, diversify funding sources and improve liquidity to facilitate the expansion of national projects and private-sector investments. In parallel, it is pursuing efforts to broaden the tax base through digitalisation. On human capital development, Rostom highlighted the government’s efforts to better align workforce skills with labour market needs. He referred to his recent meeting with LinkedIn officials to explore ways to strengthen cooperation in using big data to identify the skills most in demand, helping decision-makers plan workforce development more effectively. He also pointed to an expanded meeting with a delegation from ESLSCA University to discuss renewing and broadening the scientific and training partnership between the government and the university. The partnership focuses on qualifying and training leaders and employees of state administrative bodies. The discussions build on the results of the existing partnership, which has provided 1,500 scholarships for young government leaders to pursue a Master of Government Business Administration degree. The initiative has also helped attract new talent to the state’s administrative apparatus. At the conclusion of the meeting, Rostom stressed that developing human capabilities, leadership and management skills remains central to improving government performance and supporting institutional development.

headline: Egypt condemns Riyadh airport attack that killed Egyptian woman, injured five
summary: Egypt’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Emigration and Egyptian Expatriates Affairs strongly condemned on Sunday an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh that killed an Egyptian woman and injured five other Egyptian nationals. It identified the woman as Azza Ramzy Mohamed Hassan and said Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty, acting on instructions from President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi, had directed the Egyptian embassy and consulate in Riyadh to contact her family and expedite the repatriation of her body. headline: Iran says US’ response to its conditions for talks are insufficient — Iranian official
summary: Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaei stressed that "if the Americans do not meet these conditions, neither will the Strait of Hormuz be opened to them"
body_text:
TUNIS, October 11. /TASS/. Iran considers the United States' response to the terms set by Tehran for the start of negotiations to be insufficient, even though Washington has accepted some of them, Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaei said.

"The Americans have ow responded. In their response, they accepted some of our conditions, but certain issues remain unclear. Thus, the Americans have responded to us, but we are not responding to them. The Americans have given us a response, and we consider their response insufficient," he said, as quoted by Press TV. "Naturally, we want them to remove these ambiguities. We need to see whether they can clarify them so that the next stages can begin, or not."

According to Rezaei, in recent months, Washington has repeatedly contacted Tehran via mediators proposing to resume diplomatic contacts. "Over the past two months, the Americans have been conveying proposals to us via three channels - Pakistan, Qatar, and even Iraq - and asked us to present our own proposals to them. We have conveyed seven conditions to the Americans and stated that if they do not meet these conditions, neither will the Strait of Hormuz be opened to them, nor will there be any negotiations," he stressed.

He also said that Tehran has changed its stance on diplomatic contacts with the United States and will not return to the previous format of talks. "Our diplomacy has changed, and we will not return to the old model. Because we had three rounds of negotiations, and during each round, the Americans cut them short and attacked Iran," he stated.

The United States and Israel launched a war against Iran on February 28. In June, Washington and Tehran signed a memorandum of understanding envisaging an immediate ceasefire on all fronts, including in Lebanon. However, the United States resumed large-scale attacks on Iran overnight to July 8, having accused it of breaching the existing agreements in what concerned the Strait of Hormuz. Later, the US administration actually signaled that it was ceasing the use of military force against Iran and was embarking on a path of its economic suffocation through tougher sanctions. However, US President Donald Trump said on October 10 that he doesn’t rule out further strikes against Iran.

analysis.framing: The article frames the event through Iranian official statements, presenting Tehran's conditions and grievances as the central narrative while noting US military actions and Trump's threat of further strikes.

loaded_language.explanation: Emotionally charged metaphor that evokes physical violence and suffering, rather than a neutral description of sanctions.
Direct, forceful verb that assigns aggression, though it is part of a quote from an Iranian official.
Idiomatic phrase implying abrupt and unfair termination, loaded with judgment about US behavior.

omissions: US official statements or responses to Iran's conditions
Details of the seven conditions set by Iran
International reaction or mediation efforts beyond the three channels mentioned
Context about the Strait of Hormuz and its strategic importance

headline: Iran ready to help start dialogue btw S. Arabia, Yemen: FM
summary: TEHRAN, Oct. 12 (MNA) – In a call with his Saudi counterpart, Iranian Foreign Minister emphasized that there is no military solution to the crises in the region, adding that Tehran is ready to assist in starting dialogue between Riyadh and Sanaa.
body_text:
TEHRAN, Oct. 12 (MNA) – In a call with his Saudi counterpart, Iranian Foreign Minister emphasized that there is no military solution to the crises in the region, adding that Tehran is ready to assist in starting dialogue between Riyadh and Sanaa.

On Sunday night, October 11, Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi and Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan discussed and exchanged views on the current developments in the region in a telephone call.

The Iranian Foreign Minister expressed concern about the escalation of tensions and emphasized that insisting on a military approach and ignoring a political solution will complicate the current situation.

Araghchi also emphasized that there is no military solution to the crises in the region and stated: The Islamic Republic of Iran is ready to provide any assistance to help start dialogue between Saudi Arabia and Yemen and to help achieve a political solution.

MNA/FNA1791750859660454641

headline: Saudi, Iranian foreign ministers discuss regional tensions, state news agency says

Oct 11 (Reuters) - Saudi Arabia's foreign minister spoke with his Iranian counterpart about the recent escalation of the regional conflict and efforts to lower tensions, the Saudi state news agency reported on Sunday, the officials' first publicly reported contact since Iran-aligned Houthis intensified strikes on the kingdom.

Iran's foreign minister said Tehran is ready to provide any assistance to facilitate dialogue between Saudi Arabia and Yemen, according to a post on the minister's Telegram account.

Yemen's Houthis have struck Saudi Arabia several times in the past week, including an attack on Riyadh's international airport on Saturday that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300. It was the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade.

headline: At Spain’s National Day in Doha, ambassador says peace is ‘unattainable’ without human rights
summary: The Spanish Embassy in Qatar brought together hundreds of officials, diplomats, business leaders and members of the Spanish community at Raffles Doha for a National Day reception celebrating Spanish heritage,…
body_text:
The Spanish Embassy in Qatar brought together hundreds of officials, diplomats, business leaders and members of the Spanish community at Raffles Doha for a National Day reception celebrating Spanish heritage, growing ties with Qatar and shared diplomatic priorities, including Palestine.

As Spain marked its National Day at Raffles Doha on Sunday, Spanish Ambassador to Qatar Álvaro Renedo Zalba told Doha News in an exclusive interview that “the barbarity in Gaza is intolerable,” and called on Qatar and Spain to keep working together on international law, human rights and diplomatic solutions to the violence in Palestine and across the region.

Peace, the ambassador said, would remain “an unattainable dream” without human rights, diplomacy and international law, principles described as central to the foreign policies of both countries.

The remarks came as hundreds of Qatari officials, diplomats, business leaders and members of the Spanish community gathered at Raffles Doha for the occasion, celebrated annually on 12 October. Doha News served as the event’s official media partner.

Palestine and growing diplomatic ties

In a formal address to guests, Ambassador Zalba spoke of the “harrowing toll wrought by the barbarity in Gaza,” placing Palestine among the major challenges confronting international peace and security.

“Addressing the dire situation in Palestine is also an urgent priority for Spain,” the envoy said, reiterating Spain’s support for Palestinian statehood, humanitarian assistance and a two-state solution.

The ambassador firmly rejected the annexation of Palestinian territory, the forced displacement of Palestinians and Israeli settler violence, warning that such actions undermine international law and the prospects for a just and lasting peace.

The Spanish ambassador also expressed Spain’s solidarity with Qatar amid ongoing regional tensions, condemning attacks on the country’s sovereignty and recognising Doha’s diplomatic efforts to promote de-escalation. Drawing parallels with Qatar’s role in international diplomacy, the Spanish diplomat pointed to the two countries’ shared commitment to dialogue, peaceful conflict resolution and international cooperation.

Turning to bilateral ties, the envoy highlighted growing political, economic and cultural cooperation between Qatar and Spain, including high-level engagement, security cooperation and preparations for future sporting events. Spanish companies are also increasingly present in Qatar, particularly in energy, technology, education, agriculture and infrastructure.

Red and yellow illuminated the hotel’s façade as the Spanish Embassy welcomed guests for an evening celebrating Spain’s heritage and its relationship with Qatar.

Among the guests of honour were Qatar’s Minister of Public Health Mansoor bin Ebrahim bin Saad Al Mahmoud, Minister of State and President of Qatar National Library Hamad bin Abdulaziz Al Kawari, and Ministry of Foreign Affairs Protocol Department Director Ibrahim Yousif Abdullah Fakhro.

Türkiye’s Ambassador to Qatar Yakup Caymazoğlu was among the notable guests, alongside Dominican Republic Ambassador Georges Bahsa Hazim and Croatian Ambassador Drago Lovrić.

From the fusion Qatari Ardha with Spanish flamenco, to paella

Two young Qatari twins opened the cultural programme as masters of ceremonies, welcoming guests and introducing the evening’s performances.

An Ardha-inspired Qatari performance took the stage before moving into flamenco, shifting from local rhythms to the expressive footwork and handclaps of southern Spain. Presented back to back, the performances brought the two traditions together on one stage.

Spanish gastronomy featured throughout. Chefs flown in from Valencia exclusively for the event prepared paella at a live cooking station, while guests sampled traditional dishes from different regions of Spain.

The art display included Qatar’s edition of La Menina, created by Spanish artist Antonio Azzato and painted by Qatari artist Muna Al Bader. Inspired by Diego Velázquez’s Las Meninas, its maritime design and wave motifs bring together Spain’s artistic heritage and Qatar’s relationship with the sea.

History, tribute and gratitude

Ambassador Zalba reflected on Spain’s cultural legacy and its role in connecting communities across continents, describing the country as a bridge between Europe, the Americas, Africa and the Arab world.

The ambassador paid tribute to the late Father Amir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, recalling the transformative leadership that shaped Qatar’s development and international standing.

In the interview with Doha News, the Spanish envoy explained the historical significance of Spain’s National Day, tracing it to 12 October 1492 and Christopher Columbus’s voyage under the Catholic Monarchs, Queen Isabel I de Castilla and King Fernando II de Aragón.

“It’s a very significant date,” the ambassador said, describing the voyage as ushering in “an unprecedented era of global interconnections.”

The ambassador also thanked Doha News, praising its journalists for their professionalism and commitment to covering issues that matter around the world while delivering high-quality news to audiences in Qatar.

The reception concluded with a cake-cutting ceremony led by the Spanish ambassador alongside the guests of honour, closing an evening centred on cultural exchange, diplomacy and community.

headline: (EDITORIAL from The Korea Times on Oct. 12)
summary: South Korea's ambassador to Ukraine, Park Ki-chang, returned home Saturday, call...
body_text:
Seoul, Kyiv should resolve spat: Dialogue needed following ambassador recall, for South Korea's national interest

South Korea's ambassador to Ukraine, Park Ki-chang, returned home Saturday, called in by President Lee Jae Myung over Ukraine's disclosure that two North Korean prisoners of war (POW) who were captured in 2025 are now in South Korea.

Recalling an ambassador is one of the strongest diplomatic actions a country can take, the others being the much more drastic steps of expelling the ambassador of the offending nation or formally severing ties. The last time South Korea took such step was in 2008, when it recalled its ambassador to Japan over the Dokdo islet issue. It is regrettable that the ties between South Korea and Ukraine, which have thus far been characterized by cooperation — particularly during Ukraine's four years of war following Russia's invasion — are now under such strain.

Seoul's frustrations stem from Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's sudden and unilateral disclosure during a speech at the United Nations that the North Korean POWs had been transferred to South Korea, a disclosure that caught Seoul off guard. In the ensuing weeks, Ukraine continued to deny that there had ever been an agreement in place between the two countries to keep the information confidential — an agreement that was intended to protect the POWs and their families who remains remain in North Korea. After Ukraine's successive apologies fell short of Seoul's demands, the matter snowballed into the diplomatic rift we see today.

Zelenskyy, whose country has been at war with Russia for more than four years, has sought to bolster international support through public statements and appeals for assistance. In asking for more support, Zelenskyy in August and September projected that more North Korean soldiers will be sent to support Russia's war efforts soon. But the issue of the North Korean POWs is a highly sensitive matter, especially after the North rewrote its constitution to categorize South Korea as a hostile nation rather than an eventual partner for unification.

In that vein, the unilateral disclosure and ensuing denial may well be seen as undoing the good faith that has existed between Seoul and Kyiv. However, diplomacy requires balancing competing interests in pursuit of a country's broader goals. Achieving those goals sometimes calls for quieter negotiations and dialogue, as an unwaveringly hard-line stance can leave little room for maneuver in today's complex global order.

The foreign ministries in both South Korea and Ukraine have signaled their willingness to continue dialogue. When it announced the ambassador's recall on Thursday, Seoul also said that they would "continue consultations with the Ukrainian side." A spokesperson for Ukraine's foreign ministry said that "diplomacy" should prevail over "emotions," even while softening language used at last week's news conference. The ministry said it had "invited" the South Korean ambassador to the foreign ministry office in Kyiv to explain Ukraine's position.

Lee reportedly is considering keeping its ambassador in Seoul until Ukraine meets South Korea's demands. Both sides must now assess the fallout should the standoff continue.

South Korea remains aligned with efforts to uphold international law and de-escalate the conflict. It has provided humanitarian assistance, supported reconstruction efforts and supplied non-lethal equipment, and announced further assistance of $100 million to Kyiv in July. Ukraine, despite being embattled, remains vital to European security. In a changing global order shaped by U.S.-China rivalry, countries increasingly need to safeguard their interests through both bilateral and multilateral diplomatic ties.

South Korea's participation in Ukraine's postwar reconstruction and its continued partnership with Kyiv would serve Seoul's broader foreign policy objectives. Ukraine, in turn, must demonstrate good faith in its dealings with partner nations. Difficult circumstances may call for flexibility, but that flexibility should be guided by firm principles.

South Korea and Ukraine should work to put an end to the seeming confusion and ensure transparency and trust are restored. The two sides have clarified their differences enough to pave the way for a swift resolution and closer bilateral cooperation.(END)

analysis.framing: The editorial frames the South Korea-Ukraine diplomatic rift as a regrettable but resolvable dispute, urging both sides toward dialogue and transparency while gently faulting Ukraine's unilateral disclosure.

loaded_language.explanation: Idiomatic phrasing that casts Ukraine's action as a surprise attack on a passive South Korea, subtly assigning fault.
loaded_language.neutral_alternative: was not previously communicated to Seoul

loaded_language.explanation: Metaphorical language implying an uncontrolled escalation, adding dramatic weight beyond a factual description.

loaded_language.quote: undoing the good faith that has existed
loaded_language.explanation: Evaluative moral framing that characterizes Ukraine's actions as a betrayal of trust rather than a policy disagreement.
Characterizes a firm negotiating position negatively, editorializing against rigidity without attributing it to a specific party.
Vague characterization that implies disorganization without specifying what the confusion is or who caused it.

omissions: Specific details of what South Korea's demands on Ukraine actually are
Ukraine's stated rationale for the unilateral disclosure beyond seeking international support
Any reaction or statement from North Korea regarding the POWs
The number of North Korean POWs involved beyond the two mentioned
Whether the POWs' families in North Korea have been affected since the disclosure

The remarks came as hundreds of Qatari officials, diplomats, business leaders and members of the Spanish community gathered at Raffles Doha for the occasion, celebrated annually on 12 October. Doha News served as the event’s official media partner.

Palestine and growing diplomatic ties

In a formal address to guests, Ambassador Zalba spoke of the “harrowing toll wrought by the barbarity in Gaza,” placing Palestine among the major challenges confronting international peace and security.

“Addressing the dire situation in Palestine is also an urgent priority for Spain,” the envoy said, reiterating Spain’s support for Palestinian statehood, humanitarian assistance and a two-state solution.

The ambassador firmly rejected the annexation of Palestinian territory, the forced displacement of Palestinians and Israeli settler violence, warning that such actions undermine international law and the prospects for a just and lasting peace.

The Spanish ambassador also expressed Spain’s solidarity with Qatar amid ongoing regional tensions, condemning attacks on the country’s sovereignty and recognising Doha’s diplomatic efforts to promote de-escalation. Drawing parallels with Qatar’s role in international diplomacy, the Spanish diplomat pointed to the two countries’ shared commitment to dialogue, peaceful conflict resolution and international cooperation.

Turning to bilateral ties, the envoy highlighted growing political, economic and cultural cooperation between Qatar and Spain, including high-level engagement, security cooperation and preparations for future sporting events. Spanish companies are also increasingly present in Qatar, particularly in energy, technology, education, agriculture and infrastructure.

Red and yellow illuminated the hotel’s façade as the Spanish Embassy welcomed guests for an evening celebrating Spain’s heritage and its relationship with Qatar.

Among the guests of honour were Qatar’s Minister of Public Health Mansoor bin Ebrahim bin Saad Al Mahmoud, Minister of State and President of Qatar National Library Hamad bin Abdulaziz Al Kawari, and Ministry of Foreign Affairs Protocol Department Director Ibrahim Yousif Abdullah Fakhro.

Türkiye’s Ambassador to Qatar Yakup Caymazoğlu was among the notable guests, alongside Dominican Republic Ambassador Georges Bahsa Hazim and Croatian Ambassador Drago Lovrić.

From the fusion Qatari Ardha with Spanish flamenco, to paella

Two young Qatari twins opened the cultural programme as masters of ceremonies, welcoming guests and introducing the evening’s performances.

An Ardha-inspired Qatari performance took the stage before moving into flamenco, shifting from local rhythms to the expressive footwork and handclaps of southern Spain. Presented back to back, the performances brought the two traditions together on one stage.

Spanish gastronomy featured throughout. Chefs flown in from Valencia exclusively for the event prepared paella at a live cooking station, while guests sampled traditional dishes from different regions of Spain.

The art display included Qatar’s edition of La Menina, created by Spanish artist Antonio Azzato and painted by Qatari artist Muna Al Bader. Inspired by Diego Velázquez’s Las Meninas, its maritime design and wave motifs bring together Spain’s artistic heritage and Qatar’s relationship with the sea.

History, tribute and gratitude

Ambassador Zalba reflected on Spain’s cultural legacy and its role in connecting communities across continents, describing the country as a bridge between Europe, the Americas, Africa and the Arab world.

The ambassador paid tribute to the late Father Amir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, recalling the transformative leadership that shaped Qatar’s development and international standing.

In the interview with Doha News, the Spanish envoy explained the historical significance of Spain’s National Day, tracing it to 12 October 1492 and Christopher Columbus’s voyage under the Catholic Monarchs, Queen Isabel I de Castilla and King Fernando II de Aragón.

“It’s a very significant date,” the ambassador said, describing the voyage as ushering in “an unprecedented era of global interconnections.”

The ambassador also thanked Doha News, praising its journalists for their professionalism and commitment to covering issues that matter around the world while delivering high-quality news to audiences in Qatar.

The reception concluded with a cake-cutting ceremony led by the Spanish ambassador alongside the guests of honour, closing an evening centred on cultural exchange, diplomacy and community.

headline: (EDITORIAL from The Korea Times on Oct. 12)
summary: South Korea's ambassador to Ukraine, Park Ki-chang, returned home Saturday, call...
body_text:
Seoul, Kyiv should resolve spat: Dialogue needed following ambassador recall, for South Korea's national interest

South Korea's ambassador to Ukraine, Park Ki-chang, returned home Saturday, called in by President Lee Jae Myung over Ukraine's disclosure that two North Korean prisoners of war (POW) who were captured in 2025 are now in South Korea.

Recalling an ambassador is one of the strongest diplomatic actions a country can take, the others being the much more drastic steps of expelling the ambassador of the offending nation or formally severing ties. The last time South Korea took such step was in 2008, when it recalled its ambassador to Japan over the Dokdo islet issue. It is regrettable that the ties between South Korea and Ukraine, which have thus far been characterized by cooperation — particularly during Ukraine's four years of war following Russia's invasion — are now under such strain.

Seoul's frustrations stem from Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's sudden and unilateral disclosure during a speech at the United Nations that the North Korean POWs had been transferred to South Korea, a disclosure that caught Seoul off guard. In the ensuing weeks, Ukraine continued to deny that there had ever been an agreement in place between the two countries to keep the information confidential — an agreement that was intended to protect the POWs and their families who remains remain in North Korea. After Ukraine's successive apologies fell short of Seoul's demands, the matter snowballed into the diplomatic rift we see today.

Zelenskyy, whose country has been at war with Russia for more than four years, has sought to bolster international support through public statements and appeals for assistance. In asking for more support, Zelenskyy in August and September projected that more North Korean soldiers will be sent to support Russia's war efforts soon. But the issue of the North Korean POWs is a highly sensitive matter, especially after the North rewrote its constitution to categorize South Korea as a hostile nation rather than an eventual partner for unification.

In that vein, the unilateral disclosure and ensuing denial may well be seen as undoing the good faith that has existed between Seoul and Kyiv. However, diplomacy requires balancing competing interests in pursuit of a country's broader goals. Achieving those goals sometimes calls for quieter negotiations and dialogue, as an unwaveringly hard-line stance can leave little room for maneuver in today's complex global order.

The foreign ministries in both South Korea and Ukraine have signaled their willingness to continue dialogue. When it announced the ambassador's recall on Thursday, Seoul also said that they would "continue consultations with the Ukrainian side." A spokesperson for Ukraine's foreign ministry said that "diplomacy" should prevail over "emotions," even while softening language used at last week's news conference. The ministry said it had "invited" the South Korean ambassador to the foreign ministry office in Kyiv to explain Ukraine's position.

Lee reportedly is considering keeping its ambassador in Seoul until Ukraine meets South Korea's demands. Both sides must now assess the fallout should the standoff continue.

South Korea remains aligned with efforts to uphold international law and de-escalate the conflict. It has provided humanitarian assistance, supported reconstruction efforts and supplied non-lethal equipment, and announced further assistance of $100 million to Kyiv in July. Ukraine, despite being embattled, remains vital to European security. In a changing global order shaped by U.S.-China rivalry, countries increasingly need to safeguard their interests through both bilateral and multilateral diplomatic ties.

South Korea's participation in Ukraine's postwar reconstruction and its continued partnership with Kyiv would serve Seoul's broader foreign policy objectives. Ukraine, in turn, must demonstrate good faith in its dealings with partner nations. Difficult circumstances may call for flexibility, but that flexibility should be guided by firm principles.

South Korea and Ukraine should work to put an end to the seeming confusion and ensure transparency and trust are restored. The two sides have clarified their differences enough to pave the way for a swift resolution and closer bilateral cooperation.(END)

headline: Witkoff, Kushner postpone Russia trip for more clarity on Ukraine, Europe’s stance — Axios

WASHINGTON, October 12. /TASS/. US Special Presidential Envoy Steve Witkoff and the US leader’s son-in-law Jared Kushner want more clarity on the position of Kiev and European countries toward resolving the Ukraine conflict before traveling to Russia, Axios quoted its sources as saying.

headline: FX volatility, shipping costs and EV adoption reshape Egypt’s automotive aftermarket
summary: Badr El Din Automotive Accessories and Tuning has identified rising import and shipping costs, foreign exchange (FX) fluctuations, changing consumer preferences and the growing adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) as key factors reshaping Egypt’s automotive accessories and spare parts market. The company’s observations come as it participates in Autotech 2026, a three-day exhibition bringing together businesses operating in automotive spare parts, accessories, components and aftermarket services. Badr El Din said import costs and product availability remained major challenges for businesses, as foreign exchange fluctuations and global supply chain disruptions affected purchasing costs, inventory management and delivery schedules. Companies operating in the market are increasingly required to monitor costs, improve inventory planning and maintain supplies of high-demand products amid changing market conditions. China remains one of the main sourcing markets for automotive accessories and spare parts supplied to Egypt, supported by its extensive manufacturing base and wide range of products catering to different consumer segments. Technology is also reshaping demand, with consumers increasingly seeking accessories that combine design, functionality and modern features to enhance vehicle interiors and driving experiences. Key product categories include smart screens, LED lighting, ambient interior lighting systems, vehicle protection films and vehicle customisation solutions. The growing presence of electric vehicles in Egypt could also create new opportunities for the automotive aftermarket as adoption expands and demand evolves for accessories, equipment and components suited to EVs. This shift may encourage suppliers to diversify their product portfolios and sourcing channels to respond to changing vehicle technologies and customer requirements. Badr El Din’s participation in Autotech 2026 reflects its engagement with developments in the local automotive aftermarket. Founded in 1990, the company operates a distribution network covering Egypt’s governorates and maintains partnerships with international brands specialising in automotive accessories and customisation. Commenting on the company’s participation, Badr El Din Gamal El Din, CEO and founder of Badr El Din Automotive Accessories, said the exhibition provided an opportunity to strengthen engagement with industry partners and customers while keeping pace with market developments. He added that the event offered insights into changing customer needs and industry trends, noting that the company remained focused on expanding its product and brand portfolio in Egypt in line with evolving consumer preferences and market dynamics.

headline: One dead in new attack on Saudi airport, a day after Houthi strike kills 13
summary: By Jana Choukeir, Maha El Dahan, Timour Azhari and Yasmine GhaniaDUBAI/RIYADH, Oct 11 (Reuters) - One person was killed and nearly a dozenhurt in a new attack Riyadh's international airport on Sunday, Saudi authorities reported, a day after a strike claimed by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300.
body_text:
By Jana Choukeir, Maha El Dahan, Timour Azhari and Yasmine Ghania

DUBAI/RIYADH, Oct 11 (Reuters) - One person was killed and nearly a dozenhurt in a new attack Riyadh's international airport on Sunday, Saudi authorities reported, a day after a strike claimed by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300.

Saudi-led coalition forces in Yemen said an unidentified projectile had targeted Riyadh's international airport Terminal 4 on Sunday, causing a fire. Eleven people were woundedin addition to the fatality, the Saudi civil aviation authority said.

Coalition forces also said Saudi air defences had intercepted a cruise missile in the vicinity of King Khalid International Airport. They later added that a drone had been intercepted and destroyed in the country's Eastern Province, and a ballistic missile launched towards Khamis Mushait had been intercepted.Emergency alerts were also issued in Abha, in the south, early on Monday but the danger had since passed, the Saudi Civil Defense said.

The strikes have exposed vulnerabilities in Saudi defence capabilities as the kingdom wages an air campaign against the ​Houthis, who are fighting a ground war in Yemen against the Saudi-backed Yemeni government.

Footage released by Saudi state television of the Saturday attack on the Riyadh airport showed scores of religious pilgrims lined up at a gate as they prepared to travel to Islam's two holiest sites. A bright orange flash sent people running in panic, while parts of the roof appeared to cave in.

The airport was closed after the attack, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade.

HOUTHIS CLAIM RESPONSIBILITY FOR OTHER ATTACKS

In a televised speech on Sunday, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree claimed responsibility for Saturday's attack and said the group had also struck the airport inDammam in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province and two facilities of Saudi oil giant Saudi Aramco.

The Saudi government's media office and Aramco did not respond to requests for comment.

The Saudi civil aviation authority confirmed the strike onDammam's King Fahd International Airport late on Sunday, adding that "damage assessments and safety inspections of airport facilities are under way."

An eyewitness aboard a taxiing aircraft at Dammamtold Reuters that around 8:30 p.m. (1730 GMT) on Sunday, they saw a projectile strike the tarmac beside several parked aircraft, causing a fire. The witness said the aircraft returned to the gate. Passengers disembarked and were told to leave.

Flight-tracking website Flightradar24 showed several delays and cancellations on Sunday for arrivals and departures atDammam airport, the kingdom's third-largest.

The Houthis earlier on Sunday had ‌renewed their warning against ​using Saudi ​airports. "We urge everyone to take our warnings seriously, and Saudi Arabia bears responsibility for any failed interceptions," the group said.

Britain's embassy in Saudi Arabia in a post on X advised British citizens against all but essential travel to Jeddah, Dammam and all airports in the kingdom except the airport in Medina.

US aviation authorities issued a notice to US airlines to use caution while flying to or over the kingdom.

'WORSE IS YET TO COME,' HOUTHIS WARN

Saudi Arabia has recently stepped up its military involvement in Yemen, launching strikes against theHouthis and backing a government counteroffensive after the Houthis seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month.

The Houthis said on Sunday that Saudi Arabia carried out 124 air strikes in Yemen in the past 24 hours. "Unless the Saudi enemy stops its aggression and interference in Yemen, worse is yet to come, God willing," Yemen's Houthi-run foreign ministry said in statements carried by Al Masirah television.

US President Donald Trump said on Saturday the United States was considering joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis in the conflict, a spillover from the wider war with Iran that the US and Israel launched in February.

In a post on Telegram, Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araqchi said he told his Saudi counterpart that Tehran was ready to help facilitate dialogue between Saudi Arabia and Yemen.

ENERGY CONFERENCE STILL GOING AHEAD

Afive-day conference of international energy organization WPC Energy opened as planned on Sunday at a convention centre about 10 km (6 miles) from the Riyadh airport, the Saudi energy ministry said.

A ministerial meeting of the International Energy Forum also went ahead, according to a media advisory from the ministry. It was not clear which ministers attended.

Italy's energy minister, Gilberto Pichetto Fratin, whose country was co-hosting, had said on Friday he would participate remotely via video link.

German officials were trying to organise a return flight for economy minister Katherina Reiche. She was supposed to return to Berlin from Riyadh on Monday but the ministry said it appeared likely her flight would be unable to take off.

Separately, Saudi authorities announced that in-person classes at schools in Riyadh would be shifted to remote learning from Sunday until Thursday.

Sunday's attack brought the death toll in attacks on Riyadh's airport to 18 for the week. In Saturday's attack, the dead included four Saudis while the remainder were foreign nationals, Saudi authorities said.

(Reporting by Jana Choukeir and Maha El Dahan in Dubai, Timour Azhari Riyadh, Menna Alaa El-Din and Yasmine Ghania in Cairo, James Mackenize and Sarah El Safty; Writing by Jan Wolfe and Patricia Zengerle; Editing by Andrew Mills, Gareth Jones, Edmund Klamann and Lincoln Feast.)

headline: Fresh Houthi strike hits Riyadh airport a day after deadly attack
summary: A fresh Houthi strike hit Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport on Sunday, killing a Pakistani resident and wounding 11, Saudi authorities said. The attack followed a strike that killed at least 12 people and halted airport operations on Saturday. The Iran-backed group threatened further attacks on Saudi Arabia’s transit hubs.
body_text:
A fresh Houthi strike hit Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport on Sunday, killing a Pakistani resident and wounding 11, Saudi authorities said. The attack followed a strike that killed at least 12 people and halted airport operations on Saturday. The Iran-backed group threatened further attacks on Saudi Arabia’s transit hubs.

Issued on: 12/10/2026 - 03:01Modified: 12/10/2026 - 03:15

A fresh Houthi strike hit Riyadh's international airport on Sunday, a day after an attack claimed by the Yemeni group killed at least a dozen people and forced authorities to suspend operations there.

Saturday's attack, the deadliest on Saudi soil in more than a decade, was a sharp escalation in the Yemen war, where Riyadh has long militarily supported the internationally recognised government against the Houthis.

The Iran-backed group on Sunday claimed multiple attacks over the last 24 hours, including on the airport, and threatened to keep targeting the kingdom's transit hubs, calling them "a theatre of operations for our forces".

Hours later, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the group reported that a projectile struck King Khalid International Airport, sparking a fire. Air defences also intercepted a missile nearby, it added.

The fresh attack on the airport killed one person -- a Pakistani resident -- and wounded 11 others, Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said.

The wounded "were immediately transferred to several hospitals to receive the necessary medical care," the authority said on X.

"The attack also caused property damage, the extent of which is currently being assessed."

Authorities have extended the closure of the airport by 24 hours until 2100 GMT on Monday, the tracking site Flightradar24 said on X.

AFP journalists and locals reported hearing the sound of multiple blasts in the Saudi capital on Sunday.

"The birds went into a frenzy after the sound. The whole house shook," said one resident of the Al-Aarid neighbourhood in the north of the city.

The civil aviation authority also reported another attack on Dammam airport in the east -- which the Houthis also said they had targeted -- a day after the Saudi coalition reported a projectile landing nearby.

Shortly afterwards, the coalition reported shooting down a drone, also in the east.

The Houthis have stepped up their attacks on the Riyadh airport -- where three people were also killed on Thursday -- as well as on Saudi oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.

Although Saudi Arabia has poured billions into its military, Houthi attacks continue to slip through.

"Saudi air defences have been able to intercept some Houthi missile and drone attacks, but Saudi Arabia is so large that it's simply impossible for them to consistently defend themselves," said Thomas Juneau, security analyst at Ottawa University.

The anti-Houthi coalition called Saturday's attack a "full-fledged war crime" and vowed to "respond decisively".

Houthi media reported two Saudi strikes in Yemen's Houthi-controlled Sanaa governorate on Sunday.

Saturday's attack drew condemnation from the United Nations and leaders around the world, including US President Donald Trump, who said he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Houthis.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, whose country does not have diplomatic relations with Saudi Arabia, also denounced the "horrific terrorist attack".

Four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshis, one American, one Egyptian, one Jordanian, one Syrian, one Palestinian and one Sudanese were killed, the civil aviation authority said, with 309 people wounded.

The Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia also said one of its citizens died on Sunday after being wounded the day before.

Witnesses to Saturday's strike described chaos in the aftermath.

"People who were in Terminal 3 started running towards us," a 32-year-old Riyadh resident told AFP.

"Some had lost a hand or an arm. People were running while carrying injured people, covered in blood."

The attack prompted health officials to activate a rare mass call-up of doctors, a medical source said.

The US, Canadian, German and Spanish embassies in Saudi Arabia have warned their citizens to avoid Riyadh airport, while Australia urged its citizens on Sunday to stay indoors altogether and "shelter in place".

Read moreWhy Yemen’s war is escalating

Saturday's airport strike, on the eve of Saudi Arabia's high-profile convention and entertainment season, was the deadliest attack in the kingdom since a 2015 suicide bombing.

With the summer heat subsiding, October also usually marks the beginning of the high travel season for Umrah pilgrims, with millions of Muslims from across the world flocking to Mecca.

Saudi Arabia leads an international coalition that has supported Yemen's government militarily since 2015, including by seeking to exert control over Yemeni airspace and the airport in the Houthi-held capital Sanaa.

Ottawa University's Juneau said the Houthis now "want to do to Saudi Arabia what Saudi Arabia does to them".

On the ground in Yemen, Saudi-supported government forces were advancing in their counter-offensive against the Houthis around the Bab al-Mandab strait, a key shipping route, military sources said Saturday.

The Houthis claimed to have repelled them.

Claims by both sides have been impossible to independently verify, with the situation moving fast on the ground and access for journalists difficult.

headline: Sunday’s attack on Riyadh Airport leaves one killed, 11 others injured — agency
summary: At least 12 people were killed and 300 others were injured in a deadly attack on the same airport on October 10
body_text:
TUNIS, October 12. /TASS/. One was killed and 11 others were injured as Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport came under a fresh attack on Sunday, the kingdom’s Civil Aviation Authority said.

As a result of the latest attack on Sunday afternoon, "one Pakistani national living in the country was killed and 11 other people were injured," the agency said in a statement on X.

At least 12 people were killed and 300 others were injured in a deadly attack on the same airport on October 10.

The Saudi capital’s main air hub will remain shut for flights approximately until the end of the day amid precaution measures, a source in Riyadh’s air traffic control service told TASS.

Spokesman for the Saudi-led coalition Turki al-Maliki said an unidentified projectile hit a passenger terminal at Riyadh International Airport, causing a fire. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saria said in turn that the rebel movement had struck the airports in Riyadh and Dammam, as well as oil giant Saudi Aramco’s facilities.

headline: Riyadh airport attack: One Indian killed, 10 others injured; Government says ‘unacceptable’
body_text:
An Indian national was killed and 10 others were injured in the missile attack on Riyadh’s international airport on Saturday, the Indian Embassy said. Condemning the attack, India on Sunday said it was “completely unacceptable”.

While the government is yet to identify the victim, The Indian Express has learnt that he was a resident of Hyderabad, and was part of a 13-member group that had gone for Umrah. A part of the airport’s roof fell on him during the attack, said a relative. His family members are reported to be among those injured.

A day after the attack in which 12 others were killed and over 300 injured, Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis claimed responsibility, and also warned airlines, travellers and airport workers to stay away from airports in Saudi Arabia.

Hours later, the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said an “unidentified projectile” had targeted Riyadh’s international airport on Sunday too. It said Saudi air defences had intercepted a cruise missile in the vicinity of the airport.

Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump said Washington ⁠was considering joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis in the conflict, a spillover from the war on Iran that the US and Israel launched in February.

Among the others killed in Saturday’s attack were four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshi nationals, a Palestinian, a US citizen, an Egyptian, a Jordanian, a Syrian and a Sudanese, the Saudi civil aviation authority said.

In a post on X, the Indian Embassy in Riyadh said: “It is learnt that one Indian national injured in the Riyadh attack has unfortunately lost his life today. We convey our heartfelt condolences to the family of the deceased. We are in touch with the family and will provide all support for ensuring the early repatriation of mortal remains.”

In an earlier post, it said it “has been following up on the dastardly attack”. “It is learnt that 11 Indians are among those injured in the attack. Embassy has been in touch with local authorities to enquire about their well-being. Our officials have also reached out to the hospital authorities. We will provide further updates as they become available,” it said.

Quoting the Indian Embassy’s post, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said on X: “Our Embassy is doing everything necessary in this difficult situation.”

Earlier in the day, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) issued a statement condemning the attack. “We strongly condemn the repeated attacks on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport over the past few days, including the dastardly attack on October 10, which have led to loss of lives, injuries and damage to property. We express our condolences to the families of the deceased and wish speedy recovery to the injured persons,” it said.

“The repeated attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure are completely unacceptable and must cease immediately,” it said. “We stand in solidarity with the people and the government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in defence of their sovereignty, and hope that peace and normalcy returns to the region at the earliest,” it added.

This is the second time in the last few days that India has condemned the attacks on Saudi airports. On October 8, with two airports in Saudi Arabia targeted in the previous two days, India had issued a strong condemnation along with an advisory to its nationals there to remain alert and vigilant. headline: FX volatility, shipping costs and EV adoption reshape Egypt’s automotive aftermarket
summary: Badr El Din Automotive Accessories and Tuning has identified rising import and shipping costs, foreign exchange (FX) fluctuations, changing consumer preferences and the growing adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) as key factors reshaping Egypt’s automotive accessories and spare parts market. The company’s observations come as it participates in Autotech 2026, a three-day exhibition bringing together businesses operating in automotive spare parts, accessories, components and aftermarket services. Badr El Din said import costs and product availability remained major challenges for businesses, as foreign exchange fluctuations and global supply chain disruptions affected purchasing costs, inventory management and delivery schedules. Companies operating in the market are increasingly required to monitor costs, improve inventory planning and maintain supplies of high-demand products amid changing market conditions. China remains one of the main sourcing markets for automotive accessories and spare parts supplied to Egypt, supported by its extensive manufacturing base and wide range of products catering to different consumer segments. Technology is also reshaping demand, with consumers increasingly seeking accessories that combine design, functionality and modern features to enhance vehicle interiors and driving experiences. Key product categories include smart screens, LED lighting, ambient interior lighting systems, vehicle protection films and vehicle customisation solutions. The growing presence of electric vehicles in Egypt could also create new opportunities for the automotive aftermarket as adoption expands and demand evolves for accessories, equipment and components suited to EVs. This shift may encourage suppliers to diversify their product portfolios and sourcing channels to respond to changing vehicle technologies and customer requirements. Badr El Din’s participation in Autotech 2026 reflects its engagement with developments in the local automotive aftermarket. Founded in 1990, the company operates a distribution network covering Egypt’s governorates and maintains partnerships with international brands specialising in automotive accessories and customisation. Commenting on the company’s participation, Badr El Din Gamal El Din, CEO and founder of Badr El Din Automotive Accessories, said the exhibition provided an opportunity to strengthen engagement with industry partners and customers while keeping pace with market developments. He added that the event offered insights into changing customer needs and industry trends, noting that the company remained focused on expanding its product and brand portfolio in Egypt in line with evolving consumer preferences and market dynamics.

headline: US-Iran War Live News Updates: Tehran denies directing Houthis; urges peace talks with Saudi Arabia
body_text:
Yemen’s Houthi-run Saba news agency has reported air strikes on the Hamdan district in Sanaa governorate and two strikes on al-Zurbi Road in the Hayfan district in Taiz.

There were no immediate reports of casualties or damage.

Earlier, the agency reported that three civilians were wounded in an attack on a home in the Salah district of Taiz. It blamed Saudi forces for the attack.

Another attack on Sanaa on Sunday killed a child and wounded six others, according to the agency.

The Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen says it has intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired by the Houthis that targeted the southwestern city of Khamis Mushait.

The alert came after the Saudi civil defence authority issued an alert warning of a “potential danger” in the nearby city of Abha.

Reopening the Strait of Hormuz is impossible until Tehran's conditions are met, Hassan Ghashghavi, spokesman for the Iranian parliament's National Security and Foreign Policy Committee, said on Sunday.

Speaking to senior Iranian police officials, Ghashghavi claimed Iran's management of the strategic waterway was growing stronger each day, ISNA reported.

An Indian national who was among 11 Indians injured in the attack on Riyadh airport on October 10 has died, the Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia said.

The Embassy conveyed its condolences to the deceased’s family and said it was in contact with them to provide support and arrange the early repatriation of the remains.

Many in Saudi Arabia's ruling circles see no need for talks, because they believe Iran controls the Houthis and decides what they do. Both the Houthis and Iran have repeatedly denied this. The Houthis say they make their own decisions, and Iran says the same, though the two sides share some interests. Iran says it does not want the fighting to keep growing and believes Saudi Arabia and the Houthis would do better to negotiate peace.

Iran has offered this negotiation, mediation because I think Iran believes that escalation and military solutions are not going to lead to a peace in the region.

We have seen over the last several months – Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian asked Gulf countries to come to the negotiation table and strike a deal between themselves without foreign powers, a deal that will establish security in the region. So this could be interpreted as a continuation of that position by the Iranian leadership here.

Of course, there are a lot of issues and a lot of details still missing. Until now, we don’t know what really has been discussed other than this offer by the Iranians. We don’t know who initiated this phone call, whether it was a request from Saudi Arabia or whether it is an Iranian offer in the first place.

Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis claimed responsibility for a Saturday strike on Riyadh's international airport that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300, while Saudi authorities reported that people were injured in a new attack on the airport on Sunday.

Saudi-led coalition forces in Yemen said an unidentified projectile had targeted Riyadh's international airport Terminal 4 on Sunday, causing a fire. An unspecified number of people were injured, the Saudi civil aviation authority said, adding it was still assessing the damage.

The coalition forces also said Saudi air defences had intercepted a cruise missile in the vicinity of King Khalid International Airport. They later added that a drone had been intercepted and destroyed in the ⁠country's Eastern ​Province.

The strikes have exposed vulnerabilities in Saudi defence capabilities as the kingdom wages an air campaign against the Houthis, who are fighting a ground war in Yemen against the Saudi-backed Yemeni government.

India has condemned attacks on two commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz region, with two Indian seafarers reported missing after one of the ships was struck by a drone on Sunday.

In a statement on October 11, India’s Ministry of External Affairs said the vessel MT Petro Dolphin was reportedly hit by a drone, with two of the 11 Indian crew members on board missing.

Another vessel, the Marshall Islands-flagged MT Valthera, was struck by an unidentified projectile, triggering a fire on board. All 11 Indian seafarers on the tanker were reported safe, the ministry said

Three Indians injured in the attack at Riyadh airport are in intensive care but stable, the Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia said.

Two more injured Indian nationals have been admitted to regular hospital wards, while the remaining patients have been discharged, the embassy said.

Embassy officials have visited all hospitals where Indian nationals injured in the attack have been admitted.

The embassy earlier confirmed that one Indian was killed.

The Indian national killed in the attack in Riyadh has been identified as Yousuf Sahab, a resident of Hyderabad, according to Asaduddin Owaisi, president of the All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) and Hyderabad MP.

In an update shared on social media, Owaisi said one of Yousuf’s sons was undergoing knee surgery, while another was hospitalised after losing three toes in the attack. Yousuf’s wife and daughter were safe, Owaisi said, adding that the family’s aunt had sustained head injuries but was out of danger.

Owaisi said he was in contact with Yousuf’s brother-in-law in Riyadh and that India’s Deputy Chief of Mission had assured him that assistance was being provided to the family.

Two Indian sailors were missing after a commercial vessel was hit by a "drone attack" Sunday off the coast of Oman, New Delhi's shipping minister said.

Shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal said the tanker MT Petro Dolphin, with 11 Indian seafarers on board, was attacked at the anchorage area for the port of Sohar in northern Oman.

"While nine of our Indian crew members have been successfully rescued and are safe, two Indian nationals currently remain missing," he said on X.

Sonowal said search and rescue operations by local authorities was underway.

Saudi Arabia’s civil aviation authority says one person has been killed and 11 others injured in Sunday’s attack on Riyadh’s King Khalid International airport.

The authority identified the person killed as a Pakistani national.

“The ⁠attack resulted ⁠in material ⁠damage that is currently being assessed,” it said in a statement.

Saudi authorities earlier said two passenger terminals were struck by a projectile that caused a fire.
