body_text:
The US and its regional allies are deploying the “largest air-defence umbrella in the world” to deter Iranian attacks, US Central Command chief Adm Brad Cooper said, describing the effort as part of an “enduring security architecture” in the Middle East.

The senior US commander was speaking in a recorded message at Trends Global's sixth annual conference in Abu Dhabi on Monday, days after a Houthi attack on Riyadh’s main airport killed 13 people and wounded more than 300 others.

Adm Cooper said the combined missile defence effort throughout the Iran war, which once seemed a “distant goal”, was now “military partnership in action”.

“It was a vision we discussed with our regional allies and partners,” he told the audience at the Ritz-Carlton. “Earlier this year, during Operation Epic Fury, we validated at full scale and in actual combat the Middle East Air Defence network known as Mead.

“Through our combined efforts, we transformed a concept into the most sophisticated and largest air-defence umbrella in the world,” he added.

“For the first time in history, US air defenders stood shoulder-to-shoulder with allies and partners across the Middle East, linking national systems in real time. And so together we intercepted thousands of Iranian attack drones and missiles with an integrated shield built on mutual trust. This is partnership in action.”

Military partnerships between the US and its regional allies were key to achieving sustainable security in the Middle East, said the Centcom chief.

“Sustainable security is not the absence of conflict. It is having robust systems, partnerships and interoperability in shared leadership firmly in place to manage threats before they escalate into a crisis,” he said.

Adm Cooper said the US forged military partnerships through “training, working shoulder-to-shoulder and operating alongside regional partners because we're stronger together and sustainable security requires strength”.

“Modern threats like advanced missiles and drones, as well as attacks from space and cyber, don't respect geographic boundaries or national borders, meaning no nation alone can counter these threats effectively,” he added.

While the US positions itself as a pillar of the Middle East's security architecture, Iran is facing growing isolation, said Mike Waltz, US ambassador to the UN.

“Iran wanted a ring of fire around Israel and instead it sealed its own fate,” Mr Waltz said at Trends in a recorded message. Countries in the Middle East such as Lebanon, Iraq and Syria “refuse to ever again be treated like Tehran's pawns on an Iranian chessboard”.

The US officials' remarks come amid growing signs that Tehran and Washington are bracing for a renewed confrontation after weeks of fragile calm.

The Iran war, which erupted in late February, has engulfed the Middle East for almost eight months, with no immediate end in sight.

Iran and the US have exchanged proposals in recent weeks aimed at ending the conflict and reopening the Strait of Hormuz. However, President Donald Trump rejected Tehran's latest offer and warned military operations could intensify after the US midterm elections.

The conflict's regional spillover has also widened, with the latest escalation between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen adding to mounting instability across the Middle East.

Mr Trump said this week he was considering joining Saudi Arabia in retaliating against the Houthis following deadly attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, despite initially declining Saudi requests for military intervention, according to reports.

When asked whether the Houthi strike on Riyadh's airport would change his previous decision not to attack Iran until after the midterms, Mr Trump said: “Well, we're going to take a look.”

The situation reflects the US administration’s reluctance to open another front, as efforts to end the Iran war prove elusive and the Strait of Hormuz crisis persists. Yet the appetite for war appears to be growing on both sides.

The head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, Mohsen Rezaei, said Tehran was no longer responding to the US amid stalled negotiations, describing Washington's response to its proposals as “insufficient”.

Meanwhile, Mike Pompeo, former CIA director and US secretary of state, said the only solution was to “crush the Iranian regime … there is no solution short of that.

“We could not all be foolish to think that the regime in Iran is going to comply with any agreement,” he said at the Abu Dhabi event.

analysis.framing: The article frames the event around US and allied military strength and partnership, presenting American and allied officials' claims largely through direct quotation while giving Iran's position only brief, secondhand treatment.

loaded_language.quote: Iran wanted a ring of fire around Israel and instead it sealed its own fate
loaded_language.explanation: A vivid, metaphorical and deterministic claim attributed to a US official, presented without challenge or context, casting Iran's outcome as self-inflicted and inevitable.
loaded_language.neutral_alternative: A US official said Iran's regional strategy had backfired and left it more isolated.

loaded_language.quote: refuse to ever again be treated like Tehran's pawns on an Iranian chessboard
loaded_language.explanation: Emotionally charged metaphor framing regional states as victims of Iranian manipulation, quoted without attribution to independent sources.
loaded_language.neutral_alternative: Countries such as Lebanon, Iraq and Syria have distanced themselves from Iranian influence, according to the US ambassador.

loaded_language.quote: the most sophisticated and largest air-defence umbrella in the world
loaded_language.explanation: Superlative promotional phrasing taken directly from the US commander's remarks and used in the headline, amplifying the claim without independent verification.
loaded_language.neutral_alternative: A large integrated air-defence network, according to the Centcom chief.

loaded_language.quote: the appetite for war appears to be growing on both sides
loaded_language.explanation: Vague, editorializing characterization of an unquantified dynamic, presented as the article's own assessment rather than attributed analysis.
loaded_language.neutral_alternative: Both sides have signaled possible further military action.

loaded_language.explanation: Violent, emotive verb quoted from a former US official without counterbalancing voices or context.
loaded_language.neutral_alternative: Former US secretary of state Mike Pompeo said he saw no solution other than ending the Iranian government.

omissions: Iranian official statements beyond Mohsen Rezaei's brief remark, such as responses to the air-defence claims
Independent verification or expert assessment of the 'largest air-defence umbrella' claim
Casualty or humanitarian details from the broader Iran war beyond the Riyadh airport attack figures
Context on the Strait of Hormuz crisis and its impact on global shipping or energy markets
Reactions from regional governments other than the US and Saudi Arabia

headline: 13 comedy shows coming to Abu Dhabi, from Russell Peters to Whitney Cummings
summary: Sunday was the first day of Abu Dhabi Comedy Season, as Morgan Jay made a stop in the capital as part of his The Goofy Guy Tour. Bringing his TikTok on-screen humour to the stage at Etihad Arena, he set the standard for a season of comedy still to come. Russell Peters, Mo Amer, Maz Jobrani and Whitney Cummings are among the performers heading to the capital between October and January.The programme offers a mix of international stars and regional favourites, from the storytelling of Scottish comedian Kevin Bridges to the political satire of Maz Jobrani and the improvisational humour of Egyptian performer Mina Nader.Most shows will take place at Etihad Arena in Yas Island as part of the third Abu Dhabi Comedy Season, which has previously welcomed Dave Chappelle, Kevin Hart, Trevor Noah and Bill Burr. Smaller venues are also getting involved, including The Club, which will host a special anniversary programme of The Laughter Factory.Here are the comedy performances announced for Abu Dhabi between October and February.1. Russell Peters: October 25 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiLong before social media became an essential tool for comedians, Russell Peters was attracting millions of viewers through clips of his stand-up routines. The Canadian, whose parents emigrated from India, became internationally recognised for his observations about immigrant families, accents and misunderstandings between cultures. His specials include Outsourced; Red, White and Brown; and Deported. Audience interaction remains central to his performances, with Peters frequently turning conversations with spectators into some of the evening's biggest laughs.Tickets from Dh275 ($75)2. Mo Amer: November 6 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiPalestinian-American comedian Mo Amer has taken his experiences of displacement and immigration from the comedy stage to television. Born in Kuwait to Palestinian parents and raised in Houston, Amer created the semi-autobiographical Netflix series Mo with Ramy Youssef. The series won a Peabody Award in 2023 and concluded with its second season in 2025. His stand-up similarly draws on questions of belonging, family and identity, subjects he approaches through humour informed by his experiences of navigating different cultures.Tickets from Dh3253. Maz Jobrani: November 7 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiWhen the Axis of Evil Comedy Tour emerged in the 2000s, it offered American audiences a different perspective on the Middle East at a time when regional identities were frequently reduced to political stereotypes. Iranian-American comedian Maz Jobrani was among its founding performers, using humour to challenge assumptions about Arabs and Iranians. He has since built an international career spanning television, film and stand-up specials, with politics, parenting and contemporary society continuing to provide material. He appeared at the inaugural Abu Dhabi Comedy Week in 2024.Tickets from Dh2754. The Laughter Factory: November 8 at The Club, Abu DhabiThe UAE's stand-up scene looked considerably different when The Laughter Factory was launched in Dubai in 1996. International comedy clubs were uncommon and arena-sized performances by visiting comedians had yet to become regular fixtures. Three decades later, the organisation is celebrating its 30th anniversary with a UAE tour that includes Abu Dhabi. 30 Years of Laughs continues its tradition of bringing established and emerging comedians to smaller venues, offering the intimacy and spontaneity of a traditional comedy-club evening.The show starts at 7pm; tickets from Dh1405. Amine Radi: November 19 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiMoroccan comedian Amine Radi brings a distinctly North African flavour to Abu Dhabi's comedy programme. His performance moves between French and Arabic, drawing on the humour of everyday exchanges, social expectations and the complications of modern relationships. Radi has developed an audience across the francophone world through performances built around animated delivery and increasingly elaborate stories. His appearance will also be phone-free, with electronic devices secured in pouches during the performance, keeping the focus firmly on the stage.Tickets from Dh1506. Anubhav Singh Bassi: November 21 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiA seemingly ordinary anecdote can become an elaborate comic adventure in the hands of Indian stand-up performer Anubhav Singh Bassi. His relaxed delivery gives stories room to develop, with friendships, student life and questionable youthful decisions supplying much of his material. Bassi's performances have attracted millions of views online, introducing his Hindi-language humour to audiences beyond India. His latest show, Kisi Ko Batana Mat, meaning Don't Tell Anyone, continues this approach, finding absurdity in situations that often begin innocently enough.The show starts at 6pm; tickets from Dh1257. Aries Spears: November 21 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiFew comedians can switch between famous impersonating personalities as convincingly as Aries Spears. The American performer spent eight seasons on the sketch comedy programme Mad TV, where his impressions of entertainers and public figures helped establish his reputation. Michael Jackson, Eddie Murphy and Shaquille O'Neal are among the celebrities he has imitated. Beyond impersonations, Spears has developed a more confrontational approach to stand-up, exploring race, entertainment and American social attitudes. His Abu Dhabi performance offers a mixture of observational humour and the character work that made him famous.The show starts at 10pm; tickets start at Dh1208. Jose Manalo and Wally Bayola: November 22 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiGenerations of Filipino television viewers will recognise Jose Manalo and Wally Bayola from the long-running variety programme Eat Bulaga!. The comedy partners are particularly known for their sketches, recurring characters and ability to improvise around the unexpected. Their Abu Dhabi production, The Ultimate Dabarkads Comedy, brings that chemistry to the stage through sketches, live music and audience participation. Presented in Tagalog and English, the afternoon show is also among the few family-friendly performances in the comedy calendar, with no minimum age restriction.Tickets from Dh999. NEMR: November 22 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiLebanese-American comedian NEMR brings his Rampant Disorder show to Abu Dhabi as part of the Wagef stand-up comedy road tour, presented by MBC Group. Having grown up between Lebanon and the US, he has frequently drawn on the contradictions of those experiences, particularly the expectations placed on young people by their families and communities. His latest production takes a wider look at relationships, culture and the disorder of modern life, delivered through the energetic storytelling that has helped him attract audiences across the Middle East and internationally.Tickets from Dh15010. Mina Nader: November 22 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiNo two Mina Nader performances are quite alike. The Egyptian comedian builds much of his Arabic-language stand-up around conversations with spectators, transforming unexpected answers and personal anecdotes into improvised material. With more than 16 years of experience, Nader has performed across the Middle East, Europe and North America. Organisers credit him with more than 500 sold-out shows, a reflection of the following he has developed through his interactive approach. His Abu Dhabi appearance continues that format, with the audience helping shape the evening's direction.Doors open at 8pm; tickets start from Dh19511. Kevin Bridges: January 9 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiScottish comedian Kevin Bridges has a talent for extracting humour from the ordinary frustrations of life. Growing up in Clydebank, near Glasgow, provided much of the inspiration for his early routines, which examine working-class experiences and the peculiarities of everyday behaviour. His distinctive Glaswegian delivery has become part of his appeal, helping him build a substantial following across Britain and internationally. Bridges has also written two books, including his autobiography We Need to Talk About … Kevin Bridges, documenting his journey from aspiring comedian to arena headliner.The show starts at 8pm; tickets from Dh29512. Whitney Cummings: January 31 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiCreating one successful American sitcom is difficult enough, but Whitney Cummings helped launch two during the same television season. In 2011, she created and starred in NBC's Whitney while also co-creating the CBS comedy 2 Broke Girls. She has since continued working across television, stand-up and podcasting, hosting Good For You and releasing several comedy specials. Her routines frequently examine relationships, gender expectations and contemporary social habits. Her Big Baby tour brings her to the UAE for the first time.Show starts at 6pm; tickets from Dh21513. Paul Smith: January 31 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiLiverpudlian comedian Paul Smith has found international success by making the audience a central part of his performances. Clips filmed at the city's Hot Water Comedy Club have attracted millions of views, largely because of his ability to build jokes around unpredictable exchanges with spectators. His latest show, HAPPY, combines that spontaneous approach with stories about finding humour in the frustrations and complications of daily life. The performance also marks his first appearance at Etihad Arena, closing January's comedy line-up with an emphasis on improvisation.The show starts at 9.30pm; tickets from Dh275

When the Axis of Evil Comedy Tour emerged in the 2000s, it offered American audiences a different perspective on the Middle East at a time when regional identities were frequently reduced to political stereotypes. Iranian-American comedian Maz Jobrani was among its founding performers, using humour to challenge assumptions about Arabs and Iranians. He has since built an international career spanning television, film and stand-up specials, with politics, parenting and contemporary society continuing to provide material. He appeared at the inaugural Abu Dhabi Comedy Week in 2024.

The UAE's stand-up scene looked considerably different when The Laughter Factory was launched in Dubai in 1996. International comedy clubs were uncommon and arena-sized performances by visiting comedians had yet to become regular fixtures. Three decades later, the organisation is celebrating its 30th anniversary with a UAE tour that includes Abu Dhabi. 30 Years of Laughs continues its tradition of bringing established and emerging comedians to smaller venues, offering the intimacy and spontaneity of a traditional comedy-club evening.

The show starts at 7pm; tickets from Dh140

Moroccan comedian Amine Radi brings a distinctly North African flavour to Abu Dhabi's comedy programme. His performance moves between French and Arabic, drawing on the humour of everyday exchanges, social expectations and the complications of modern relationships. Radi has developed an audience across the francophone world through performances built around animated delivery and increasingly elaborate stories. His appearance will also be phone-free, with electronic devices secured in pouches during the performance, keeping the focus firmly on the stage.

A seemingly ordinary anecdote can become an elaborate comic adventure in the hands of Indian stand-up performer Anubhav Singh Bassi. His relaxed delivery gives stories room to develop, with friendships, student life and questionable youthful decisions supplying much of his material. Bassi's performances have attracted millions of views online, introducing his Hindi-language humour to audiences beyond India. His latest show, Kisi Ko Batana Mat, meaning Don't Tell Anyone, continues this approach, finding absurdity in situations that often begin innocently enough.

The show starts at 6pm; tickets from Dh125

Few comedians can switch between famous impersonating personalities as convincingly as Aries Spears. The American performer spent eight seasons on the sketch comedy programme Mad TV, where his impressions of entertainers and public figures helped establish his reputation. Michael Jackson, Eddie Murphy and Shaquille O'Neal are among the celebrities he has imitated. Beyond impersonations, Spears has developed a more confrontational approach to stand-up, exploring race, entertainment and American social attitudes. His Abu Dhabi performance offers a mixture of observational humour and the character work that made him famous.

The show starts at 10pm; tickets start at Dh120

Generations of Filipino television viewers will recognise Jose Manalo and Wally Bayola from the long-running variety programme Eat Bulaga!. The comedy partners are particularly known for their sketches, recurring characters and ability to improvise around the unexpected. Their Abu Dhabi production, The Ultimate Dabarkads Comedy, brings that chemistry to the stage through sketches, live music and audience participation. Presented in Tagalog and English, the afternoon show is also among the few family-friendly performances in the comedy calendar, with no minimum age restriction.

Lebanese-American comedian NEMR brings his Rampant Disorder show to Abu Dhabi as part of the Wagef stand-up comedy road tour, presented by MBC Group. Having grown up between Lebanon and the US, he has frequently drawn on the contradictions of those experiences, particularly the expectations placed on young people by their families and communities. His latest production takes a wider look at relationships, culture and the disorder of modern life, delivered through the energetic storytelling that has helped him attract audiences across the Middle East and internationally.

No two Mina Nader performances are quite alike. The Egyptian comedian builds much of his Arabic-language stand-up around conversations with spectators, transforming unexpected answers and personal anecdotes into improvised material. With more than 16 years of experience, Nader has performed across the Middle East, Europe and North America. Organisers credit him with more than 500 sold-out shows, a reflection of the following he has developed through his interactive approach. His Abu Dhabi appearance continues that format, with the audience helping shape the evening's direction.

Doors open at 8pm; tickets start from Dh195

Scottish comedian Kevin Bridges has a talent for extracting humour from the ordinary frustrations of life. Growing up in Clydebank, near Glasgow, provided much of the inspiration for his early routines, which examine working-class experiences and the peculiarities of everyday behaviour. His distinctive Glaswegian delivery has become part of his appeal, helping him build a substantial following across Britain and internationally. Bridges has also written two books, including his autobiography We Need to Talk About … Kevin Bridges, documenting his journey from aspiring comedian to arena headliner.

The show starts at 8pm; tickets from Dh295

Creating one successful American sitcom is difficult enough, but Whitney Cummings helped launch two during the same television season. In 2011, she created and starred in NBC's Whitney while also co-creating the CBS comedy 2 Broke Girls. She has since continued working across television, stand-up and podcasting, hosting Good For You and releasing several comedy specials. Her routines frequently examine relationships, gender expectations and contemporary social habits. Her Big Baby tour brings her to the UAE for the first time.

Show starts at 6pm; tickets from Dh215

Liverpudlian comedian Paul Smith has found international success by making the audience a central part of his performances. Clips filmed at the city's Hot Water Comedy Club have attracted millions of views, largely because of his ability to build jokes around unpredictable exchanges with spectators. His latest show, HAPPY, combines that spontaneous approach with stories about finding humour in the frustrations and complications of daily life. The performance also marks his first appearance at Etihad Arena, closing January's comedy line-up with an emphasis on improvisation.

The show starts at 9.30pm; tickets from Dh275

body_text:
Pakistan completed a T20 series win against Sri Lanka on Sunday, securing an 82-run victory in the second match of the three-game series in Rawalpindi.

New captain and opener Sahibzada Farhan hit a quick 73, his second straight fifty, and young middle order bat Maaz Sadaqat smashed 96 from 51 balls to help Pakistan post 215-3. Sri Lanka batters did not even come close, restricted to 133-7.

On paper, it is a routine result in a bilateral series well away from a T20 World Cup cycle. But for Pakistan, it was a significant milestone.

Pakistan's Babar and Zaman are poor relations as millions spent at ILT20 auction

Pakistan have tried to hit the reset button in white-ball cricket for quite some time. After successive misses at ICC tournaments and a growing trend of failing to even qualify for the semi-finals, the team needed a fresh set of eyes to look at the issue.

In 2026, they have started to get more things right than wrong.

If you look at the bigger picture, Pakistan did not win any major titles – either the T20 World Cup or Asian Games.

However, they lost just four out of 15 completed matches this year and two of those losses were against double world champions India, including in the Asian Games gold medal match.

Pakistan thrashed Australia 3-0 at home ahead of the T20 World Cup and were largely competitive in the main tournament, losing to India and England (by 2 wickets).

So what has changed? For starters, Pakistan are putting more faith in T20 specialists. Farhan – top scorer at the T20 World Cup and ranked third in the world among T20 batters – was named captain for the ongoing Sri Lanka series.

There was no space for tried and tested fast-bowler Shaheen Afridi or all-rounder Salman Agha. Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan are almost certainly out of the T20 scheme of things for good.

The selectors and team management have backed players who live and breathe the 20-over format.

Hasan Nawaz is one such name and almost snatched the T20 Asian Games gold medal from India’s grasp with a destructive 96 in the final.

Left-arm fast bowler Salman Mirza has played more T20Is than first-class matches and should get an extended run, albeit at the age of 32, now that Pakistan seem to have had enough Afridi the T20 bowler. Mirza picked up 2-28 from three overs against Sri Lanka on Sunday.

There are many more waiting in the wings. There always have been. It was just that some players were turned into multi-format players for the sake of it, which took away precious spots in the T20 side which could have easily gone to specialists.

One can sense change in the air. Captain Farhan made it clear what he wants from his team, especially the batters.

“We have been a different T20 side in 2026 as our six-hitting ratio has improved and our batters are scoring at more than 150 [strike rate]. If we continue this way, we will end up scoring more than 200 every time,” the opener said after the Sri Lanka series win.

That is a significant statement because it is the only way successful teams operate. And also because those words came from a player who is a genuine trend setter in the country.

Farhan is one among only five batters to hits four T20 centuries in one year. Also, Farhan is the first Pakistan batter to hit a six against India’s Jasprit Bumrah – after a staggering 400 deliveries bowled by the Indian ace.

That alone broke the shackles that had gripped the minds of many Pakistan players and supporters after successive defeats against their neighbours at ICC events.

India still obviously hold the upper hand but Pakistan are beginning to believe that the gap with the world champions and other leading T20 teams is probably not as vast as it was a couple of seasons back.

headline: Closure of Riyadh airport extended after deadly Houthi strikes
summary: By Gianluca Lo NostroOct 12 (Reuters) - Saudi authorities said on Monday they were extending the suspension of operations at the international airport in the capital, Riyadh, after deadly weekend attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis. Operations at King Khalid International Airport, Saudi Arabia's second-busiest airport after Jeddah, were suspended to "allow for the completion of procedures to ensure the safety and operational readiness of the airport's facilities", the Saudi civil aviation authority said in a statement.
body_text:
By Gianluca Lo Nostro

Oct 12 (Reuters) - Saudi authorities said on Monday they were extending the suspension of operations at the international airport in the capital, Riyadh, after deadly weekend attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis.

Operations at King Khalid International Airport, Saudi Arabia's second-busiest airport after Jeddah, were suspended to "allow for the completion of procedures to ensure the safety and operational readiness of the airport's facilities", the Saudi civil aviation authority said in a statement.

The airport has been shut since an attack on Saturday that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade. On Sunday, another attack killed one person and injured nearly a dozen others.

The attacks marked one of the most significant disruptions to Saudi aviation in years, adding to pressures on an industry already grappling with conflict across the Middle East.

The airport cancelled 99.7% of all scheduled flights on Sunday, according to aviation analytics firm Cirium. An air traffic tracker from Flightradar24 showed no planes over the city.

The disruption has forced airlines across Europe and Asia to suspend services, while the Federal Aviation Administration advised US carriers on Sunday to exercise caution when flying to or over Saudi Arabia.

Lufthansa Group has cancelled all flights to Riyadh until October 16, while Air France-KLM has extended a previous suspension of services to and from the Saudi capital until the end of the month.

Abu Dhabi’s Etihad Airways was among the airlines that further extended Saudi flight cancellations, affecting around 20 flights to Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam on Monday and Tuesday.

The escalation with the Houthis has raised concerns over the broader economic impact. Saudi Arabia's real GDP is projected to contract by 3.6% this year, reflecting a combination of factors including lower oil activity.

The attacks have put events scheduled in Riyadh this month under pressure, including the kingdom's flagship investment conference and the WPC Energy Congress, where several top oil executives were dropped from the programme.

(Reporting by Joanna Plucinska in London, Gianluca Lo Nostro in Gdansk, Federico Maccioni in Dubai and Menna Alaa El Din in Cairo; Editing by Matt Scuffham, Aidan Lewis)

By Gianluca Lo Nostro and Menna AlaaElDin

Oct 12 (Reuters) - The skies over the Saudi capital Riyadh were virtually empty on Monday as authorities extended the suspension of operations at the city's international airport after deadly weekend attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis.

The airport cancelled 99.7% of all scheduled flights on Sunday, according to aviation analytics firm Cirium. An air traffic tracker from Flightradar24 showed planes avoiding the city on Monday, though jets were crossing Saudi airspace and landing at top hub Jeddah on the country's west coast.

The disruption has forced airlines across Europe and Asia to suspend services, while the Federal Aviation Administration advised US carriers on Sunday to exercise caution when flying to or over Saudi Arabia. EU aviation body EASA widened a Saudi airspace warning on Friday, citing missile and drone attacks.

Lufthansa Group has cancelled all flights to Riyadh until October 16, while Air France-KLM has extended a previous suspension of services to and from the Saudi capital until the end of the month.

Abu Dhabi's Etihad Airways was among the airlines that further extended Saudi flight cancellations, affecting around 20 flights to Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam on Monday and Tuesday.

The escalation with the Houthis has raised concerns over the broader economic impact. Saudi Arabia's real GDP is projected to contract by 3.6% this year, reflecting a combination of factors including lower oil activity.

The attacks have put events scheduled in Riyadh this month under pressure, including the kingdom's flagship investment conference and the WPC Energy Congress, where several top oil executives were dropped from the programme.

headline: Americans Hall, Woodford win Nobel prize for work on stabilising economies
summary: By Simon Johnson and Johan AhlanderSTOCKHOLM, Oct 12 (Reuters) - US academics Robert Hall and Michael Woodford won the 2026 Nobel economics prize on Monday for decades of work developing ground-up models currently used by central banks and finance ministries across the world to stabilise economies."With them, we are better equipped to deal with shocks in the economy, such as energy crises or sudden changes in how much households consume," John Hassler, Chair of the Committee for the Prize in Economic Sciences, said in a statement.
body_text:
By Simon Johnson and Johan Ahlander

STOCKHOLM, Oct 12 (Reuters) - US academics Robert Hall and Michael Woodford won the 2026 Nobel economics prize on Monday for decades of work developing ground-up models currently used by central banks and finance ministries across the world to stabilise economies.

"With them, we are better equipped to deal with shocks in the economy, such as energy crises or sudden changes in how much households consume," John Hassler, Chair of the Committee for the Prize in Economic Sciences, said in a statement.

The prestigious award, formally known as the Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel, is the final prize to be given out this year and is worth 12 million Swedish crowns ($1.2 million).

One of the laureates' key insights is that economies could only be kept on an even keel by taking into account the millions of decisions made at a micro-level by households and businesses, rather than by using top-down theories of how economies work.

"...Authorities shouldn't view stabilization of the economy as an exercise that is simply conducted by people pulling levers to control the economy independently of what people in the economy understand about this," Columbia University's Woodford, 70, told a news conference.

In contrast to the oil shocks of the 1970s, when central banks struggled to combat sky-high inflation, Woodford said the new framework was useful during the global financial crisis of the late-2000s to bolster traditional tools of monetary policy.

"Making more explicit statements about the likely future path of interest rate policy, as opposed to relying on simply being able to cut interest rates further immediately, that was an important part of the policy response in the years from 2009 onward," he said.

Beyond so-called "forward guidance" on the future path of monetary policy, the work of Woodford and Hall, 83, at Stanford University promoted other concepts used today such as the idea of "sticky" inflation when price changes lag changes in demand.

Another is the "output gap", a measure of demand pressure building up in an economy and how efficiently resources are being used - the goal of stabilisation policy being to steer that gap towards zero.

The economics prize, first awarded in 1969, is not one of the original five awards created in the 1895 will of industrialist and dynamite inventor Alfred Nobel, but was established by Sweden's central bank.

The majority of previous laureates have been from the United States. Only three women have ever won, most recently Claudia Goldin in 2023 for work on how gender has affected pay and employment over time in the United States.

Analysis by the Institute for Scientific Information, part of Clarivate, had picked researchers working on monetary policy, the economics of information technology and evolutionary economic theory as possible recipients.

Last year's winners, Joel Mokyr, Philippe Aghion and Peter Howitt, won for work on "creative destruction" and how new technology and production methods can boost growth and living standards.

The Nobel prizes for medicine, physics, chemistry, literature and peace were announced last week.

($1 = 10.0028 Swedish crowns)

(Reporting by Simon Johnson, Niklas Pollard, Johan Ahlander and Marie Mannes in Stockholm, Terje Solsvik in Oslo, Mark John in London; Editing by Alex Richardson and Toby Chopra)

By Simon Johnson and Johan Ahlander

STOCKHOLM, Oct 12 (Reuters) - US academics Robert Hall and Michael Woodford won the 2026 Nobel economics prize on Monday for decades of work developing ground-up models currently used by central banks and finance ministries across the world to stabilise economies.

"With them, we are better equipped to deal with shocks in the economy, such as energy crises or sudden changes in how much households consume," John Hassler, Chair of the Committee for the Prize in Economic Sciences, said in a statement.

Woodford and Hall are frequently name-checked by the world's top central banks which, after a 2022 inflation surge in the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic, are currently grappling with the energy shock triggered by the Iran war.

One of the laureates' key insights is that economies could only be kept on an even keel by taking into account the millions of decisions made at a micro-level by households and businesses, rather than by using top-down theories of how economies work.

"...Authorities shouldn't view stabilization of the economy as an exercise that is simply conducted by people pulling levers to control the economy independently of what people in the economy understand about this," Columbia University's Woodford, 70, told a news conference.

Beyond so-called "forward guidance" on the future path of monetary policy, the work of Woodford — and Hall, 83, at Stanford University — promoted other concepts used today such as the idea of "sticky" inflation when price changes lag changes in demand.

Another is the "output gap", a measure of demand pressure building up in an economy and how efficiently resources are being used - the goal of stabilisation policy being to steer that gap towards zero.

CORE CENTRAL BANK CONCEPTS

Hall has served as adviser to the US Treasury Department, the Justice Department and the Federal Reserve Board.

His insight in a 1978 paper that household decisions on consumption are a perfect indicator of their expectations was used by Woodford in a model on how consumption is determined.

Woodford also showed that central banks can stimulate or suppress economic activity by adjusting interest rates, rather than just by the amount of money in circulation.

Such concepts remain core to central banking today. Forward guidance became especially important after the 2008 financial crisis, when rates were near zero or even negative and standard monetary policy seemed to be out of ammunition.

Now, however, some are questioning how relevant it is given the amount of uncertainty in the global economy - with new US Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh a notable sceptic.

The economics prize, formally known as the Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel, is the final award to be given out this year and is worth 12 million Swedish crowns ($1.2 million).

First awarded in 1969, it is not one of the original five awards created in the 1895 will of industrialist and dynamite inventor Alfred Nobel, but was established by Sweden's central bank.

The majority of previous laureates have been from the United States. Only three women have ever won, most recently Claudia Goldin in 2023 for work on how gender has affected pay and employment over time in the United States.

Last year's winners, Joel Mokyr, Philippe Aghion and Peter Howitt, won for work on "creative destruction" and how new technology and production methods can boost growth and living standards.

The Nobel prizes for medicine, physics, chemistry, literature and peace were announced last week.

($1 = 10.0028 Swedish crowns)

(Reporting by Simon Johnson, Niklas Pollard, Johan Ahlander and Marie Mannes in Stockholm, Terje Solsvik in Oslo, Mark John in London; Editing by Alex Richardson and Toby Chopra)

headline: Russian troops liberate two communities in Ukraine operation over past day — top brass
summary: Russia's Battlegroup Center units took control over the settlement of Lidino in the DPR and Battlegroup East units - over the settlement of Nikolskoye in the Zaporozhye Region
body_text:
MOSCOW, October 12. /TASS/. Russian troops liberated two communities in the Donetsk People’s Republic and the Zaporozhye Region over the past 24 hours in the special military operation in Ukraine, Russia’s Defense Ministry reported.

"Battlegroup Center units liberated the settlement of Lidino in the Donetsk People’s Republic through active operations. <…> Battlegroup East units kept advancing deep into the enemy’s defenses and liberated the settlement of Nikolskoye in the Zaporozhye Region," the ministry said in a statement.

The Ukrainian army lost roughly 1,355 troops in battles with Russian forces in all the frontline areas over the past 24 hours, according to the latest data on the special military operation in Ukraine released by Russia’s Defense Ministry.

The latest figures show that the Ukrainian army lost over 295 troops, an armored personnel carrier and two armored combat vehicles in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup North, roughly 220 troops and two armored combat vehicles in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup West and about 195 troops and an armored combat vehicle in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup South.

During the last 24-hour period, the Ukrainian army also lost roughly 330 troops and four armored combat vehicles in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup Center, over 275 troops and an armored combat vehicle in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup East and more than 40 troops and an armored combat vehicle in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup Dnepr, the latest figures show.

Russia’s Battlegroup North forces are fighting for the liberation of four communities in the Kharkov Region and tightening the ring of encirclement of Ukrainian troops in that area, the ministry reported.

"Battlegroup North units are tightening the ring of encirclement in the Kharkov Region and expanding the outer area of control. In the pocket of encirclement, they are fighting for the liberation of the communities of Nikolayevka, Varvarovka, Nefyodovka and Chyornoye in the Kharkov Region," the ministry said.

During the last 24-hour period, the Ukrainian army lost over 55 troops, a motor vehicle and five ground robotic platforms in the pocket of encirclement, it specified.

Battlegroup North forces are expanding the outer area of control and continue battles for taking control of the settlements of Prikolotnoye, Kotovka and Gogino in the Kharkov Region, the ministry said.

Russia’s Battlegroup North forces inflicted more than 295 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed an enemy armored personnel carrier and two armored combat vehicles in its areas of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.

In the Kharkov direction, Battlegroup North units "inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of two mechanized brigades, a motorized infantry brigade, an assault regiment of the Ukrainian army and a territorial defense brigade in areas near the settlements of Svetlichnoye, Slatino, Martovoye, Shirokoye, Bugayevka and Veliky Burluk in the Kharkov Region," the ministry said.

In the Sumy direction, Battlegroup North units struck formations of two mechanized brigades of the Ukrainian army and three territorial defense brigades in areas near the settlements of Yuryevo, Barilovka, Radkovka, Velikaya Rybitsa and Olshanka in the Sumy Region, it said.

Overall, the Ukrainian army lost more than 295 personnel, an armored personnel carrier, two armored combat vehicles, eight motor vehicles and a field artillery gun in the areas of responsibility of Russia’s Battlegroup North over the past 24 hours, it specified.

Russia’s Battlegroup West inflicted roughly 220 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed two enemy armored combat vehicles in its area of responsibility over the past day, the ministry reported.

"Battlegroup West units improved their forward positions and inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of two mechanized brigades, an assault brigade of the Ukrainian army and a territorial defense brigade in areas near the settlements of Volchy Yar, Berezovka, Blagodatovka, Tamarganovka, Osinovo, Maleyevka and Grushevka in the Kharkov Region," the ministry said.

The Ukrainian army lost an estimated 220 personnel, two armored combat vehicles, nine motor vehicles and two electronic warfare stations in that frontline area over the past 24 hours, it said.

Russia’s Battlegroup South inflicted roughly 195 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed an enemy armored combat vehicle in its area of responsibility over the past day, the ministry reported.

"Battlegroup South units gained better lines and positions and inflicted losses on formations of two mechanized brigades, a mountain assault brigade, an unmanned systems brigade of the Ukrainian army and a marine infantry brigade in areas near the settlements of Yasnogorka, Belenkoye, Nikolayevka, Vasilevskaya Pustosh, Druzhkovka, Semyonovka, Kramatorsk and Slavyansk in the Donetsk People’s Republic," the ministry said.

The Ukrainian army lost an estimated 195 personnel, an armored combat vehicle, 23 motor vehicles, two artillery guns and an electronic warfare station in that frontline area over the past 24 hours, it specified.

Russia’s Battlegroup Center forces continue advancing in their battles for the liberation of Dobropolye in the Donetsk People’s Republic, the ministry reported.

"In Dobropolye in the Donetsk People’s Republic, assault groups of the 51st Army advanced in the town’s central and northwestern parts. Marine infantry formations continued mopping up western quarters of the town and the territory of the Dobropolskaya coalmine," the ministry said.

During the last 24-hour period, Battlegroup Center forces thwarted the Ukrainian army’s attempt using up to a platoon of personnel without armor to relieve the surrounded enemy troops, it said.

In the past 24 hours, Battlegroup Center units liberated 216 buildings, including four production structures and eliminated roughly 35 Ukrainian troops in Dobropolye, the ministry said.

Russia’s Battlegroup Center inflicted roughly 330 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed four enemy armored combat vehicles in its area of responsibility over the past day, the ministry reported.

During the last 24-hour period, Battlegroup Center units "inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of three mechanized brigades, a jaeger brigade, an airborne brigade of the Ukrainian army and three National Guard brigades in areas near the settlements of Staroraiskoye, Novoandreyevka, Maryevka, Novoyavlenka, Svyatogorovka, Belozerskoye and Vesyolaya Gora in the Donetsk People’s Republic, Andronovka and Tarasovka in the Dnepropetrovsk Region," the ministry said.

The Ukrainian army lost an estimated 330 personnel, four armored combat vehicles, eight motor vehicles, a field artillery gun, two electronic warfare stations and an electronic surveillance system in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup Center over the past 24 hours, it specified.

Russia’s Battlegroup East inflicted more than 275 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed an enemy armored combat vehicle in its area of responsibility over the past day, the ministry reported.

During the last 24-hour period, Battlegroup East units "inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of a mechanized brigade, two air assault brigades, an assault regiment of the Ukrainian army and a marine infantry brigade in areas near the settlements of Ivanovka, Podgavrilovka, Kolomiytsy, Orestopol and Skotovatoye in the Dnepropetrovsk Region, Vasinovka, Ternovka and Volnyanka in the Zaporozhye Region," the ministry said.

The Ukrainian army lost more than 275 personnel, an armored combat vehicle and 12 motor vehicles in that frontline area over the past 24 hours, it specified.

Russia’s Battlegroup Dnepr eliminated more than 40 Ukrainian troops and destroyed an enemy armored combat vehicle in its area of responsibility over the past day, the ministry reported.

"Battlegroup Dnepr units gained better lines and positions and inflicted losses on formations of a mechanized brigade, a mountain assault brigade and an assault regiment of the Ukrainian army in areas near the settlements of Orekhov, Kushugum, Zapasnoye and Preobrazhenka in the Zaporozhye Region," the ministry said.

"Over 40 Ukrainian military personnel, an armored combat vehicle, 19 motor vehicles and two electronic warfare stations were destroyed," it said.

Russian troops struck transport infrastructure used by the Ukrainian army and enemy deployment areas over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.

"Operational/tactical aircraft, attack unmanned aerial vehicles, missile troops and artillery of the Russian groups of forces struck transport infrastructure facilities used by the Ukrainian army, workshops producing unmanned aerial vehicles and their launch sites, and also temporary deployment areas of Ukrainian armed formations and foreign mercenaries in 149 locations," the ministry said.

Russian air defense forces intercepted and destroyed 646 Ukrainian unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and five smart bombs over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.

"Air defense capabilities shot down five guided aerial bombs and 646 fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles," the ministry said.

Overall, the Russian Armed Forces have destroyed 674 Ukrainian combat aircraft, 284 helicopters, 259,820 unmanned aerial vehicles, 672 surface-to-air missile systems, 31,202 tanks and other armored combat vehicles, 1,786 multiple rocket launchers, 36,701 field artillery guns and mortars and 74,309 special military motor vehicles since the start of the special military operation, the ministry reported.

headline: IN BRIEF: Kremlin remarks on 'energy truce,' US negotiators’ efforts
summary: Russia wants lasting peace in Ukraine and is ready to do everything necessary to achieve it, Dmitry Peskov pointed out
body_text:
MOSCOW, October 12. /TASS/. The possibility of an "energy truce," US negotiators’ efforts on Ukraine, and the Nord Stream sabotage investigation were the main topics of Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov’s briefing.

TASS has compiled the key statements by the Kremlin spokesman.

- The Kremlin cannot comment on the "energy truce" issue at this point: "Communication is ongoing. As soon as we have something to say on the issue, we will certainly inform you."

- Russia wants lasting peace in Ukraine and is ready to do everything necessary to achieve it: "The Kremlin has said repeatedly, and President [of Russia Vladimir] Putin has said so as well, along with officials at other levels: we want lasting peace, not a ceasefire, and we are ready to do everything possible to achieve it."

- Europe clearly does not belong to the "peace camp" seeking a settlement to the Ukrainian conflict; instead, it is part of the "war camp" that is doing everything it can to prolong the crisis: "The Europeans clearly do not belong to the ‘peace camp,’ which seeks a path to a peaceful settlement [of the conflict in Ukraine]. The Europeans are, rather, the ‘war camp,’ which continues to do everything it can to prevent this conflict from ending."

- Moscow welcomes the work of American negotiators on a peaceful settlement in Ukraine: "We are much more impressed by the efforts of American negotiators. We are grateful to them for pursuing those efforts."

- Russia is not seeking a split between the United States and Europe over the Ukraine conflict but a solution that could help pave the way toward a peaceful settlement: "We aren’t seeking a split here but we are looking for really effective measures and responsible solutions that will enable us to reach a peaceful settlement."

- The Kremlin expects the perpetrators and those behind the Nord Stream pipeline sabotage to be identified during the trial, which is set to begin on October 14: "We expect objectivity. We expect a verdict to be announced. We expect the perpetrators to be named, as well as those who ordered the attack. That would be very important."

- "I think no one has any doubt about who was actually behind it."

- Russian President Vladimir Putin and Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev did not discuss the case of 11 Russians detained by Azerbaijan last year during the CIS summit. The 11 Russians remain in detention in Azerbaijan, and Moscow continues to stay in touch with Baku on the issue: "This issue was not discussed at the highest level. However, we are in contact with our Azerbaijani friends on this matter as well."

- Russia genuinely hopes the issue will be resolved soon: "We sincerely hope that this problem, too, will be resolved soon."

headline: US and regional allies shielded by ‘world's largest air-defence umbrella’, says Centcom chief
summary: The US and its regional allies are deploying the “largest air-defence umbrella in the world” to deter Iranian attacks, US Central Command chief Adm Brad Cooper said, describing the effort as part of an “enduring security architecture” in the Middle East.The senior US commander was speaking in a recorded message at Trends Global's sixth annual conference in Abu Dhabi on Monday, days after a Houthi attack on Riyadh’s main airport killed 13 people and wounded more than 300 others.Adm Cooper said the combined missile defence effort throughout the Iran war, which once seemed a “distant goal”, was now “military partnership in action”.“It was a vision we discussed with our regional allies and partners,” he told the audience at the Ritz-Carlton. “Earlier this year, during Operation Epic Fury, we validated at full scale and in actual combat the Middle East Air Defence network known as Mead.“Through our combined efforts, we transformed a concept into the most sophisticated and largest air-defence umbrella in the world,” he added.“For the first time in history, US air defenders stood shoulder-to-shoulder with allies and partners across the Middle East, linking national systems in real time. And so together we intercepted thousands of Iranian attack drones and missiles with an integrated shield built on mutual trust. This is partnership in action.”Collective securityMilitary partnerships between the US and its regional allies were key to achieving sustainable security in the Middle East, said the Centcom chief.“Sustainable security is not the absence of conflict. body_text:
The US and its regional allies are deploying the “largest air-defence umbrella in the world” to deter Iranian attacks, US Central Command chief Adm Brad Cooper said, describing the effort as part of an “enduring security architecture” in the Middle East.

The senior US commander was speaking in a recorded message at Trends Global's sixth annual conference in Abu Dhabi on Monday, days after a Houthi attack on Riyadh’s main airport killed 13 people and wounded more than 300 others.

Adm Cooper said the combined missile defence effort throughout the Iran war, which once seemed a “distant goal”, was now “military partnership in action”.

“It was a vision we discussed with our regional allies and partners,” he told the audience at the Ritz-Carlton. “Earlier this year, during Operation Epic Fury, we validated at full scale and in actual combat the Middle East Air Defence network known as Mead.

“Through our combined efforts, we transformed a concept into the most sophisticated and largest air-defence umbrella in the world,” he added.

“For the first time in history, US air defenders stood shoulder-to-shoulder with allies and partners across the Middle East, linking national systems in real time. And so together we intercepted thousands of Iranian attack drones and missiles with an integrated shield built on mutual trust. This is partnership in action.”

Military partnerships between the US and its regional allies were key to achieving sustainable security in the Middle East, said the Centcom chief.

“Sustainable security is not the absence of conflict. It is having robust systems, partnerships and interoperability in shared leadership firmly in place to manage threats before they escalate into a crisis,” he said.

Adm Cooper said the US forged military partnerships through “training, working shoulder-to-shoulder and operating alongside regional partners because we're stronger together and sustainable security requires strength”.

“Modern threats like advanced missiles and drones, as well as attacks from space and cyber, don't respect geographic boundaries or national borders, meaning no nation alone can counter these threats effectively,” he added.

While the US positions itself as a pillar of the Middle East's security architecture, Iran is facing growing isolation, said Mike Waltz, US ambassador to the UN.

“Iran wanted a ring of fire around Israel and instead it sealed its own fate,” Mr Waltz said at Trends in a recorded message. Countries in the Middle East such as Lebanon, Iraq and Syria “refuse to ever again be treated like Tehran's pawns on an Iranian chessboard”.

The US officials' remarks come amid growing signs that Tehran and Washington are bracing for a renewed confrontation after weeks of fragile calm.

The Iran war, which erupted in late February, has engulfed the Middle East for almost eight months, with no immediate end in sight.

Iran and the US have exchanged proposals in recent weeks aimed at ending the conflict and reopening the Strait of Hormuz. However, President Donald Trump rejected Tehran's latest offer and warned military operations could intensify after the US midterm elections.

The conflict's regional spillover has also widened, with the latest escalation between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen adding to mounting instability across the Middle East.

Mr Trump said this week he was considering joining Saudi Arabia in retaliating against the Houthis following deadly attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, despite initially declining Saudi requests for military intervention, according to reports.

When asked whether the Houthi strike on Riyadh's airport would change his previous decision not to attack Iran until after the midterms, Mr Trump said: “Well, we're going to take a look.”

The situation reflects the US administration’s reluctance to open another front, as efforts to end the Iran war prove elusive and the Strait of Hormuz crisis persists. Yet the appetite for war appears to be growing on both sides.

The head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, Mohsen Rezaei, said Tehran was no longer responding to the US amid stalled negotiations, describing Washington's response to its proposals as “insufficient”.

Meanwhile, Mike Pompeo, former CIA director and US secretary of state, said the only solution was to “crush the Iranian regime … there is no solution short of that.

“We could not all be foolish to think that the regime in Iran is going to comply with any agreement,” he said at the Abu Dhabi event.

headline: 13 comedy shows coming to Abu Dhabi, from Russell Peters to Whitney Cummings
summary: Sunday was the first day of Abu Dhabi Comedy Season, as Morgan Jay made a stop in the capital as part of his The Goofy Guy Tour. Bringing his TikTok on-screen humour to the stage at Etihad Arena, he set the standard for a season of comedy still to come. Russell Peters, Mo Amer, Maz Jobrani and Whitney Cummings are among the performers heading to the capital between October and January.The programme offers a mix of international stars and regional favourites, from the storytelling of Scottish comedian Kevin Bridges to the political satire of Maz Jobrani and the improvisational humour of Egyptian performer Mina Nader.Most shows will take place at Etihad Arena in Yas Island as part of the third Abu Dhabi Comedy Season, which has previously welcomed Dave Chappelle, Kevin Hart, Trevor Noah and Bill Burr. Smaller venues are also getting involved, including The Club, which will host a special anniversary programme of The Laughter Factory.Here are the comedy performances announced for Abu Dhabi between October and February.1. Russell Peters: October 25 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiLong before social media became an essential tool for comedians, Russell Peters was attracting millions of viewers through clips of his stand-up routines. The Canadian, whose parents emigrated from India, became internationally recognised for his observations about immigrant families, accents and misunderstandings between cultures. His specials include Outsourced; Red, White and Brown; and Deported. Audience interaction remains central to his performances, with Peters frequently turning conversations with spectators into some of the evening's biggest laughs.Tickets from Dh275 ($75)2. Mo Amer: November 6 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiPalestinian-American comedian Mo Amer has taken his experiences of displacement and immigration from the comedy stage to television. Born in Kuwait to Palestinian parents and raised in Houston, Amer created the semi-autobiographical Netflix series Mo with Ramy Youssef. The series won a Peabody Award in 2023 and concluded with its second season in 2025. His stand-up similarly draws on questions of belonging, family and identity, subjects he approaches through humour informed by his experiences of navigating different cultures.Tickets from Dh3253. Maz Jobrani: November 7 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiWhen the Axis of Evil Comedy Tour emerged in the 2000s, it offered American audiences a different perspective on the Middle East at a time when regional identities were frequently reduced to political stereotypes. Iranian-American comedian Maz Jobrani was among its founding performers, using humour to challenge assumptions about Arabs and Iranians. He has since built an international career spanning television, film and stand-up specials, with politics, parenting and contemporary society continuing to provide material. He appeared at the inaugural Abu Dhabi Comedy Week in 2024.Tickets from Dh2754. The Laughter Factory: November 8 at The Club, Abu DhabiThe UAE's stand-up scene looked considerably different when The Laughter Factory was launched in Dubai in 1996. International comedy clubs were uncommon and arena-sized performances by visiting comedians had yet to become regular fixtures. Three decades later, the organisation is celebrating its 30th anniversary with a UAE tour that includes Abu Dhabi. 30 Years of Laughs continues its tradition of bringing established and emerging comedians to smaller venues, offering the intimacy and spontaneity of a traditional comedy-club evening.The show starts at 7pm; tickets from Dh1405. Amine Radi: November 19 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiMoroccan comedian Amine Radi brings a distinctly North African flavour to Abu Dhabi's comedy programme. His performance moves between French and Arabic, drawing on the humour of everyday exchanges, social expectations and the complications of modern relationships. Radi has developed an audience across the francophone world through performances built around animated delivery and increasingly elaborate stories. His appearance will also be phone-free, with electronic devices secured in pouches during the performance, keeping the focus firmly on the stage.Tickets from Dh1506. Anubhav Singh Bassi: November 21 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiA seemingly ordinary anecdote can become an elaborate comic adventure in the hands of Indian stand-up performer Anubhav Singh Bassi. His relaxed delivery gives stories room to develop, with friendships, student life and questionable youthful decisions supplying much of his material. Bassi's performances have attracted millions of views online, introducing his Hindi-language humour to audiences beyond India. His latest show, Kisi Ko Batana Mat, meaning Don't Tell Anyone, continues this approach, finding absurdity in situations that often begin innocently enough.The show starts at 6pm; tickets from Dh1257. Aries Spears: November 21 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiFew comedians can switch between famous impersonating personalities as convincingly as Aries Spears. The American performer spent eight seasons on the sketch comedy programme Mad TV, where his impressions of entertainers and public figures helped establish his reputation. Michael Jackson, Eddie Murphy and Shaquille O'Neal are among the celebrities he has imitated. Beyond impersonations, Spears has developed a more confrontational approach to stand-up, exploring race, entertainment and American social attitudes. His Abu Dhabi performance offers a mixture of observational humour and the character work that made him famous.The show starts at 10pm; tickets start at Dh1208. Jose Manalo and Wally Bayola: November 22 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiGenerations of Filipino television viewers will recognise Jose Manalo and Wally Bayola from the long-running variety programme Eat Bulaga!. The comedy partners are particularly known for their sketches, recurring characters and ability to improvise around the unexpected. Their Abu Dhabi production, The Ultimate Dabarkads Comedy, brings that chemistry to the stage through sketches, live music and audience participation. Presented in Tagalog and English, the afternoon show is also among the few family-friendly performances in the comedy calendar, with no minimum age restriction.Tickets from Dh999. NEMR: November 22 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiLebanese-American comedian NEMR brings his Rampant Disorder show to Abu Dhabi as part of the Wagef stand-up comedy road tour, presented by MBC Group. Having grown up between Lebanon and the US, he has frequently drawn on the contradictions of those experiences, particularly the expectations placed on young people by their families and communities. His latest production takes a wider look at relationships, culture and the disorder of modern life, delivered through the energetic storytelling that has helped him attract audiences across the Middle East and internationally.Tickets from Dh15010. Mina Nader: November 22 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiNo two Mina Nader performances are quite alike. The Egyptian comedian builds much of his Arabic-language stand-up around conversations with spectators, transforming unexpected answers and personal anecdotes into improvised material. With more than 16 years of experience, Nader has performed across the Middle East, Europe and North America. Organisers credit him with more than 500 sold-out shows, a reflection of the following he has developed through his interactive approach. His Abu Dhabi appearance continues that format, with the audience helping shape the evening's direction.Doors open at 8pm; tickets start from Dh19511. Kevin Bridges: January 9 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiScottish comedian Kevin Bridges has a talent for extracting humour from the ordinary frustrations of life. Growing up in Clydebank, near Glasgow, provided much of the inspiration for his early routines, which examine working-class experiences and the peculiarities of everyday behaviour. His distinctive Glaswegian delivery has become part of his appeal, helping him build a substantial following across Britain and internationally. Bridges has also written two books, including his autobiography We Need to Talk About … Kevin Bridges, documenting his journey from aspiring comedian to arena headliner.The show starts at 8pm; tickets from Dh29512. Whitney Cummings: January 31 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiCreating one successful American sitcom is difficult enough, but Whitney Cummings helped launch two during the same television season. In 2011, she created and starred in NBC's Whitney while also co-creating the CBS comedy 2 Broke Girls. She has since continued working across television, stand-up and podcasting, hosting Good For You and releasing several comedy specials. Her routines frequently examine relationships, gender expectations and contemporary social habits. Her Big Baby tour brings her to the UAE for the first time.Show starts at 6pm; tickets from Dh21513. Paul Smith: January 31 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiLiverpudlian comedian Paul Smith has found international success by making the audience a central part of his performances. Clips filmed at the city's Hot Water Comedy Club have attracted millions of views, largely because of his ability to build jokes around unpredictable exchanges with spectators. His latest show, HAPPY, combines that spontaneous approach with stories about finding humour in the frustrations and complications of daily life. The performance also marks his first appearance at Etihad Arena, closing January's comedy line-up with an emphasis on improvisation.The show starts at 9.30pm; tickets from Dh275

headline: Are Pakistan turning over a new leaf in T20 cricket?
summary: Pakistan completed a T20 series win against Sri Lanka on Sunday, securing an 82-run victory in the second match of the three-game series in Rawalpindi.New captain and opener Sahibzada Farhan hit a quick 73, his second straight fifty, and young middle order bat Maaz Sadaqat smashed 96 from 51 balls to help Pakistan post 215-3. Sri Lanka batters did not even come close, restricted to 133-7.On paper, it is a routine result in a bilateral series well away from a T20 World Cup cycle. But for Pakistan, it was a significant milestone.Pakistan have tried to hit the reset button in white-ball cricket for quite some time. After successive misses at ICC tournaments and a growing trend of failing to even qualify for the semi-finals, the team needed a fresh set of eyes to look at the issue.In 2026, they have started to get more things right than wrong. If you look at the bigger picture, Pakistan did not win any major titles – either the T20 World Cup or Asian Games. Maaz Sadaqat is the only batter from Pakistan who has a combo of 1000plus runs, 30plus average and 150plus strike rate in T20s. And there are just 21 men in the world with this combination.— Mazher Arshad (@MazherArshad) October 12, 2026However, they lost just four out of 15 completed matches this year and two of those losses were against double world champions India, including in the Asian Games gold medal match.Pakistan thrashed Australia 3-0 at home ahead of the T20 World Cup and were largely competitive in the main tournament, losing to India and England (by 2 wickets).So what has changed? For starters, Pakistan are putting more faith in T20 specialists. Farhan – top scorer at the T20 World Cup and ranked third in the world among T20 batters – was named captain for the ongoing Sri Lanka series. There was no space for tried and tested fast-bowler Shaheen Afridi or all-rounder Salman Agha. Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan are almost certainly out of the T20 scheme of things for good. The selectors and team management have backed players who live and breathe the 20-over format.Hasan Nawaz is one such name and almost snatched the T20 Asian Games gold medal from India’s grasp with a destructive 96 in the final.Left-arm fast bowler Salman Mirza has played more T20Is than first-class matches and should get an extended run, albeit at the age of 32, now that Pakistan seem to have had enough Afridi the T20 bowler. Mirza picked up 2-28 from three overs against Sri Lanka on Sunday.There are many more waiting in the wings. There always have been. It was just that some players were turned into multi-format players for the sake of it, which took away precious spots in the T20 side which could have easily gone to specialists.One can sense change in the air. Captain Farhan made it clear what he wants from his team, especially the batters.“We have been a different T20 side in 2026 as our six-hitting ratio has improved and our batters are scoring at more than 150 [strike rate]. If we continue this way, we will end up scoring more than 200 every time,” the opener said after the Sri Lanka series win.That is a significant statement because it is the only way successful teams operate. And also because those words came from a player who is a genuine trend setter in the country.Farhan is one among only five batters to hits four T20 centuries in one year. Also, Farhan is the first Pakistan batter to hit a six against India’s Jasprit Bumrah – after a staggering 400 deliveries bowled by the Indian ace. That alone broke the shackles that had gripped the minds of many Pakistan players and supporters after successive defeats against their neighbours at ICC events.India still obviously hold the upper hand but Pakistan are beginning to believe that the gap with the world champions and other leading T20 teams is probably not as vast as it was a couple of seasons back.
body_text:
Pakistan completed a T20 series win against Sri Lanka on Sunday, securing an 82-run victory in the second match of the three-game series in Rawalpindi.

New captain and opener Sahibzada Farhan hit a quick 73, his second straight fifty, and young middle order bat Maaz Sadaqat smashed 96 from 51 balls to help Pakistan post 215-3. Sri Lanka batters did not even come close, restricted to 133-7.

On paper, it is a routine result in a bilateral series well away from a T20 World Cup cycle. But for Pakistan, it was a significant milestone.

Pakistan's Babar and Zaman are poor relations as millions spent at ILT20 auction

Pakistan have tried to hit the reset button in white-ball cricket for quite some time. After successive misses at ICC tournaments and a growing trend of failing to even qualify for the semi-finals, the team needed a fresh set of eyes to look at the issue.

In 2026, they have started to get more things right than wrong.

If you look at the bigger picture, Pakistan did not win any major titles – either the T20 World Cup or Asian Games.

However, they lost just four out of 15 completed matches this year and two of those losses were against double world champions India, including in the Asian Games gold medal match.

Pakistan thrashed Australia 3-0 at home ahead of the T20 World Cup and were largely competitive in the main tournament, losing to India and England (by 2 wickets).

So what has changed? For starters, Pakistan are putting more faith in T20 specialists. Farhan – top scorer at the T20 World Cup and ranked third in the world among T20 batters – was named captain for the ongoing Sri Lanka series.

There was no space for tried and tested fast-bowler Shaheen Afridi or all-rounder Salman Agha. Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan are almost certainly out of the T20 scheme of things for good.

The selectors and team management have backed players who live and breathe the 20-over format.

Hasan Nawaz is one such name and almost snatched the T20 Asian Games gold medal from India’s grasp with a destructive 96 in the final.

Left-arm fast bowler Salman Mirza has played more T20Is than first-class matches and should get an extended run, albeit at the age of 32, now that Pakistan seem to have had enough Afridi the T20 bowler. Mirza picked up 2-28 from three overs against Sri Lanka on Sunday.

There are many more waiting in the wings. There always have been. It was just that some players were turned into multi-format players for the sake of it, which took away precious spots in the T20 side which could have easily gone to specialists.

One can sense change in the air. Captain Farhan made it clear what he wants from his team, especially the batters.

“We have been a different T20 side in 2026 as our six-hitting ratio has improved and our batters are scoring at more than 150 [strike rate]. If we continue this way, we will end up scoring more than 200 every time,” the opener said after the Sri Lanka series win.

That is a significant statement because it is the only way successful teams operate. And also because those words came from a player who is a genuine trend setter in the country.

Farhan is one among only five batters to hits four T20 centuries in one year. Also, Farhan is the first Pakistan batter to hit a six against India’s Jasprit Bumrah – after a staggering 400 deliveries bowled by the Indian ace.

That alone broke the shackles that had gripped the minds of many Pakistan players and supporters after successive defeats against their neighbours at ICC events.

India still obviously hold the upper hand but Pakistan are beginning to believe that the gap with the world champions and other leading T20 teams is probably not as vast as it was a couple of seasons back.

headline: Global oil demand to grow by 0.4 mln barrels daily in 2026 — OPEC Secretary General
summary: It is lower than the organization forecast at the start of 2026, OPEC Secretary General Haitham Al-Ghais said
body_text:
MOSCOW, October 12. /TASS/. The Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) expects the global oil demand will grow by 0.4 mln barrels per day this year, which is lower than the organization forecast at the start of 2026, OPEC Secretary General Haitham Al-Ghais said at the WPC Energy congress.

"At OPEC, we have revised our demand figure forecast for this year down from the beginning of the year in tandem with the events and the unfolding of events," Al-Ghais said. "We are now seeing demand growth this year at 400,000 barrels a day versus in the beginning of the year we had it at 1.4 million barrels a day," he noted.

"However, this demand... To be fair, [it] has been deferred to 2027, where we believe there will be pent-up demand next year. We have it now at a level of 1.7 million barrels a day growth for 2027," the Secretary General added.

headline: India-Sri Lanka ODI to remain in Delhi, BCCI clarifies
body_text:
The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has dismissed reports suggesting that the opening ODI of the upcoming three-match series against Sri Lanka has been shifted from Delhi to Ahmedabad.

In a brief statement on Monday, BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia said the match, scheduled for December 13, was allotted to Delhi as per standard policy and no change has been made to the venue. “Reports suggesting that the India-Sri Lanka ODI match scheduled in Delhi may be shifted to Ahmedabad are not accurate. There has been no such decision by the BCCI,” Saikia was quoted as saying by PTI.

“Further, it needs to be reiterated that bilateral matches are primarily allotted by following a standard policy,” he added.

The reports had suggested that the match was being moved to Ahmedabad, which is set to host the series finale on December 19, due to ongoing construction work at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in Delhi.

The denial comes amid a packed calendar for the Indian team. India are currently engaged in a white-ball series against West Indies, with the T20I leg underway and the ODI leg having concluded earlier this month. Following that, the team will travel to New Zealand for a multi-format series beginning October 22, featuring five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests across Christchurch, Wellington, Auckland, Hamilton and Mount Maunganui.

The New Zealand tour will be followed by a home assignment against Sri Lanka, which includes both ODI and T20I series. The Delhi venue last hosted an international fixture during India’s clash against Afghanistan, and the Arun Jaitley Stadium remains a regular stop on the BCCI’s home calendar.

Apart from the three ODIs, Sri Lanka will also play a three-match T20 International series during their tour.
