headline: Lebanon wants to strengthen ties with Russia — top diplomat
summary: Lebanese Foreign Minister Youssef Rajji praised Russia’s role as a member of the United Nations Security Council in promoting stability and security in Lebanon
body_text:
BEIRUT, October 12. /TASS/. The Lebanese government wants to develop the strongest possible ties with Russia while duly taking into account mutual interests, Lebanese Foreign Minister Youssef Rajji said.

"We sincerely strive to maintain the best possible relations with Russia in the political, economic, and cultural spheres, taking into account our mutual interests," he said during talks with his Russian counterpart, Sergey Lavrov, in Moscow, according to the Lebanese Foreign Ministry.

He praised Russia’s role as a member of the United Nations Security Council in promoting stability and security in Lebanon and reiterated the Lebanese government’s commitment to extending state sovereignty across the entire country, which requires an end to hostilities in its southern part.

"The current difficult situation stems from Israel’s refusal to withdraw its troops and its continuing aggression, as well as from Hezbollah’s unwillingness to disarm," Rajji noted, stressing that decisions on war and peace are for the Lebanese government and legitimate institutions to make.

The top Lebanese diplomat welcomed the growing number of scholarships awarded by Russia to Lebanese students and expressed hope for the gradual return of Russian tourists to Beirut. "I am happy to visit Moscow and am convinced that this will not be my last visit to Russia," he added.

headline: Oil shipping and insurance costs exceed one-third of the commodity value — OPEC
summary: The ministers affirmed the critical importance of safeguarding the international maritime routes to ensure the uninterrupted flow of energy
body_text:
MOSCOW, October 12. /TASS/. Current disruptions in oil supplies have driven up insurance and transportation costs, which now account for more than one-third of the oil's price, according to an OPEC statement released following the meeting of OPEC and OPEC+ ministers in Riyadh.

"In this context, the Ministers affirmed the critical importance of safeguarding the international maritime routes to ensure the uninterrupted flow of energy. They also noted that the current interruption of energy flows has elevated the cost of shipping and insurance which have reached unprecedented levels of more than one third of the commodity value, impeding the timely and efficient movement of crude oil and products, and placing additional inflationary pressures on the global economy," the statement says.

During a meeting held on the sidelines of the World Petroleum Congress (WPC Energy) and the International Energy Forum (IEF) session, ministers also emphasized that these extremely high costs ultimately ripple through the entire oil industry value chain, increasing the financial burden on both producing and consuming nations and impacting global economic growth.

"The Ministers will continue monitoring the situation, and will engage with governments, industry stakeholders, and international organizations such as the IEF, IEA, and others to improve global shipping conditions," the statement says.

At the meeting the ministers also reviewed the market situation and agreed to continue consultations with all OPEC+ countries within the framework of existing mechanisms--including the Joint Ministerial Monitoring Committee (JMMC) and OPEC+ ministerial meetings--and reaffirmed their commitment to the decisions adopted on June 7, 2026, at the ministerial meeting aimed at maintaining oil market stability.

headline: U.S., Japan reaffirm commitment to complete denuclearization of N. Korea in high-level talks
summary: WASHINGTON, Oct. 12 (Yonhap) -- The United States and Japan reaffirmed their com...
body_text:
WASHINGTON, Oct. 12 (Yonhap) -- The United States and Japan reaffirmed their commitment to the complete denuclearization of North Korea during high-level talks in Tokyo on Monday, the U.S. State Department said.

U.S. Under Secretary of State for Political Affairs Allison Hooker and Japanese Senior Deputy Minister for Foreign Affairs Hiroyuki Namazu made the commitment during the countries' second U.S.-Japan Free and Open Indo-Pacific (FOIP) Dialogue held in Tokyo, according to a department press release.

"They noted progress in U.S.-Japan defense industrial cooperation and reaffirmed their commitment to the complete denuclearization of the DPRK and the immediate resolution of the abductions issue," the department said, referring to North Korea by its official name, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea.

The statement comes as U.S. President Donald Trump has repeatedly expressed his willingness to resume dialogue with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, raising speculation over the possibility of renewed diplomacy between Washington and Pyongyang.

The two sides also discussed ways to strengthen cooperation with regional allies and partners on security issues, while welcoming Japan's growing cooperation with the North Atlantic Treaty Organization.

The dialogue also covered economic security, critical minerals supply chains, energy security and maritime security cooperation in Southeast Asia and the Pacific Islands, according to the department.

headline: Germany needs diesel deal with Russia — politician
summary: There is no way to halt the decline of German industry without affordable energy sources from Russia, Sahra Wagenknecht emphasized
body_text:
BERLIN, October 12. /TASS/. Sahra Wagenknecht, the founder of Germany’s BSW party (formerly known as the Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance - Reason and Justice party), has called on the German government to strike a diesel deal with Russia, as the United States has done, and to abandon the anti-Russian sanctions.

"This is utter madness - the US administration is again importing diesel from Russia in an effort to curb the rapidly growing fuel prices for American consumers. But the German government continues to adhere to its futile sanctions policy, which is driving our economy toward collapse and making our citizens increasingly poorer," she wrote on X.

She noted that fuel prices in Germany are too high. "Germany also needs a diesel deal with Russia and, more broadly, the resumption of Russian oil and gas supplies," she stated. "There is no way to halt the decline of our industry without affordable energy sources from Russia," Wagenknecht emphasized.

She recalled that on Wednesday, Saxony-Anhalt’s state parliament will vote on a joint resolution put forward by her party and Alternative for Germany, which calls on the German government to lift sanctions against Russia and support diplomatic efforts to resolve the conflict in Ukraine.

Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump held a phone call on October 9, during which they discussed, among other things, petroleum product supplies. The Russian president said that Moscow had reiterated its readiness to supply oil and petroleum products to the United States and global markets. According to Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak, Russia will lift its ban on diesel exports ahead of schedule and is ready to supply 300,000 tons of diesel in October, increasing the volume to 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons in December. Monthly supplies could subsequently reach 3 million tons. The US administration, in turn, issued a general license authorizing Russian diesel supplies to the global market until April 7, 2027.

headline: Vietnam attaches great importance to strengthening strategic partnership with Russia
summary: Vietnamese Minister of Public Security Luong Tam Quang noted that transnational criminal groups, organized crime, high-tech crime and emerging forms of crime, including offenses involving foreign nationals, pose numerous challenges to both countries
body_text:
HANOI, October 12. /TASS/. Vietnam has always attached great importance to strengthening and developing its traditional friendship and comprehensive strategic partnership with Russia, Vietnamese Minister of Public Security Luong Tam Quang said at a meeting with a delegation from Russia’s Federal Penitentiary Service (FSIN) led by its director, Arkady Gostev, in Hanoi.

The Vietnamese minister of Public Security said Vietnam seeks to strengthen cooperation in security and law enforcement by building political trust, improving coordination and reinforcing the long-standing ties between the two countries. He was quoted by the Vietnam News Agency as saying that such cooperation should be reliable, substantive and effective.

Quang discussed the current security and law enforcement situation. He noted that transnational criminal groups, organized crime, high-tech crime and emerging forms of crime, including offenses involving foreign nationals, pose numerous challenges to both countries. These challenges require the Vietnamese and Russian authorities to continue enhancing coordination, exchanging information and expertise, and improving cooperation in security and law enforcement, including the enforcement of criminal judgments, he said.

The director of Russia’s FSIN, in turn, praised the traditional friendship between Moscow and Hanoi and the positive results of cooperation between the Russian government and Vietnam’s Ministry of Public Security in recent years. Gostev reaffirmed Russia’s commitment to expanding ties between the two agencies, particularly through the exchange of expertise in correctional facility management, prisoner education and rehabilitation, and staff training, thereby further deepening security and law enforcement cooperation between the two countries.

body_text:
A teacher from the UAE injured in an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh has been assured she will be able to complete her Umrah pilgrimage once she recovers.

The teacher, whose name was not released, was travelling with a colleague from Abu Dhabi to Makkah via Riyadh when the airport came under attack on Saturday.

Saudi Health Minister Fahad Al Jalajel visited the two women in hospital on Sunday when he went to see people injured in the attack and find out about their medical care.

AnalysisHouthi attacks stretch Saudi air defences to all corners of country

One of the teachers told the minister how their journey had been interrupted, according to Saudi state-run television channel Al Ekhbariya. She praised the doctors treating her.

Mr Al Jalajel said King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman had instructed officials to ensure the women received full support throughout their recovery.

“You’re not part of what happened. We know that. For that reason, King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman are telling us to take full care of you, even the recovery, and that you continue on your Umrah,” he told her.

Saudi Arabia has extended the suspension of operations at the airport following the deadly attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels at the weekend.

The General Authority of Civil Aviation said on Monday that the suspension would continue while checks on the safety and operational readiness of airport sites were completed. It did not give a date or time for the reopening.

Etihad Airways has cancelled all flights between Abu Dhabi and Riyadh until October 19, extending disruption to services between the UAE and the Saudi capital into next week. Flydubai has cancelled Riyadh flights until Wednesday, while Emirates and Air Arabia services have been affected.

Services to other Saudi destinations have also been impacted. Etihad cancelled four flights between Abu Dhabi and Dammam on Monday, with all services on the route cancelled on Tuesday and Wednesday. Selected Jeddah flights have been cancelled until Thursday.

headline: Houthi official warns of 'swift, painful response' if US enters Yemen war
summary: A Houthi official on Monday warned the US it would receive a "painful response" if it entered the war in Yemen, where Saudi Arabia has reportedly requested Washington's help in dealing with the group as it weathers repeated attacks. Yemen's civil war -- in which a Saudi-led military coalition supports the government against the Iran-backed Houthis -- reignited in July, months into the wider regional conflict that has roiled energy markets and plunged the Middle East into crisis.
body_text:
A Houthi official on Monday warned the US it would receive a "painful response" if it entered the war in Yemen, where Saudi Arabia has reportedly requested Washington's help in dealing with the group as it weathers repeated attacks.

Yemen's civil war -- in which a Saudi-led military coalition supports the government against the Iran-backed Houthis -- reignited in July, months into the wider regional conflict that has roiled energy markets and plunged the Middle East into crisis.

The Houthis quickly began targeting Saudi oil facilities, tankers and transport hubs, including with a string of lethal strikes on Riyadh's airport, rocking the world's top oil exporter.

Following an attack Saturday at the airport that killed 13 people, US President Donald Trump said he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the group, after having reportedly rebuffed previous requests for help from the kingdom.

"If the US becomes involved in the aggression against Yemen, we will not deliberate over the decision to respond, rather, there will be a swift and painful response targeting the US and all its interests in the region," Houthi political bureau member Mohammed Al Bukhaiti told AFP in an interview.

He also warned "all employees and workers at Saudi oil facilities and airports to stay away from these sites, as they have become legitimate targets".

Saturday's strike on King Khalid International Airport was the deadliest attack on Saudi soil in more than a decade, and also left hundreds wounded.

Trump said the attack was "not acceptable" and that he would be speaking to the kingdom's de facto leader Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, telling reporters the US was "going to look at" the possibility of joining Saudi strikes.

Four people died in earlier strikes on Wednesday and Thursday, and another was killed on Sunday. Operations remained suspended at the sprawling airport on Riyadh's outskirts on Monday.

Bukhaiti said the purpose of the campaign against Saudi targets was to send a message to the crown prince "that he can no longer wage aggression against Yemen from a safe position".

Saudi energy minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman told an energy conference in Riyadh on Monday that the recent events had "tested our infrastructure, our institutions, our people, and our resilience".

"The events of recent weeks are serious, our response must be equally serious."

CCTV footage of Saturday's attack released by Saudi authorities showed Muslim pilgrims in religious attire waiting in departure lounges before a sudden blast tore through the building and brought down flaming debris.

The atmosphere in Riyadh remained tense on Monday, as state broadcaster Al Ekhbariya said the military coalition was responding to drone and missile threats, and Australia's embassy warned its citizens in the city to shelter in place.

The US embassy in Saudi Arabia said US government employees must obtain its authorisation before using any airport in the kingdom, and urged US citizens to "take extreme caution" if they chose to do so.

The mission also said "American citizens have been detained for taking photos of recent events" in Saudi Arabia, without specifying how many or whether they had been released.

The UAE's national carrier Etihad Airways announced on Monday that it was cancelling all flights to and from Riyadh until next week due to "regional disruption", and also suspended flights to Dammam and Jeddah.

Bahrain's national carrier Gulf Air said it too was cancelling all Riyadh flights until Saturday.

US operator Delta announced it would delay the launch of direct flights from Atlanta to Riyadh -- scheduled for October 23 -- as US air safety regulators warned of continued safety risks.

Despite vast spending on military hardware, the Houthi attacks on oil, military and transport facilities across the large, mostly desert country are stretching Saudi defences.

Thomas Juneau, security analyst at Ottawa University, said that despite some success, "Saudi Arabia is so large that it's simply impossible for them to consistently defend themselves".

Riyadh leads an international coalition that has supported Yemen's government militarily since 2015, including by seeking to exert control over Yemeni airspace and the airport in the Houthi-held capital Sanaa.

Juneau said the Houthis now "want to do to Saudi Arabia what Saudi Arabia does to them".

The long-running Yemeni civil war has created a deeply entrenched humanitarian crisis in the impoverished country.

UN rights chief Volker Turk said he was "appalled by the repeated attacks" on Saudi Arabia, but urged both sides to back down.

"The disastrous toll of this conflict on civilians, both in Yemen and in Saudi Arabia, is a reminder to all parties that continued fighting will only unleash further misery with no end in sight."

Our correspondents are already on the next chapter. Read everything they file, from $2/week.

body_text:
Yemen's Houthi rebels launched fresh attacks against Saudi Arabia on Monday, following deadly missile strikes on Riyadh's international airport that killed passengers, some of whom were preparing to board flights to perform Umrah.

Saudi authorities extended the suspension of operations at King Khalid International Airport until midnight on October 17 following an attack on Saturday that killed 13 people and injured more than 300, and another on Sunday in which one person was killed.

The King Fahd International Airport in Dammam was also hit on Sunday evening, Saudi Arabia's General Authority for Civil Aviation said, with the damage being assessed.

Pilot, flight attendant and widow among victims of Houthi attacks

The strikes came as Yemeni government forces, backed by the Saudi-led coalition, clashed with Houthi rebels on the outskirts of the strategic south-western city of Taiz, repelling fresh attacks amid warnings that a tightening rebel siege is worsening conditions inside the Yemeni city. A military spokesman said on Monday that air strikes prevented the Houthis from sending reinforcements to Taiz.

At least 20 people have been killed in a series of attacks since last week on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and the Abha international airport in Saudi Arabia’s Asir province. Saudi state TV broadcast footage of the moment a missile struck the passenger terminal in Riyadh on Saturday, with flashes of light filling the screen as travellers, including pilgrims in white robes, scrambled for cover.

Ali, from Hyderabad, was travelling with his family on an Umrah pilgrimage when he was injured in Saturday’s attack. The Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia confirmed his death on Sunday and said it was in contact with his family to help arrange the repatriation of his remains.

Etihad Airways cancelled all flights between Abu Dhabi and Riyadh until Monday, October 19, extending disruption to services between the UAE and the Saudi capital into next week. Flydubai has also cancelled Riyadh flights until Wednesday, October 14, while Emirates and Air Arabia services have been affected.

The Saudi-led coalition said it responded to drone and cruise missile threats against the kingdom on Monday, as hostilities with the Iran-backed Houthis continued despite diplomatic efforts, including a phone call between the foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia and Iran, which supports the Houthis.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told his Saudi counterpart Prince Faisal bin Farhan that Tehran was ready to "provide assistance" to start talks between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis to reach a "political solution", Iranian state media reported.

"The Foreign Minister of our country, expressing concern over the escalation of tensions, emphasised that insisting on a military approach and ignoring political solutions would complicate the existing situation," Mr Araghchi was quoted as saying.

Amid the continued attacks on Saudi Arabia, Dr Anwar Gargash, diplomatic adviser to President Sheikh Mohamed, called for stronger Gulf security and collective defence.

In his statement posted on X, Dr Gargash said the security of Gulf states as a whole was "indivisible". He stressed that attacks against Saudi Arabia also threatened the wider Gulf. “Targeting our sisterly kingdom of Saudi Arabia undermines the security of the UAE and all Gulf states,” he added. He warned that shortcomings in regional co-operation had contributed to the current challenges.

US Central Command chief Adm Brad Cooper said the US and its regional allies were deploying the “largest air-defence umbrella in the world” to deter Iranian attacks, describing the effort as part of an “enduring security architecture” in the Middle East.

“It was a vision we discussed with our regional allies and partners,” he told the audience in a recorded message at Trends Global's sixth annual conference in Abu Dhabi on Monday. “Earlier this year, during Operation Epic Fury, we validated at full scale and in actual combat the Middle East Air Defence network known as Mead.

“Through our combined efforts, we transformed a concept into the most sophisticated and largest air-defence umbrella in the world,” he added.

“For the first time in history, US air defenders stood shoulder-to-shoulder with allies and partners across the Middle East, linking national systems in real time. And so together we intercepted thousands of Iranian attack drones and missiles with an integrated shield built on mutual trust. This is partnership in action.”

headline: (2nd LD) S. Korean envoy says progress made in intelligence cooperation with U.S. amid friction concerns
summary: WASHINGTON, Oct. 12 (Yonhap) -- South Korea's top envoy to the United States sai...
body_text:
By Chang Dong-woo(ATTN: REWRITES headline, lead; ADDS more details in paras 8-9; RECASTS throughout)

WASHINGTON, Oct. 12 (Yonhap) -- South Korea's top envoy to the United States said Monday that progress has been made in improving intelligence cooperation between Seoul and Washington, amid concerns over apparent friction between the two allies.

Ambassador Kang Kyung-wha made the remarks during a parliamentary audit at the South Korean Embassy in Washington, responding to questions about bilateral intelligence cooperation.

Regarding the controversy, the ambassador said she is aware that "intelligence agencies of the two countries have communicated with each other" and that "progress has been made" in terms of improving cooperation.

The remarks follow growing speculation over bilateral friction after South Korea's National Intelligence Service acknowledged it was excluded from a June trilateral meeting, also involving Japan, on North Korean cyber threats. Local media reports indicated the agency was left out at Washington's request.

South Korea and the U.S. have experienced friction in the intelligence field after Seoul Unification Minister Chung Dong-young's public disclosure of a North Korean uranium enrichment facility in Kusong, North Korea, in March.

Kang also said she is unaware of any complaints raised by the U.S. side against the unification minister or South Korea's National Intelligence Service Director Lee Jong-seok.

"There have been various consultations regarding problems in connection with intelligence cooperation, but there have not been any complaints raised against any individual," Kang said.

Kang said she had received a phone call from Chung following his remarks about North Korea's nuclear facility in Kusong and had conveyed his explanation to U.S. officials through diplomatic channels.

She did not elaborate on how U.S. officials responded to Chung's explanation.

The ambassador also acknowledged limitations in high-level communication with the White House.

"I acknowledge that there are limitations in our communication with the White House," Kang said.

Regarding the possibility of another North Korea-U.S. summit, the ambassador said she is aware that there has not been any concrete progress. "There is always the possibility, but it is hard to speak (of) in terms of numbers (likelihood)."

According to Kang, the subject of a possible North Korea-U.S. summit has become a topic of daily consultation between Seoul and Washington in terms of intelligence sharing.

body_text:
Al Ahli Saudi left Dubai with three points towards their bid for a hat-trick of Asian Champions League titles after a fiery meeting with Al Wasl.

Roger Ibanez and Francisco Trincao, two big-money imports to Saudi Arabian football, scored, before Feras Albrikan clinched a 3-1 win in stoppage time.

The margin of defeat was harsh on a spirited Wasl side, who deserved more than the lone strike by Pedro Malheiro in first-half stoppage time.

Given the gap they were bridging to the high-spending Saudi Pro League side, the home players fully merited the backing they got from their fans on a hostile night in Zabeel.

Before kick-off, Ahli’s players stood on the 18-yard line and were serenaded with their club anthem by the travelling supporters.

Around 200 had made the trip from Jeddah, but they were drowned out by the noise of the home faithful. The Ultras Junoon are always loud, but they were particularly rowdy when the Ahli anthem was being sung.

The home players responded. Wasl’s start was bright, and they fashioned the first opening, only for Siaka Sidibe to blaze over from the edge of the box.

Home optimism was dissipated in the 20th minute, though, when Ibanez headed in the opener for Ahli.

The Brazil centre-back, who was called into the Selecao squad by Carlo Ancelotti for the World Cup this summer, is renowned for his leap.

Despite common knowledge of his aerial prowess, he was unchallenged at the back post to make it 1-0.

The visitors nearly doubled their lead 10 minutes later, but were saved by the post as Eduard Spertsyan’s shot bounced away to safety.

Wasl’s defence was being cut open with greater regularity, and they were lucky not to be a long way behind by the break.

Their fortune continued when Adryelson, the Wasl defender evaded a red card.

After a confrontation in the box, Saleh Abu Al Shamat, the Ahli forward, went down. Replays showed Adryelson had squared up to him, and lightly pushed his forehead towards his opponent.

Shamat tumbled to the floor and rolled around as if he was mortally wounded. It was enough of a show to persuade VAR to recommend the referee take a second look at the monitor.

Usually, that is ominous for the perceived offender. Justice was served, though, as Abdulrahman Al Jassim, the Qatari official, decided he was right the first time, and stayed with a yellow card.

Adryelson nearly provided the perfect riposte; from the ensuing free-kick for Wasl, he bundled the ball into the net, only for it to be ruled out for offside.

The hosts were level by the break, though. In stoppage time at the end of the half, a long range effort from Malheiro, Wasl’s right back, found its way into the net after some limp goalkeeping.

Shamat had fully established himself as public enemy No 1. At the start of the second half, he was playing on the wing in front of the hardcore or Wasl’s supporters.

They frequently lobbed plastic water bottles in his direction. Rather than fuss, he waved a hand at them, encouraging the fans to bring it on.

Just before the hour mark, Trincao ruined the home fans’ fun. The Portuguese forward finished clinically to restore the away side’s lead.

Wasl should have levelled shortly after following a rapid counter-attack, but Serginho hit the post with the goal at his mercy.

Even when he went off, Shamat caused rancour. After an innocuous incident, he went down clutching his shoulder.

He looked in genuine pain, and had to be stretchered off on the back of the medical golf buggy.

It turned out that his injury was not so severe that he could wave with both arms as he was taken past the Ahli supporters.

That added to the fury of the home fans, and even the players were so incensed they threw bottles in his direction as the buggy went past the home dugout.

Ahli’s bench sprung to his defence, and the two sets of replacements and substituted players had to be separated.

Wasl had their chances as they chased the game, but their hopes were finally dashed when Albrikan scored Ahli’s third in stoppage time.

headline: Egypt’s FM discusses expanding economic, parliamentary ties with Thai officials
summary: Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty held a series of meetings with government and parliamentary officials in Thailand on Monday at the start of a visit to Bangkok aimed at strengthening political, economic, investment and educational cooperation between the two countries. Abdelatty met Thai Industry Minister Varawut Silpa-archa to discuss ways to expand trade and investment and strengthen industrial cooperation, including potential joint manufacturing projects in rubber, petrochemicals and tyres. He said Egypt sought to benefit from Thailand’s experience in industrial localisation, innovation, digital transformation and sustainability while boosting domestic production and industrial exports. Abdelatty also highlighted investment opportunities in the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE), citing HI TECH as the first Thai industrial project in the zone. He called for leveraging the project’s presence to attract further Thai investment to Egypt. Thailand’s industry minister expressed interest in expanding cooperation within the economic zone and exploring new manufacturing and investment opportunities in Egypt. In a separate meeting, Abdelatty met Sophon Saram, President of Thailand’s House of Representatives and National Assembly, to discuss bilateral relations, parliamentary cooperation and ways to expand economic and investment ties. Abdelatty said bilateral relations had gained momentum in 2026, citing the eighth round of political consultations held in Cairo and reciprocal parliamentary visits. He called for developing a practical roadmap to advance political, economic and development cooperation between the two countries. He invited the Thai parliamentary speaker to visit Egypt and discussed strengthening educational and cultural ties, including partnerships between Egyptian and Thai universities, scholarship programmes and Al-Azhar’s role in educating Thai students. Abdelatty also called for increased Thai investment in Egypt and improved access for Egyptian agricultural products to the Thai market. He later met Yoonadi Waba, chairman of the Thai-Egyptian Parliamentary Friendship Group, and other group members to discuss expanding parliamentary exchanges, establishing direct contacts between specialised committees and maintaining regular dialogue with Egypt’s House of Representatives and Senate. The talks also covered vocational training, expanding scholarship exchanges and ways for parliamentarians to encourage closer ties between the two countries’ business communities. In another meeting, Abdelatty held talks with Nirat Yoopakdee, chairman of the Senate Foreign Affairs Committee, on parliamentary and economic cooperation, as well as regional and international developments. Abdelatty called for activating the joint trade committee agreed upon in December 2024, stressing that Egypt could serve as a gateway for Thai companies seeking access to African and European markets, while Thailand could offer Egyptian products and investors greater access to the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) markets. He also welcomed Thailand’s efforts to deepen its engagement with Africa and affirmed Egypt’s readiness to support stronger Thai-African economic and development cooperation. The two sides exchanged views on developments in the Asia-Pacific region and the Middle East and agreed to continue consultations on issues of mutual interest.

Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty held a series of meetings with government and parliamentary officials in Thailand on Monday at the start of a visit to Bangkok aimed at strengthening political, economic, investment and educational cooperation between the two countries.

Abdelatty met Thai Industry Minister Varawut Silpa-archa to discuss ways to expand trade and investment and strengthen industrial cooperation, including potential joint manufacturing projects in rubber, petrochemicals and tyres.

He said Egypt sought to benefit from Thailand’s experience in industrial localisation, innovation, digital transformation and sustainability while boosting domestic production and industrial exports.

Abdelatty also highlighted investment opportunities in the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE), citing HI TECH as the first Thai industrial project in the zone. He called for leveraging the project’s presence to attract further Thai investment to Egypt.

Thailand’s industry minister expressed interest in expanding cooperation within the economic zone and exploring new manufacturing and investment opportunities in Egypt.

In a separate meeting, Abdelatty met Sophon Saram, President of Thailand’s House of Representatives and National Assembly, to discuss bilateral relations, parliamentary cooperation and ways to expand economic and investment ties.

Abdelatty said bilateral relations had gained momentum in 2026, citing the eighth round of political consultations held in Cairo and reciprocal parliamentary visits. He called for developing a practical roadmap to advance political, economic and development cooperation between the two countries.

He invited the Thai parliamentary speaker to visit Egypt and discussed strengthening educational and cultural ties, including partnerships between Egyptian and Thai universities, scholarship programmes and Al-Azhar’s role in educating Thai students.

Abdelatty also called for increased Thai investment in Egypt and improved access for Egyptian agricultural products to the Thai market.

He later met Yoonadi Waba, chairman of the Thai-Egyptian Parliamentary Friendship Group, and other group members to discuss expanding parliamentary exchanges, establishing direct contacts between specialised committees and maintaining regular dialogue with Egypt’s House of Representatives and Senate.

The talks also covered vocational training, expanding scholarship exchanges and ways for parliamentarians to encourage closer ties between the two countries’ business communities.

In another meeting, Abdelatty held talks with Nirat Yoopakdee, chairman of the Senate Foreign Affairs Committee, on parliamentary and economic cooperation, as well as regional and international developments.

Abdelatty called for activating the joint trade committee agreed upon in December 2024, stressing that Egypt could serve as a gateway for Thai companies seeking access to African and European markets, while Thailand could offer Egyptian products and investors greater access to the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) markets.

He also welcomed Thailand’s efforts to deepen its engagement with Africa and affirmed Egypt’s readiness to support stronger Thai-African economic and development cooperation.

The two sides exchanged views on developments in the Asia-Pacific region and the Middle East and agreed to continue consultations on issues of mutual interest.

headline: Lebanon wants to strengthen ties with Russia — top diplomat
summary: Lebanese Foreign Minister Youssef Rajji praised Russia’s role as a member of the United Nations Security Council in promoting stability and security in Lebanon
body_text:
BEIRUT, October 12. /TASS/. The Lebanese government wants to develop the strongest possible ties with Russia while duly taking into account mutual interests, Lebanese Foreign Minister Youssef Rajji said.

"We sincerely strive to maintain the best possible relations with Russia in the political, economic, and cultural spheres, taking into account our mutual interests," he said during talks with his Russian counterpart, Sergey Lavrov, in Moscow, according to the Lebanese Foreign Ministry.

He praised Russia’s role as a member of the United Nations Security Council in promoting stability and security in Lebanon and reiterated the Lebanese government’s commitment to extending state sovereignty across the entire country, which requires an end to hostilities in its southern part.

"The current difficult situation stems from Israel’s refusal to withdraw its troops and its continuing aggression, as well as from Hezbollah’s unwillingness to disarm," Rajji noted, stressing that decisions on war and peace are for the Lebanese government and legitimate institutions to make.

The top Lebanese diplomat welcomed the growing number of scholarships awarded by Russia to Lebanese students and expressed hope for the gradual return of Russian tourists to Beirut. "I am happy to visit Moscow and am convinced that this will not be my last visit to Russia," he added.

headline: Oil shipping and insurance costs exceed one-third of the commodity value — OPEC
summary: The ministers affirmed the critical importance of safeguarding the international maritime routes to ensure the uninterrupted flow of energy
body_text:
MOSCOW, October 12. /TASS/. Current disruptions in oil supplies have driven up insurance and transportation costs, which now account for more than one-third of the oil's price, according to an OPEC statement released following the meeting of OPEC and OPEC+ ministers in Riyadh.

"In this context, the Ministers affirmed the critical importance of safeguarding the international maritime routes to ensure the uninterrupted flow of energy. They also noted that the current interruption of energy flows has elevated the cost of shipping and insurance which have reached unprecedented levels of more than one third of the commodity value, impeding the timely and efficient movement of crude oil and products, and placing additional inflationary pressures on the global economy," the statement says.

During a meeting held on the sidelines of the World Petroleum Congress (WPC Energy) and the International Energy Forum (IEF) session, ministers also emphasized that these extremely high costs ultimately ripple through the entire oil industry value chain, increasing the financial burden on both producing and consuming nations and impacting global economic growth.

"The Ministers will continue monitoring the situation, and will engage with governments, industry stakeholders, and international organizations such as the IEF, IEA, and others to improve global shipping conditions," the statement says.

At the meeting the ministers also reviewed the market situation and agreed to continue consultations with all OPEC+ countries within the framework of existing mechanisms--including the Joint Ministerial Monitoring Committee (JMMC) and OPEC+ ministerial meetings--and reaffirmed their commitment to the decisions adopted on June 7, 2026, at the ministerial meeting aimed at maintaining oil market stability.

headline: U.S., Japan reaffirm commitment to complete denuclearization of N. Korea in high-level talks
summary: WASHINGTON, Oct. 12 (Yonhap) -- The United States and Japan reaffirmed their com...
body_text:
WASHINGTON, Oct. 12 (Yonhap) -- The United States and Japan reaffirmed their commitment to the complete denuclearization of North Korea during high-level talks in Tokyo on Monday, the U.S. State Department said.

U.S. Under Secretary of State for Political Affairs Allison Hooker and Japanese Senior Deputy Minister for Foreign Affairs Hiroyuki Namazu made the commitment during the countries' second U.S.-Japan Free and Open Indo-Pacific (FOIP) Dialogue held in Tokyo, according to a department press release.

"They noted progress in U.S.-Japan defense industrial cooperation and reaffirmed their commitment to the complete denuclearization of the DPRK and the immediate resolution of the abductions issue," the department said, referring to North Korea by its official name, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea.

The statement comes as U.S. President Donald Trump has repeatedly expressed his willingness to resume dialogue with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, raising speculation over the possibility of renewed diplomacy between Washington and Pyongyang.

The two sides also discussed ways to strengthen cooperation with regional allies and partners on security issues, while welcoming Japan's growing cooperation with the North Atlantic Treaty Organization.

The dialogue also covered economic security, critical minerals supply chains, energy security and maritime security cooperation in Southeast Asia and the Pacific Islands, according to the department.

headline: Germany needs diesel deal with Russia — politician
summary: There is no way to halt the decline of German industry without affordable energy sources from Russia, Sahra Wagenknecht emphasized
body_text:
BERLIN, October 12. /TASS/. Sahra Wagenknecht, the founder of Germany’s BSW party (formerly known as the Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance - Reason and Justice party), has called on the German government to strike a diesel deal with Russia, as the United States has done, and to abandon the anti-Russian sanctions.

"This is utter madness - the US administration is again importing diesel from Russia in an effort to curb the rapidly growing fuel prices for American consumers. But the German government continues to adhere to its futile sanctions policy, which is driving our economy toward collapse and making our citizens increasingly poorer," she wrote on X.

She noted that fuel prices in Germany are too high. "Germany also needs a diesel deal with Russia and, more broadly, the resumption of Russian oil and gas supplies," she stated. "There is no way to halt the decline of our industry without affordable energy sources from Russia," Wagenknecht emphasized.

She recalled that on Wednesday, Saxony-Anhalt’s state parliament will vote on a joint resolution put forward by her party and Alternative for Germany, which calls on the German government to lift sanctions against Russia and support diplomatic efforts to resolve the conflict in Ukraine.

Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump held a phone call on October 9, during which they discussed, among other things, petroleum product supplies. The Russian president said that Moscow had reiterated its readiness to supply oil and petroleum products to the United States and global markets. According to Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak, Russia will lift its ban on diesel exports ahead of schedule and is ready to supply 300,000 tons of diesel in October, increasing the volume to 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons in December. Monthly supplies could subsequently reach 3 million tons. The US administration, in turn, issued a general license authorizing Russian diesel supplies to the global market until April 7, 2027.

headline: Vietnam attaches great importance to strengthening strategic partnership with Russia
summary: Vietnamese Minister of Public Security Luong Tam Quang noted that transnational criminal groups, organized crime, high-tech crime and emerging forms of crime, including offenses involving foreign nationals, pose numerous challenges to both countries
body_text:
HANOI, October 12. /TASS/. Vietnam has always attached great importance to strengthening and developing its traditional friendship and comprehensive strategic partnership with Russia, Vietnamese Minister of Public Security Luong Tam Quang said at a meeting with a delegation from Russia’s Federal Penitentiary Service (FSIN) led by its director, Arkady Gostev, in Hanoi.

The Vietnamese minister of Public Security said Vietnam seeks to strengthen cooperation in security and law enforcement by building political trust, improving coordination and reinforcing the long-standing ties between the two countries. He was quoted by the Vietnam News Agency as saying that such cooperation should be reliable, substantive and effective.

Quang discussed the current security and law enforcement situation. He noted that transnational criminal groups, organized crime, high-tech crime and emerging forms of crime, including offenses involving foreign nationals, pose numerous challenges to both countries. These challenges require the Vietnamese and Russian authorities to continue enhancing coordination, exchanging information and expertise, and improving cooperation in security and law enforcement, including the enforcement of criminal judgments, he said.

The director of Russia’s FSIN, in turn, praised the traditional friendship between Moscow and Hanoi and the positive results of cooperation between the Russian government and Vietnam’s Ministry of Public Security in recent years. Gostev reaffirmed Russia’s commitment to expanding ties between the two agencies, particularly through the exchange of expertise in correctional facility management, prisoner education and rehabilitation, and staff training, thereby further deepening security and law enforcement cooperation between the two countries.

analysis.framing: The article frames the meeting as a diplomatic affirmation of Vietnam-Russia security cooperation, emphasizing mutual commitment to strengthening ties without critical scrutiny or context.

This term evokes a warm, longstanding bond and is a standard diplomatic euphemism that may gloss over complexities or tensions.

body_text:
A teacher from the UAE injured in an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh has been assured she will be able to complete her Umrah pilgrimage once she recovers.

The teacher, whose name was not released, was travelling with a colleague from Abu Dhabi to Makkah via Riyadh when the airport came under attack on Saturday.

Saudi Health Minister Fahad Al Jalajel visited the two women in hospital on Sunday when he went to see people injured in the attack and find out about their medical care.

AnalysisHouthi attacks stretch Saudi air defences to all corners of country

One of the teachers told the minister how their journey had been interrupted, according to Saudi state-run television channel Al Ekhbariya. She praised the doctors treating her.

Mr Al Jalajel said King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman had instructed officials to ensure the women received full support throughout their recovery.

“You’re not part of what happened. We know that. For that reason, King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman are telling us to take full care of you, even the recovery, and that you continue on your Umrah,” he told her.

Saudi Arabia has extended the suspension of operations at the airport following the deadly attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels at the weekend.

The General Authority of Civil Aviation said on Monday that the suspension would continue while checks on the safety and operational readiness of airport sites were completed. It did not give a date or time for the reopening.

Etihad Airways has cancelled all flights between Abu Dhabi and Riyadh until October 19, extending disruption to services between the UAE and the Saudi capital into next week. Flydubai has cancelled Riyadh flights until Wednesday, while Emirates and Air Arabia services have been affected.

Services to other Saudi destinations have also been impacted. Etihad cancelled four flights between Abu Dhabi and Dammam on Monday, with all services on the route cancelled on Tuesday and Wednesday. Selected Jeddah flights have been cancelled until Thursday.

headline: Houthi official warns of 'swift, painful response' if US enters Yemen war
summary: A Houthi official on Monday warned the US it would receive a "painful response" if it entered the war in Yemen, where Saudi Arabia has reportedly requested Washington's help in dealing with the group as it weathers repeated attacks. Yemen's civil war -- in which a Saudi-led military coalition supports the government against the Iran-backed Houthis -- reignited in July, months into the wider regional conflict that has roiled energy markets and plunged the Middle East into crisis.
body_text:
A Houthi official on Monday warned the US it would receive a "painful response" if it entered the war in Yemen, where Saudi Arabia has reportedly requested Washington's help in dealing with the group as it weathers repeated attacks.

Yemen's civil war -- in which a Saudi-led military coalition supports the government against the Iran-backed Houthis -- reignited in July, months into the wider regional conflict that has roiled energy markets and plunged the Middle East into crisis.

The Houthis quickly began targeting Saudi oil facilities, tankers and transport hubs, including with a string of lethal strikes on Riyadh's airport, rocking the world's top oil exporter.

Following an attack Saturday at the airport that killed 13 people, US President Donald Trump said he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the group, after having reportedly rebuffed previous requests for help from the kingdom.

"If the US becomes involved in the aggression against Yemen, we will not deliberate over the decision to respond, rather, there will be a swift and painful response targeting the US and all its interests in the region," Houthi political bureau member Mohammed Al Bukhaiti told AFP in an interview.

He also warned "all employees and workers at Saudi oil facilities and airports to stay away from these sites, as they have become legitimate targets".

Saturday's strike on King Khalid International Airport was the deadliest attack on Saudi soil in more than a decade, and also left hundreds wounded.

Trump said the attack was "not acceptable" and that he would be speaking to the kingdom's de facto leader Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, telling reporters the US was "going to look at" the possibility of joining Saudi strikes.

Four people died in earlier strikes on Wednesday and Thursday, and another was killed on Sunday. Operations remained suspended at the sprawling airport on Riyadh's outskirts on Monday.

Bukhaiti said the purpose of the campaign against Saudi targets was to send a message to the crown prince "that he can no longer wage aggression against Yemen from a safe position".

Saudi energy minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman told an energy conference in Riyadh on Monday that the recent events had "tested our infrastructure, our institutions, our people, and our resilience".

"The events of recent weeks are serious, our response must be equally serious."

CCTV footage of Saturday's attack released by Saudi authorities showed Muslim pilgrims in religious attire waiting in departure lounges before a sudden blast tore through the building and brought down flaming debris.

The atmosphere in Riyadh remained tense on Monday, as state broadcaster Al Ekhbariya said the military coalition was responding to drone and missile threats, and Australia's embassy warned its citizens in the city to shelter in place.

The US embassy in Saudi Arabia said US government employees must obtain its authorisation before using any airport in the kingdom, and urged US citizens to "take extreme caution" if they chose to do so.

The mission also said "American citizens have been detained for taking photos of recent events" in Saudi Arabia, without specifying how many or whether they had been released.

The UAE's national carrier Etihad Airways announced on Monday that it was cancelling all flights to and from Riyadh until next week due to "regional disruption", and also suspended flights to Dammam and Jeddah.

Bahrain's national carrier Gulf Air said it too was cancelling all Riyadh flights until Saturday.

US operator Delta announced it would delay the launch of direct flights from Atlanta to Riyadh -- scheduled for October 23 -- as US air safety regulators warned of continued safety risks.

Despite vast spending on military hardware, the Houthi attacks on oil, military and transport facilities across the large, mostly desert country are stretching Saudi defences.

Thomas Juneau, security analyst at Ottawa University, said that despite some success, "Saudi Arabia is so large that it's simply impossible for them to consistently defend themselves".

Riyadh leads an international coalition that has supported Yemen's government militarily since 2015, including by seeking to exert control over Yemeni airspace and the airport in the Houthi-held capital Sanaa.

Juneau said the Houthis now "want to do to Saudi Arabia what Saudi Arabia does to them".

The long-running Yemeni civil war has created a deeply entrenched humanitarian crisis in the impoverished country.

UN rights chief Volker Turk said he was "appalled by the repeated attacks" on Saudi Arabia, but urged both sides to back down.

"The disastrous toll of this conflict on civilians, both in Yemen and in Saudi Arabia, is a reminder to all parties that continued fighting will only unleash further misery with no end in sight."

headline: Reform UK leader says will revise assistance to Ukraine due to corruption there
summary: Nigel Farage described Ukraine as one of the most corrupt countries in the world
body_text:
LONDON, October 12. /TASS/. Nigel Farage, the leader of the Reform UK party, says he may revise financial assistance to Ukraine amid the wide-spread corruption in that country if his party comes to power in the United Kingdom.

"I’ve never said we shouldn’t support Ukraine, ever. But I have said I would have a keen look to make sure British taxpayers’ money is not being swallowed up in corruption," he said at a press conference on his party’s program for reforming the UK’s asylum system.

According to Farage, Ukraine is "one of the most corrupt countries on earth," with Vladimir Zelensky and his administration being bogged down in corruption. "Zelensky’s administration has been rocked by corruption claims, which perhaps makes at some point a general election there an important thing to do," he said.

According to the latest opinion poll conducted by YouGov, Reform UK is second in terms of popularity in the country, with 22% of voters being ready to support it. The ruling Labour Party tops the list (27%) and the Conservative Party is third (20%). The Liberal Democrats and the Green Party are supported by 11% of voters each. The next parliamentary elections are to be held before August 2029.

headline: Rising freight, transport costs account for bulk of oil price increase — Novak
summary: According to Russian Deputy Prime Minister, during a meeting in Riyadh, OPEC and OPEC+ ministers discussed the global surge in transport, freight, and insurance costs, which have increased five-to tenfold on certain routes
body_text:
MOSCOW, October 12. /TASS/. Rising costs for oil transportation and vessel freight have accounted for the majority of the increase in oil prices, Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said in an interview with the Vesti news program.

According to Novak, during a meeting in Riyadh, OPEC and OPEC+ ministers discussed the global surge in transport, freight, and insurance costs, which have increased five-to tenfold on certain routes. "Today, ministers noted that the rise in freight, transport, and insurance costs accounted for the bulk of this price increase [for oil]," he said.

"Clearly, this reflects current global risks, a shortage of vessels, the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, and military risks. We are also seeing attacks on civilian vessels transporting oil or petroleum products in various parts of the world. This, too, contributes to rising shipping costs," he added.

Novak noted that during the meeting, OPEC and OPEC+ ministers expressed concern over the situation, agreeing to monitor it jointly and work with international organizations to stabilize the market. "We also agreed to continue our meetings in order to discuss such issues by consensus and make joint decisions aimed at balancing the market," he emphasized.

headline: Houthis say Saudi Arabia delivered nearly 120 strikes against Yemen in past day

DOHA, October 12. /TASS/. The Houthis from the Yemeni rebel movement Ansar Allah say that Saudi Arabia has delivered nearly 120 strikes against Yemen during the day.

According to a post on Houthi spokesman Yahya Saria’s Telegram channel, Saudi F-16 and Typhoon fighter jets "delivered 119 air and missile strikes" over the past 24 hours targeting "civilian facilities in the capital city of Sanaa," as well as in the Ibb, Lahij, Marib, Saada, Taiz, Al Bayda, and Al Jawf governorates. Missiles were launched from Najran and Jizan.

Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport was attacked by the Houthis on October 10 and 11. According to the Saudi authorities, the October 10 attack killed 12 people and left 309 others injured. One person was killed and eleven others were wounded in the second attack on October 11, which also caused material damage to the airport. Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation announced earlier that the airport’s suspension would be extended following recent attacks.

"I can ⁠confirm our assessment that it is highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran, almost certainly directed by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard," Burnham told parliament. Iran has rejected any connection to the Fairford incident.

"Tehran has had no involvement in this matter, and if the British ​government possesses any documents or evidence to support its claims, it should present them," said Iran's Ambassador to Britain, Seyed ‌Ali Mousavi, according to Iranian state news agency, IRNA.

British foreign minister Ed Miliband said he had summoned the Iranian ambassador.

Details around the suspected plot remain thin. The five detained men were later released without charge on police bail "under stringent conditions", and two other men who were arrested – including a British-Iranian national – were also subsequently released.

British Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood told parliament that a known individual based in Iran – whom she did not name – was believed to be behind what had happened.

"The UK has also concluded this event demonstrates the IRGC’s continued willingness to project hostile activity beyond its borders through covert networks and proxy actors," the statement said.

headline: Slovak PM says EU has paid heavy price for oil crisis, continuing war
summary: The European Union is isolating itself from the rest of the world and has no say in settling military conflicts around the world and in addressing the most pressing international issues, Robert Fico said
body_text:
BRATISLAVA, October 12. /TASS/. The European Union has paid a heavy price for the oil crisis and the ongoing wars, Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico said.

"So far, only the European Union has been paying a huge price for the oil crisis and the wars taking place around us," he said on a video posted by his party Direction-Social Democracy, known as SMER, on its Facebook page (Facebook is banned in Russia due to its ownership by Meta, which has been designated as extremist).

The European Union is isolating itself from the rest of the world and has no say in settling military conflicts around the world and in addressing the most pressing international issues, Fico said, adding that the EU’s sanctions policy is ineffective.

The Slovak prime minister stressed that his country is against halting Russian oil and gas imports to Europe. He pledged that Slovakia will remain committed to a sovereign foreign policy and will spare no effort to persuade the European Union to revise its decision banning energy supplied from Russia. Thus, Bratislava challenged the European Commission’s ban on Russian gas imports with the European Court of Justice, he recalled.

Slovakia will take an active role in the European Union, Fico stated. "We must say something about what we intend to do regarding the pro-war policy that currently dominates within the EU," he emphasized, noting that the EU summit will take place this Thursday and Friday. The international situation, he said, is "very bad." "I fear that a military conflict could break out," the Slovak prime minister added.

headline: What we know about Pope Leo XIV's planned lung operation this week
summary: Pope Leo XIV is expected to undergo surgery to remove a lung nodule this week at Rome’s Gemelli hospital, with doctors anticipating a recovery of about seven days. body_text:
Pope Leo XIV is expected to undergo surgery to remove a lung nodule this week at Rome’s Gemelli hospital, with doctors anticipating a recovery of about seven days. The 71-year-old pontiff is due to travel to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru on November 6, though the Vatican has not confirmed the operation date.

Issued on: 13/10/2026 - 00:20

Pope Leo XIV has said he will undergo an operation to remove a lump on his lung this week, marking an unusual personal medical announcement by a pontiff. The 71-year-old is expected to recover in about a week, potentially allowing him to begin an 11-day visit to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru on November 6.

Pope Leo XIV has said he will have an operation to remove a lump on his lung this week, the first time a pope has made a personal medical announcement of this kind.

The 71-year-old is otherwise healthy and is known for his love of sport.

Here is what we know:

The pope said the operation was planned "in the coming days" and the Vatican press office said it would be at the beginning of the week, without giving a date.

Italian media have speculated that the operation could be on Tuesday, although the pope is due to preside over a Mass in St Peter's Basilica on Wednesday morning with Church leaders from around the world and there have so far been no announced changes in his schedule.

The Vatican press office has said doctors expect the pope's recovery to take around a week. That would make it possible for him to leave for his visit to Latin America as planned on November 6.

The 11-day trip will take him to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru – a country close to the pope's heart as he worked there as a missionary for two decades and took on Peruvian citizenship.

To display this content from YouTube, you must enable advertisement tracking and audience measurement.

One of your browser extensions seems to be blocking the video player from loading. To watch this content, you may need to disable it on this site.

A pulmonary nodule is a small growth of tissue in the lung. Most are benign, meaning they are non-cancerous. But a small percentage can be an early stage of lung cancer.

Most small nodules cause no symptoms and are only discovered during checks for other health issues.

Larger nodules can cause shortness of breath, chest pain and persistent coughing – sometimes with blood.

The operation is normally carried out under general anaesthetic with the patient breathing through a tube.

Read morePope Leo says will undergo surgery for early-stage lung nodule

The operation is expected to take place at Rome's Gemelli hospital, where popes are usually treated.

Leo's predecessor Francis spent weeks there for treatment before his death last year.

John Paul II, head of the Church from 1978 until his death in 2005, was treated nine times at Gemelli – Rome's largest hospital – and spent a total of 153 days there.

He quipped that the hospital was like "Vatican number three".

The Vatican ultimately created a top-floor apartment at the hospital site, accessed by a long corridor guarded by Italian and Vatican police.

Besides the pope's room, the suite reportedly includes a meeting room for medical staff, a kitchen, bathroom and rest areas.

There is also a small chapel.

SEOUL, Oct. 13 (Yonhap) -- North Korea has test-fired a tactical ballistic missile as part of efforts to upgrade a key component of its weapons systems, state media reported Tuesday.

The report came a day after South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) detected multiple ballistic missiles launched from the Pyongyang area toward the East Sea.

The North's missile administration "test-fired a tactical ballistic missile on October 12 to confirm the success in the research for the technical upgrading of an important core element," the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) reported.

The administration claimed that the upgrade "was a big success heralding an important change in improving the performance and sophistication of all offensive weapon systems," the KCNA said, describing the test as part of its regular activities.

Pope Leo XIV is expected to undergo surgery to remove a lung nodule this week at Rome’s Gemelli hospital, with doctors anticipating a recovery of about seven days. The 71-year-old pontiff is due to travel to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru on November 6, though the Vatican has not confirmed the operation date.

Issued on: 13/10/2026 - 00:20

Pope Leo XIV has said he will undergo an operation to remove a lump on his lung this week, marking an unusual personal medical announcement by a pontiff. The 71-year-old is expected to recover in about a week, potentially allowing him to begin an 11-day visit to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru on November 6.

Pope Leo XIV has said he will have an operation to remove a lump on his lung this week, the first time a pope has made a personal medical announcement of this kind.

The 71-year-old is otherwise healthy and is known for his love of sport.

Here is what we know:

The pope said the operation was planned "in the coming days" and the Vatican press office said it would be at the beginning of the week, without giving a date.

Italian media have speculated that the operation could be on Tuesday, although the pope is due to preside over a Mass in St Peter's Basilica on Wednesday morning with Church leaders from around the world and there have so far been no announced changes in his schedule.

The Vatican press office has said doctors expect the pope's recovery to take around a week. That would make it possible for him to leave for his visit to Latin America as planned on November 6.

The 11-day trip will take him to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru – a country close to the pope's heart as he worked there as a missionary for two decades and took on Peruvian citizenship.

A pulmonary nodule is a small growth of tissue in the lung. Most are benign, meaning they are non-cancerous. But a small percentage can be an early stage of lung cancer.

Most small nodules cause no symptoms and are only discovered during checks for other health issues.

Larger nodules can cause shortness of breath, chest pain and persistent coughing – sometimes with blood.

The operation is normally carried out under general anaesthetic with the patient breathing through a tube.

Read morePope Leo says will undergo surgery for early-stage lung nodule

The operation is expected to take place at Rome's Gemelli hospital, where popes are usually treated.

Leo's predecessor Francis spent weeks there for treatment before his death last year.

John Paul II, head of the Church from 1978 until his death in 2005, was treated nine times at Gemelli – Rome's largest hospital – and spent a total of 153 days there.

He quipped that the hospital was like "Vatican number three".

The Vatican ultimately created a top-floor apartment at the hospital site, accessed by a long corridor guarded by Italian and Vatican police.

Besides the pope's room, the suite reportedly includes a meeting room for medical staff, a kitchen, bathroom and rest areas.

There is also a small chapel.

headline: (2nd LD) N. Korea reports test-firing of 'tactical' ballistic missile to improve weapons systems
summary: SEOUL, Oct. 13 (Yonhap) -- North Korea has test-fired a tactical ballistic missi...
body_text:
(ATTN: ADDS more info in 7th para; CHANGES photo)

SEOUL, Oct. 13 (Yonhap) -- North Korea has test-fired a tactical ballistic missile to upgrade a key component of its weapons systems, which it called a "big success," the country's state media reported Tuesday.

The report came a day after South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) detected multiple ballistic missiles launched from the Pyongyang area toward the East Sea.

North Korea's missile administration "test-fired a tactical ballistic missile on October 12 to confirm the success in the research for the technical upgrading of an important core element," the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) reported.

The administration claimed that the upgrade "was a big success heralding an important change in improving the performance and sophistication of all offensive weapon systems," it added, describing the test as part of regular activities.

The North did not disclose further details about the test-firing.

The JCS earlier noted that North Korea launched multiple types of ballistic missiles, with one specific kind of missile flying more than 900 kilometers, and that South Korean and U.S. authorities were conducting a detailed analysis of their specifications.

U.S. Pacific Command (PACOM) said Monday that North Korea's latest launches involved two ballistic missiles.

Monday's launches marked the North's 16th ballistic missile launch of the year, coming nine days after its previous launch on Oct. 3.

They also came four days after South Korea publicly announced its first and successful test-firing of a homegrown hypersonic glide vehicle (HGV) in an event also attended by President Lee Jae Myung.

Hypersonic missiles are often described as potential "game changers" on the battlefield, as they travel at speeds of Mach 5 or faster and can maneuver along unconventional trajectories, making them difficult to track and intercept.

The South Korean government's disclosure of the advanced weapons test was seen as an apparent demonstration of its deterrence capabilities against North Korea following a land mine explosion in the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) on Sept. 21 that injured three South Korean soldiers.

headline: Saudi warning system stayed silent before deadly airport attacks
summary: By Timour AzhariRIYADH, Oct 13 (Reuters) - Saudi Arabia stopped issuing public warnings of imminent military attacks days before a series of deadly strikes on Riyadh airport that killed at least 18 people and wounded more than 300.The government has not said why there were no alerts to the public before the four Riyadh attacks in the past week. The warnings had served to highlight the violence undermining the kingdom's efforts to project an image of calm to its people and the world during its war with Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis.
body_text:
RIYADH, Oct 13 (Reuters) - Saudi Arabia stopped issuing public warnings of imminent military attacks days before a series of deadly strikes on Riyadh airport that killed at least 18 people and wounded more than 300.

The government has not said why there were no alerts to the public before the four Riyadh attacks in the past week.

The warnings had served to highlight the violence undermining the kingdom's efforts to project an image of calm to its people and the world during its war with Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis.

Their absence during the airport strikes raised questions about Saudi Arabia's vulnerability to attack and about its ability to protect residents and visitors, four Western and Arab officials in the region and political analysts told Reuters.

It also reflected efforts to maintain a sense of normalcy, they said.

"They (the Saudi government) want to have it both ways: to launch a military operation and at the same time try to give confidence to the population and external stakeholders," said Sultan Alamer, a US-based Saudi academic and Senior Resident Fellow at the Middle East Policy Council think tank.

The Saudi civil defence - a national emergency management, rescue and firefighting agency which operates under the interior ministry and issues early warning alerts - and the Saudi government media office did not respond to emailed questions on why no alerts were issued.

Saudi Arabia's approach is also one that some regional analysts said risked backfiring because the absence of warnings has heightened uncertainty in the kingdom.

On Monday, Saudi Arabia's civil defence authority issued its first alerts since September 29, warning of potential threats in Riyadh and southern cities.

Reuters was unable to ascertain whether the decision to issue alerts again was a response to the airport attacks, and the Saudi government did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the matter.

All Gulf countries have been hit by Iranian drones and missiles since the US-Iran war began in February, but their governments have handled public warnings differently.

Qatar's interior ministry has issued mobile phone alerts before nearly every attack, including most recent attacks in July, when residents were warned to stay inside and away from windows.

Bahrain and Kuwait have repeatedly sounded sirens urging people to take shelter.

Saudi Arabia began issuing threat alerts to mobile phones and social media accounts via a national early warning system in May. But despite increasing Houthi attacks leading up to last week, the system went silent.

The last alert before last week's attacks was issued on September 29, for the southern province of Najran, according to posts on the civil defence X account.

The civil defences authority has continued to issue warnings about staying out of harm's way during adverse weather, including rain and flooding, and did so as recently as Monday.

It also warned residents not to share images, rumours or information about interceptions and impact sites, including in a post on Monday, under government regulations issued in March.

Reuters could not determine whether anyone had faced prosecution for sharing such information, and the Saudi government media office did not respond to a request for comment on the matter.

Before last week's airport attacks, officials from an allied Western government asked Saudi authorities why the alerts had stopped, two officials with direct knowledge of the matter said.

The response was that the alerts were too disruptive and many citizens had complained they were being woken by them at night, the officials said.

The Saudi government media office and Saudi officials did not respond to requests for comment on the assertion.

Former US ambassador to Saudi Arabia Michael Ratney said Riyadh was trying to balance public messaging on attacks with efforts to prevent disruption in the kingdom but had ended up adding to a sense of unease about the strikes.

"Their approach to public messaging seems like a corollary to the quandary they are in: They need to respond to the Houthis but don't want that to result in societal disruption and their public messaging is a reflection of that," he said.

"But the lack of alerts of incoming Houthi attacks creates the very nervousness they are trying to avoid."

Ali Shihabi, a Saudi analyst close to the government, said that with or without early warnings, the kingdom would struggle to defend all of its assets because of its size.

"In Saudi Arabia you have too much to protect. It's a huge country with airports, pipelines and oil facilities. There is just not enough coverage to defend everything at once, not enough Patriots (missile defence systems), interceptors and missile batteries to do it all," he said.

"Saudi Arabia has an unlimited need for air defences," he added."

Despite the attacks, Saudi Arabia hosted an international conference on Monday, though major oil bosses dropped out.

At the World Petroleum ‌Council Energy Congress in Riyadh, Saudi Prince Abdulaziz bin Salaman, a brother of the Saudi crown prince and the kingdom's energy minister, struck a defiant tone while acknowledging risks and Saudi Arabia's intent to keep its economic plans on track. He thanked all who had travelled to Riyadh "because you know this country is safe" but added: "Our gatheringhere does not mean the risk is gone." "We will never forfeit any chance to maintain our commitment and our vision," he said.

EMBASSIES ISSUE THEIR OWN INTERNAL ALERTS

Despite no public alerts being issued this month until Monday, Riyadh has been attacked about a dozen times, two of the Western officials said.

During that time, Western embassies in the kingdom have been issuing their own internal missile and drone alerts to staff, according to three people familiar with the matter and alerts seen by Reuters.

These internal alerts are compiled from a mixture of US and other Western government intelligence and input from Saudi authorities, one of those people said.

They include alerts sent to staff around the time of two first airport strikes last week according to the people familiar with the matter.

They said that even the embassies had received no internal warning before Saturday's airport strike, without offering an explanation.

Reuters could not determine why no warning came before Saturday's attack, the deadliest of last week's attacks.

On Sunday, Saudi state TV released footage of Saturday's strike.

It showed several shots of travellers in the airport terminal. Dozens lined up to board a flight. Men and women sat in chairs waiting, their eyes trained on the screens of their mobile phones as they scrolled.

Then, the bright orange flash of a missile explosion.

(Reporting by Timour Azhari; Editing by Andrew Mills and Timothy Heritage)

headline: Latvia launches reconnaissance drone along borders with Russia, Belarus
summary: This refers to the Penguin C UAS, designed to detect moving targets, conduct surveillance and gather intelligence
body_text:
MOSCOW, October 13. /TASS/. Latvia’s security agencies launched a reconnaissance drone that is flying near the borders with Russia and Belarus, a source in air traffic control services told TASS.

"The drone was launched near the village of Cibuli, close to the Russian border. It then flew parallel to the border and is now flying near the border with Belarus," the source said.

He identified the aircraft as a Penguin C UAS, designed to detect moving targets, conduct surveillance and gather intelligence.

"The drone is flying at an altitude of about 1.2 kilometers, outside flight corridors designated for civil and general aviation, including low-altitude routes," the source said, adding that this was not the first such launch this month.
