headline: IMF upgrades 2026 growth forecast but warns of 'split' outlook
summary: The International Monetary Fund on Tuesday forecast that global growth in 2026 would slow less than previously expected due to advanced economies' "resilience" in the face of war-fuelled energy prices, but warned that low-income countries remained vulnerable to the supply shock. In its World Economic Outlook (WEO) released at the organization's Annual Meetings in Bangkok, the Fund raised its 2026 global growth forecast by 0.1 percentage points to 3.1 percent, compared to 3.5 percent growth in 2025.
body_text:
The International Monetary Fund on Tuesday forecast that global growth in 2026 would slow less than previously expected due to advanced economies' "resilience" in the face of war-fuelled energy prices, but warned that low-income countries remained vulnerable to the supply shock.

In its World Economic Outlook (WEO) released at the organization's Annual Meetings in Bangkok, the Fund raised its 2026 global growth forecast by 0.1 percentage points to 3.1 percent, compared to 3.5 percent growth in 2025.

The IMF warned that while many advanced economies have been buoyed by rising investment in artificial intelligence (AI) technology, poorer countries that are not benefiting from that boom face stark choices as they deal with high energy prices due to the US war on Iran.

"The global economy has been resilient, but that resilience is under strain, with risks to growth tilted to the downside," said Silvana Tenreyro, the IMF's chief economist.

The United States' war on Iran, launched in February, has plunged the Middle East into violence and seen global energy prices skyrocket as a result of Tehran's retaliatory actions.

Prices of refined petroleum products remain between 70 and 95 percent above pre-war levels, putting pressure on countries dependent on energy imports for economic activity.

The war is in its eighth month, and Tenreyro warned that "a prolonged conflict in the Middle East could put additional pressures on inflation and slow down growth."

Energy-importing countries not exposed to the AI boom remain the most vulnerable, creating what the IMF termed a "bifurcated outlook" in its WEO report.

The report detailed that the twin economic forces of the war in Iran and the AI technology boom had created a "fragmented" world economy.

"Headwinds from a prolonged war and persistent geopolitical tensions could revive inflationary pressures, strain fiscal and external positions, and hit energy-importing and low-income countries hardest," it said.

"At the same time, the current technology tailwind could stop abruptly if expectations about AI-related profits and productivity gains are reassessed, weakening investment and tightening financial conditions."

The IMF's split view of the world economy was evident in its specific projections.

The Middle East and Central Asia region, exposed directly to the Iran war as Tehran has targeted Washington's Gulf allies, saw the IMF forecast economic contraction of 0.3 percent in 2026.

Saudi Arabia saw one of the sharpest falls in projected growth, with the IMF forecasting a contraction of 3.3 percent -- a cut in the forecast of 5.0 percentage points.

The IMF said the region is expected to bounce back quickly once the war is over, but there remains high uncertainty as to when that will be.

In advanced economies, growth fuelled by the AI boom and other factors remained strong.

The world's advanced economies were forecast to grow by 2.1 percent in 2026, with those in the AI supply chain such as Taiwan and South Korea posting significantly higher figures.

Growth in China, the world's second-largest economy, was expected to slow by 0.5 percentage points to 4.5 percent this year, the IMF said, mainly due to weak domestic demand.

Global inflation remained set to accelerate to 4.7 percent in 2026, fuelled by the Iran war and the AI boom, with effects spread across both advanced and developing economies.

IMF Chief Economist Tenreyro warned that "urgent action" was required by all countries in the face of downside risks.

On the fiscal side, she called on governments to only use temporary and targeted measures to help ease the burden on the public of high energy and other costs.

In lockstep, "monetary policy should remain firmly focused on price stability," she added, indicating that interest rate hikes to curb high inflation were appropriate.

"The economy has been resilient, but that resilience is reaching its limits," she said. "The task ahead is to move from coping to rebuilding, restoring fiscal space, and rebuilding supply-side resilience."

body_text:
Cristiano Ronaldo was on the scoresheet as Al Nassr got their AFC Champions League Elite campaign back on track with a comfortable win over Neftchi Fergana.

Ronaldo scored the second of Nassr's goals just before the break after Angelo Gabriel had given the hosts a 33rd-minute lead.

Alishev Odilov had reduced the deficit in the 51st minute before an Anvarjon Gofurov own goal sealed a 3-1 victory for Nassr.

Al Ahli overcome Al Wasl in fiery AFC Champions League clash

Kick-off was delayed at Al Awwal Park due to a security alert issued by Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence. Riyadh has suffered a series of ​deadly ​attacks ‌by the ⁠Iran-aligned Houthis over the past week.

Supporters were allowed to remain in their seats as authorities carried out safety protocols before the match kicked off 20 minutes after it was scheduled.

Ronaldo, 41, was spotted kissing the badge on his shirt during the warm-up. He was also pictured holding the shirt up to his face to cover his eyes in an emotional moment.

The Portuguese superstar scored the 981st goal of his career in the 42nd minute, latching on to a knockdown from Ayman Yahya in the area before firing past Neftchi goalkeeper Botirali Ergashev.

"Important win tonight. We keep building," Ronaldo posted in a message on his social media channels after the match.

Angelo broke the deadlock in the 33rd minute, meeting a cross inside the box and turning the ball into the net to give Al Nassr the lead.

Odilov capitalised on a Nawaf Boushal blunder to spark life back into the Uzbek champions in the 51st minute, but a red card shown to Ali Bayev for violent conduct after he caught Nassr defender Mohamed Simakan swung momentum back in Nassr's favour.

Nassr made the extra man count on 78 minutes. Bojan Cecer turned the ball into his own net, handing the Saudi champions all three points and their first win in this season's competition after they were routed 4-0 in their first match at Al Ain.

Ange Postecoglou revealed after the match that he had been worried about his players' mental state before the match following the deadly attacks on Riyadh.

“I was worried about the players during the match because I care about them, but I was very happy with the professionalism they showed,” the Australian told reporters.

Postecoglou said the club will monitor injuries to Kingsley Coman and Mohamed Simakan.

French forward Coman was forced off injured after only 13 minutes, while Simakan was withdrawn following the red-card challenge by Bayev.

Al Ain maintained their 100 per cent start to the league phase with a thumping win over Iraq's Al Quwa Al Jawiya in Basrah.

Houssine Rahimi struck twice as Al Ain raced to a 4-0 lead at the break, as the former champions cruised to a second successive win in emphatic fashion.

Alejandro Romero had opened the scoring in the 13th minute before Saed Al Rodsan turned into his own net to double Al Ain's advantage.

Rahimi, who struck twice for Al Ain in their victory over Nassr in September, grabbed another brace against Al Quwa before half-time to kill the contest.

Mohammed Jawad grabbed a consolation goal in the 89th minute.

“We know what we can do, and the players did their job excellently until the end. They deserve this victory," Al Ain coach Vladimir Ivic told reporters.

“We sent a message to ourselves about what we can do, and that is the most important thing for me.”

Victory took Al Ain top of Group B ahead of Esteghlal on goal difference.

Tijjani Reijnders was on target as Al Qadsiah were held to a 1-1 draw at Pakhtakor.

headline: Russia says Europe bought $320 billion in hydrocarbons since 2022
summary: Russia said on Monday that European Union countries had bought $320.7 billion worth of its energy resources since 2022, despite sanctions over the war in Ukraine. The figure fuelled tensions as European officials criticised a US deal to import Russian diesel, while Stockholm called for the bloc to use frozen Russian assets to boost support for Kyiv.

Russia said on Monday that European Union countries had bought $320.7 billion worth of its energy resources since 2022, despite sanctions over the war in Ukraine. The figure fuelled tensions as European officials criticised a US deal to import Russian diesel, while Stockholm called for the bloc to use frozen Russian assets to boost support for Kyiv.

Issued on: 13/10/2026 - 05:10

Russia said on Monday that it had sold European countries more than $320 billion worth of hydrocarbons since 2022, despite sanctions imposed over the war in Ukraine.

"For the period from 2022 to today, this figure amounts to $320.7 billion. This is the volume of energy resource deliveries to European Union countries," Russian Deputy Prime Minister in charge of energy Alexander Novak said on television.

He said European countries purchased $21.3 billion worth of Russian hydrocarbons in the first nine months of 2026 alone.

"In other words, despite sanctions-related restrictions, we continue to supply energy resources in certain areas for which exemptions have been granted," he added.

Novak said Russian oil exports may reach their pre-war levels by the end of the year.

Swedish Foreign Minister Maria Malmer Stenergard pointed to the Russian figure as she arrived in Luxembourg on Monday for a meeting with her European Union counterparts.

She contrasted it with the 218.7 billion euros ($244 billion) in support that the EU had sent to Ukraine since the start of the war.

"That would be a game-changer, and a game-changer is exactly what Ukraine needs."

The European Union has adopted numerous sanctions against Russia since the start of the war in Ukraine in 2022, yet many countries – including France – continue to source hydrocarbons, particularly liquefied natural gas (LNG), from Moscow.

body_text:
Yesterday’s call for stronger collective defence in the Gulf by Dr Anwar Gargash, diplomatic adviser to President Sheikh Mohamed, comes at a moment when a beleaguered Iran and its remaining armed proxies have decided to escalate and target the Arab world's largest economy.

As the Iran-backed Houthis’ repeated strikes on travellers at Riyadh’s King Khalid airport show, the human cost of failing to deter attacks or intercept missiles is steep. Such attacks also strike at the region's prosperity, something that depends on transport networks, energy infrastructure, the environment and the confidence that connect active economies and those who benefit from them.

A threat to an airport or a shipping route has consequences well beyond the country directly targeted. Airlines reassess risks to flights and businesses are forced to reconsider other supply chains. Investors also have to debate the costs of operating in a volatile region. Even the mere threat of disruption can come with a heavy price tag.

As we have seen since the Iran conflict began in February, aviation is particularly vulnerable. The Gulf’s position as a global hub depends on reliable connections between Europe, Asia and Africa. Attacks, such as those seen in Riyadh, can force airlines to reroute flights, increasing costs and disrupting travel. From this tourism, trade and international connections are imperilled.

Environmental security presents another shared challenge. Attacks on oil centres, tankers and other energy infrastructure risk causing pollution that crosses international borders and presents a generational problem. The region's marine environment is already under pressure, while the concentration of energy infrastructure and shipping in a relatively confined Strait of Hormuz makes the consequences of a major spill particularly serious.

Economic security is equally inseparable from the wider crisis. Arab states may be competitors in some markets, but their economies are also linked. Disruption in one country can ripple through its neighbours.

Joint environmental response arrangements and plans to protect critical infrastructure could also improve the region’s joint ability to withstand the kind of shocking events witnessed in recent days in Saudi Arabia.

This does not mean individual Gulf countries suddenly dropping their individual national priorities or resolving every difference of opinion. It is more a question of building on the long-standing ties that unite Gulf societies and recognising the that although economic interdependence can create shared prosperity it can also come with common responses to threats. At a time when ideological actors are lashing out at those around them, the eventual outcome may just be a more aligned approach by Arab neighbours to the challenges that face them.

headline: AI investment props up global growth, but war and debt threaten outlook, IMF says
summary: By David LawderBANGKOK, Oct 13 (Reuters) - The global economy will still manage to top 3% real GDP growth this year as strong AI investment offsets the energy shock from the war in the Middle East, but downside risks are mounting and more countries are being left behind and vulnerable to rising debt loads, the International Monetary Fund said on Tuesday.Despite a more protracted conflict that has kept oil prices above $100 a barrel, the IMF is forecasting 2026 global growth at 3.1%, a slight uptick from the 3.0% it predicted in July.
body_text:
BANGKOK, Oct 13 (Reuters) - The global economy will still manage to top 3% real GDP growth this year as strong AI investment offsets the energy shock from the war in the Middle East, but downside risks are mounting and more countries are being left behind and vulnerable to rising debt loads, the International Monetary Fund said on Tuesday.

Despite a more protracted conflict that has kept oil prices above $100 a barrel, the IMF is forecasting 2026 global growth at 3.1%, a slight uptick from the 3.0% it predicted in July.

The World Economic Outlook forecast, released as global economic and finance leaders gather in Bangkok for the IMF and World Bank annual meetings, is about even with the most optimistic scenario issued in April but below 2025 global growth of 3.5%.

For 2027, the IMF predicts 3.4% global growth, flat with the July forecast and up 0.2 percentage point from April.

The slight improvement is largely due to continued strong investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure, prompting growth upgrades for key advanced economies building AI platforms and especially for countries supplying AI hardware, including South Korea, Malaysia, Mexico and Thailand, which is hosting the meetings this week.

"The global economy has been resilient, but that resilience is reaching its limits, so we need to move from just coping to rebuilding," the IMF's chief economist, Silvana Tenreyro, told a news conference. "We need to restore fiscal space. We need to rebuild supply-side resilience."

She said major downside risks to growth include a prolonged, intensified war in the Middle East that spikes inflation pressures, rising bond yields that raise government borrowing costs, El Nino-driven extreme weather events and a reassessment of AI profitability that craters investment and asset prices.

Countries and companies moved quickly to mitigate the oil price shock, drawing down reserves, substituting other suppliers and energy sources and cutting oil demand, Petya Koeva Brooks, the IMF's deputy research director, told Reuters in a separate interview. She said global growth would have fallen to 2.5% this year without these measures, but their effect is fading as the war drags on.

The IMF noted a growing divergence between countries benefiting from AI and those bypassed by it. Just 32 countries now account for 95% of global growth, compared to 54 countries in April.

Downward growth revisions have become more widespread, with the IMF downgrading 47% of economies since the April forecasts were issued, including several energy importers outside AI value chains.

Hardest hit by downgrades were the Gulf countries directly impacted by the US-Israeli war against Iran, with Saudi Arabia's GDP now forecast to contract 3.3% this year compared with the 1.7% growth predicted in July.

Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates are also expected to fall into deep recessions, with 2026 contractions of 7.6%, 16%, 16.7%, 15.6% and 3.9%, respectively.

UNITED STATES FLAT, IMPROVEMENT IN EUROPE

Among major economies, the IMF forecast US growth of 2.3% for both 2026 and 2027, unchanged for this year and 0.1 percentage point higher for next year. The US economy is expected to be supported by robust private consumption, tax cuts and AI investment, though the boost from AI will be offset by its large import content.

Euro zone growth for 2026 was upgraded to 1.1% from 0.9% in July due to stronger investment in AI, participation in AI value chains such as chemical production in Germany, and higher defense spending in EU countries. Britain's 2026 growth forecast also was upgraded by 0.3 percentage point from July to 1.3% due to larger AI investment.

The IMF forecast China's growth at 4.5% for 2026 and 4.0% for 2027, both down 0.1 percentage point from July, as higher oil prices exacerbate weak domestic demand despite strong exports.

India remains the world's fastest-growing major economy at 7.0% for both 2026 and 2027, up 0.6 percentage point this year and 0.3 percentage point next year compared with the July forecasts amid robust domestic demand, services activity and AI investment.

The AI investment surge is projected to keep upward pressure on prices, with global headline consumer price inflation forecast at 4.7% in 2026 and 4.1% for 2027.

ENERGY PRICE, AI RISKS

Participants at the IMF and World Bank meetings in Bangkok will be assessing a precarious outlook. The IMF forecasts are based on assumptions that the Strait of Hormuz will reopen in March 2027 with a broad return to pre-war shipping conditions occurring by October 2027. The IMF assumes an average oil price of $96 per barrel for 2026 and $87 in 2027.

But under an adverse scenario highlighted in the report, in which a worsening war pushes oil prices to $130 per barrel through the first quarter of 2027, growth would be reduced by 0.2 percentage point in 2026 and 0.5 percentage point in 2027. Inflation in 2027 would surge by another 1.1 percentage point to 5.2%.

AI is also a huge source of uncertainty, with major downside and upside risks, the IMF report said. Under a scenario of faster adoption of the technology and accelerated investment, global GDP could rise a further 0.6% by 2029, with the bulk of the benefits going to the US and China.

But if productivity gains from AI fail to materialize, prompting a sharp decline in investment, US GDP could fall by 0.8% directly, causing spillovers to Asian technology exporters with a total direct GDP impact of as much as 0.4% by 2028.

This shift would also trigger a sharp reduction in asset prices and tighter financial conditions that cause a major drop in consumption, particularly in the US, the IMF said. Higher global bond yields would further reduce activity, with a combined global output reduction of 1.1% by 2028, including a 1.8% drop in US output.

The IMF also warned that elevated public debt levels, particularly in advanced economies, increase the risk of sharply higher borrowing costs that can weigh on growth prospects. It urged governments to stop delaying action to rebuild fiscal buffers and articulate credible medium-term plans to bring debt back to sustainable levels — advice that IMF officials plan to push at the Bangkok meetings.

(Reporting by David Lawder; Editing by Paul Simao and John Mair)

headline: UK, EU use media influence to sabotage Ukraine peace efforts — Russian envoy
summary: Kirill Dmitriev called the UK’s leftist government’s desire for a "forever war in Ukraine" the "elephant in the room"
body_text:
MOSCOW, October 13. /TASS/. The UK and the EU use their considerable media influence to sabotage peace efforts in Ukraine and cooperation between Moscow and Washington, Kirill Dmitriev, the Russian president’s special representative for investment and economic cooperation with foreign countries and head of the Russian Direct Investment Fund (RDIF), said.

"The UK uses its oversized media muscle to sabotage any Ukrainian peace effort and any US-Russia cooperation. The EU follows," Dmitriev wrote on X.

"The elephant in the room: the UK’s leftist government’s desire for a 'forever war in Ukraine' to distract from its destruction of the British way of life," he added.

headline: Qatar Airways suspends flights to Riyadh, Dammam
summary: The carrier said it is closely monitoring developments in Saudi Arabia in coordination with the relevant authorities
body_text:
DOHA, October 13. /TASS/. Qatar Airways has temporarily suspended flights to and from the Saudi cities of Riyadh and Dammam for safety reasons, the airline said in a notice.

The carrier said it is closely monitoring developments in Saudi Arabia in coordination with the relevant authorities. "Due to the current situation, flights to and from Riyadh (RUH) and Dammam (DMM) are temporarily suspended," the notice said. The airline stressed that passenger and crew safety remains its highest priority.

Earlier, Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation announced an extension of the closure of Riyadh’s airport following recent attacks, citing the need to "complete the necessary procedures to verify the safety of airport facilities and their operational readiness in coordination with the competent authorities."

Yemen’s rebel Ansar Allah movement - the Houthis - attacked the airport in the Saudi capital on October 10 and 11. According to Saudi authorities, the first strike killed at least 12 people and injured more than 300. The second attack killed one person, injured 11 others and caused damage to the airport.

headline: Morocco's first female prime minister secures deal to form government
summary: Morocco's centrist Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM), led by the country's first designated prime minister Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, has ⁠reached a deal with three other parties to form a coalition government.The coalition, which includes moderate socialist parties ⁠and the nationalist Istiqlal, together hold 207 seats in parliament, above the 198 needed for a majority.PAM, which topped last month's parliamentary election vote, was founded in 2008 by a royal adviser and has positioned itself as an advocate of social modernisation.Its leader, Ms El Mansouri, has been named Morocco's first female prime minister, the latest chapter in a career that has taken her from Marrakesh's city hall to the top levels of the country's political establishment.Ms El Mansouri, 50, the Mayor of Marrakesh, has also been Urban Planning and Housing Minister under Prime Minister Aziz Akhannouch since 2021.The deal "produces a ⁠strong political government, made up of components marked by ​ideological ⁠and political proximity, ‌united in, and committed to, a shared reformist vision,” ​the coalition said in a joint statement, adding that they will next propose a cabinet lineup.The statement added that the four parties would propose the names of male and female ministers "who possess competence, political acumen, integrity and probity, as part of a cohesive and strong government capable of implementing the government programme, which will be drawn up as quickly as possible".Ms El Mansouri's party has pledged to protect purchasing power by raising incomes and regulating markets, while making youth employment a priority. Its 2027-2031 programme aims to support one million young people, amid 29.2 per cent unemployment among 15- to 24-year-olds.Other priorities include improving healthcare, education, housing and digital services, advancing the official use of Amazigh, strengthening water, food and energy security, embracing artificial intelligence, and driving inclusive economic growth while safeguarding public finances.The new government will oversee the final stages of preparations for the 2030 World Cup, which Morocco will co-host with Portugal and Spain.

headline: Fighting intensifies in Yemen as Houthis fire on Saudi Arabia
summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels launched fresh attacks against Saudi Arabia on Monday, following deadly missile strikes on Riyadh's international airport that killed passengers, some of whom were preparing to board flights to perform Umrah.Saudi authorities extended the suspension of operations at King Khalid International Airport until midnight on October 17 following an attack on Saturday that killed 13 people and injured more than 300, and another on Sunday in which one person was killed.The King Fahd International Airport in Dammam was also hit on Sunday evening, Saudi Arabia's General Authority for Civil Aviation said, with the damage being assessed. A missile launched at Riyadh by the Yemeni Houthi militia has been intercepted and destroyed, the Saudi-led coalition said.The interception was announced shortly after authorities sounded a threat alarm, followed by three explosions, in the Saudi capital on Sunday night.The strikes came as Yemeni government forces, backed by the Saudi-led coalition, clashed with Houthi rebels on the outskirts of the strategic south-western city of Taiz, repelling fresh attacks amid warnings that a tightening rebel siege is worsening conditions inside the Yemeni city. A military spokesman said on Monday that air strikes prevented the Houthis from sending reinforcements to Taiz. At least 20 people have been killed in a series of attacks since last week on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and the Abha international airport in Saudi Arabia’s Asir province. Saudi state TV broadcast footage of the moment a missile struck the passenger terminal in Riyadh on Saturday, with flashes of light filling the screen as travellers, including pilgrims in white robes, scrambled for cover.Ali, from Hyderabad, was travelling with his family on an Umrah pilgrimage when he was injured in Saturday’s attack. The Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia confirmed his death on Sunday and said it was in contact with his family to help arrange the repatriation of his remains.Etihad Airways cancelled all flights between Abu Dhabi and Riyadh until Monday, October 19, extending disruption to services between the UAE and the Saudi capital into next week. Flydubai has also cancelled Riyadh flights until Wednesday, October 14, while Emirates and Air Arabia services have been affected.The Saudi-led coalition said it responded to drone and cruise missile threats against the kingdom on Monday, as hostilities with the Iran-backed Houthis continued despite diplomatic efforts, including a phone call between the foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia and Iran, which supports the Houthis.The coalition said a missile launched at Riyadh by the Houthis on Monday night was intercepted and destroyed. The interception was announced shortly after authorities sounded a threat alarm, followed by three explosions, in the Saudi capital.Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told his Saudi counterpart Prince Faisal bin Farhan that Tehran was ready to "provide assistance" to start talks between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis to reach a "political solution", Iranian state media reported."The Foreign Minister of our country, expressing concern over the escalation of tensions, emphasised that insisting on a military approach and ignoring political solutions would complicate the existing situation," Mr Araghchi was quoted as saying. Amid the continued attacks on Saudi Arabia, Dr Anwar Gargash, diplomatic adviser to President Sheikh Mohamed, called for stronger Gulf security and collective defence.In his statement posted on X, Dr Gargash said the security of Gulf states as a whole was "indivisible". He stressed that attacks against Saudi Arabia also threatened the wider Gulf. “Targeting our sisterly kingdom of Saudi Arabia undermines the security of the UAE and all Gulf states,” he added. He warned that shortcomings in regional co-operation had contributed to the current challenges.US Central Command chief Adm Brad Cooper said the US and its regional allies were deploying the “largest air-defence umbrella in the world” to deter Iranian attacks, describing the effort as part of an “enduring security architecture” in the Middle East. “It was a vision we discussed with our regional allies and partners,” he told the audience in a recorded message at Trends Global's sixth annual conference in Abu Dhabi on Monday. “Earlier this year, during Operation Epic Fury, we validated at full scale and in actual combat the Middle East Air Defence network known as Mead.“Through our combined efforts, we transformed a concept into the most sophisticated and largest air-defence umbrella in the world,” he added.“For the first time in history, US air defenders stood shoulder-to-shoulder with allies and partners across the Middle East, linking national systems in real time. And so together we intercepted thousands of Iranian attack drones and missiles with an integrated shield built on mutual trust. This is partnership in action.”

headline: Galatasaray v Barcelona: Lamine Yamal and Co aim to make it perfect 10 in Champions League clash
summary: Despite a three-week international break and the absence of La Liga's current top scorer, there was no stopping Barcelona's perfect start to the campaign at the weekend.Hansi Flick's table-toppers secured their eighth win in eight La Liga matches when they brushed aside Getafe 3-0 on Saturday – with Anthony Gordon, Gabriel Jesus and Jules Kounde on target – equalling their best start to a domestic campaign. And European football's form team managed that without 12-goal forward Raphinha, who missed the game after picking up a thigh injury while away with the Brazil national team.Win at Real Betis next weekend, and Barca will have matched Real Madrid's Spanish top-flight record of nine consecutive wins at the start of a season, achieved in 1968.After also thrashing Feyenoord 5-1 in the opening round of the UEFA Champions League last month, Flick recorded nine victories across all competitions, breaking a club record set a century ago.That is a flying start that even legendary Barca coaches Johan Cruyff, Pep Guardiola and Luis Enrique could not match. Strength in depth meant Flick could hand rare starts to the likes of Kounde, Gavi and Jesus against Getafe, with all three making valuable contributions at Camp Nou.“In every position, we have two or three players performing at an outstanding level,” said the German coach. “There is a great atmosphere in the team. That is what I like most. Everything is about the team, not one player or the coach.“The important thing is the team, and they have to understand that sometimes they need to be on the bench. That’s what’s important to win titles.“Everyone has to contribute in attack and defence. Everyone feels a responsibility to help the team and stay connected. Gabriel Jesus is a great player; you saw his goal. He’s different from Raphinha, yes, but today he showed his quality and I’m very happy for him.”Barcelona return to Champions League duty on Tuesday, when they face Galatasaray in what is sure to be a white-hot atmosphere in Istanbul, where the Catalans will again be without Raphinha.Having secured back-to-back La Liga titles, Flick's young side will now attempt to transfer that success onto the European stage, which saw them reach the semi-finals in 2024/25 and the quarter-finals last season.The five-time European champions last ruled the continent when Luis Enrique's side defeated Juventus 3-1 in the 2015 final.This is a Barca squad being built for long-term success. The starting XI against Getafe had an average age of less than 25, with only Rodri, 30, into his third decade. The five players brought off the bench – Fermin Lopez (23), Marc Bernal (19), Pedri (23), Karim Adeyemi (24) and Hamza Abdelkarim (18) – averaged just 21.4 years old.Leading the charge for European domination for the foreseeable future will be Ballon d'Or favourite Lamine Yamal, who continues to shine for both club and country. In four Uefa Nations League matches during the international window, the 19-year-old scored four and assisted another as world champions Spain stretched their unbeaten run to 43 games. “Lamine never stops surprising us,” said Spain coach Luis de la Fuente after Yamal scored in Spain's 3-1 win over Czech Republic. “He has so much talent and so much quality … Lamine is on the path to becoming a legend.”Against Getafe, Yamal added a seventh assist of the campaign to go with his eight goals across nine matches. “We all know Lamine’s level. He’s fantastic. He’s very difficult to stop, even when you take precautions,” admitted Getafe manager Jose Bordalas. “He’s excellent in one-on-one situations, finishing and passing. He’s a magnificent young player, and he shows the level he has … He will improve much more and can win the Ballon d’Or. I have no doubt.”Before the Getafe match, Flick made clear the talent Yamal had at his disposal. “He will be the best player in the world, if he isn't already,” said the German. “With his attitude, his mentality, his will to improve every day … That is the right mentality. For now, he is on that path and I am very happy.”Yamal's next test will be against Turkish Super Lig leaders Galatasaray at Rams Park, with an atmosphere Flick described on Monday as "one of the best in the world".Okan Buruk's team have won four successive domestic league titles and go into the match on the back of a 3-1 win over Kasımpasa on Friday – despite having Uruguayan midfielder Lucas Torreira sent off in the 65th minute – but started their Champions League campaign by losing at Portuguese side Sporting by the same scoreline. And Ismael Garcia, Galatasaray's assistant coach, acknowledged the challenge facing his side. “Yes, of course. In the end, playing against Barca is like going to the dentist: you know it's going to hurt, but you have to go and take it as well as possible,” the Spaniard said.“Hopefully things go well. We know that they are possibly the most in-form team in Europe, but we are confident that we can put them in trouble.”And Garcia also insisted they had the “perfect” man to hurt Barca in fit-again Nigerian striker Victor Osimhen, whose five games this season have produced six goals, while his Galatasaray record stands at 65 in 79 matches.“The top players do well in every game, but perhaps, because of Barcelona's way of defending, so aggressive and with the defensive line in the middle of the field, Osimhen is the striker who ... is perfect against that type of defence,” he said.“Beyond the fact that he is an extraordinary striker, we hope that he can do a lot of damage to Barcelona with the way he plays.”

And European football's form team managed that without 12-goal forward Raphinha, who missed the game after picking up a thigh injury while away with the Brazil national team.Win at Real Betis next weekend, and Barca will have matched Real Madrid's Spanish top-flight record of nine consecutive wins at the start of a season, achieved in 1968.After also thrashing Feyenoord 5-1 in the opening round of the UEFA Champions League last month, Flick recorded nine victories across all competitions, breaking a club record set a century ago.That is a flying start that even legendary Barca coaches Johan Cruyff, Pep Guardiola and Luis Enrique could not match. He’s different from Raphinha, yes, but today he showed his quality and I’m very happy for him.”Barcelona return to Champions League duty on Tuesday, when they face Galatasaray in what is sure to be a white-hot atmosphere in Istanbul, where the Catalans will again be without Raphinha.Having secured back-to-back La Liga titles, Flick's young side will now attempt to transfer that success onto the European stage, which saw them reach the semi-finals in 2024/25 and the quarter-finals last season.The five-time European champions last ruled the continent when Luis Enrique's side defeated Juventus 3-1 in the 2015 final.This is a Barca squad being built for long-term success. headline: Africa: WHO Pandemic Hub Sets Ambitious Goal to Detect New Outbreaks Within 24 Hours
summary: [Nigeria Health Watch] The World Health Organization (WHO) launched a new five-year strategy for its Hub for Pandemic and Epidemic Intelligence, charting a path towards a world where every country can detect and understand emerging health threats within 24 hours of their appearance by 2030. Strengthening rapid detection is a cornerstone of global health security, helping countries contain outbreaks before they escalate into larger epidemics or spread internationally.
body_text:
The World Health Organization (WHO) launched a new five-year strategy for its Hub for Pandemic and Epidemic Intelligence, charting a path towards a world where every country can detect and understand emerging health threats within 24 hours of their appearance by 2030. Strengthening rapid detection is a cornerstone of global health security, helping countries contain outbreaks before they escalate into larger epidemics or spread internationally.

The Hub's strategy aims to equip every country with the capabilities needed to rapidly identify and understand emerging health threats, thus supporting them in developing the systems, capacities and partnerships necessary to prevent outbreaks from escalating into epidemics or pandemics.

Speaking at the opening of the World Health Summit in Berlin, in the presence of Germany's Parliamentary State Secretary at the Federal Ministry of Health, Georg Kippels, WHO Director-General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus reflected on the Hub's achievements in the five years since its creation.

"Five years after its establishment, the WHO Hub for Pandemic and Epidemic Intelligence has become an integral part of the global health security system," he said. "Its new strategy charts a clear path towards 2030, uniting governments and partners around a shared goal: a world in which every country can rapidly respond to health threats before they turn into major crises."

Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines

The WHO Hub was created in 2021 with foundational support from the German Government in response to the critical gaps exposed by the COVID-19 pandemic. Since then, it has worked with 160 WHO Member States, 190 partner organizations, and thousands of scientists and policymakers to detect new epidemic threats, sequence and identify pathogens, and support rapid action to protect communities around the world.

body_text:
The situation in Saudi Arabia has been tense for many weeks, with Iran-backed Houthi rebels intensifying their attacks on the kingdom.

Over the past week, attacks on Saudi Arabia’s airports in Riyadh, Abha, Jazan and Najran caused multiple deaths and major destruction.

As the kingdom faces a major security challenge, the crisis is casting a shadow over live sports. Here we take a look at where things stand in Saudi Arabia.

Ronaldo's 981st goal helps Al Nassr win as Al Ain go top of AFC Champions League

The Saudi Pro League continued on Sunday even as Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport endured deadly attacks over the weekend, leaving 13 dead and hundreds injured.

Al Shabab’s match against Al Taawoun in Riyadh went ahead, with Shabab completing a comfortable 3-0 win. Al Fayha and Al Riyadh played out a draw, but the game between Abha and Al Faisaly was postponed until later in the month. The SPL continues this Thursday.

Cristiano Ronaldo's Al Nassr hosted Uzbek side Neftchi in their AFC Champions League Elite match in Riyadh on Monday.

There was uncertainty surrounding the match, especially after training for the game at Al Awwal Park was called off.

Kick-off was delayed due to a security alert issued by Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence, but the match went ahead and Nassr eased to a 3-1 win.

Fellow SPL heavyweights Al Ittihad are all set to take on Shabab Al Ahli in Jeddah on Tuesday.

The world's top men’s tennis players are scheduled to compete in the third edition of the Six Kings Slam, to be shown on Netflix from October 21-24.

Carlos Alcaraz, Alexander Zverev, Novak Djokovic, Alex de Minaur and Taylor Fritz are set to compete at the ANB Arena. However, defending champion Jannik Sinner has been replaced by Learner Tien in the line-up. Tickets for the tournament have gone on sale, with no changes announced so far.

Earlier in the year, it was announced that the 2026 WTA Finals had been relocated from Riyadh to Indian Wells, California, after Saudi Arabia relinquished the right to host the tournament.

Boxing great Saul "Canelo" Alvarez is scheduled to take on Christian Mbilli for the WBC super middleweight title in Riyadh on October 31.

There was uncertainty over the bout after several days of deadly strikes on the city. However, organiser Turki Alalshikh said Canelo would fulfil his commitment and compete in the Saudi capital.

“Canelo reached out and told me he’ll still fight in Riyadh this October, no matter what happens,” Alalshikh posted on X. “He fears nothing.”

World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE)'s Crown Jewel event is set to take place on November 7 at Riyadh Season Stadium. It is the 16th event that WWE will hold in Saudi Arabia under a 10-year partnership.

At the event, Roman Reigns will face Sami Zayn, while in the women’s category, Liv Morgan is scheduled to fight Chelsea Green.

The 2026/27 racing season in Riyadh is scheduled to start on Friday and end April 17 next year. As things stand, the season is set to last six months and include 69 races.

The total prize pool on offer is 197.8 million Saudi riyals.

headline: Africa: Ghana Will Resume Evacuations From South Africa If Lives Are Threatened - Ablakwa
summary: [Ghanaian Times] Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa has assured Ghanaians that the government remains ready to evacuate nationals from South Africa if their lives are threatened by further attacks.
body_text:
Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa has assured Ghanaians that the government remains ready to evacuate nationals from South Africa if their lives are threatened by further attacks.

He said the completion of the recent evacuation exercise did not mean Ghana had closed the door on bringing home citizens who may need assistance.

Mr Ablakwa made the remarks during an interview on TV3's The Key Points on October 10, 2026, following concerns over renewed tensions in South Africa after a decision by the country's highest court on the rights of asylum seekers.

He explained that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, through its Consular and Humanitarian Bureau (COHAB), continued to monitor the situation and assess the welfare of Ghanaians in distress.

Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines

"The Consular and Humanitarian Bureau (COHAB) of the Foreign Ministry continues to be active, and continues to assess every situation, particularly the situation of Ghanaians in distress. And I watch that space very closely," he said.

The minister stressed that the government would intervene if there were further attacks or a deterioration in the security situation that placed Ghanaians at risk.

He noted that the ministry had continued to evacuate citizens from other parts of the world even after concluding the recent exercise in South Africa.

According to him, Ghana has evacuated nationals from Libya, Myanmar and Cambodia, among other places, as part of efforts to protect citizens facing difficult or dangerous situations abroad.

Mr Ablakwa disclosed that more than 6,300 Ghanaians had been evacuated from various distress situations across the world since 2025.

He added that the ministry's Consular and Humanitarian Bureau and Ghana's 72 diplomatic missions worldwide remained active in monitoring the welfare of citizens within their areas of responsibility.

The missions, he said, were expected to keep track of developments affecting Ghanaians in their respective jurisdictions and areas where they also had responsibility for other countries.

Mr Ablakwa assured the public that the government would act swiftly to bring Ghanaians home if the need arose.

headline: Iran Army Navy built new weapons to target US vulnerabilities
summary: TEHRAN, Oct. 13 (MNA) – Deputy Commander of the Iranian Army Navy Admiral Bamani has said Iran has developed new weapons designed to target America's vulnerabilities and is responding to enemy tactics with its own new approaches.
body_text:
TEHRAN, Oct. 13 (MNA) – Deputy Commander of the Iranian Army Navy Admiral Bamani has said Iran has developed new weapons designed to target America's vulnerabilities and is responding to enemy tactics with its own new approaches.

Speaking in an interview, he stated that the powerful Armed Forces of the country have learned from the experience of recent wars, and the Army Navy has proceeded to produce new weaponry in compatible with the vulnerabilities and weaknesses of the enemy.

Enemies’ threats are nothing new, he said, adding, “Islamic Republic of Iran has consistently faced threats since the beginning of the Islamic Revolution, the threats that have been voiced sometimes covertly and at other times openly.”

headline: Tehran slams UK over baseless Fairford claims
summary: TEHRAN, Oct. 13 (MNA) – Iran's Foreign Ministry strongly condemned British claims linking Tehran to an alleged security incident at RAF Fairford, calling them a false-flag plot to advance anti-Iran campaigns.
body_text:
TEHRAN, Oct. 13 (MNA) – Iran's Foreign Ministry strongly condemned British claims linking Tehran to an alleged security incident at RAF Fairford, calling them a false-flag plot to advance anti-Iran campaigns.

Iran's Foreign Ministry strongly condemned British allegations linking Tehran to an alleged security incident at RAF Fairford air base, describing them as a despicable plot designed to advance an anti-Iran campaign and to evade accountability for Britain's role in the US-Israeli military aggression against the Iranian nation.

In a formal statement, the ministry said the British government cannot escape its political and legal responsibility, or the potential consequences of its claims, by relying on vague language without presenting any solid evidence or proof.

The statement specifically criticized the use of terms such as "highly likely" and "almost certainly," calling them a blatant attempt to lend false credibility to the attribution while sidestepping accountability for baseless accusations.

The ministry highlighted Britain's well-known track record of fabricating security-related allegations against other nations, noting that such practices have, in some instances, contributed to tensions and destructive conflicts in West Asia. It said the British government must be held accountable for persisting in this dangerous approach that undermines international peace and security.

Categorically rejecting the accusations, the Foreign Ministry held the British government, as well as the planners and perpetrators of false-flag operation, fully responsible for all consequences arising from the fabrication.

headline: Africa: General Assembly Adopts Pandemic Declaration, but Not By Consensus
summary: [UN News] The General Assembly on Monday adopted a political declaration on pandemic prevention, preparedness and response, by 153 in favour to three against (Argentina, Israel and United States) with two abstentions (New Zealand and Paraguay).
body_text:
The General Assembly on Monday adopted a political declaration on pandemic prevention, preparedness and response, by 153 in favour to three against (Argentina, Israel and United States) with two abstentions (New Zealand and Paraguay).

The text was due to be approved by consensus at a high-level meeting on 25 September.

Objections from the United States and a few other States blocked that, pushing the issue back to the assembly.

Read the full political declaration here.

Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines

Chile's representative summed up one prevailing view, saying that "no country, no matter how big it might be or how prepared it might be, can alone address a threat that knows no borders."

The declaration is political and non-binding. It calls for stronger national, regional and international cooperation, guided by science, equity and respect for human rights, and it welcomes last year's landmark adoption of the World Health Organization (WHO) Pandemic Agreement.

The agreement cannot be opened for signature until Member States complete an annex on pathogen access and benefit-sharing - the system by which countries would share samples and genetic data.

Those that do so would receive a share of any resulting vaccines, treatments and diagnostics.

Talks have stalled amid a standoff between developing countries and some high-income European nations together with the US.

The World Health Assembly - comprising the WHO's 194 members - is due to return to the annex next May.

The US representative had previously cited "divisive ideologies that lack definitional consensus" as well as the declaration's references to the continuing annex negotiations.

More action in the General Assembly

In addition to adopting the pandemic declaration, the 193-member world body had a number of items on its agenda on Monday, including the consideration of draft resolutions on the UN Declaration on Sea Level Rise and a political declaration of the high-level meeting to mark the 25th anniversary of the adoption of the anti-racism Durban Declaration and Programme of Action.

Read a summary of the meeting here.

WHO aims to spot new outbreaks within 24 hours

The World Health Organization (WHO) on Monday launched a five-year strategy for its Hub for Pandemic and Epidemic Intelligence, with the goal of detecting emerging health threats within 24 hours.

headline: Africa: 'Efficiency Has Limits' - UNHCR Chief Warns Refugee Protection Is Buckling Under Cuts
summary: [UN News] The money is running out faster than needs are growing: with 117 million men, women and children now forced from their homes, the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) has received just $3 billion of the $8.5 billion it needs this year - and its chief, Barham Salih, warns that the global support system for asylum-seekers risks buckling.
body_text:
The money is running out faster than needs are growing: with 117 million men, women and children now forced from their homes, the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) has received just $3 billion of the $8.5 billion it needs this year - and its chief, Barham Salih, warns that the global support system for asylum-seekers risks buckling.

UNHCR was created after the Second World War with the pledge that people fleeing persecution should be protected and not sent back to places where they might be in danger. Today, that pledge is under strain as deep funding cuts take effect.

In his first keynote address to UNHCR's Executive Committee meeting in Geneva on Monday, Mr. Salih stressed that the world's most vulnerable are going without the help they need.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"There is...a difference between doing more with less and being asked to do the impossible," he said, while also highlighting the "exceptionally difficult year" at the agency, marked by the departure of 8,000 staff since 2024.

Cost of cuts in Sudan, Chad and beyond

He added: "In Sudan, insufficient funding threatens specialised medical care, legal assistance and psychological support for more than 50,000 survivors of conflict-related sexual violence. In Chad, services for thousands of unaccompanied and separated children and children with specific protection needs are at risk."

In Ethiopia, meanwhile, refugee registration has been halted for tens of thousands of people arriving from South Sudan and Eritrea, while hundreds of thousands more are awaiting verification and integration into the national identification system.

Conflicts are uprooting people faster than governments and aid agencies can help them.

So far in 2026, UNHCR has responded to 22 emergencies in 18 countries, from Yemen to the Horn of Africa and from Sudan to the Sahel.

Despite growing humanitarian needs, the agency has received less than one third of its funding requirement for this year.

Mr. Salih warned that countries that have hosted refugees for decades are frustrated at the lack of international solidarity, while refugees themselves are increasingly afraid for their safety, amid deep cuts to assistance.

The result is that women and girls are more exposed to violence and exploitation, children are losing years of education and persons with disabilities face protection barriers, the High Commissioner said, in an appeal for greater support.

"Efficiency has limits. There comes a point when greater efficiency cannot compensate for fewer resources. When funding falls below that point, the consequences are not abstract, they are borne by people who depend on it," he insisted.

At the end of last month, Mr. Salih - a former Kurdish politician and President of Iraq - told the Security Council that the situation for refugees today was "genuinely, truly, inhumane".

Speaking in Geneva, the UNHCR chief highlighted an initiative launched earlier this year that aims to halve the number of refugees living in protracted displacement and depending on humanitarian assistance by 2035.

Nearly 14.5 million refugees in low and middle-income countries currently rely on aid to meet their basic requirements, he said.

"We cannot claim success simply because assistance has been reduced or responsibility has been transferred to host countries," he added.

"Success is measured by whether people's lives have genuinely improved and whether they have become self-reliant and active contributors to their communities. For those who still require humanitarian support, our responsibility remains."

Mr. Salih urged solidarity and empathy with asylum-seekers, whose long-standing plight and hardship remains unresolved around the world. "When we speak about refugees and displacement, we should do so with humility," he said.

"None of us knows who may be forced to flee tomorrow, or who may be called upon to offer refuge."

headline: Africa: WHO Pandemic Hub Sets Ambitious Goal to Detect New Outbreaks Within 24 Hours
summary: [Nigeria Health Watch] The World Health Organization (WHO) launched a new five-year strategy for its Hub for Pandemic and Epidemic Intelligence, charting a path towards a world where every country can detect and understand emerging health threats within 24 hours of their appearance by 2030. Strengthening rapid detection is a cornerstone of global health security, helping countries contain outbreaks before they escalate into larger epidemics or spread internationally.
body_text:
The World Health Organization (WHO) launched a new five-year strategy for its Hub for Pandemic and Epidemic Intelligence, charting a path towards a world where every country can detect and understand emerging health threats within 24 hours of their appearance by 2030. Strengthening rapid detection is a cornerstone of global health security, helping countries contain outbreaks before they escalate into larger epidemics or spread internationally.

The Hub's strategy aims to equip every country with the capabilities needed to rapidly identify and understand emerging health threats, thus supporting them in developing the systems, capacities and partnerships necessary to prevent outbreaks from escalating into epidemics or pandemics.

Speaking at the opening of the World Health Summit in Berlin, in the presence of Germany's Parliamentary State Secretary at the Federal Ministry of Health, Georg Kippels, WHO Director-General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus reflected on the Hub's achievements in the five years since its creation.

"Five years after its establishment, the WHO Hub for Pandemic and Epidemic Intelligence has become an integral part of the global health security system," he said. "Its new strategy charts a clear path towards 2030, uniting governments and partners around a shared goal: a world in which every country can rapidly respond to health threats before they turn into major crises."

Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines

The WHO Hub was created in 2021 with foundational support from the German Government in response to the critical gaps exposed by the COVID-19 pandemic. Since then, it has worked with 160 WHO Member States, 190 partner organizations, and thousands of scientists and policymakers to detect new epidemic threats, sequence and identify pathogens, and support rapid action to protect communities around the world.

Under the next five-year strategy, the Hub will build on the achievements and deliver its work through five priority initiatives:

body_text:
The situation in Saudi Arabia has been tense for many weeks, with Iran-backed Houthi rebels intensifying their attacks on the kingdom.

Over the past week, attacks on Saudi Arabia’s airports in Riyadh, Abha, Jazan and Najran caused multiple deaths and major destruction.

As the kingdom faces a major security challenge, the crisis is casting a shadow over live sports. Here we take a look at where things stand in Saudi Arabia.

Ronaldo's 981st goal helps Al Nassr win as Al Ain go top of AFC Champions League

The Saudi Pro League continued on Sunday even as Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport endured deadly attacks over the weekend, leaving 13 dead and hundreds injured.

Al Shabab’s match against Al Taawoun in Riyadh went ahead, with Shabab completing a comfortable 3-0 win. Al Fayha and Al Riyadh played out a draw, but the game between Abha and Al Faisaly was postponed until later in the month. The SPL continues this Thursday.

Cristiano Ronaldo's Al Nassr hosted Uzbek side Neftchi in their AFC Champions League Elite match in Riyadh on Monday.

There was uncertainty surrounding the match, especially after training for the game at Al Awwal Park was called off.

Kick-off was delayed due to a security alert issued by Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence, but the match went ahead and Nassr eased to a 3-1 win.

Fellow SPL heavyweights Al Ittihad are all set to take on Shabab Al Ahli in Jeddah on Tuesday.

The world's top men’s tennis players are scheduled to compete in the third edition of the Six Kings Slam, to be shown on Netflix from October 21-24.

Carlos Alcaraz, Alexander Zverev, Novak Djokovic, Alex de Minaur and Taylor Fritz are set to compete at the ANB Arena. However, defending champion Jannik Sinner has been replaced by Learner Tien in the line-up. Tickets for the tournament have gone on sale, with no changes announced so far.

Earlier in the year, it was announced that the 2026 WTA Finals had been relocated from Riyadh to Indian Wells, California, after Saudi Arabia relinquished the right to host the tournament.

Boxing great Saul "Canelo" Alvarez is scheduled to take on Christian Mbilli for the WBC super middleweight title in Riyadh on October 31.

There was uncertainty over the bout after several days of deadly strikes on the city. However, organiser Turki Alalshikh said Canelo would fulfil his commitment and compete in the Saudi capital.

“Canelo reached out and told me he’ll still fight in Riyadh this October, no matter what happens,” Alalshikh posted on X. “He fears nothing.”

World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE)'s Crown Jewel event is set to take place on November 7 at Riyadh Season Stadium. It is the 16th event that WWE will hold in Saudi Arabia under a 10-year partnership.

At the event, Roman Reigns will face Sami Zayn, while in the women’s category, Liv Morgan is scheduled to fight Chelsea Green.

The 2026/27 racing season in Riyadh is scheduled to start on Friday and end April 17 next year. As things stand, the season is set to last six months and include 69 races.

The total prize pool on offer is 197.8 million Saudi riyals.

headline: Africa: Ghana Will Resume Evacuations From South Africa If Lives Are Threatened - Ablakwa
summary: [Ghanaian Times] Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa has assured Ghanaians that the government remains ready to evacuate nationals from South Africa if their lives are threatened by further attacks.
body_text:
Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa has assured Ghanaians that the government remains ready to evacuate nationals from South Africa if their lives are threatened by further attacks.

He said the completion of the recent evacuation exercise did not mean Ghana had closed the door on bringing home citizens who may need assistance.

Mr Ablakwa made the remarks during an interview on TV3's The Key Points on October 10, 2026, following concerns over renewed tensions in South Africa after a decision by the country's highest court on the rights of asylum seekers.

He explained that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, through its Consular and Humanitarian Bureau (COHAB), continued to monitor the situation and assess the welfare of Ghanaians in distress.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"The Consular and Humanitarian Bureau (COHAB) of the Foreign Ministry continues to be active, and continues to assess every situation, particularly the situation of Ghanaians in distress. And I watch that space very closely," he said.

The minister stressed that the government would intervene if there were further attacks or a deterioration in the security situation that placed Ghanaians at risk.

He noted that the ministry had continued to evacuate citizens from other parts of the world even after concluding the recent exercise in South Africa.

According to him, Ghana has evacuated nationals from Libya, Myanmar and Cambodia, among other places, as part of efforts to protect citizens facing difficult or dangerous situations abroad.

Mr Ablakwa disclosed that more than 6,300 Ghanaians had been evacuated from various distress situations across the world since 2025.

He added that the ministry's Consular and Humanitarian Bureau and Ghana's 72 diplomatic missions worldwide remained active in monitoring the welfare of citizens within their areas of responsibility.

The missions, he said, were expected to keep track of developments affecting Ghanaians in their respective jurisdictions and areas where they also had responsibility for other countries.

Mr Ablakwa assured the public that the government would act swiftly to bring Ghanaians home if the need arose.

headline: Iran Army Navy built new weapons to target US vulnerabilities
summary: TEHRAN, Oct. 13 (MNA) – Deputy Commander of the Iranian Army Navy Admiral Bamani has said Iran has developed new weapons designed to target America's vulnerabilities and is responding to enemy tactics with its own new approaches.
body_text:
TEHRAN, Oct. 13 (MNA) – Deputy Commander of the Iranian Army Navy Admiral Bamani has said Iran has developed new weapons designed to target America's vulnerabilities and is responding to enemy tactics with its own new approaches.

Speaking in an interview, he stated that the powerful Armed Forces of the country have learned from the experience of recent wars, and the Army Navy has proceeded to produce new weaponry in compatible with the vulnerabilities and weaknesses of the enemy.

Enemies’ threats are nothing new, he said, adding, “Islamic Republic of Iran has consistently faced threats since the beginning of the Islamic Revolution, the threats that have been voiced sometimes covertly and at other times openly.”

He claimed that following Iranian retaliatory strikes, adversaries have withdrawn significantly from Iran's maritime borders, now positioned at their greatest distance since the Iran-Iraq War.

Referring to the two wars imposed against Iran [June 13 and February 28], Rear Admiral Bamani added that the Army Navy, alongside the Navy of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), has at times dealt heavy blows to the American enemy, have occasionally been acknowledged by the opposing side as well.

Following these blows, US forces have moved away from Iran's maritime borders and are now positioned at the greatest distance from them compared to previous periods, he stipulated.

The deputy commander of the Army Navy also addressed the issue of the naval blockade, stating that the government is pursuing strategies to counter this situation in the political and economic spheres.

headline: Tehran slams UK over baseless Fairford claims
summary: TEHRAN, Oct. 13 (MNA) – Iran's Foreign Ministry strongly condemned British claims linking Tehran to an alleged security incident at RAF Fairford, calling them a false-flag plot to advance anti-Iran campaigns.
body_text:
TEHRAN, Oct. 13 (MNA) – Iran's Foreign Ministry strongly condemned British claims linking Tehran to an alleged security incident at RAF Fairford, calling them a false-flag plot to advance anti-Iran campaigns.

Iran's Foreign Ministry strongly condemned British allegations linking Tehran to an alleged security incident at RAF Fairford air base, describing them as a despicable plot designed to advance an anti-Iran campaign and to evade accountability for Britain's role in the US-Israeli military aggression against the Iranian nation.

In a formal statement, the ministry said the British government cannot escape its political and legal responsibility, or the potential consequences of its claims, by relying on vague language without presenting any solid evidence or proof.

The statement specifically criticized the use of terms such as "highly likely" and "almost certainly," calling them a blatant attempt to lend false credibility to the attribution while sidestepping accountability for baseless accusations.

The ministry highlighted Britain's well-known track record of fabricating security-related allegations against other nations, noting that such practices have, in some instances, contributed to tensions and destructive conflicts in West Asia. It said the British government must be held accountable for persisting in this dangerous approach that undermines international peace and security.

Categorically rejecting the accusations, the Foreign Ministry held the British government, as well as the planners and perpetrators of false-flag operation, fully responsible for all consequences arising from the fabrication.

headline: Africa: General Assembly Adopts Pandemic Declaration, but Not By Consensus
summary: [UN News] The General Assembly on Monday adopted a political declaration on pandemic prevention, preparedness and response, by 153 in favour to three against (Argentina, Israel and United States) with two abstentions (New Zealand and Paraguay).
body_text:
The General Assembly on Monday adopted a political declaration on pandemic prevention, preparedness and response, by 153 in favour to three against (Argentina, Israel and United States) with two abstentions (New Zealand and Paraguay).

The text was due to be approved by consensus at a high-level meeting on 25 September.

Objections from the United States and a few other States blocked that, pushing the issue back to the assembly.

Read the full political declaration here.

Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines

Chile's representative summed up one prevailing view, saying that "no country, no matter how big it might be or how prepared it might be, can alone address a threat that knows no borders."

The declaration is political and non-binding. It calls for stronger national, regional and international cooperation, guided by science, equity and respect for human rights, and it welcomes last year's landmark adoption of the World Health Organization (WHO) Pandemic Agreement.

The agreement cannot be opened for signature until Member States complete an annex on pathogen access and benefit-sharing - the system by which countries would share samples and genetic data.

Those that do so would receive a share of any resulting vaccines, treatments and diagnostics.

Talks have stalled amid a standoff between developing countries and some high-income European nations together with the US.

The World Health Assembly - comprising the WHO's 194 members - is due to return to the annex next May.

The US representative had previously cited "divisive ideologies that lack definitional consensus" as well as the declaration's references to the continuing annex negotiations.

More action in the General Assembly

In addition to adopting the pandemic declaration, the 193-member world body had a number of items on its agenda on Monday, including the consideration of draft resolutions on the UN Declaration on Sea Level Rise and a political declaration of the high-level meeting to mark the 25th anniversary of the adoption of the anti-racism Durban Declaration and Programme of Action.

Read a summary of the meeting here.

WHO aims to spot new outbreaks within 24 hours

The World Health Organization (WHO) on Monday launched a five-year strategy for its Hub for Pandemic and Epidemic Intelligence, with the goal of detecting emerging health threats within 24 hours.

headline: Africa: 'Efficiency Has Limits' - UNHCR Chief Warns Refugee Protection Is Buckling Under Cuts
summary: [UN News] The money is running out faster than needs are growing: with 117 million men, women and children now forced from their homes, the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) has received just $3 billion of the $8.5 billion it needs this year - and its chief, Barham Salih, warns that the global support system for asylum-seekers risks buckling.
body_text:
The money is running out faster than needs are growing: with 117 million men, women and children now forced from their homes, the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) has received just $3 billion of the $8.5 billion it needs this year - and its chief, Barham Salih, warns that the global support system for asylum-seekers risks buckling.

UNHCR was created after the Second World War with the pledge that people fleeing persecution should be protected and not sent back to places where they might be in danger. Today, that pledge is under strain as deep funding cuts take effect.

In his first keynote address to UNHCR's Executive Committee meeting in Geneva on Monday, Mr. Salih stressed that the world's most vulnerable are going without the help they need.

Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines

"There is...a difference between doing more with less and being asked to do the impossible," he said, while also highlighting the "exceptionally difficult year" at the agency, marked by the departure of 8,000 staff since 2024.

Cost of cuts in Sudan, Chad and beyond

He added: "In Sudan, insufficient funding threatens specialised medical care, legal assistance and psychological support for more than 50,000 survivors of conflict-related sexual violence. In Chad, services for thousands of unaccompanied and separated children and children with specific protection needs are at risk."

In Ethiopia, meanwhile, refugee registration has been halted for tens of thousands of people arriving from South Sudan and Eritrea, while hundreds of thousands more are awaiting verification and integration into the national identification system.

Conflicts are uprooting people faster than governments and aid agencies can help them.

So far in 2026, UNHCR has responded to 22 emergencies in 18 countries, from Yemen to the Horn of Africa and from Sudan to the Sahel.

Despite growing humanitarian needs, the agency has received less than one third of its funding requirement for this year.

Mr. Salih warned that countries that have hosted refugees for decades are frustrated at the lack of international solidarity, while refugees themselves are increasingly afraid for their safety, amid deep cuts to assistance.

The result is that women and girls are more exposed to violence and exploitation, children are losing years of education and persons with disabilities face protection barriers, the High Commissioner said, in an appeal for greater support.

"Efficiency has limits. There comes a point when greater efficiency cannot compensate for fewer resources. When funding falls below that point, the consequences are not abstract, they are borne by people who depend on it," he insisted.

At the end of last month, Mr. Salih - a former Kurdish politician and President of Iraq - told the Security Council that the situation for refugees today was "genuinely, truly, inhumane".

Speaking in Geneva, the UNHCR chief highlighted an initiative launched earlier this year that aims to halve the number of refugees living in protracted displacement and depending on humanitarian assistance by 2035.

Nearly 14.5 million refugees in low and middle-income countries currently rely on aid to meet their basic requirements, he said.

"We cannot claim success simply because assistance has been reduced or responsibility has been transferred to host countries," he added.

"Success is measured by whether people's lives have genuinely improved and whether they have become self-reliant and active contributors to their communities. For those who still require humanitarian support, our responsibility remains."

Mr. Salih urged solidarity and empathy with asylum-seekers, whose long-standing plight and hardship remains unresolved around the world. "When we speak about refugees and displacement, we should do so with humility," he said.

"None of us knows who may be forced to flee tomorrow, or who may be called upon to offer refuge."

headline: Morning Briefing: Oct. 13, 2026
summary: Anadolu’s recap of top stories from around the globe
body_text:
Here's a rundown of all the news you need to start your Tuesday, including Saudi Arabia extending the suspension of operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh following a series of attacks by Yemen’s Houthi group, UK blaming Iran for air base plot and announcing sanctions, and federal law enforcement authorities conducting a raid on US Rep. Ilhan Omar’s Washington, DC residence.

Saudi Arabia announced that it had extended the suspension of operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh following a series of attacks on the facility.

In a statement, the General Authority of Civil Aviation said the suspension was extended to complete necessary procedures to verify the safety of airport facilities and their operational readiness.

The authority did not specify when operations would resume.

The decision followed attacks on the airport over the weekend.

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Monday that last month’s alleged terror plot targeting a British air base was “almost certainly” directed by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), as he announced fresh sanctions against two Iranian men.

Addressing Parliament, Burnham said the UK assessment was that the alleged plot, which led to five arrests on suspicion of terror offenses, was highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran.

“I can confirm our assessment that it is highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran, almost certainly directed by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard,” he told MPs.

In late September, a major security incident occurred at RAF Fairford, a Gloucestershire airbase used by the US Air Force. The incident triggered a large-scale counter-terrorism investigation.

Iran on Monday again rejected British allegations that Tehran was involved in the incident, while reiterating its willingness to cooperate in examining the case, state news agency IRNA reported.

Federal law enforcement authorities raided the Washington, DC residence of Democratic US Rep. Ilhan Omar amid an investigation into her immigration records.

Federal personnel executed the court-approved operation around 6 am local time (1000GMT), centering on a criminal fraud inquiry concerning immigration documents completed during the childhood of the Democratic lawmaker, who was born in the Horn of Africa nation of Somalia.

"Homeland Security Investigations executed a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the Department of Justice," a department spokesperson told Fox News, underlining that the raid is part of an ongoing federal investigation.

Omar criticized the search at her home, describing the operation as an effort by the Trump administration to intimidate political opponents.

Microsoft on Monday unveiled its third-generation Maia AI accelerator, with plans to expand deployment of its own chips starting in 2027 and make them the primary inference system for its products and services.

Microsoft expects Maia 300 to deliver 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading graphics processing unit-based systems. A configuration containing 96 accelerators can deliver up to seven times the rack-level token throughput of Maia 200, according to the company.

South Korea’s Defense Ministry on Monday opened the military’s first artificial intelligence (AI) transformation base to develop robotic systems capable of performing dangerous military operations.

The facility, located in Pangyo, south of Seoul, will train humanoid and multi-legged robots using physical AI data and advanced AI models, Yonhap News Agency reported, citing the ministry.

Around 150 officials, including representatives from the science and industry ministries, attended the opening ceremony.

US actor RJ Mitte, best known for playing Walter White Jr. in the television series "Breaking Bad," has died at the age of 34, according to media reports.

Representatives for Mitte confirmed his death to US-based entertainment news outlets Variety and TMZ. The cause of death was not immediately disclosed.

Mitte portrayed the son of Walter White, played by Bryan Cranston, and Skyler White, played by Anna Gunn, in the AMC crime drama created by Vince Gilligan which aired 2008-2013.

A jersey worn by sports legend Michael Jordan during the 1998 NBA Finals has sold for $14 million, setting what auction house Hunt Auctions said is a record for basketball memorabilia.

Jordan wore the Chicago Bulls’ red jersey during Game 2 of the finals against the Utah Jazz, helping his team secure a victory that tied the series at 1-1. The Bulls went on to win the series in six games, securing Jordan’s sixth and final NBA championship.

Hunt Auctions said the jersey was purchased in a private sale by Miami real estate investor Ron Firman, according to The Guardian.

summary: The 16th Airshow China, formally the China International Aviation and Aerospace Exhibition, will be held Dec. 7-13 in Zhuhai, southern China's Guangdong Province, organizers said Tuesday at a news conference in Beijing.
