headline: US wants Israel to 'crack down' on settler violence in West Bank, Rubio says
summary: WASHINGTON, Oct 17 (Reuters) - The United States wants Israel to do more to deter attacks committed by settlers in the West Bank, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday."We're very disturbed by those images and what we're seeing," Rubio said. "We've asked the Israelis and continue to ask them to crack down on that stuff."
body_text:
WASHINGTON, Oct 17 (Reuters) - The United States wants Israel to do more to deter attacks committed by settlers in the West Bank, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday.

"We're very disturbed by those images and what we're seeing," Rubio said. "We've asked the Israelis and continue to ask them to crack down on that stuff."

His comments to reporters came after the widespread dissemination of video showing multiple individuals attacking Heidi Levine, an American photojournalist with the Washington Post. Levine was one of at least two people injured in the Friday incident, which took place as Israeli settlersattacked Palestinian civilians.

European ‌diplomats and a French mayor also were attacked in the occupied West Bank, Belgium's foreign minister said.

The US State Department, Rubio said, has inquired about the event that included Levine's attack. Rubio, who spoke to reporters before boarding a flight to Uzbekistan, said he expects to hear back from the US Embassy in Jerusalem by Sunday.

Israeli settlers in the West Bankhave been involved in at least 170 attacks on Palestinians since September 27, around the start of the annual olive harvest, according toYesh Din, an Israeli settlements monitoring group.

(Reporting by Gram Slattery and Jasper Ward in Washington; Editing by Sergio Non and Franklin Paul)

headline: US 'very disturbed' by attack on American journalist in occupied West Bank: Rubio
summary: US secretary of state says Washington has urged Israel to crack down on violence by occupiers, stressing Trump does not want to see new crisis in West Bank
body_text:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Saturday that Washington was "very disturbed" by reports of an attack on an American photojournalist in the occupied West Bank and urged Israel to curb such violence.

"We've asked the Israelis and continue to ask them to crack down on that stuff," Rubio said, referring to the attack on photojournalist Heidi Levine.

He said that US President Donald Trump "has been very clear" that he did not want to see "friction" or a new crisis in the West Bank.

Rubio said the US had contacted its embassy to gather more information about the incident. He added that media reports indicated Levine had been beaten after being caught in an attack by groups of Israeli occupiers.

"It didn't look good," he said, describing the incident as "disturbing."

Asked about Trump's decision to lift sanctions against Israeli occupiers on his first day in office last year, Rubio said the move did not mean the president supported such attacks.

"Lifting sanctions ... does not mean he's a supporter of what he's seeing now on television, what he's reading about," he said.

Rubio added that Washington was closely monitoring concerns over violence during the olive harvest season in the occupied West Bank, noting that the period traditionally draws many people to the area.

He also said similar concerns could arise in Lebanon.

Meanwhile, US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee called on Israeli authorities to prosecute and imprison those responsible for the attack on Levine.

"Attacking a female photographer is a despicable act of terror carried out by masked cowards," Huckabee wrote on US social media company X on Saturday.

"Those who attacked unarmed reporter should spend (years) in prison," he added, calling for a full investigation and the arrest and prosecution of everyone involved "to the fullest extent of the law."

Levine was covering the annual Palestinian olive harvest in the occupied West Bank on Friday when Israeli occupiers attacked her and several Palestinians.

Witnesses said the occupiers stormed the area, beat Levine and took her passport, phone, wallet and camera equipment.

Levine said the attackers, who were armed with bottles and slingshots, “were kicking me for like 10 minutes, and I was trying to hold onto my cameras and my bag.”

headline: Dubai's economy reaches Dh473bn in first half of 2026 as key sectors expand
summary: Dubai's economy reached Dh473 billion in the first half of 2026, down 2.3 per cent from a year earlier, as growth in financial services, healthcare and construction helped offset weakness in other sectors.The emirate's real gross domestic product declined from Dh484 billion in the same period last year, according to figures released on Sunday by the Dubai Data and Statistics Establishment at Digital Dubai.The slowdown came as the Iran war, which began on February 28, disrupted regional travel and trade, weighing on Dubai's tourism and transport sectors and dampening economic activity during the first half of the year.GDP at current prices, however, increased by 0.2 per cent to Dh505 billion, reflecting growth across several key sectors.The figures mark a reversal from the 2.4 per cent annual growth recorded in the first quarter, when Dubai's economy reached Dh232 billion despite regional economic challenges.Financial and insurance activities were among the strongest performers body_text:
Dubai's economy reached Dh473 billion in the first half of 2026, down 2.3 per cent from a year earlier, as growth in financial services, healthcare and construction helped offset weakness in other sectors.

The emirate's real gross domestic product declined from Dh484 billion in the same period last year, according to figures released on Sunday by the Dubai Data and Statistics Establishment at Digital Dubai.

The slowdown came as the Iran war, which began on February 28, disrupted regional travel and trade, weighing on Dubai's tourism and transport sectors and dampening economic activity during the first half of the year.

GDP at current prices, however, increased by 0.2 per cent to Dh505 billion, reflecting growth across several key sectors.

The figures mark a reversal from the 2.4 per cent annual growth recorded in the first quarter, when Dubai's economy reached Dh232 billion despite regional economic challenges.

Financial and insurance activities were among the strongest performers in the first half, expanding 8.8 per cent in real terms to Dh65.9 billion, compared with Dh60.6 billion a year earlier.

The sector's contribution to GDP increased to 14 per cent from 12.5 per cent, highlighting its growing importance to the emirate's economy.

The expansion comes as the Dubai International Financial Centre continues to attract international financial institutions, with the number of companies operating at the financial hub exceeding 10,000 in the first half of the year.

Healthcare and social work activities recorded the fastest growth, expanding 14.3 per cent, while information and communication activities increased 2.7 per cent.

Construction grew 2.4 per cent in real terms, generating Dh33.2 billion in value added, while government services expanded 2.9 per cent.

However, several major sectors contracted during the period.

Wholesale and retail trade, Dubai's largest economic activity, declined 6 per cent in real terms, although it continued to account for 20.5 per cent of GDP.

Transport and storage fell 7.4 per cent, while real estate activity contracted 2.5 per cent in constant prices, despite growing 5.4 per cent at current prices.

Manufacturing also declined 0.9 per cent in real terms.

The slowdown reflects wider economic challenges across the region, with the UAE's economy expanding just 0.4 per cent in the first half amid disruption caused by the Iran war.

Helal Almarri, director general of the Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism, said the figures demonstrated the emirate's ability to navigate global uncertainty.

"Dubai’s H1 2026 GDP performance reflects the strength and adaptability of an economy built to navigate periods of significant global uncertainty," he said.

Dubai is also moving ahead with Dh2.1 trillion in projects covering housing, aviation and transport, including the expansion of Al Maktoum International Airport, as part of efforts to support long-term economic growth.

Meanwhile, Dubai CommerCity announced a Dh1.8 billion expansion this month to boost its digital commerce sector and attract more technology investment.

He added that continued growth across strategic sectors highlighted the strength of Dubai's economic fundamentals and its focus on long-term development.

Dubai is pressing ahead with its D33 economic agenda, which aims to strengthen its position as a global business and investment centre.

The emirate has also introduced measures to support businesses, including a Dh1.5 billion economic relief package announced in May to help sectors affected by regional uncertainty.

IPL 2027 will be the 20th edition of the T20 league, with the Indian cricket board planning to celebrate the milestone moment on a big scale.

The teams too are busy. A number of sides have already made changes ahead of the new season, with most developments taking place at the management level. Here is the story so far ahead of IPL 2027.

One of the bigger developments ahead of IPL 2027 is the recruitment of India’s multiple World Cup winner Yuvraj Singh as coach.

IPL team Delhi Capitals add Saudi Arabia to global academy network

Former India all-rounder Yuvraj was unveiled as Delhi Capitals' assistant and batting coach.

It will be Yuvraj’s first official stint as coach, having earlier mentored young batters like Abhishek Sharma in his personal capacity.

“I am excited to begin a new chapter in my life with the Delhi Capitals,” Yuvraj said in a statement. “I have an old association with the franchise and know the owners well, which makes this a special opportunity for me.”

Delhi Capitals have once again undergone a major personnel change, coinciding with change of management control; the franchise’s co-owners exchange management control every two years.

Former India captain Sourav Ganguly will be in charge of Delhi Capitals franchise after being appointed ⁠as head coach for the 2027 season.

Ganguly will have his protege Yuvraj in the dugout as he embarks upon another stint with the franchise that is yet to the win the league title.

Ganguly joined the Delhi franchise as an adviser in 2019 and also was the ⁠team's director of cricket in 2023/24. The former opener took over from Hemang Badani.

The biggest move in the IPL happened at Chennai as Stephen Fleming stepped down as head coach of the highly successful Super Kings after 18 years in charge.

Fleming had formed a wildly successful partnership with Chennai icon MS Dhoni, which brought in five IPL and two (defunct) Champions League T20 titles.

However, with Dhoni largely out of the picture and the Super Kings struggling over the last three seasons, Fleming’s tenure came to an end.

The former New Zealand captain quickly moved to a set-up that should suit his cricket philosophy – the England Test squad.

Fleming took over from Brendon McCullum, who remains England’s white-ball coach, after a tumultuous year which was riddled with questionable player and team behaviour.

Fleming’s former Chennai associate Eric Simons has joined him as Test bowling coach.

The wicketkeeper batter returned to Delhi Capitals for the 2027 season after completing his trade from Lucknow Super Giants.

Pant had become the most expensive Indian player in IPL history when he was acquired by Lucknow for a record $3.2 million in 2025. But that price tag weighed him down as he failed to turn things around at the Super Giants, resulting in a trade that has seen Pant take a substantial pay cut.

In return, Lucknow got the services of left-arm spinner Kuldeep Yadav. Both players returned to the cities where they played at the domestic level.

For Pant, it will be a critical season as he seems to be slipping down the pecking order in Indian cricket, being frozen out of the T20 side and not considered in ODIs as well. A good IPL 2027 could see him force his way into the team for the ODI World Cup in southern Africa next year.

The 2011 World Cup winner has been appointed as the new Chennai coach, taking over from Fleming, and reuniting with his former captain Dhoni who remains an active player on paper.

Zaheer was with Mumbai Indians management from 2018 until 2022, before being named as mentor of Lucknow. Now, he takes over as head coach of the most successful franchise in IPL history, with the aim of forming a clear path ahead with the talismanic Dhoni expected to move further away from the playing side of the team.

This seems like a never ending saga. India all-rounder Hardik Pandya left the Mumbai Indians franchise, enjoyed a wildly successful two seasons at Gujarat Titans, was brought back to Mumbai in a hugely controversial move and has been struggling there since, with Rohit Sharma, Suryakumar Yadav and Jasprit Bumrah also in leadership positions.

Now, there is a strong possibility that Rohit is handed the captaincy once again, with the India opener having hit form at the international level in ODIs. Pandya, meanwhile, is struggling with fitness with multiple injuries this season and doubts over his long-term availability.

Pandya, however, remains an attractive option for many franchises as he is one of the few quality all-rounders in the country with a proven record with title winning sides. The seam-bowling all-rounder could be traded ahead of IPL 2027.

Elsewhere, Sunrisers Hyderabad brought left-arm seamer T. Natarajan back into the team, trading him from Delhi Capitals who got leg-spinner Zeeshan Ansari in return.

Big changes are taking place at Mumbai Indians. The franchise parted ways with head coach Mahela Jayawardene.

The Sri Lankan great was Mumbai's head coach for the last two seasons - his second stint with the franchise - and coincided with a leadership crisis where Pandya was brought in as captain despite the presence of MI veterans Rohit, Suryakumar and Bumrah.

"Mumbai Indians has been a very special part of my journey for over a decade now," Jayawardene said in an statement. "The players, coaching team, and above all the fans have made this an experience I will always treasure."

headline: Iran freestyle wrestlers win gold at World U23 C’ships in US
summary: TEHRAN, Oct. 18 (MNA) – Iranian freestyle wrestlers “Abolfazl Mohammadnejad” (125kg) and “Abolfazl Rahmani” (92kg) claimed gold at the World U23 Championships in the United States.
body_text:
TEHRAN, Oct. 18 (MNA) – Iranian freestyle wrestlers “Abolfazl Mohammadnejad” (125kg) and “Abolfazl Rahmani” (92kg) claimed gold at the World U23 Championships in the United States.

The medal matches and finals for the 61kg, 74kg, 86kg, 92kg, and 125kg weight classes at the U23 World Freestyle Wrestling Championships took place early this morning in Las Vegas, the United States. In 125kg category, Abolfazl Mohammadnejad defeated Kochanov of Ukraine 10–0 to advance to the quarterfinals.

Mohammadnejad defeated Bestayev from Russia 11–0 and advanced to the semifinals. At that stage, Mohammadnejad overcame Khetag Karsanov of Azerbaijan 5–0 to reach the final. In the final, Mohammadnejad secured a 10–0 victory over Abramishvili from Georgia, clinching Iran’s second gold medal.

headline: Rubio heads to Central Asia while other US officials hit foreign policy hot spots
summary: By Gram Slattery and Simon LewisWASHINGTON, Oct 18 (Reuters) - While the Iran war smolders, Saudi Arabia fights theHouthis and a new rift opens in US-Ukraine relations, Secretary of State Marco Rubio travels on Sunday to Uzbekistan, a nation far removed from the biggest US foreign policy challenges.The top US diplomat is scheduled to land in Samarkand on Sunday to meet with leaders from the C5+1, a grouping that brings together the United States and the Muslim-majority post-Soviet states of Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan.
body_text:
By Gram Slattery and Simon Lewis

WASHINGTON, Oct 18 (Reuters) - While the Iran war smolders, Saudi Arabia fights theHouthis and a new rift opens in US-Ukraine relations, Secretary of State Marco Rubio travels on Sunday to Uzbekistan, a nation far removed from the biggest US foreign policy challenges.

The top US diplomat is scheduled to land in Samarkand on Sunday to meet with leaders from the C5+1, a grouping that brings together the United States and the Muslim-majority post-Soviet states of Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan.

US officials have portrayed resource-rich Central Asia —the region between China, Russia and Iran — as worthy of more attention than it received from US President Donald Trump's predecessors.

Trump hosted C5 leaders at the White House last November, when Kazakhstan agreed to join the Abraham Accords, a series of agreements under which Muslim-majority countries have normalized or deepened relations with Israel. Separately, Trump met with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev at the United Nations General Assembly last September.

Regional politics aside, thetrip fits an emerging pattern in which Rubio often visits regions not at the center of the news cycle, while leaving some more fraught foreign-policyportfolios to other Trump aides, including special envoys SteveWitkoff and Jared Kushner and Vice President JD Vance.

For instance, Rubio has not visited Kyiv or Moscow since becoming secretary of state. He was not present for talks between US and Ukrainian officials in Florida earlier this month, when US officials pressed Ukraine to stop hitting Russian refineries. Vance, not Rubio, represented the US in Pakistan during peace talks with Iran in April.

Rubio's previous foreign trip, in early October, took him to Greece, Portugal and Iceland.

Trump administration officials have typically rejected any suggestion that cabinet-level officials should focus their travels on geopolitical capitals and hot spots.

Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau, for instance, said on X last week that the idea only certain destinations were worthy of visits from secretaries of state "perfectly encapsulates the decadence and degeneracy of the contemporary US foreign policy establishment."

US-RUSSIA RELATIONS LOOM

One Central Asian diplomat, speaking on the condition of anonymity, said officials in the region are wondering to what extent the US will continue targeting Russian sanctions evasion. All C5 states, while drawing closer to the US, have deep historical ties with Moscow, and the region has facilitated Russian imports and exports that violate US and European Union sanctions, Western officials say.

In the past, the US has pushed regional states to clamp down on those illicit flows.

But Trump struck a deal with Moscow this month toimport Russian diesel, a move to lower domestic fuel prices before the congressional midterm elections. On Friday, Trump waived all provisions of legislation that would have allowed him to slap massive tariffs on some nations that buy significant amounts of Russian crude or otherwise help Moscow evade sanctions. Among the nations that could have been affected, experts have said, are India and Kazakhstan.

India, which Rubio will visit after Uzbekistan, remains the world's No. 2 Russian crude importer after China, despite Trump saying in February that India had agreed to stop buying oil from Russia.

Additional questions hang over a potential trade deal with India and an expansion of the Abraham Accords in Central Asia.

A US official, speaking on the condition of anonymity, described the trade deal on Friday as "pretty much done," raising the possibility that an agreement could be announced during the Rubio trip.

Separately, the US has talked to additional Central Asian nations aboutjoining the Abraham Accords, Reuters reported last year, conversations that could in theory continue in Samarkand.

More than 200 business executives will accompanyRubioto Uzbekistan, the State Department said. The Central Asian diplomat said the Trump administration has focused its commercial efforts on expanding access to the area's rare earth mineral resources.

The trip to Uzbekistanwas largely organized by SergioGor, the US ambassador to India, the Central Asian diplomat said.Gor, who was born in Uzbekistan and is a friend of Rubio, also serves as the US special envoy for South and Central Asian affairs.

After Uzbekistan,Rubio will visit the Indian cities of Mumbai and Jamnagar to meet with business leaders, including Reliance Industries Chairman Mukesh Ambani, who earned the Trump administration's favor earlier in the year by backing a new refinery in Texas. Rubio most recently visited India five months ago.

The trip is due to wrap up on Thursday.

(Reporting by Gram Slattery and Simon Lewis; Editing by Sergio Non and Rod Nickel)

headline: 'It's family': Lebanese villagers dread looming UN peacekeeper pullout
summary: From his shop in south Lebanon near the Israeli border, Mark Diab says life in his village will be turned upside down when a decades-long United Nations peacekeeping force pulls out next year. "UNIFIL isn't just business, to us it's family," said Diab, 59, whose sister is among residents of Ibl al-Saqi who have married peacekeepers from the UN Interim Force in Lebanon over the years. She now lives in Spain.
body_text:
From his shop in south Lebanon near the Israeli border, Mark Diab says life in his village will be turned upside down when a decades-long United Nations peacekeeping force pulls out next year.

"UNIFIL isn't just business, to us it's family," said Diab, 59, whose sister is among residents of Ibl al-Saqi who have married peacekeepers from the UN Interim Force in Lebanon over the years. She now lives in Spain.

"We're basically open because of the UN. We started when I was young," Diab said from his shop, just down the road from a UNIFIL base, selling clothes along with other items including alcohol and headphones.

The force's withdrawal will hurt the local economy and "will impact our relationships... and we'll lose security and stability," he said, as the sound of an explosion rang out in the distance.

"I'm very sad they're leaving... We've spent a lifetime with them."

UNIFIL has served as a buffer since Israel first invaded Lebanon in 1978.

It has become part of the fabric of south Lebanese villages like Ibl al-Saqi after decades spent monitoring border hostilities and supporting local communities, including with humanitarian assistance.

But after pressure from Washington, the UN Security Council last year voted to end the force's mandate on December 31, 2026.

In a narrow garden in Ibl al-Saqi called Norway Square, tattered Norwegian and Lebanese flags flew near plaques paying tribute to peacekeepers from the Scandinavian country whose arrival decades ago forged ties that run deep.

A street sign points to a town in Norway about 5,200 kilometres (more than 3,200 miles) away.

Nearby, an Indian flag flew at Mahatma Gandhi Park close to a statue, posters and plaques set up by Indian peacekeepers.

Ibl al-Saqi is located just outside an Israeli-declared "security zone" which runs around 10 kilometres deep in Lebanese territory along the border. It was established after the latest war between Israel and the Iran-backed Hezbollah group erupted this year.

Israeli troops operate nearby, and locals advised AFP journalists to avoid southern parts of the otherwise quiet, peaceful village, nestled among hills covered in olive groves.

From his municipal office near framed UNIFIL pictures and paraphernalia, mayor George Rahhal said the peacekeepers had brought stability and reassurance to villagers over years of conflict and uncertainty.

"They've left a positive mark on everybody's hearts, firstly through security, then the economy, healthcare, supporting schools, the sick," said Rahhal, who like others in the village also has Norwegian citizenship and speaks the language.

"At some point the UN has to leave... but not in these circumstances."

Lebanon has called for UNIFIL's mandate to be extended, fearing a security vacuum at a time when hostilities prevent the Lebanese army, whose resources are limited, from deploying across the country's south.

Rahhal said many Ibl al-Saqi residents were UNIFIL employees or contractors.

Almost "the entire community will be impacted" economically by the withdrawal, directly or indirectly, he said.

"We can live after the international force (leaves), but how and where and who will be responsible for us?"

UNIFIL now counts about 7,500 personnel from nearly 50 countries.

Spokesperson Kandice Ardiel told AFP it also "has around 400 national staff" and works with numerous local companies providing contracted services.

Peacekeepers are stationed in many Israeli-occupied areas now off-limits to most Lebanese after the most recent war. Many border villages have seen heavy destruction.

More than 4,300 people have been killed in Lebanon since March, including seven peacekeepers caught in the crossfire.

Israel still carries out strikes and demolitions despite a lull in hostilities since late June.

Andrea Tenenti, who served as UNIFIL spokesperson for almost 20 years, told AFP that the force's presence "was not simply about maintaining peace and security".

UNIFIL "has long been the second largest employer and economic contributor in southern Lebanon, after the Lebanese state", he said.

"Its economic footprint, however, extended far beyond its direct workforce," he added, with associated activities "supporting a much wider network of businesses and livelihoods".

Its withdrawal "risks creating a significant vacuum... at a particularly critical time".

At a workshop in Ibl al-Saqi, labourers supervised clattering embroidery machines sewing customised items including banners and tags for peacekeepers stationed nearby.

Shelves were packed with colourful souvenirs and keepsakes for UNIFIL personnel -- the business's main market after Lebanon's economy collapsed in 2019.

Co-owner Khaled Nahra, 48, said the workshop had been running for some 25 years and had around a dozen employees, but would be forced to close when UNIFIL leaves.

"We've stayed in our village... this was the best thing about working with the UN," he said.

"There are people who've been working here for 15... 20 years. They're like me. They don't know what to do."

Our correspondents are already on the next chapter. Read everything they file, from $2/week.

headline: Live: Vance blames immigration for violence during protests in France
summary: US Vice President JD Vance blamed immigration for violence during protests in France on Saturday, sharing footage of a city hall on fire and warning Americans that congressional Democrats sought a similar future for the United States. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.
body_text:
Issued on: 18/10/2026 - 05:09Modified: 18/10/2026 - 07:00

US Vice President JD Vance blamed immigration for violence during protests in France on Saturday, sharing footage of a city hall on fire and warning Americans that congressional Democrats sought a similar future for the United States. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

France's Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said police arrested 1,200 people in protests across the country on Saturday, adding that 150 police were hurt.

"It's a miracle the toll wasn't higher," he said.

It's not clear how many demonstrators were wounded in the violent clashes with police that broke out on the outskirts of the largely peaceful marches that took place across France, though one 17-year-old boy in Saint-Etienne had his hand blown off by a police stun grenade.

US Vice President JD Vance posted on X Saturday blaming immigration for violence during protests in France, while sharing a video showing the city hall in Limoges on fire.

"Western liberals imported the third world into France and other countries in the name of diversity and compassion. They ignored fundamental questions of assimilation and compatibility. They were told it would lead to this and they didn't listen," Vance wrote on X.

"I pray that France, a beautiful country of amazing people, will stop this madness before more of its landmarks burn," he added.

Vance, 42, represents the most nationalist and identitarian wing of the Republican Party, and has been a virulent critic of Europe's immigration policies, which he considers too lax.

Welcome to the France 24 liveblog covering the student protests in France. You can catch up on yesterday's key developments here.

• Looters seized the opportunity to raid and vandalise a host of shops and businesses across France, from bakeries and supermarkets to tech stores.

• A protester's hand was blown off by a police crowd-control grenade as nationwide demonstrations continued, with an estimated 800,000 people taking part.

• Students, unions, and yellow vest protesters joined forces to protest against austerity measures and the cost of living.

(FRANCE 24 with Reuters, AP and AFP)

headline: Iran's Araghchi, OIC chief discuss Islamic world issues
summary: TEHRAN, Oct. 18 (MNA) – Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met Organisation of Islamic Cooperation Secretary-General Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed in Baghdad, discussing issues facing the Islamic world and the organization's agenda.
body_text:
TEHRAN, Oct. 18 (MNA) – Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met Organisation of Islamic Cooperation Secretary-General Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed in Baghdad, discussing issues facing the Islamic world and the organization's agenda.

Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi, in Iraq to attend the annual session of the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers, met Secretary-General Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed on Saturday afternoon.

The two exchanged views on issues facing the Islamic world and items on the organization's agenda.

Araghchi congratulated the new secretary-general and stressed the importance of the OIC playing an effective role in strengthening solidarity among Islamic countries and confronting common challenges and threats against the Islamic world, particularly regarding occupied Palestine.

Pointing to Iran's status as a founding member of the OIC, Araghchi said the Islamic Republic expects the secretariat to act with a professional and impartial approach to strengthen Islamic understanding and solidarity, and to prevent any impression of bias by the secretariat for or against any member state.

The meeting also covered developments in the Arabian Peninsula and the escalation of conflicts, with Araghchi stressing Iran's readiness to help facilitate dialogue and engagement between Saudi Arabia and Yemen.

The OIC secretary-general, for his part, thanked the Iranian foreign minister for attending the summit and said the secretariat is keen to draw on Iran's experience and capacities to design and advance new initiatives on mediation and the settlement of disputes among Islamic countries.

headline: 12 killed as truck runs over devotees near temple in central India: police

The accident occurred in Gwalior when a truck loaded with paddy lost control on a steep road and crashed into the outer wall and gate of the Sheetla Mata Temple, senior police official Dharmveer Singh said.

He said 39 people were taken to a hospital, of whom 12 died.

Ruchika Chauhan, a local civil official, said an investigation was underway to determine the cause of the accident.

body_text:
Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport reopened on Sunday, after it was closed because of attacks by the Houthi rebels in Yemen.

However, many airlines have not yet lifted their suspension of flights to the Saudi capital and other destinations in the kingdom.

Some carriers have extended cancellations into November and beyond, while others are preparing to resume services. The disruption comes amid wider regional uncertainty, which has already affected airlines’ Middle East operations.

UAE flight delays possible as autumn weather causes reduced visibility

Here’s how major airlines have adjusted operations and when flights are expected to resume.

Etihad Airways has cancelled all flights between Abu Dhabi and Riyadh until Monday, October 19.

Services to Dammam and Jeddah have also been affected, although flight listings show Dammam services and Jeddah flights EY601, EY602, EY603 and EY604 scheduled to operate on Sunday, October 18.

Emirates services from Dubai to Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam have been affected by cancellations and schedule changes.

Google’s flight listings show six services between Dubai and Riyadh scheduled for October 20. These include outbound flights EK815, EK817 and EK819, along with return services EK816, EK818 and EK820.

The airline has cancelled flights to Riyadh, Dammam and Abha up to October 19.

Air Arabia has cancelled services between Sharjah and several Saudi destinations including Riyadh, Abha, Dammam and Taif. No resumption date has been announced.

The airline has temporarily suspended flights to and from Riyadh and Dammam. A resumption date has not yet been announced.

Gulf Air has said flights after Sunday, October 18 are currently proceeding as scheduled, following its previously announced Riyadh cancellations.

Oman Air has announced that all flights to and from Riyadh are suspended until October 22.

The Omani low-cost airline has cancelled flights to and from Riyadh and Dammam until October 31, citing regional security developments.

The French airline has extended its suspension of flights to and from Riyadh up to October 24.

British Airways is scheduled to return with a limited service to Riyadh on November 3, operating one flight daily, according to previously announced plans.

The airline discontinued flights to Jeddah in April as part of wider changes to its Middle East operations.

Air India and Air India Express have suspended flights to and from Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam until October 24.

The Indian low-cost airline has suspended flights to and from Riyadh until October 24 and Jeddah until October 21.

The Hong Kong airline has extended its suspension of flights to Riyadh up to January 31, 2027.

The airline announced a temporary suspension of flights to Riyadh on October 9, without setting out a resumption date. The Pakistan Airports Authority said at the time that its other Saudi services were continuing as usual.

The US airline has postponed the launch of flights between Atlanta and Riyadh until March 2027. Services had been scheduled to begin on October 23.

The Indian airline has cancelled flights to and from Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah up to October 24.

The German airline has suspended flights to Riyadh until November 18, extending its previously announced October 16 deadline.

The Lufthansa Group’s advisory also lists Dammam services as suspended through November 30. Eurowings, part of the group, is scheduled to resume flights to Jeddah on November 12.

Malaysia Airlines has announced that flights to and from Jeddah and Madinah will resume on October 18 after a safety review.

The Dutch airline has extended cancellations of all flights to Riyadh and Dammam up to October 31.

The Philippine flag carrier has suspended Riyadh flights PR654 and PR655 until November 29, citing the security situation at King Khalid International Airport.

headline: Xi stresses prioritizing ecological conservation
summary: TEHRAN, Oct. 18 (MNA) – Chinese President Xi Jinping has emphasized the need to unswervingly follow the path of prioritizing ecological conservation and pursuing green development.
body_text:
TEHRAN, Oct. 18 (MNA) – Chinese President Xi Jinping has emphasized the need to unswervingly follow the path of prioritizing ecological conservation and pursuing green development.

Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks during an inspection trip on Friday to the city of Ulanqab, north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. Huangqihai Lake in Ulanqab was once on the verge of drying up due to climate and other impacts. After years of comprehensive conservation, its water body has gradually been restored and expanded. During the inspection trip, Xi visited the Huangqihai Lake nature reserve, where he was briefed on Inner Mongolia's efforts to strengthen ecological conservation, and inspected the lake's shoreline and mudflats and observed birds inhabiting the area. He stressed the need to fully implement the country's wetland protection law, firmly uphold ecological red lines, and safeguard biodiversity. For degraded wetland ecosystems, he called for giving priority to natural restoration, supplemented by human intervention, and carrying out restoration in a scientific and sound manner. Xi also visited Chahar High Tech Development Zone in Ulanqab, and learned about Inner Mongolia's progress in advancing the construction of a hub for the "East Data, West Computing" project and the development of the green computing power industry. Noting that implementing the "East Data, West Computing" project and building a national integrated computing power network is an important decision made by the CPC Central Committee, Xi stressed the need to ensure the efficient operation of completed projects and finish the construction of follow-up projects on schedule. He called on all parties to earnestly implement the requirements for efficient, green and safe development, actively promote the development of the green computing power industry, and make greater contributions to building Digital China and developing new quality productive forces. Xi also viewed displays of local agricultural and livestock specialties, encouraging local authorities to better align production with sales to help farmers and herders increase their incomes. Source: Xinhua

body_text:
Millions of Sudanese displaced by the country’s war are struggling to rebuild their lives amid worsening humanitarian conditions and a severe shortfall in aid funding, as political figures urge greater international pressure to end the conflict.

Mohamed Abdel Hakam, a leader of the Sumoud alliance, which advocates civilian rule in Sudan, described the crisis as one of the world’s largest humanitarian disasters and called for greater attention to the plight of millions seeking safety and a return to normal life.

“I believe the catastrophe unfolding in Sudan, which is weighing on millions of Sudanese, is the largest humanitarian disaster in the world at this time,” he told Sky News Arabia.

Deadly air strike on goldminers lays bare Sudan's economic deprivation

He said the crisis had been described by the UN secretary-general and other UN officials as a “forgotten crisis”, leaving millions struggling to live with dignity amid displacement, harsh conditions in shelters and an uncertain future.

“Millions of Sudanese are now living in a state of loss and uncertainty. They want nothing more than to return safely to their homes and places of residence and have normal life restored after enduring immense hardship as a result of this brutal war,” he said.

Dr Salah Al Amin, a Sudanese expert in humanitarian affairs, said millions of people had been displaced within Sudan or had fled abroad as refugees, many of whom were facing additional hardship because of funding shortages.

“Funding has fallen this year compared with previous years, to the point that there is a shortfall of more than 47 per cent in the funding that should reach these refugees,” he told Sky News Arabia.

He said international organisations aiding refugees were also struggling financially.

“Even Unicef and the UN refugee agency, which is responsible for refugees around the world, are complaining about funding problems, to the extent that many employees who were working to provide services to refugees have been laid off,” he said.

The conflict between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), led by Gen Abdel Fattah Al Burhan, and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces has devastated the country of 50 million people and battered its economy. International efforts aimed at ending the war have struggled to secure a lasting ceasefire.

The war, now well into its fourth year, has created one of ​the world's worst humanitarian crises, displacing about 14 million people.

Mohamed Al Faky, a former civilian member of Sudan’s ruling Sovereignty Council, urged the international community to maintain pressure on army chief Gen Al Burhan to end the war, accusing him of breaking promises and derailing peace initiatives.

“This man is, of course, a professional liar and has derailed a number of initiatives,” Mr Al Faky said in an interview with Sky News Arabia.

“He had promised regional countries and the United States in September 2024 that he would go to Geneva, but then backed out at the last minute,” he said.

“Therefore, the pressure must continue, and the siege must continue. I believe the international community has finally seen through this man’s lies and is now exerting sustained pressure on him.”

Mr Al Faky also criticised what he described as attempts by Gen Al Burhan to manufacture popular support through public appearances, including videos showing him playing cards with soldiers and mingling with crowds.

“These are desperate attempts that can only come from a desperate political mind that does not understand what is happening in Sudan or recognise the suffering that Sudanese people are enduring in exile and inside the country,” he said.

“It is a mentality that mocks the suffering of Sudanese people and the major issues they face, including displacement, hunger, and the loss of their land, property and memories.”

Mr Al Faky said the videos had become a source of ridicule in Sudanese media and on social media, despite being portrayed by Gen Al Burhan’s inner circle as a way to boost his popularity.

He challenged the army chief to demonstrate his support by organising a public rally rather than appearing unannounced at markets and celebrations.

“If you have popular support, organise an event in your own name and deliver a speech in one of the major squares, whether Freedom Square or Martyrs’ Square. Invite people,” Mr Al Faky said.

“But showing up uninvited at markets and celebrations is not a measure of popular support. These people are simply walking along the streets and visiting markets to meet their daily needs, only for this man to suddenly confront them.”

Mr Al Faky also claimed that Gen Al Burhan’s reported ambition to become president lacked support within the military establishment and the Islamic Movement.

He said the three remaining military members of the Sovereignty Council — Shams Al Din Kabbashi, Yasser Al Atta and Ibrahim Jaber — opposed the idea, as did the Islamic Movement, which he said believed Gen Al Burhan could not assume the presidency without an agreement.

“No such agreement has been reached,” Mr Al Faky said.

body_text:
Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid, Vice President and Ruler of Dubai, has launched the seventh edition of the Arab Hope Makers initiative, celebrating philanthropists across the region who dedicate their efforts to improving communities.

The initiative, the largest of its kind in the Arab world, recognises individuals, volunteer groups and non-profit organisations driving change through charitable, social and humanitarian work. Applications are open at arabhopemakers.com, with the winner receiving a prize of Dh1 million ($272,000).

"Nurturing hope is a triumph for life itself," said Sheikh Mohammed. "The hope we cultivate today will yield prosperity, peace and safety in people's lives tomorrow."

'Everyone's a winner': Sheikh Hamdan crowns Arab Hope Makers champions

The UAE will "always remain a nation of good deeds and optimism, inspiring positive change across the region and the world", said Sheikh Mohammed.

Mohammed Al Gergawi, Minister of Cabinet Affairs and Secretary General of Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum Global Initiatives, said the initiative has contributed significantly to humanitarian action and volunteering across the Arab world since its launch in 2017. More than 335,000 participants have taken part in six iterations.

"The initiative shines a light on the great aspects of our Arab societies and the potential and talents dedicated to sincerely improving people's lives," Mr Al Gergawi said.

The most recent edition crowned Fouzia Mahmoudi from Morocco as the 2025 Arab Hope Maker after her foundation, Operation Smile, performed more than 19,000 surgeries on children born with cleft lips and palates.

The two other finalists, Hend Alhajri from Kuwait and Abderrahmane Rais from Morocco, were also awarded Dh1 million each, bringing the total prize pool for the sixth edition to Dh3 million ($817,000).

Ms Alhajri founded Fatima House, a refuge for orphaned children in Tanzania, while Mr Rais launched a humanitarian initiative supporting widows and women in need across Morocco.

Operating under MBRGI, the initiative is open to applicants from across the Arab world and globally whose projects address community development, alleviate suffering or tackle local challenges on a voluntary, non-profit basis.

Egypt's top security body on Sunday pledged “all necessary and possible forms of support” to Saudi Arabia.

It met hours before parliament convened to vote on authorising President Abdel Fattah El Sisi to help defend the kingdom against attacks by the Houthi rebels in Yemen.

The National Defence Council, chaired by Mr El Sisi at Al Ittihadiya Palace in Cairo, said Saudi Arabia's security was inextricably linked to Egypt's own and to wider Arab national security.

The support would help the kingdom defend its security and territory, as well as the Islamic holy sites, the presidency said.

It cited the “escalating unacceptable attacks” on the kingdom and called for more diplomacy to calm the region.

The statement did not mention troops. But Mostafa Bakry, an MP and TV host close to the state, said on X that the council had approved sending forces to Saudi Arabia on “a defensive mission”.

The Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly, Speaker of Parliament Hisham Badawy, Defence Minister Lt Gen Ashraf Zaher and intelligence chiefs attended.

Under Article 152 of Egypt's constitution, the President cannot declare war or send the army on a combat mission abroad without consulting the council. He also needs the approval of two-thirds of MPs. Parliament's rules require the vote to take place in an urgent closed session.

The emergency sitting was set for 1pm on Sunday. The House has a majority of pro-Sisi legislators who are widely expected to approve the request, as they have backed previous policies championed by the President.

Mr El Sisi made the request on Saturday.

“It is inconceivable that we would allow Saudi Arabia, its security or stability to be harmed,” he said. Egypt would act only if Riyadh asked, he said in a speech at the Military Academy. “We do not want to fight or attack anyone. We will only defend Saudi Arabia,” he added.

The move drew a swift warning from Sanaa. Yahya Al Raei, speaker of the Houthi-run parliament there, wrote to Mr Badawi on Saturday.

The Houthi-controlled body is not recognised internationally.

“We categorically reject Egypt being dragged” into “the same trench as the takfiri forces and the Israeli occupation entity,” he wrote. Such a path “would pose a grave danger to its national security,” he said, urging Cairo to take a “courageous stance”.

He accused Riyadh of waging “aggression and siege” against Yemen for more than 12 years. He said it had walked away from a peace road map and ended a period of calm by striking Sanaa airport. The letter was carried by the Houthis' Al Masirah TV.

Early on Sunday, the Saudi-led coalition said it had shot down two ballistic missiles fired at Khamis Mushait and three drones over Riyadh and the Eastern Province.

The Houthis have launched 20 attacks on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport since October 1, coalition spokesman Maj Gen Turki Al Malki said on Thursday. Attacks on Saudi airports have killed 19 people and wounded 364, he said. The deadliest, on October 10 in Riyadh, killed 13, including an Egyptian flight attendant.

The coalition also said it intercepted a missile aimed at Madinah on Thursday. The Houthis denied firing it. The UN Security Council condemned the attacks as “escalatory” that same day and backed the kingdom's right to self-defence.

Cairo's move also comes as a new alliance takes shape around Riyadh. Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement on August 7.

The pact provides that an attack on one member is treated as an attack on all. Riyadh activated it on October 5, and Pakistan said the partners would send the “agreed military forces” to the kingdom.

While Egypt is not yet a member, Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said last week that joining was “under serious consideration”.

Cairo has long been wary of binding pacts. Joining one could strain its ties with Iran and its peace treaty with Israel, while potentially drawing Egypt into a war with the Houthis.

Houthi attacks on Red Sea shipping have already caused heavy losses in Suez Canal revenue.

Over the past week, many commentators have cited Egypt's costly intervention in Yemen in the 1960s as a reason not to rush into such an agreement.

Instead, Cairo has taken smaller steps. On August 13, it joined a Saudi-led naval coalition set up after the Houthis declared a blockade on Saudi shipping.

Egypt joined the Saudi-led coalition that intervened in Yemen in 2015. In July 2020, MPs voted unanimously in a closed session to allow combat missions abroad as fighting in Libya neared Egypt's western border.

Approval of the request would not, in itself, mean that troops would be deployed.

headline: Iran urges US to accept proposal to reopen Strait of Hormuz
summary: DUBAI, Oct 18 (Reuters) - Iran's offer to the United States to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days is still on the table, Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi told Iranian media outlets on Sunday.Iran presented its proposal in mid-September after an interim ceasefire collapsed. Tehran later acknowledged receiving a US response but Iran’s security chief said last week negotiations have stalled because Washington failed to address all seven conditions for reopening the strait.
body_text:
DUBAI, Oct 18 (Reuters) - Iran's offer to the United States to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days is still on the table, Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi told Iranian media outlets on Sunday.

Iran presented its proposal in mid-September after an interim ceasefire collapsed. Tehran later acknowledged receiving a US response but Iran’s security chief said last week negotiations have stalled because Washington failed to address all seven conditions for reopening the strait.

"Our situation is clear and based on the seven-days proposal presented to the US. They shared comments which we are reviewing, but our proposal is still on the table and if there is any honesty on the US part, which there isn't, the way to reopening the Strait of Hormuz is obvious," Araqchi said while in Baghdad for a meeting of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation.

Iran's conditions include, among other demands, the lifting of the US blockade on its ports, the lifting of US sanctions on its oil exports as well as ending hostilities on all regional fronts.

If Washington accepts Tehran's conditions, the strait could reopen within six days, with talks resuming the following day, Araqchi said.

A central point of disagreement has been Washington’s insistence on addressing Iran's nuclear programme from the outset.

US Vice President JD Vance said earlier this month that Iran must make a "meaningful" reduction in its uranium enrichment capacity to satisfy US demands and end the countries' eight-month war.

Tehran says negotiations should initially focus on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, which before the war carried about a fifth of the global trade in oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG), and restoring security in the waterway.

(Reporting by Dubai Newsroom; Editing by Joe Bavier, Elaine Hardcastle)

headline: Saudi landmark closes offices, chopper pilots killed near Yemen
summary: Riyadh's Kingdom Centre skyscraper ordered remote working for office tenants on Sunday following repeated Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, as the Saudi-led coalition said two pilots were killed in a crash near the Yemen border. The imposing, 99-storey landmark announced "mandatory" remote working until further notice. No reason was given for the order, but it comes a week after 13 people were killed in a major Houthi attack on Riyadh's international airport.
body_text:
Riyadh's Kingdom Centre skyscraper ordered remote working for office tenants on Sunday following repeated Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, as the Saudi-led coalition said two pilots were killed in a crash near the Yemen border.

The imposing, 99-storey landmark announced "mandatory" remote working until further notice. No reason was given for the order, but it comes a week after 13 people were killed in a major Houthi attack on Riyadh's international airport.

The Saudi coalition's decade-plus war with the Iran-backed Houthis has reignited during the US-Iran war, with regular attacks reported by both sides.

Tenants of the Kingdom Centre, which towers over central Riyadh, include financial services giant Merril Lynch, management consultancy McKinsey and the International Monetary Fund.

"Please be advised that remote working arrangements are mandatory for all office employees at Kingdom Centre, effective immediately and until further notice," the building's management said in an email seen by AFP.

"Kindly refrain from attending the offices during this period," it added. The mall at the foot of the building remains open.

It comes as schools recently extended remote learning measures and Riyadh's airport remains closed after last week's attack.

The order came after the coalition announced the death of two helicopter pilots in Najran near the border with Yemen, blaming a "technical malfunction", after the Houthis said they shot down an Apache helicopter in the area.

"An AH-6i reconnaissance helicopter belonging to the Ministry of National Guard crashed inside Saudi territory in Najran Region due to a technical malfunction," coalition spokesman Turki Al-Malki said, according to the official Saudi Press Agency.

"The accident resulted in the martyrdom of its aircrew, consisting of two officers."

Late on Saturday, Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said the group had "downed an Apache helicopter belonging to the Saudi enemy" in the same area.

After an uneasy, four-year truce, Yemen's conflict has surged back to life and intensified when the group seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month.

The Houthis have hit Saudi targets including tankers in the Red Sea, oil facilities and Riyadh's King Khalid International airport.

The Saudi-led coalition backing the internationally recognised government has launched repeated air raids on Houthi territory.

The coalition said overnight it intercepted two drones in the Riyadh area and a third over the oil-rich Eastern Province. Saudi authorities had earlier issued a threat alert in the capital.

The coalition also said two ballistic missiles were intercepted in the kingdom's south.

On Saturday, the Houthis reported that Saudi strikes killed 12 people in Yemen, including three children.

The Houthis have declared a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia and captured territory around the Bab al-Mandab strait, the Red Sea chokepoint and vital export route for Saudi oil since Iran blockaded the Gulf's Strait of Hormuz.

The Red Sea is a key shipping route, connecting Asia with Europe via Egypt's Suez Canal.

On Sunday, Egypt's parliament will hold an emergency session after President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi asked lawmakers to authorise support to defend Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks.

Sisi said he was willing to "carry out any measure to protect" Saudi Arabia if its leaders requested it.

"I'm not talking about fighting anyone or attacking anyone," he said on Saturday. "We are speaking only about defence."

body_text:
The UAE has formally signed the agreement to host the 2029 annual meetings of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund in Abu Dhabi.

The deal signed at the conclusion of the IMF and the WB 2026 annual meetings in Thailand, is a mark of growing international confidence in the UAE’s economic and financial ecosystem, the UAE Ministry of Finance said in a statement on Sunday.

The formal pact to host the meetings also reinforce the stature of UAE, the Arab world’s second-largest economy as a global financial hub that is helping in shaping up the stability and future of the global economic system.

CommentThe UAE's fiscal model is built to handle uncertainty

Mohamed bin Hadi Al Hussaini, Minister of State for Financial Affairs, and Khaled Balama, governor of the Central Bank of the UAE signed the agreement in the Thai capital Bangkok with World Bank president Ajay Banga, IMF managing director Kristalina Georgieva.

“The signing of the agreement marks a significant milestone, reflecting … confidence in the UAE’s readiness, the efficiency of its infrastructure and financial system, and its ability to host major international events of strategic importance,” Mr Al Hussaini said.

The hosting of the event in the UAE will provide global financial leaders and decision-makers a platform to explore how to advance the financial and monetary stability agenda as well as building development finance, the minister added.

The UAE’s selection to host the global event builds on the country’s track record in hosting major economic events. Scheduled to be held in October 2029, the summit will mark the return of the key event to the Emirates after more than a quarter-century. Dubai was chosen to host the meetings in 2003.

Participation in the annual meetings has continued to grow over the years, with more than 10,000 in-person and virtual attendees being welcomed at each event. Country group meetings, civil society forums, and press conferences with the World Bank president and IMF managing director are also held which are closely watched by financial experts and policymakers from the around the world.

The World Bank-IMF annual meetings are traditionally at their headquarters in Washington DC, and every third year a member country is selected to host them.

London was the first city outside the US to host the meetings in 1947, while the UAE and Turkey remain the only countries in the Middle East to have hosted them.

“The UAE has built institutions and infrastructure with a spirit of bold ambition and partnership, cementing its role as a global hub for economic dialogue,” Mr Banga of the World Bank Group, said.

“Abu Dhabi is a fitting host for the annual meetings where our focus is on development impact, and delivering jobs, growth, and financing at scale.”

The meetings usually bring together finance ministers, central bank governors, policymakers and economic experts, private sector representatives, civil society, media, and academics from more than 190 countries to examine the challenges and opportunities facing the global economy. The IMF and World Bank also release their outlook for growth and financial stability, discuss future policy direction that support inclusive and sustainable development.

“The UAE has become an important hub for ideas, finance, innovation, and international cooperation,” Ms Georgieva said.

The 2029 meeting in Abu Dhabi will provide an opportunity to discuss the “challenges and opportunities ahead and help shape a better future”, the IMF managing director added.

headline: Hormuz Strait to be opened once US accepts Iran’s conditions
summary: TEHRAN, Oct. 18 (MNA) – Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi says the strategic Strait of Hormuz will be reopened if the United States accepts Iran’s terms and conditions.
body_text:
TEHRAN, Oct. 18 (MNA) – Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi says the strategic Strait of Hormuz will be reopened if the United States accepts Iran’s terms and conditions.

Speaking on the sidelines of the meeting of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)’s Council of Foreign Ministers in Baghdad on Sunday, Iran’s top diplomat emphasized that the Strait of Hormuz will be reopened after the United States accepts Iran’s conditions.

In response to a question on Iran’s conditions and the possibility of a revision in the country’s nuclear positions, Araghchi stated that Iran’s conditions are entirely clear and have been presented to the American side in the form of a seven-point plan.

Referring to the meeting of the OIC’s Council of Foreign Ministers and the transfer of its chairmanship to Iraq, he stated that Iraq, as a friendly and neighboring country, has special significance for the Islamic Republic, and its success in leading the Organization of Islamic Cooperation is also of paramount importance.

Turning to the participation of OIC’s member states in this meeting, Araghchi underlined that the meeting was highly received with approximately 20 foreign ministers and over 20 deputy foreign ministers from member states attended this prestigious event.

Emphasizing the necessity for the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) to play a constructive role in resolving disputes among Muslim nations, he stated, "I raised the issue during meetings with the prime minister and foreign minister of Iraq and also the newly-appointed secretary-general of the Organization.”

Regarding the meeting’s final statement and resolutions, Araghchi stated, "At present, the resolutions have not yet been adopted, and the drafting of the final declaration is not yet complete. Our colleagues have been working over the past few days to contribute to the formulation of all the resolutions."

In response to a question regarding Iran’s conditions and the possibility of a revision in country’s nuclear stance, the foreign minister stated, "Our conditions are entirely clear and have been presented to the American side in the form of a seven-point plan. The American side has also offered its own views, which we are currently reviewing."

body_text:
Anger was growing on Sunday at Israeli settler violence in the occupied West Bank after European diplomats and an American journalist were caught up in the unrest.

Visitors from France, Belgium and Poland were among those targeted by masked settlers near the village of Taybeh on Saturday. It came a day after Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine suffered serious injuries when she was attacked by Israeli settlers.

The EU on Sunday demanded “effective measures” from Israel to stop the unrest. Poland said the attack in Taybeh, a Christian village, was evidence of what Palestinians in the West Bank face on a daily basis.

Settlers beat US journalist in attack on Palestinian olive harvest

“The attack should be met with a firm response from the Israeli authorities,” the Polish Foreign Ministry said.

US ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee demanded arrests and the prosecution of those responsible after the attack on the journalist. “Attacking a female photographer is a despicable act of terror carried out by masked cowards,” Mr Huckabee said in a post on X early on Sunday. “Dishonourable act of senseless violence.”

The US envoy said Ms Levine had been clearly identified as a journalist and was unarmed. He called for those involved to spend years in prison and demanded prosecution “to the fullest extent of the law”.

The Washington Post said Ms Levine was attacked when “dozens of masked settlers” set fire to shrubs and threw rocks in a “co-ordinated assault” on Palestinian olive harvesters.

“She was knocked to the ground, kicked repeatedly and stripped of her cameras and phone,” the paper said.

Ms Levine was later taken to hospital in Ramallah. Photos showed her lying on a trolley with a wound dressing on the left leg and a gash on her right knee, among other injuries.

On Sunday, the Post welcomed the support of the US ambassador.

“We appreciate the support we’ve gotten today for our photographer, Heidi Levine, after the brutal and unwarranted attack on her. We reiterate the call for action from the government. Press freedoms are a cornerstone for democracies,” editor Matt Murray wrote on X.

The attack comes amid renewed international concern over Israeli settler violence in the West Bank, after European diplomats and a French mayor were assaulted by masked people in a separate incident on Saturday.

Belgium criticised the attack on its consul general and the other diplomats and urged Israel to bring those responsible to justice.

Poland’s Foreign Ministry said preliminary evidence indicated Israeli settlers were responsible for the assault. Polish diplomats travelling in the convoy were unharmed, the ministry said.

“We expect the Israeli authorities to provide urgent and detailed explanations, identify those responsible and ensure that they are held accountable,” it added. “We also expect effective measures to be taken to prevent similar incidents from occurring in the future.”

French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said the mayor of a French town had also been assaulted by what he described as “extremist settlers” during Saturday’s incident. He called on Israeli authorities to stop the violence.

Israeli President Isaac Herzog called Ms Levine to apologise for the attack and urged an investigation. The Israeli military described the violence as intolerable and said the incidents would be investigated.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s office said the circumstances remained unclear and more evidence was needed before responsibility could be established. It also noted that the diplomats’ visit had not been co-ordinated with Israeli security officials.

Britain, France, Canada and other countries announced sanctions focused on Israeli settlements last month, while the US said it would not join those measures.

WASHINGTON, Oct 18 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump endorsed his ally Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday for the upcoming Israeli parliamentary election.

"Bibi Netanyahu has been Strong, Brave, and Brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition, including that coming from even Israel, itself," Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social.

"This is the kind of Partner that the United States of America is demanding of Israel, a Country for which it has done so much. Please let this Letter serve to represent my Complete and Total Endorsement of Bibi Netanyahu in his upcoming Race for Re-Election as Prime Minister of Israel."

Israel will hold a national election on October 27, its first vote since the Hamas attack on October 7, 2023 that shook the country and plunged the Middle East into turmoil, as Israel went to war in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.

The election could determine whether Netanyahu remains in power after one of the most consequential periods in Israel’s history, or is defeated by centrist rivals promising to usher in a new era.

headline: Egypt says ready to give Saudi Arabia necessary support amid Houthi conflict
summary: Oct 18 (Reuters) - Egypt is ready to provide Saudi Arabia with the support it needs to defend its security and stability, the presidency said on Sunday, as Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis intensify their attacks on the world's largest oil exporter.Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi requested an urgent parliament session to authorise the military, one of the Arab world's largest, to help defend Saudi Arabia if the kingdom requested its support.
body_text:
Oct 18 (Reuters) - Egypt is ready to provide Saudi Arabia with the support it needs to defend its security and stability, the presidency said on Sunday, as Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis intensify their attacks on the world's largest oil exporter.

Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi requested an urgent parliament session to authorise the military, one of the Arab world's largest, to help defend Saudi Arabia if the kingdom requested its support.

A parliamentary vote had been expected on authorizing the request for military support on Sunday, but discussions were due to continue on Monday, two lawmakers and local media reports said.

HOUTHIS RAMP UP ATTACKS ON SAUDI ARABIA

The Houthis have in recent days attacked Riyadh's international airport and the ​state oil giant Saudi Aramco, amid renewed fighting with the Saudi-backed forces of ​the internationally recognised government following the collapse of a truce.

"Egypt will provide Saudi Arabia with all necessary and possible forms of support to defend its security and stability, protect its resources, territorial integrity and Islamic holy sites," the Egyptian presidency said in a statement.

It followed a meeting of Egypt's National Defence Council chaired by Sisi and attended by the parliamentary speaker, the prime minister and the army chief.

Sisi said in a speech on Saturday that Egypt would act in accordance with guidance from Saudi King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, who visited Sisi on September 15, after fighting in Yemen reignited.

Egypt and ​Saudi Arabia are close strategic and economic partners. Saudi ​Arabia and ⁠other oil-rich Gulf states provided Egypt with billions of dollars in aid, central-bank deposits and investments after the military ouster of Islamist President Mohamed ⁠Morsi ​in 2013.

Egypt had previously joined the Saudi-led coalition that intervened in Yemen in 2015 to support the government against the Houthis, but played a limited combat role.

(Reporting by Momen Atallah and Mohamed Hendawy; Writing by Eman Abouhassira and Nayera Abdallah; Editing by Joe Bavier and Helen Popper)

headline: Russian, Saudi foreign ministers voice concern over tensions in southern Arabian Peninsula, Bab el-Mandeb Strait
summary: Sergey Lavrov meets Saudi, Kuwaiti counterparts in Bahrain on sidelines of Russia-GCC Strategic Dialogue meeting
body_text:
Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and his Saudi counterpart, Prince Faisal bin Farhan, expressed concern Sunday over tensions in the southern Arabian Peninsula and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait during talks in Bahrain.

The ministers met on the sidelines of the ninth ministerial meeting of the Russia-Gulf Cooperation Council Strategic Dialogue in Manama, the capital of Bahrain, and stressed the importance of maritime safety and the unimpeded passage of vessels through international waterways, according to a Russian Foreign Ministry statement.

They also discussed key issues in bilateral relations, reaffirming their commitment to regular, trust-based political dialogue and expanded trade, economic, investment, cultural and humanitarian cooperation.

Both sides also highlighted the importance of continued cooperation within the OPEC+ framework, the statement said.

Lavrov also met with Kuwaiti Foreign Minister Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah to discuss international and regional issues, focusing on the situation in the Gulf.

The ministers called for the rapid de-escalation of tensions “in this strategically important part of the world” and stressed that political and diplomatic means were the only way to resolve differences while respecting the interests of all regional countries involved.

They also reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening Russia-Kuwait ties through regular political dialogue and expanded trade, economic, cultural and humanitarian cooperation.

summary: Bahrain will become the first stop on Sergey Lavrov's Middle East tour
body_text:
MANAMA /Bahrain/, October 17. /TASS/. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov has arrived in Manama to participate in the ninth strategic dialogue between Russia and the Gulf Cooperation Council, a TASS correspondent reported.

Bahrain will become the first stop on the top Russian diplomat’s Middle East tour.

Later, Lavrov is expected to travel to Tehran for consultations with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi.

Russian Foreign Ministry’s Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said Lavrov is expected to hold a number of bilateral meetings on the sidelines of the Russia-GCC dialogue.

The previous GCC meeting in this format at the level of foreign ministers was held in Russia’s Black Sea resort city of Sochi in September 2025.

The GCC comprises Bahrain, Qatar, Kuwait, the UAE, Oman and Saudi Arabia.

Hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets across France on Saturday, October 17, to protest against rising living costs, run-down schools and cuts to public services, with demonstrations turning violent in several cities. Smaller protests over living costs also took place in Belgium, Italy and Portugal, and students rallied again in Albania.

In France, about 550,000 people took part, according to the interior ministry. The CGT union put the figure at 800,000. More than 1,200 people were arrested and more than 150 police officers were hurt. Shops were looted in Paris, the city hall in Limoges was largely destroyed by fire, protesters broke into the town hall in Marseille, and police fired tear gas in several cities.

French police clashed with protesters and rioters across France on Saturday as around 550,000 people joined nationwide protests, including 110,000 in Paris. https://t.co/yqCumaHBBp

Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu blamed the “ultra-left” and criminals for the violence. Reuters described the day as some of the worst violence in France for decades.

Most protests began around midday, Reuters said. In Paris, a peaceful march near Place de la République turned violent. Masked rioters in black threw fireworks and paving stones, attacked a bank and looted a sports shop while police fired tear gas. “We’re taking the Bastille!” one demonstrator shouted.

This is the moment a town hall collapsed as protests sweep across France. The 140-year-old town hall in the French city of Limoges caught fire during protests in the city Read the latest on the Sky News website and app: https://t.co/oaLTf7aDbP https://t.co/3OC3eU3Hf7

Protesters set bins on fire, and a lorry was burned. Flames spread to a nearby building. On Boulevard Magenta, in a mostly working-class area north of the square, dozens of shops were looted. Groups tried to get into the Galeries Lafayette department store, vandalised banks, ransacked a Lacoste shop and looted a mobile phone shop. Residents closed their windows and doors as tear gas rose to roof level. Paris mayor Emmanuel Grégoire said whole streets “have been devastated”.

In Limoges, masked protesters set fire to the city hall. The local prefect, Maurice Barate, told AFP the roof had fallen onto the lower floors and two-thirds of the outside wall was gone. He called the loss of the 143-year-old building a “catastrophe for heritage”.

In Marseille, protesters rammed the town hall door with security barriers taken from the street and got inside for a short time. One of them spray-painted an “A”, for anarchy, on a wall before police removed them. In Lyon, protesters set fire to the city’s tourist office, Reuters said.

Lecornu said the government would not give way to the violence. “We will not let ourselves be intimidated,” he wrote on X. He said some people wanted to use the unrest as a “warm-up” before next year’s presidential election.

Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said the official march had been taken over by “opportunistic delinquents” who saw a chance to loot. He said the state did not plan to declare a state of emergency, but that he “very strongly” condemned the violence.

President Emmanuel Macron said he would see the attackers prosecuted and punished. He said the country would stand united against the “sowers of chaos”. On Friday, he had asked for calm and said the right to protest comes with a duty of “respect for people, respect for property”.

The far left and the far right both tried to gain from the unrest, The Guardian said. Jean-Luc Mélenchon, leader of the far-left France Unbowed party, urged protesters to stay away from looting, which he said was “contrary to our methods”. Far-right leader Marine Le Pen condemned the rioters and said Mélenchon’s party had “legitimised the violence”.

The protests began last month at high schools in poor northern suburbs of Paris, where anger over teacher shortages and run-down buildings grew into a wider movement over inequality, public spending and living standards. Calls on social media to revive the gilets jaunes (yellow vests) movement of 2018 helped to bring more people out on Saturday. Some protesters wore high-visibility vests and blocked streets.

The CGT, one of France’s biggest unions, has backed the protests and called for higher wages and pensions and lower prices. The interior ministry put turnout at 550,000. The CGT said 800,000 people took part. Reuters said the crowds were bigger than at the peak of the yellow vest protests, but far smaller than those against Macron’s pension changes in 2023.

“We are fighting because the cost of living is too harsh,” said Lola, a 19-year-old protester in Paris. She also pointed to high fuel prices and to pupils who, she said, were being attacked and hurt for asking for more teachers.

A survey of 2,000 people in October found that about 45% of French people are worried about rising prices and inflation. Reuters said France’s efforts to cut public debt have not calmed investors, and government borrowing costs are at their highest in more than two decades. Macron is in the last stretch of his presidency, and the political scene is split.

Lecornu said more than 150 police officers were hurt on Saturday. He did not say whether any protesters were injured. The Guardian reported that more than 900 officers have been hurt in recent weeks, with thousands of arrests, hundreds of injuries and schools set on fire.

Police tactics are under scrutiny. The police watchdog is looking into at least two dozen claims of police violence. Nuñez had stopped the use of one type of stun grenade against young protesters after a 15-year-old lost a hand, but said it could be used on Saturday. He confirmed that one person had a hand torn off in clashes that day. French media said the man tried to pick up a stun grenade, Reuters reported.

The UNSA police union posted a video on X that it said showed crowds attacking police vans with clubs and bricks. It said officers were at a breaking point. “The rope is stretched to its maximum,” the union said.

Many Métro stations were closed at the request of the police, including those near the Champs-Élysées and government offices. Police banned some gatherings in central Paris.

Reuters said there were smaller protests in other countries as living costs rise. In Brussels, several hundred mostly young people marched, and some clashed with the police. Belgian student groups say they are against rising education costs. In Albania, police appeared to fire rubber bullets on the fifth day of student protests calling for Prime Minister Edi Rama to resign. In Lisbon, tens of thousands marched over housing and living costs. Portuguese housing prices have doubled since 2017.

In Milan, a march against high living costs turned to disorder, and police used tear gas to clear the square in front of the cathedral. In Bologna, police used water cannon and made seven arrests, according to the news agency ANSA.
