headline: Pope Leo says he will gradually resume duties after cancer surgery
summary: Pope Leo XIV thanked thousands of faithful in St. Peter's Square on Sunday for their prayers while he was hospitalized, and said he plans to gradually return to his usual duties.(Image credit: Alessandra Tarantino)
body_text:
Pope Leo XIV appears at the window of his study in the Apostolic Palace overlooking St. Peter's Square at the Vatican for the traditional noon blessing after praying the Angelus, Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, a day after he returned from the hospital, where he had lung cancer removed on Tuesday. Alessandra Tarantino/AP hide caption

VATICAN CITY — Pope Leo XIV thanked thousands of faithful in St. Peter's Square on Sunday for their prayers while he was hospitalized for an operation to remove a malignant tumor, and said he plans to gradually return to his usual duties.

The crowd erupted in cheers when the pontiff showed himself in the window overlooking the square, where a week ago on the same occasion of the traditional Angelus blessing he revealed that a nodule had been located on his lung, and that it would be surgically removed.

''Now that this delicate phase is behind me, I will gradually resume my activities, always with God's help and your prayers," Leo said, his voice sounding strong four days after the lower lobe of his right lung was removed.

The pontiff said the experience of the last week "has made me feel especially close to those facing illness and infirmity." He told the faithful that he had ''truly felt your support,'' and expressed ''particular gratitude to the doctors, nurses and all the staff at Gemelli hospital'' where he was treated.

The pope paused for a moment and waved to the crowd before retreating into his apartment in the Apostolic Palace.

A delegation from Africa in Rome for a congress danced and ululated after the pope's blessing.

''He was always in our prayers when he was sick, and we are happy to see him today,″ said Alain Kalembu of the Democratic Republic of Congo. ″This is an expression of our joy.″

The 71-year-old pontiff had the lower lobe of his right lung removed on Tuesday in the first major health event of his 17-month pontificate. The surgery confirmed he had adenocarcinoma, the most common type of lung cancer.

He told a reporter in English that he was doing ''much better'' as he drove away from Rome's Gemelli hospital to return to the Vatican, after a shorter hospital stay than had initially been anticipated.

"I don't believe it, because he was just operated on the other day," Cosimo Mastrocinque, a retired factory worker visiting the Vatican from the southern region of Puglia, said. "It is a miracle that he recovered already."

American tourists were especially eager to pray alongside the first pope born in the United States. Marla Marsala of Michigan was supposed to attend a Mass with the pope last week that was canceled due to his hospitalization.

''I am just happy that we are praying with him today instead of for him, like we were before,'' Marsala said. "It was a tough week for all of the people who love him, which are many. He seems like a very strong soul. So I think he will pull through and fight it, and succeed and keep doing the wonderful work he is doing.''

Claire Holland from Jacksonville, Florida, said she felt "very blessed" to be present for the pope's return to his flock.

"I'm so happy that he has recovered so quickly. I think there have been millions and millions of prayers. And he is a strong, determined man, and I am so happy that he is feeling well enough to do this," Holland said.

Leo's next major engagement is an ambitious Nov. 6-17 trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, including a dozen flights and two helicopter rides to high altitudes. His surgeon, Dr. Stefano Margaritora, told Vatican News on Saturday that "there are no clinical reasons why it should not take place."

"The Holy Father has put his heart and soul into his recovery," Margaritora told Vatican News, adding that he expected the pope to recover fully from surgery "in another 10 days or so."

Histological testing of the tumor and related lymph nodes was underway. The results, along with details of the tumor's molecular and genetic makeup, will help doctors determine whether the pope needs additional treatment. Options include chemotherapy, a combination of chemotherapy and immunotherapy, or targeted oral therapy based on the tumor's genetic characteristics.

headline: SCZONE seeks Shaanxi investment in clean energy, automotive manufacturing
summary: Mostafa Sheikhoun, Chairperson of the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE), received a high-level trade delegation from China’s Shaanxi Province, led by Jia Chenglan, Chairperson of the Shaanxi Sub-Council of the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade (CCPIT), to explore investment opportunities in SCZONE’s priority sectors for industrial localisation, particularly clean energy and automotive manufacturing. The meeting was coordinated by the Federation of African Chambers in Egypt and attended by several senior SCZONE executives. The Chinese delegation also included representatives of provincial government bodies, senior banking executives and representatives of major companies operating in the energy, manufacturing, investment and logistics sectors. At the beginning of the meeting, Sheikhoun stressed that SCZONE looks forward to working with Shaanxi’s business community, particularly in clean energy and heavy industries, where the province has considerable expertise, as well as advanced technology, electronics, automotive manufacturing and logistics. He highlighted the strategic partnership between Egypt and China, which covers numerous fields. He explained that SCZONE has a strong track record of successful Chinese investments, particularly in the TEDA industrial zone and, more recently, the West Qantara Industrial Zone, as well as Sokhna Port. Sheikhoun also emphasised that SCZONE’s direct and indirect investment incentives, extensive availability of utilities and infrastructure, skilled technical workforce, and strategic location at the crossroads of global trade routes, supported by international free trade agreements, provide competitive advantages over comparable economic zones. These advantages, he said, support the success of projects established within SCZONE, help boost Egyptian exports to international markets and promote industrial localisation across various sectors. The SCZONE Chairperson stressed that the visit coincided with the positive response to Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit to Cairo and the signing of several memoranda of understanding with SCZONE. He said these developments reflect the depth of bilateral relations and the comprehensive strategic partnership between Egypt and China, demonstrating both countries’ commitment to advancing economic development and expanding opportunities for joint investment across key sectors. For her part, Jia Chenglan, Chairperson of the CCPIT Shaanxi Sub-Council, expressed her pleasure at visiting SCZONE and gaining first-hand knowledge of its investment advantages and opportunities across several sectors in which companies from Shaanxi Province have extensive experience. She stressed that working with SCZONE represents a significant step forward for companies, as it provides investors with extensive access to global markets. Jia invited SCZONE representatives to visit Shaanxi Province and explore industrial and logistics activities that could be attracted to the economic zone. She noted that companies based in Shaanxi make a substantial contribution to China’s industrial gross domestic product, reflecting their strong capabilities and leadership across numerous manufacturing and logistics sectors.

headline: Egypt’s non-oil exports reach $48bn in 2025: Minister
summary: Mohamed Farid, Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade, said that technology and artificial intelligence (AI) can help boost merchandise and services exports, revealing that Egypt’s non-oil merchandise exports reached $48bn in 2025. Farid attended the opening of the Egyptian Exchange (EGX) trading session to mark World Investor Week, organised by the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO). The event was also attended by Omar Radwan, EGX Chairperson; Mohamed Sabry, EGX Vice Chairperson; and Mohamed Abdel Aziz, Assistant Chairperson of the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA). Farid stressed that promoting financial, investment and export awareness, alongside empowering young people to participate in economic activity, is a key pillar of supporting development. Achieving these objectives requires coordinated awareness-raising efforts, the development of regulatory frameworks and the adoption of technology, he said. He also praised the EGX’s efforts to promote financial literacy, noting that regulatory amendments introduced in line with FRA rules have created broader opportunities for individuals under the age of 21 to participate in the capital market. He emphasised the need to protect new investors from harmful practices and strengthen cooperation among the EGX, FRA and universities to develop human capital. On exports, Farid underscored the importance of familiarising young people with the trade agreements to which Egypt is a party and the preferential advantages they offer in facilitating Egyptian products’ access to foreign markets. He also highlighted the importance of understanding rules of origin and regulatory export requirements. He explained that raising awareness of trade agreements with the European Union, Arab countries, Latin American and Caribbean countries, and Türkiye would help Egyptian companies expand internationally and broaden the exporter base. He also called for cooperation with universities to familiarise students with employment opportunities at exporting companies. Farid further highlighted the importance of developing technological solutions to help companies identify target markets and export opportunities, understand rules of origin and meet the required standards. He also highlighted the role of TradeTech initiatives, including the TradeTech Sandbox, in encouraging young people to develop innovative solutions that facilitate access to international markets.

headline: Japanese education group, Egypt to transform 20 technical schools for nursing and IT
summary: Egypt is collaborating with Japan’s Kyoto Ikueikan Educational Group to transform 20 technical schools into international applied technology institutions specialising in nursing, elderly care, and information technology by the next academic year. Minister of Education and Technical Education Mohamed Abdel Latif met on Sunday with Hidetaka Matsuo, CEO of the Kyoto Ikueikan Educational Group, alongside a delegation from the Kyoto University of Nursing and Health Sciences, to follow up on the executive steps of the cooperation agreement. The initiative will upgrade 10 nursing schools, five information technology schools, and five elderly care schools. Abdel Latif explained that the upgraded institutions will operate on an integrated model based on Japanese curricula and standards, with laboratories and training facilities equipped to match Japan’s education and training systems. The agreement, which Abdel Latif signed during a recent visit to Japan, marks the first cooperation of its kind between the two nations in the field of technical education. The minister highlighted the depth of Egyptian-Japanese relations, noting that broader educational cooperation is continually evolving, with the number of Egyptian-Japanese schools now reaching 103. Matsuo expressed his pride in cooperating with Egypt and commended the ministry’s dedication to developing technical education. He affirmed the group’s commitment to supporting Egyptian technical education and preparing qualified cadres by providing opportunities to study and gain experience in Japan, enabling them to return and contribute to national development. The two sides discussed the executive steps required to equip and raise the efficiency of the targeted schools, alongside the proposed educational and training programmes, agreeing to continue coordination to ensure classes commence next year. The Japanese delegation included Yang Yong Chun, Director of International Affairs at the Ikueikan Educational Foundation, and Amani Takeda, Associate Professor at Ikueikan University. Egyptian officials in attendance included Deputy Minister Ayman Bahaa El-Din; Yasser Osman, the Minister’s Advisor for International Relations and Agreements; and Amal Refaat, Executive Director of the Hiroshima Teacher Training Program and the Minister’s Advisor for Egyptian-Japanese Relations.

headline: Trump’s approach to Iranian leadership harmful to stability in region — Lavrov
summary: "I think was essentially about what the United States and Israel have done," Russian Foreign Minister said
body_text:
MANAMA /Bahrain/, October 18. /TASS/. US President Donald Trump’s approach to the Iranian leadership in no way helps the region reach peace agreements, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said.

"This is absolutely the right thing to do, and I fully and unreservedly support it, so that the situation returns to normal and freedom of navigation is fully guaranteed, just as it was before February 28. Until February 28, there was full freedom, with no hint of any payments, and the situation was entirely normal, and, of course, we cannot fail to take into account how all of this happened," he told a news conference after the 9th round of the Russia-Gulf Cooperation Council Strategic Dialogue. "And my friend also said: for an end to hostilities, for mutual respect based on recognition of each other’s sovereignty, non-interference in internal affairs, and the peaceful resolution of all disputes rather than through the use of armed force. I think was essentially about what the United States and Israel have done."

"If anyone can tell me that the actions listed here are not those of the United States and Israel, I think it would be very difficult to argue against that. Especially given the fundamental principle of resolving conflicts peacefully, without the use of force and without interfering in internal affairs," he noted. "When President Trump speaks openly about this: We have knocked out Iran’s entire leadership, they appointed a second leadership, and we knocked them out too, now there’s a third leadership, but we don’t really understand who’s doing what or making decisions there. This is probably not the kind of an approach that can help a distant region seek those very agreements based on mutual respect and international law. We are only in favor of.".

body_text:
The Gulf Co-operation Council has urged Russia to use its position on the UN Security Council to press Iran to halt attacks on Gulf states, at a meeting with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in Bahrain.

Speaking at a Gulf-Russia foreign ministers' meeting in Manama on Sunday, GCC Secretary General Jasem Al Budaiwi said member states faced unprecedented attacks as well as risks to shipping and energy supplies.

The GCC called on Moscow to “play an active role in pressing Tehran” to comply with UN resolutions, cease its attacks and engage in “serious dialogue” with Gulf states.

Iran names new defence minister as he warns US over ‘Mother of All Bombs’

Mr Lavrov said Russia supports diplomatic efforts to prevent a return to full-scale war as he presented an updated Russian concept for collective security in the Gulf.

On Ukraine, where Russia has waged war for almost five years, Mr Al Budaiwi said the bloc continues to support dialogue and diplomacy aimed at a peaceful, comprehensive political settlement.

He said Iranian attacks on GCC states since February 28, when the US and Israel began their war against Iran, had involved more than 7,000 ballistic missiles and drones, striking airports, ports, power stations, water desalination plants and oil and gas facilities.

Mr Al Budaiwi also condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, singling out the October 10 attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which killed 12 people and injured more than 300.

He reaffirmed the GCC’s full solidarity with Saudi Arabia, calling on the international community to adopt a firm stance against attacks on the kingdom.

Mr Al Budaiwi said Iran’s disruption of maritime navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and threats to shipping in the Red Sea and Bab Al Mandeb strait posed risks to global energy and food security and international supply chains. He called for maritime traffic through Hormuz to return to its status before February 28.

The proposal envisages direct dialogue among the Gulf’s coastal states and neighbouring countries, including Iraq and Jordan, with possible support from the Arab League, the Organisation of Islamic Co-operation and permanent members of the UN Security Council.

Mr Lavrov said the Gulf states themselves should have the decisive voice in determining the region’s security arrangements.

“Our concept is specifically designed to foster conditions for direct dialogue among the Gulf’s coastal states and their neighbours, such as Iraq and Jordan,” he said.

He also described ties with GCC states as a priority of Russia's foreign policy, noting that trade between Russia and the bloc’s member states rose by 45 per cent in 2025.

He said the crisis in the region had been triggered by an “unprovoked act of aggression” by the US and Israel against Iran.

The meeting, chaired by Bahrain’s Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani, also addressed the Palestinian cause, Syria and the Russia-Ukraine war.

Mr Al Budaiwi reiterated the GCC’s support for an independent Palestinian state along the borders of 1967, with East Jerusalem as its capital. He called for the consolidation of the Gaza ceasefire and the enactment of its second phase, securing a full Israeli withdrawal and ensuring unhindered humanitarian aid.

On Syria, he reaffirmed the GCC’s support for the country’s sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity. The ministers also discussed expanding co-operation in trade, energy, education, health, agriculture and other sectors under the GCC-Russia Joint Action Plan for 2023-2028.

headline: S. Korea, Ukraine had no discussion on timing of disclosing N.K. POW repatriation: diplomat
summary: WARSAW, Oct. 18 (Yonhap) -- South Korea and Ukraine had formed a consensus to ke...
body_text:
WARSAW, Oct. 18 (Yonhap) -- South Korea and Ukraine had formed a consensus to keep discussions on the repatriation of captured North Korean soldiers confidential for as long as possible, a South Korean diplomat said Sunday.

Yoon Ji-wan, charge d'affaires at the South Korean Embassy in Ukraine, made the remark during a parliamentary audit by the subcommittee on foreign affairs conducted at the South Korean Embassy in Poland.

"We had no discussions on a timeline for disclosure, but we did share the idea that confidentiality should be maintained for as long as possible," Yoon said via video.

Yoon said the embassy in Ukraine was caught off guard when Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy revealed the repatriation of the North Korean prisoners of war (POWs) during his address to the U.N. General Assembly on Sept. 23. Yoon added that Ukraine had yet to provide a specific explanation on why Zelenskyy made that disclosure.

"Even within Ukraine, there has been criticism over the lack of internal coordination and the spontaneous breach of confidentiality," Yoon said. "The Ukrainian side has not refuted our claims further. This has led us to believe that they cannot deny the existence of the non-disclosure agreement."

South Korea and Ukraine have seen their relations turn frosty in light of Zelenskyy's revelation. Seoul has accused Kyiv of breaching the non-disclosure agreement, while Ukraine has shot back that no such pact existed in the first place.

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha recently claimed in a media interview that he considered the matter closed, shunning South Korea's demand for an apology.

Amid the diplomatic row, South Korea recalled its ambassador to Ukraine, Park Ki-chang.

When lawmakers pointed out that the failure to secure the non-disclosure deal in writing had caused the friction, Yoon said, "Formalizing a diplomatic agreement in writing would amount to a treaty," adding that it was difficult to publicly disclose specific proof of diplomatic discussions.

"The repatriation of the POWs is a major achievement for both nations," Yoon added. "There is a mutual understanding that bilateral relations should be built on stability and trust, and that this issue must be resolved wisely."

Yoon attended the parliamentary audit virtually from Kyiv, representing the embassy following Ambassador Park's recall.(END)

headline: Trump endorses embattled Israeli PM Netanyahu ahead of October 27 election
summary: US President Donald Trump on Sunday endorsed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ahead of Israel's October 27 elections. It was not clear what impact the endorsement would have on voters, since many Israelis have expressed disappointment with Trump over the outcome of the Iran war and the US president's ceasefire proposal.
body_text:
US President Donald Trump on Sunday endorsed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ahead of Israel's October 27 elections. It was not clear what impact the endorsement would have on voters, since many Israelis have expressed disappointment with Trump over the outcome of the Iran war and the US president's ceasefire proposal.

Issued on: 18/10/2026 - 18:25

President Donald Trump on Sunday endorsed embattled Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu late in his reelection campaign, a coveted boost because of Trump’s popularity but one that the American had withheld for months as the vote neared and the leaders' strategies in the Middle East diverged.

Trump said in a post on social media that Netanyahu “has been a Great Warrior Prime Minister, and an even greater Partner for Peace in combating the Islamic Republic of Iran”.

Read moreHow Netanyahu survived the political fallout from the October 7 attacks

Israelis are set to vote October 27, in the first national elections since Hamas attacked Israel on October 7, 2023.

The absence of an endorsement was a setback for the Likud politician, who had billed his tight ties to the Republican president as a selling point for staying in power.

“Thank you, President Trump, for the tremendous support and work together,” Netanyahu said in a statement in Hebrew posted on X. “Together we will complete the mission!”

His Likud Party attached to the statement a 35-second video showing clips of the two leaders together and Trump praising Netanyahu.

It was not immediately clear what impact the endorsement would have on what is expected to be a tight race. Trump is still popular in Israel, but many Israelis, including leading commentators, have expressed disappointment over the inconclusive outcome of the Iran war and Trump’s ceasefire proposal, which fell short of many of the countries’ key goals when they jointly launched the war in February.

In his post, Trump again threatened to “soon finish the job” against Iran “unless they change their ways, rapidly”, but added he might not want to if Netanyahu loses the election. “If Israel has the wrong Leader, which would be anyone other than Bibi, America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so,” Trump said.

He said Netanyahu had been “Strong, Brave, and Brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition, including that coming from even Israel, itself.”

The main election rival to Netanyahu responded to Trump's endorsement of the incumbent premier, saying "only Israelis can choose their leader".

Speaking at a conference in Tel Aviv ahead of upcoming elections, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot said he "admires" Trump, but "Israel is a democratic country: only Israelis can choose their leader".

To display this content from YouTube, you must enable advertisement tracking and audience measurement.

One of your browser extensions seems to be blocking the video player from loading. To watch this content, you may need to disable it on this site.

Trump endorsed Netanyahu in past elections and in November he sent a letter to Israeli President Isaac Herzog asking him to pardon Netanyahu on corruption charges.

But Trump's comments about Netanyahu in recent months had been much more subdued, and he repeatedly demurred when asked if he would back the prime minister. The president, when asked in a Time magazine interview published this month about backing the Israeli leader, said, ”I’m not involved in politics anymore,” despite his campaigning for and endorsing US politicians.

Trump, especially in his second term, has sought to give his stamp of approval to candidates in foreign elections and claimed credit when they have been successful. He endorsed Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán in his unsuccessful bid for a fifth term, as well as Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Polish President Karol Nawrocki, and several Latin American leaders.

Trump and Netanyahu have been close allies and seemed more aligned than ever in the wake of the joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran's nuclear facilities in 2025. But over the course of the nearly eight-month war with Iran this year, they have had disagreements.

Trump criticised Israel’s decision to attack a key Iranian gas field in the first weeks of the war. In June, he called Netanyahu “crazy." Trump also said that he was “a little bit perturbed” as Israel’s fighting with Hezbollah militants in Lebanon was holding back peace talks with Iran.

Beyond Iran, Netanyahu in August rejected Trump’s latest plan to advance a stalled ceasefire in Gaza, pushing back on the US administration’s call for Israel to withdraw from territory it controls in Gaza until Hamas has been disarmed.

(FRANCE 24 with AP and AFP)

headline: Egypt secures EU market access for farmed fish exports
summary: Egypt has secured approval to export aquaculture products to all 27 European Union (EU) member states after meeting the bloc’s technical and regulatory requirements, the Ministry of Investment and Foreign Trade announced. The Egyptian Commercial Service, through its office in Brussels, worked with the National Food Safety Authority (NFSA) and other relevant national bodies to secure the inclusion of Egyptian aquaculture products on the EU’s list of countries authorised to export such products. The approval follows Egypt’s fulfilment of European requirements governing exports of products of animal origin, opening new opportunities for Egyptian farmed fish and crustaceans to enter the European market. Mohamed Farid Saleh, Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade, said that removing technical and regulatory barriers to Egyptian exports was a priority for expanding market access and strengthening the competitiveness of national products. He stressed the importance of coordination among national authorities, overseas commercial representation offices and the ministry’s affiliated bodies to facilitate access to international markets, diversify export destinations and translate trade opportunities into sustainable export flows. Securing the approval involved technical and institutional efforts, including preparing a comprehensive dossier in line with EU requirements, strengthening monitoring systems for chemical residues and contaminants, and developing the regulatory and oversight frameworks governing Egypt’s aquaculture sector. The Egyptian Commercial Service’s office in Brussels played a key role in coordinating with the European Commission, particularly its Directorate-General for Health and Food Safety, and following up on technical requirements in cooperation with the relevant Egyptian authorities. Abdel Aziz El-Sherif, First Undersecretary of the Ministry of Investment and Foreign Trade and head of the Egyptian Commercial Service, said that coordination with European authorities would create new opportunities for Egyptian aquaculture exports. He added that the next phase would focus on ensuring that exporting facilities continued to comply with approved requirements and maintaining coordination among the relevant authorities to translate the approval into sustained exports of farmed fish and crustaceans to the European market.

headline: Egypt's Al Azhar calls for mediation committee to end fighting in Arab region

body_text:
Egypt's Al Azhar has called for the “urgent” formation of a mediation committee with representatives from Arab and Islamic countries to help end conflicts across the region.

The call by Al Azhar, the world's top Sunni Islam institution, comes as hostilities worsen between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-aligned Houthi militia in a new round of Middle East conflict.

In a statement on Sunday, Al Azhar's Grand Imam Dr Ahmed Al Tayeb urged Arab and Muslim leaders “to uphold the spirit of brotherhood and the bonds of religion, blood and language, give precedence to wisdom, and embrace reason and dialogue, while bringing about an immediate and comprehensive halt to all acts of war, fighting, destruction and sabotage that deplete peoples’ resources and claim innocent lives”.

He warned that divisions and infighting were weakening the Arab and Muslim world, undermining its security and sovereignty, and depleting its resources and wealth at a time when unity was urgently needed.

The 1,000-year-old Al Azhar carries considerable weight among the world's Sunni Muslims, with its current leader, Imam Ahmed Al Tayeb, enjoying wide popularity in the Arab and Islamic worlds. While the call for a mediation committee to end conflicts in the region is a rare foray by the revered institution into politics and diplomacy, it will probably be treated as a largely symbolic gesture.

Al Azhar said the proposed committee should bring together wise and sincere figures from across Arab and Islamic countries to defuse escalating crises, bridge differences and resolve disputes. It said the initiative aimed to preserve the strength and sovereignty of Arab countries, protect lives and safeguard the resources and future of their people.

The institution also expressed its readiness to provide the committee with all possible support. It expressed confidence that those involved could overcome their differences and turn the page on the past in the interests of peace and stability.

Earlier in the day, Egypt's top security body pledged “all necessary and possible forms of support” to Saudi Arabia. It met hours before parliament was due to vote on authorising President Abdel Fattah El Sisi to help defend the kingdom against attacks by the Houthi rebels. It later emerged that the parliament would reconvene for two further days to discuss the authorisation.

On Sunday, six people were injured when a projectile launched by Yemen’s Houthi militia struck a residential site in the Saudi city of Najran, the civil defence said. The incident caused material damage to three houses and three vehicles, the civil defence spokesman said in a statement. The Saudi-led coalition said it had shot down two ballistic missiles fired at Khamis Mushait and three drones over Riyadh and the Eastern Province.

The Houthis have launched 20 attacks on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport since October 1, coalition spokesman Maj Gen Turki Al Malki said on Thursday. Attacks on Saudi airports have killed 19 people and wounded 364, he said. The deadliest, on October 10 in Riyadh, killed 13, including an Egyptian flight attendant.

headline: Trump endorses Netanyahu in close Israeli election
summary: By Doina Chiacu and Alexander CornwellWASHINGTON/TEL AVIV, Oct 18 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump on Sunday endorsed his ally Benjamin Netanyahu as the longtime Israeli prime minister struggles for an edge in next week's parliamentary election.
body_text:
By Doina Chiacu and Alexander Cornwell

WASHINGTON/TEL AVIV, Oct 18 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump on Sunday endorsed his ally Benjamin Netanyahu as the longtime Israeli prime minister struggles for an edge in next week's parliamentary election.

Trump praised Netanyahu as a "great warrior prime minister" and peace partner, crediting him with joining the United States in launching strikes on Iran in February. The conflict, in its seventh month, has disrupted energy markets globally and wreaked havoc across the Middle East, damaging critical infrastructure and destabilizing regional economies.

"Bibi Netanyahu has been Strong, Brave, and Brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition, including that coming from even Israel, itself," Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social.

"Despite all of that, he has endured and, in fact, he has thrived! I have watched Bibi under the most trying of times. Normal men or women in such situations would have wilted under the pressure — But Bibi did not wilt, he actually got stronger, and maintains that same Strength today."

In his message, addressed to "the Great People of Israel," Trump added, "Please let this Letter serve to represent my Complete and Total Endorsement of Bibi Netanyahu in his upcoming Race for Re-Election as Prime Minister of Israel."

The Trump endorsement is not certain to give Netanyahu and his right-wing Likud party a boost in the October 27 national election, as Israeli public support for Trump has diminished amid Israeli-US disagreements over Iran.

Polls have suggested no candidate has a clear path to power. Israel's prime minister is chosen through coalition-building in parliament rather than by direct popular vote.

It will be Israel's first vote since the Hamas attack on October 7, 2023, that shook the country and plunged the Middle East into turmoil, as Israel went to war in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.

The election could determine whether Netanyahu remains in power after one of the most consequential periods in Israel’s history, or is defeated by centrist rivals promising to usher in a new era.

Netanyahu promptly expressed his thanks to his "dear friend Donald" on X, saying, "Together we will complete the mission!"

Trump has broken with longtime US tradition by endorsing candidates in elections in foreign countries including Hungary, Colombia, Argentina, Japan and Honduras.

ENDORSEMENT MIGHT HELP, CAN'T HURT

Trump's relationship with Netanyahu has been close but also fractious, with the president at times publicly and privately criticizing Israel's longest-serving prime minister.

The war that the US and Israel launched against Iran is unpopular with Americans, who vote November 3 in congressional elections, while support for Israel among Americans has also decreased over the Iran war and Israel's conduct in the three-year war in Gaza that Trump has promised to end. Both leaders on Sunday mentioned finishing the job in Iran.

Tamar Hermann, a senior research fellow at the non-partisan Israel Democracy Institute in Jerusalem, said Trump's late endorsement could help win back wavering Netanyahu voters but was unlikely to draw widespread support.

Most Israelis, even those who are critical of Netanyahu and his government, were largely in favor of the Iran war.

In an election this close, "it couldn't hurt him, and it might help," said analyst Aaron David Miller of the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace in Washington.

Netanyahu's religious-nationalist coalition is projected to lose its governing majority, although the opposition may also struggle to form a government, opinion polls show. That could lead to Netanyahu serving as a caretaker prime minister while another election is held.

The US president passed up earlier opportunities to endorse Netanyahu, perhaps because he wanted to see what leverage he could exercise on issues like Gaza or Lebanon, said Miller. In the end, he said, Trump sided with a leader he sees as strong and unfairly persecuted.

"However angry Trump may be at Netanyahu for pushing this Iran war, this in the end was a Trump decision," Miller added.

A Trump decision not to endorse Netanyahu would have raised "legitimate questions about whether or not the whole Iran venture was in fact something Trump should have done," he said.

(Reporting by Doina Chiacu in Washington, Steve Scheer, Alexander Cornwell, Rami Ayyub in Israel; Editing by Joe Bavier and Cynthia Osterman)

headline: Iran needs no gasoline imports anymore: president
summary: TEHRAN, Oct. 18 (MNA) – President Masoud Pezeshkian has said that Iran does not need to import gasoline anymore through adopting proper policies.
body_text:
TEHRAN, Oct. 18 (MNA) – President Masoud Pezeshkian has said that Iran does not need to import gasoline anymore through adopting proper policies.

Speaking at a Sunday meeting of the Government Information Council, President Pezeshkian pointed to high energy consumption and fuel supply under the economic blockade, saying the administration put saving and consumption management on its agenda to prevent further problems in energy and fuel, which led to significant savings with the cooperation of the nation.

"Today we have become needless of gasoline imports, whereas we had to spend 12 billion dollars for importing needed gasoline," he said.

Stressing that all revenues from fuel price adjustments, savings and consumption management will be paid back to the people themselves, the president said media capacity must be used to accompany people on important issues such as energy consumption management, gasoline saving, and strengthening national unity and social cohesion.

He called on managers in administrative bodies and organizations to work with empathy to encourage government employees, including through plans such as car-free Tuesdays, reduced use of personal cars, increased productivity, and use of teleworking capacity, to control and manage excessive energy and fuel consumption.

headline: Captain of flydubai plane describes blocking axe blows as co-pilot attacked
summary: Oct 18 - The captain of a flydubai flight who was attacked by a co-pilot who intended to crash the plane has described blockingaxe blows to the head and screaming for help as he reached for a knob to open the cockpit door.Captain Smit Machchhar has been hailed as a hero for his role in averting disaster on the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv last month, helping to thwart what the UAE attorney general has said was an attempted suicide attack by the co-pilot who intended to crash the plane into Ben Gurion Airport.
body_text:
Oct 18 - The captain of a flydubai flight who was attacked by a co-pilot who intended to crash the plane has described blockingaxe blows to the head and screaming for help as he reached for a knob to open the cockpit door.

Captain Smit Machchhar has been hailed as a hero for his role in averting disaster on the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv last month, helping to thwart what the UAE attorney general has said was an attempted suicide attack by the co-pilot who intended to crash the plane into Ben Gurion Airport.

Speaking in an interview with The National newspaper from a hospital bed in Abu Dhabi, his head and left arm bandaged,Machchhar said that when the first blow landed, he thought something had gone "horribly wrong the aircraft structure", before quickly realising he was being attacked and things had "taken a drastic turn".

"The next thought was I need to get help in here," he said in the interview published on Saturday.

"My immediate action was to free myself from the seat belts and I tried to just block the blows as much as I could," he said, pointing to his arm that was wounded as he defended himself."The blows were coming on the head."

"Immediately my hand went to the knob which opens the door and screaming for my colleagues, screaming his name."

"I believe that was the first time when I lost my consciousness."

The aircraft, flight FZ1073, was in Saudi airspace when the co-pilot attacked Machchhar with a crash axe, typically kept in the cockpit for emergency use.

The incident caused the airliner to plunge 16,000 feet (4,900 meters) in 30 seconds before the attacker was overwhelmed and two other pilots who were on board landed the aircraft safely in Saudi Arabia. The suspect, an Omani national, was transferred to the UAE, flydubai's home country.

The plan was inspired by the September 11, 2001, attacks on the US, UAE public prosecutors say, as a result of their criminal investigation launched on October 1.

Machchhar said he heard the cockpit door opening and screaming "between my colleague and the guy".

He said the scariest thing he felt was the aircraft nose "steeply going down."

"I was not very sure that I'll make it out alive from this. Did I give up? No."

(Writing by Tom Perry; Editing by Christina Fincher)

headline: France’s National Rally leader calls for Macron’s resignation amid riots
summary: Jordan Bardella called what is happening in the country "a humiliation for France"
body_text:
PARIS, October 18. /TASS/. France’s National Rally party leader Jordan Bardella has demanded President Emmanuel Macron step down amid the riots raging in the country since October 17.

"This evening, I expect Macron to apologize and leave," he wrote.

Iraq’s Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said on Sunday that stability in the Middle East must come from within the region itself, not from external powers, renewing calls for a security dialogue with Gulf states.

Speaking after the Organisation of Islamic Co-operation (OIC) held a council of foreign ministers in Baghdad, Mr Hussein described the security situation as critical.

“The security situation in the region is complex and the region, in fact, as a whole is under fire, so the first priority we need is stability and security,” Mr Hussein said at a joint press conference with the OIC's Secretary General Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed.

Iran names new defence minister as he warns US over ‘Mother of All Bombs’

“We cannot buy security from abroad, we need internal security, and that internal security is the co-operation between the countries of the region,” he added.

The high-level OIC meeting was first of its kind in the Iraqi capital in 45 years, and is seen as part of Iraq's broader effort to reassert itself as a regional mediator.

Iraq has in recent years positioned itself as a rare interlocutor able to talk to all sides – maintaining close ties with Gulf Co-operation Council states, a strategic partnership with Iran and a security relationship with the US.

The call for a home-grown security architecture is not new for Baghdad. Three years ago, Iraq had proposed a formula bringing together the six GCC states plus Iraq and Iran, but “due to certain circumstances there was no response to this initiative”, Mr Hussein said.

The initiative, which he referred to as 6+2, was revisited after the Iran war broke out in February. The current push comes amid a renewed wave of instability across the region, from the war in Gaza and escalations in Lebanon and the Red Sea to continued tensions with Iran and threats to shipping in the Gulf.

“Recently there have been important contacts between the concerned countries, especially between Gulf states, Iraq and Iran, to activate this initiative,” he added. The minister said that “we will work to hold a meeting in this regard and we look forward to being in Baghdad.”

However, the initiative still needs “intensive contacts”, he added. “If a meeting is held between these countries, the issue of security will be raised, the issue of stopping the war will be raised, and initiatives to start peace and stability will be raised,” he said.

The 6+2 concept has been touted by Baghdad as a pragmatic framework that acknowledges geographic reality. The idea is that the eight coastal states of the Gulf share inseparable security and economic interests, from oil exports and freedom of navigation to climate change and water scarcity, regardless of political rivalries.

The economic argument is central to Baghdad’s pitch. Iraq is pursuing its ambitious Development Road project linking the Gulf to Turkey and Europe, and Gulf states are looking to invest in Iraqi gas, electricity and infrastructure. Officials in Baghdad argue that such projects cannot move forward while the region remains locked in a cycle of confrontation and external security dependency.

Without stability, the minister continued, “we cannot move towards economic development, we cannot move towards building the economy, nor towards investment, so we need security and stability”.

He added that regional countries, not foreign powers, should lead peace initiatives. “The priority is about security and stability, and I believe it is incumbent upon our countries, the countries of the region, to put forward initiatives on how to achieve security and peace, not foreign countries,” he said.

Foreign countries “come but only think of their own interests, while the countries of the region and the people of the region are the stakeholders, therefore we seek to achieve stability in the region”.

Iraq will continue to communicate with these countries with the help of the Secretary General of the OIC “until we reach this outcome”, he said.

headline: US defends Russia sanctions waiver as Zelenskyy rift deepens
summary: Top officials from US President Donald Trump's administration on Sunday defended a recent decision to waive sanctions on Russian diesel, as relations between Washington and Ukraine soured further.Mr Trump on Friday waived key provisions of a recent package of sanctions against Russia, saying in an executive order that “such a waiver is in the national interests” of the US. The order waived a requirement by him to raise duties on Russian goods imported into the US by up to 500 per cent, and a separate requirement to place tariffs of up to 100 per cent on China, India and other top buyers of Russian energy.The order was signed two days before the law's implementation deadline and came a week after Mr Trump's surprising decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel, a move that drew opposition from Europe and his Republican party.Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the administration invoked the law's 60-day pause “so we can see what's going on”.“The only thing that has been lifted is the diesel embargo,” he said.As part of the diesel deal, Mr Trump last week said Russia would immediately send 300,000 tonnes of diesel to US and global markets, with another 500,000 tonnes in November and 1 million tonnes “immediately thereafter”. The move was quickly condemned by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who said it would help to support Russia's war machine.The Kremlin on Thursday said Russian diesel had begun to reach global markets after its agreement with Mr Trump.Energy Secretary Chris Wright told ABC the waiver does not hand Russia an “economic lifeline”. He also dismissed the backlash.“They are all wrong,” Mr Wright said. “They don’t understand what President Trump’s doing.” “This is an incentive to Russia that if they can reduce the conflict with Ukraine, they can get an energy ceasefire or reduce the conflict such that they have diesel to export will allow it to flow to world markets. This is a carrot to try to end a war.”The Trump administration is seeking to lower US diesel prices – which have surged past $6 a gallon ($1.59 a litre) in recent weeks – before the country's midterm elections on November 3.“Does it come with some short-term political pain? It does. But that's called leadership. President Trump wants to bring peace to the world and drive energy prices down,” Mr Wright said.But Mr Zelenskyy called the diesel deals “dangerous”, adding it does not have any meaningful influence on US energy prices. He said the Strait of Hormuz's prolonged closure was the driver behind this year's energy price shock.He also told NBC he believed the US government was responsible for a recent slowdown in US-provided Starlink internet. He said he believed the decision to limit the internet speed was “the message from [the] American government”. He said Ukraine was “blocked” from US intelligence “for some period of time, and then it was deblocked by the American side”. The Ukrainian leader said during this time his country did not see Russian attacks.The US has denied it has ordered restrictions on Starlink satellite internet services to Ukraine.“President Zelenskyy should be very careful about making statements like this that aren't true,” Mr Bessent said.He also appeared to dodge the question of whether Ukraine was still a US ally. “President Trump has made it clear that he wants to end this war; that it must stop. And President Zelenskyy presented a false binary this morning that Ukraine must win,” Mr Bessent said.“The war must end, and that will be with some kind of a negotiated settlement. And President Trump is working on that every day.”He also said the US supports Ukraine through providing intelligence, the Starlink service, and allowing Nato to buy US arms and resell them to Ukraine.“We're not providing those to Russia,” he said.When asked a third time if Ukraine is still a US ally, Mr Bessent said: “I'm not the Secretary of State. I'm not the President.”
body_text:
Top officials from US President Donald Trump's administration on Sunday defended a recent decision to waive sanctions on Russian diesel, as relations between Washington and Ukraine soured further.

Mr Trump on Friday waived key provisions of a recent package of sanctions against Russia, saying in an executive order that “such a waiver is in the national interests” of the US. The order waived a requirement by him to raise duties on Russian goods imported into the US by up to 500 per cent, and a separate requirement to place tariffs of up to 100 per cent on China, India and other top buyers of Russian energy.

The order was signed two days before the law's implementation deadline and came a week after Mr Trump's surprising decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel, a move that drew opposition from Europe and his Republican party.

US extends sanctions waiver on Russia's Lukoil until 2027

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the administration invoked the law's 60-day pause “so we can see what's going on”.

“The only thing that has been lifted is the diesel embargo,” he said.

As part of the diesel deal, Mr Trump last week said Russia would immediately send 300,000 tonnes of diesel to US and global markets, with another 500,000 tonnes in November and 1 million tonnes “immediately thereafter”. The move was quickly condemned by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who said it would help to support Russia's war machine.

The Kremlin on Thursday said Russian diesel had begun to reach global markets after its agreement with Mr Trump.

Energy Secretary Chris Wright told ABC the waiver does not hand Russia an “economic lifeline”. He also dismissed the backlash.

“They are all wrong,” Mr Wright said. “They don’t understand what President Trump’s doing.”

“This is an incentive to Russia that if they can reduce the conflict with Ukraine, they can get an energy ceasefire or reduce the conflict such that they have diesel to export will allow it to flow to world markets. This is a carrot to try to end a war.”

The Trump administration is seeking to lower US diesel prices – which have surged past $6 a gallon ($1.59 a litre) in recent weeks – before the country's midterm elections on November 3.

“Does it come with some short-term political pain? It does. But that's called leadership. President Trump wants to bring peace to the world and drive energy prices down,” Mr Wright said.

But Mr Zelenskyy called the diesel deals “dangerous”, adding it does not have any meaningful influence on US energy prices. He said the Strait of Hormuz's prolonged closure was the driver behind this year's energy price shock.

He also told NBC he believed the US government was responsible for a recent slowdown in US-provided Starlink internet.

He said he believed the decision to limit the internet speed was “the message from [the] American government”. He said Ukraine was “blocked” from US intelligence “for some period of time, and then it was deblocked by the American side”. The Ukrainian leader said during this time his country did not see Russian attacks.

The US has denied it has ordered restrictions on Starlink satellite internet services to Ukraine.

“President Zelenskyy should be very careful about making statements like this that aren't true,” Mr Bessent said.

He also appeared to dodge the question of whether Ukraine was still a US ally.

“President Trump has made it clear that he wants to end this war; that it must stop. And President Zelenskyy presented a false binary this morning that Ukraine must win,” Mr Bessent said.

“The war must end, and that will be with some kind of a negotiated settlement. And President Trump is working on that every day.”

He also said the US supports Ukraine through providing intelligence, the Starlink service, and allowing Nato to buy US arms and resell them to Ukraine.

“We're not providing those to Russia,” he said.

When asked a third time if Ukraine is still a US ally, Mr Bessent said: “I'm not the Secretary of State. I'm not the President.”

analysis.framing: The article frames the US sanctions waiver as a controversial move that has deepened a rift with Ukraine, presenting official justifications alongside Ukrainian and European criticism in a largely balanced, quote-driven manner.

Emphasizes the speed and severity of criticism, adding dramatic weight.
Metaphorical language that conveys deterioration with emotional connotation.
Suggests evasion, implying the official was avoiding the question rather than simply not answering.

omissions: Specific details of the sanctions package being waived beyond tariffs on Russian goods and buyers of Russian energy
Reactions from European allies beyond the mention that the move drew opposition
Any statement from Russian officials beyond the Kremlin confirming diesel shipments
Context on the legal mechanism of the 60-day pause and what it entails
Zelenskyy's full remarks or any Ukrainian government statement beyond the quotes provided

headline: National Bank of Egypt retains Global Finance’s safest bank title for sixth consecutive year
summary: The National Bank of Egypt (NBE) has been named the safest bank in Egypt for 2026 by US-based Global Finance magazine, maintaining the position for the sixth consecutive year in an annual assessment of financial institutions across 114 countries and territories. The recognition is part of Global Finance’s 35th annual ranking of the world’s safest banks, which has served as a reference for assessing the soundness of banking institutions for over three decades. The evaluations are based on long-term foreign currency credit ratings from international agencies Moody’s, Standard & Poor’s, and Fitch for the world’s 1,000 largest banks, providing a basis to evaluate their financial strength and ability to maintain stability and face risks. Mohamed El-Etreby, Chief Executive Officer of the National Bank of Egypt, expressed his pride in the classification and the bank’s top position, particularly in light of mounting economic challenges and global market volatility. He affirmed that the stability of banks and their ability to face crises is crucial to ensuring the continuity of global trade. El-Etreby noted that the ranking, which relies on reports from global credit rating agencies assessing the world’s largest banks, reflects the NBE’s ability to adhere to international technical and legal standards, thereby contributing to preserving the strength of the bank’s assets and the stability of its performance. The classification further enhances confidence in the bank’s performance, stability, and growth rates, as it places safety standards at the top of its priorities, the CEO added. He stated that this encourages financial institutions to strengthen their partnerships with the bank and develop long-term relationships to achieve greater successes on local, regional, and global levels. El-Etreby also highlighted that National Bank of Egypt’s ranking bolsters confidence in Egypt’s financial climate and affirms the strength and stability of the Egyptian banking sector, especially given the continuous economic reform measures undertaken by the state and the Central Bank of Egypt. The full Global Finance results feature regional lists covering Africa, Asia, Australasia, Central and Eastern Europe, Latin America, the Middle East, North America, and Western Europe. The publication also includes lists of the top 50 commercial banks, top 50 emerging market banks, and the safest Islamic financial institutions.

headline: Egypt launches investment zone for Qatar’s Alam Al Roum project in North Coast
summary: Egypt has launched an investment zone for Qatar’s Alam Al Roum project in North Coast, in a move aimed at attracting domestic and foreign investment, expanding economic activity and accelerating the development of one of the country’s major coastal destinations. The launch was attended by Mohamed Farid, Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade, and Randa El-Menshawy, Minister of Housing, Utilities and Urban Communities, alongside government officials and representatives of Qatari developer Qatari Diar. The launch marks a new step in developing the investment components of the Alam Al Roum project and creating opportunities for diversified activities in tourism, real estate and services, supporting Egypt’s efforts to attract Arab and foreign capital and expand economic development beyond the Nile Valley and Delta. Farid said investment zones are an effective mechanism for attracting local and foreign investment, facilitating procedures, accelerating project implementation and generating direct and indirect employment opportunities for surrounding communities. He added that such zones also help stimulate economic and service activities while maximising the benefits of existing roads and infrastructure. The minister stressed the importance of simplifying procedures and digitising government services to enable investors to track applications, licences and approvals electronically, improving transparency and the efficiency of public services. He added that the Ministry of Investment and Foreign Trade would continue coordinating with the Ministry of Housing and other relevant authorities to expand public and private investment zones, as well as free zones. Private sector accounts for 65% of investment Farid said the private sector accounted for approximately 65% of total investment in Egypt during the third quarter of fiscal year 2025/2026, up from a previous range of 40% to 45%. He noted that the private sector employs more than 70% of Egypt’s workforce, underscoring its importance in supporting economic growth and creating jobs. Egypt has diverse opportunities for attracting foreign direct investment across real estate, productive industries, manufacturing, fertilisers, building materials and construction, the minister said. Foreign direct investment inflows reached approximately $18bn by the end of fiscal year 2025/2026, according to Farid, who expressed expectations that inflows would continue to grow. He added that achieving economic growth of between 5.5% and 6.5% over the coming years would require raising the investment-to-GDP ratio to approximately 25%, helping expand productive capacity and generate employment. Farid also praised cooperation among the government bodies involved in finalising the Alam Al Roum agreement, including the Prime Minister’s Advisory Authority, the Ministry of Housing and its affiliated entities, the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones, and other relevant agencies. He called on Qatari Diar to explore additional investment opportunities in Egypt and benefit from the country’s investment frameworks and available incentives. Housing Ministry highlights development potential El-Menshawy said the launch reflects Egypt’s commitment to strengthening partnerships with the private sector and attracting Arab and foreign investment. She stressed that urban development is no longer limited to establishing new cities and residential communities, but has become an integrated process aimed at maximising the use of national resources and creating investment opportunities that support sustainable development. The minister described Alam Al Roum as an opportunity to translate this vision into an integrated development project that capitalises on the northwestern coast’s natural, tourism and investment potential. She noted that the region represents one of Egypt’s main axes for urban expansion and investment, offering opportunities to develop tourism, real estate and service activities while establishing modern communities capable of attracting capital and creating jobs. According to El-Menshawy, the government’s approach to developing the northwestern coast extends beyond urban expansion. It seeks to redistribute investment and economic activity, establish new economic centres, and strengthen integration between tourism, real estate and services to generate added value for the national economy. She added that Alam Al Roum is expected to contribute to these objectives through an integrated urban and investment vision that balances economic returns with the preservation of the area’s natural and environmental assets. The government is committed to supporting the project and coordinating with Qatari Diar and relevant authorities to establish the conditions necessary for implementation, El-Menshawy said. She described the launch of the investment zone as an important step in enhancing the project’s ability to attract capital and accommodate a wider range of activities, boosting economic activity and creating direct and indirect employment opportunities. The minister emphasised that the success of major projects should be measured not only by the volume of investment they attract, but also by their contribution to economic development, job creation, productive and service activities, and the establishment of sustainable urban communities. El-Menshawy concluded that the Ministry of Housing would continue coordinating with relevant government bodies and the private sector to accelerate major development projects and achieve their investment and development objectives.

MANAMA /Bahrain/, October 18. /TASS/. The next meeting of the Russia-Gulf Cooperation Council Strategic Dialogue will be held in Russia and will be chaired by Saudi Arabia, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said.

"The next meeting of the strategic dialogue will be held in Russia on the rotational basis," he told a news conference after the 9th round of the Russia-Gulf Cooperation Council Strategic Dialogue. "Next year, Bahrain will be succeeded by Saudi Arabia as president. Together with out friends, we will be preparing the next ministerial meeting and will try to respond with no less hospitability than we were met with here."

The Gulf Cooperation Council is a regional organization of six countries, namely Bahrain, Qatar, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, Oman, and Saudi Arabia. The organization's goal is to expand cooperation among member countries in all areas and to develop common positions on key international and regional issues.

summary: Five UAE aid convoys carrying 789 tonnes of food and shelter supplies have entered Gaza this week, continuing the country's relief efforts for Palestinians.The convoys, comprising 60 lorries, were dispatched as part of Operation G3, Gallant Knight 3, the UAE's continuing humanitarian initiative aimed at addressing the basic needs of Palestinians in the Gaza Strip.The latest deliveries bring the total number of lorries that have entered Gaza under the operation since its launch to 14,579, collectively transporting 138,030 tonnes of humanitarian aid to the territory.The supplies are intended to address food and shelter shortages among the Palestinian population, supporting the broader humanitarian response and easing the suffering of those affected by the conflict in Gaza.The Operation Gallant Knight 3 team continues to co-ordinate aid shipments through the UAE Humanitarian Aid Logistics Centre in Al Arish, Egypt. body_text:
Five UAE aid convoys carrying 789 tonnes of food and shelter supplies have entered Gaza this week, continuing the country's relief efforts for Palestinians.

The convoys, comprising 60 lorries, were dispatched as part of Operation G3, Gallant Knight 3, the UAE's continuing humanitarian initiative aimed at addressing the basic needs of Palestinians in the Gaza Strip.

The latest deliveries bring the total number of lorries that have entered Gaza under the operation since its launch to 14,579, collectively transporting 138,030 tonnes of humanitarian aid to the territory.

Gaza traders halt imports amid tax dispute with Hamas

The supplies are intended to address food and shelter shortages among the Palestinian population, supporting the broader humanitarian response and easing the suffering of those affected by the conflict in Gaza.

The Operation Gallant Knight 3 team continues to co-ordinate aid shipments through the UAE Humanitarian Aid Logistics Centre in Al Arish, Egypt. The facility manages the full logistics pipeline, including receiving, sorting and preparing supplies before they are transported across the border into Gaza, ensuring a steady flow of assistance reaches those in need.

headline: Egypt’s FM holds calls with Pakistan, Oman and Somalia on regional de-escalation
summary: Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty held separate phone calls with his counterparts from Pakistan, Oman and Somalia on Sunday, discussing regional military escalation, diplomatic efforts to ease tensions, and developments in the Horn of Africa and Red Sea. Abdelatty received a call from Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar, during which the two officials reviewed proposals aimed at containing regional tensions and restoring diplomatic efforts. Abdelatty said Egypt supports continued coordination through the regional quadrilateral mechanism and rejects threats against Gulf states or the use of strategic straits and maritime routes as tools of pressure or escalation. According to Egypt’s Foreign Ministry, the two ministers stressed the need for the United States and Iran to resume dialogue and negotiations aimed at reaching understandings that could end the current crisis and limit its impact on the region. In a separate call with Omani Foreign Minister Badr bin Hamad Al Busaidi, Abdelatty discussed bilateral relations and the latest regional escalation. The two ministers stressed the need for continued Egyptian-Omani coordination with regional and international actors to support de-escalation and prioritise political and diplomatic solutions. Abdelatty also received a call from Somali Foreign Minister Abdulsalam Abdi Ali to discuss bilateral relations and developments in the Horn of Africa and the Red Sea. Abdelatty reiterated Egypt’s support for Somalia’s unity, sovereignty and territorial integrity, as well as efforts to strengthen Somali state institutions. The two ministers also discussed follow-up on the outcomes of a quadrilateral consultative summit hosted in New Alamein, focusing on supporting security, stability, development and de-escalation in the Horn of Africa and Red Sea region.

headline: Trump backs ally Netanyahu ahead of Israel's tight election
summary: US President Donald Trump on Sunday endorsed his ally Benjamin Netanyahu before Israel's close-fought parliamentary election on October 27, providing a boost to the veteran prime minister's bid to win a new mandate. Netanyahu touted his close relationship with the US president in a video released by his Likud party, saying that together they had "crushed Iran" and adding that re-election would allow him to work with Trump to "elminate the Iranian threat over the next two years, or even sooner".
body_text:
US President Donald Trump on Sunday endorsed his ally Benjamin Netanyahu before Israel's close-fought parliamentary election on October 27, providing a boost to the veteran prime minister's bid to win a new mandate.

Netanyahu touted his close relationship with the US president in a video released by his Likud party, saying that together they had "crushed Iran" and adding that re-election would allow him to work with Trump to "elminate the Iranian threat over the next two years, or even sooner".

The endorsement comes less than two weeks before Israel's first vote since the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack, which opposition politicians have accused Netanyahu of bearing personal responsibility for after allegedly ignoring warnings.

Trump and Netanyahu, who polls show is in a tight election race, have worked closely together on Israel's multi-front wars after the Hamas-led attack, including bombarding Iran, and the endorsement could be a boon to his re-election campaign.

"Bibi Netanyahu has been Strong, Brave, and Brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition, including that coming from even Israel, itself," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform, using a common nickname for the Israeli leader.

"This is the kind of Partner that the United States of America is demanding of Israel, a Country for which it has done so much. Please let this Letter serve to represent my Complete and Total Endorsement of Bibi Netanyahu in his upcoming Race for Re-Election as Prime Minister of Israel."

The election is seen as a referendum on Netanyahu, who quickly thanked the US leader for his support on Sunday.

"Thank you, President Trump, for your tremendous support and for our work together. Together we will complete the mission!" he wrote on X.

"I ask you to listen carefully to what President Trump said this evening," Netanyahu told voters. "He said that together we have accomplished extraordinary things... But there is still a mission to complete."

Trump joined Netanyahu in a US-Israeli attack on Iran in late February but agreed to a ceasefire in April in the face of widespread US public opposition to the war, which had sent oil prices spiralling.

Speaking at an event in August, Netanyahu said Trump "is our greatest friend, one of the greatest friends we have had in the White House".

But relations between the two have at times been strained on Iran, with Netanyahu saying no diplomatic agreement was possible with Iran's leadership, while Trump sought a negotiated end to the months-long conflict.

The endorsement comes after US Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned against a brewing "crisis" in the occupied West Bank after an American photojournalist for The Washington Post was injured in a brutal attack by Israeli settlers.

"We're very disturbed by those images and what we're seeing," Rubio told reporters Saturday. Netanyahu's office said it was investigating the circumstances around the attack.

With Israel and Netanyahu looking increasingly isolated on the world stage, Trump's support is vital.

Netanyahu, who turns 77 on October 21, is Israel's longest-serving prime minister, having served as prime minister on and off for more than 19 years.

The wily political operator returned to power in December 2022 bringing in once-shunned ultra-nationalists and quickly tried to rein in the judiciary, which is examining corruption charges that could land him in jail.

His main election rival is opposition politician Gadi Eisenkot, the leader of the centre-right Yashar party and a former military chief who regularly accuses Netanyahu of bearing personal responsibility for the October 7 attack.

Some seven million Israelis will be eligible to vote in the legislative election.

Current polls show that neither Netanyahu's bloc nor that led by Eisenkot is in a position to win the 61 seats needed to control the 120-seat parliament and form a governing coalition.

Eisenkot said that only Israelis could choose who they want to run the country.

Speaking at a conference in Tel Aviv, Eisenkot said he "admires" Trump "but Israel is a democratic country, only Israelis can choose their leaders".

But Trump warned against Israel electing "anyone other than Bibi", writing that if voters chose one of his rivals "America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so".

On Sunday, Israel's far-right National Security Minister National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir said "there is only one person capable of serving as Prime Minister, and that is Benjamin Netanyahu".

headline: Saudi coalition, Houthis trade strikes as disruption spreads
summary: The Saudi-led coalition and Iran-backed Houthis traded strikes Sunday as fighting raged in the intensifying conflict that has disturbed life for residents of the kingdom's capital Riyadh and war-wracked Yemen. Disruption in the world's top crude oil exporter has continued to spread as the Houthis keep up their strikes, with Riyadh's landmark Kingdom Centre skyscraper ordering "mandatory" remote working until further notice for office tenants on Sunday.
body_text:
The Saudi-led coalition and Iran-backed Houthis traded strikes Sunday as fighting raged in the intensifying conflict that has disturbed life for residents of the kingdom's capital Riyadh and war-wracked Yemen.

Disruption in the world's top crude oil exporter has continued to spread as the Houthis keep up their strikes, with Riyadh's landmark Kingdom Centre skyscraper ordering "mandatory" remote working until further notice for office tenants on Sunday.

No reason was given for the order, but it follows a security alert and two drone interceptions around the capital on top of waves of Houthi attacks on Saudi targets in recent weeks.

Meanwhile the Saudi-led coalition backing the internationally recognised government has launched repeated air raids on Houthi-controlled regions of Yemen.

An alleged Saudi airstrike in northern Yemen's Saada governorate on Sunday killed at least nine people and wounded 16 others, the Houthis' Saba news agency reported.

The coalition meanwhile said Sunday that two pilots were killed when their helicopter crashed in Najran near the Yemen border, while the Houthis said they "downed an Apache helicopter belonging to the Saudi enemy" in the same area.

The coalition blamed a "technical malfunction" for the incident, which inflicted its first military fatalities since the long-running war with the Houthis reignited in July.

Schools in the Saudi capital and surrounding areas also extended online learning into a second week, while Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport remains closed after 13 people were killed in a major attack last week.

The Saudi coalition's decade-plus war with the Iran-backed Houthis has returned with ferocity during the US-Iran war, with regular attacks reported by both sides.

Egypt's parliament on Sunday postponed a vote on President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi's request to authorise military support for Saudi Arabia, two lawmakers told AFP, extending deliberations to Monday.

And Iran's newly appointed Defence Minister Mehrdad Akhlaghi threatened to inflict "enormous damage" on the United States and its allies if Washington resumes its military campaign.

Tenants of the Kingdom Centre, which towers over central Riyadh, include financial services giant Merril Lynch, management consultancy McKinsey and the International Monetary Fund.

"Please be advised that remote working arrangements are mandatory for all office employees at Kingdom Centre, effective immediately and until further notice," the building's management said in an email seen by AFP.

The mall at the foot of the building remains open.

After an uneasy, four-year truce, Yemen's conflict has surged back to life and intensified when the group seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month.

The Houthis have hit Saudi targets including tankers in the Red Sea, oil facilities and Riyadh's King Khalid International airport.

A Houthi projectile injured at least six people in southern Saudi Arabia on Sunday after it struck a residential area in Najran near the border with Yemen, according to the kingdom's civil defence agency.

The coalition also said two ballistic missiles were intercepted in the kingdom's south. Threat alerts for Najran city and As Sulayyil governorate in Riyadh province were issued but quickly cancelled on Sunday.

The Houthis have declared a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia and captured territory around the Bab al-Mandab strait, the Red Sea chokepoint and vital export route for Saudi oil since Iran blockaded the Gulf's Strait of Hormuz.

On Sunday, Egypt's parliament held an emergency session after President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi asked lawmakers to authorise support to defend Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks.

The session was extended into Monday "to give all lawmakers the opportunity to speak and express their views", one of them told AFP.

Sisi had said he was willing to "carry out any measure to protect" Saudi Arabia if its leaders requested it.

The hostilities were the focus of a meeting on Sunday between the Russian and Saudi foreign ministers on the sidelines of a summit between Gulf states and Russia in Bahrain's Manama.

They discussed "regional developments, particularly the escalation in Yemen, as well as the persistent threats to shipping in the Straits of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab", the Saudi Foreign Ministry said on X.

Saudi Arabia's defence minister Khalid bin Salman also wrote on X that he met with UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, with the two discussing regional developments.

French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot is due to arrive in Riyadh on Sunday evening before President Emmanuel Macron's tour of the Gulf where he is expected to reaffirm Paris' support for the kingdom.
