headline: Israel violating US-mediated framework agreement, Lebanese president says
summary: Joseph Aoun says Lebanon remains committed to diplomatic solution despite continued Israeli attacks, calling it less costly than devastating war
body_text:
Lebanese President Joseph Aoun said Monday that Israel has failed to comply with a US-mediated framework agreement signed in June and continues daily violations in southern Lebanon, reaffirming his country’s commitment to a diplomatic solution.

Aoun made the remarks during a meeting with Arab League Secretary-General Nabil Fahmy at the presidential palace in Baabda, east of Beirut, according to a statement from the Lebanese presidency.

“The Israelis have not adhered to the framework agreement, and the south continues to face daily violations,” Aoun said.

He stressed that continued Israeli violations would not achieve their objectives but would instead strengthen the Lebanese people’s determination to defend their land and rights.

Aoun said the violations were obstructing the Lebanese state’s efforts to implement its stated objectives.

He reaffirmed Lebanon’s commitment to a diplomatic solution despite its difficulties, saying it was “far less costly than the devastating war” for which the Lebanese people, particularly residents of the south, continue to pay the price.

“It is time for Lebanon to have some peace,” he added.

The president also welcomed any efforts by the Arab League to help Lebanon overcome the difficult circumstances it faces.

For his part, Fahmy reaffirmed the Arab League’s support for the Lebanese state and its institutions, rejecting any infringement on the country’s sovereignty.

He expressed readiness to engage with Arab and Western countries to mobilize support for Lebanon and its people.

Fahmy stressed that the Arab position toward Lebanon remained united and that the organization was working to translate that support into practical measures and financial assistance.

Israel has carried out attacks on Lebanon since March 2, killing and injuring thousands of people and displacing over 1.5 million residents.

On June 26, Lebanon and Israel signed a US-sponsored framework agreement providing for a gradual Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory, the deployment of the Lebanese army and the disarmament of Hezbollah.

Despite the agreement, Israel has continued its attacks on southern Lebanon.

​​​​​​​Israeli forces also continue to occupy Lebanese territory, including areas held for decades and others seized during more recent wars and military operations.

headline: Georgia exported record-breaking 948.4 tons of figs to Russia in September 2026
summary: The previous record for fig shipments to Russia was set in August 2025 and amounted to 916.6 metric tons
body_text:
TBILISI, October 19. /TASS/. Georgian fig deliveries to Russia stood at 948.4 metric tons in September 2026, marking a record-breaking monthly high, according to data from the Georgian national statistical service reviewed by TASS.

According to the authority, exports of fresh or dried figs from Georgia to Russia in September reached 948.4 metric tons valued at $1.3 mln, which is 1.7 times higher than the figure of September of last year. The previous record for fig shipments to Russia was set in August 2025 and amounted to 916.6 metric tons.

In total, since July, the start of the fig ripening season, Georgia has exported 1,800 metric tons to Russia valued at $2.4 mln. Apart from Russia, this commodity was purchased from Georgia in minor quantities by Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan (18 metric tons each), and Armenia (2.5 metric tons).

headline: Macron opens Gulf tour after violent protests in France
summary: French President Emmanuel Macron on Monday began a Gulf tour aimed at securing oil and diesel supplies in an effort to bring down prices, after a weekend of violent protests sparked by soaring living costs. Macron, just hours after slamming France's "unbridled" violence in an address late on Sunday, arrived in OPEC member Kuwait where he was welcomed by the emir, Sheikh Mishal Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah.
body_text:
French President Emmanuel Macron on Monday began a Gulf tour aimed at securing oil and diesel supplies in an effort to bring down prices, after a weekend of violent protests sparked by soaring living costs.

Macron, just hours after slamming France's "unbridled" violence in an address late on Sunday, arrived in OPEC member Kuwait where he was welcomed by the emir, Sheikh Mishal Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah.

He will also visit the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Qatar by Wednesday on a trip aimed at strengthening "economic and defence partnerships" in the Gulf, which has been thrown into turmoil by the US-Iran war since February.

Macron acknowledged security and intelligence failures but refused his interior minister's resignation after more than 2,500 people were arrested in some of France's worst violence in years, with town halls and shops looted and set on fire.

Before flying to Kuwait, he said the visit was needed to "secure our supplies", pointing out that the demonstrators had expressed "concern" about fuel prices.

Talks in Kuwait were focused on delivering pre-positioned stocks of kerosene and diesel from Oman to the French overseas territories of Reunion and Mayotte, the presidency said.

French armed forces minister Catherine Vautrin also signed a letter of intent on defence cooperation with her Kuwaiti counterpart, with discussions covering arms sales, according to a member of the French delegation.

Aviation giant Airbus signed a letter of intent to support the renewal of the Kuwait Airways fleet and cooperate on maintenance and training.

Macron's tour "may give an impression of normality... but may also appear out of touch and suggest a kind of power vacuum", said constitutional expert Benjamin Morel.

During his trip, "the goal is to secure a certain number of commitments" on diesel and oil volumes, the French presidency said.

Macron is accompanied by senior executives from France's two biggest energy groups, TotalEnergies and Engie.

The G7 countries, chaired this year by France, agreed in early October to draw up to 100 million barrels of oil from their strategic reserves to ease pressure.

Crude oil prices have ballooned during the eight-month war, as Iran blockades the Strait of Hormuz -- the main exit route for the Gulf's energy exports.

Yemen's Houthis have compounded the pressure by firing on Saudi tankers in the Red Sea, striking the kingdom's oil sites and carrying out deadly attacks on Riyadh's international airport.

Francis Perrin, an energy expert at the French Institute for International and Strategic Relations, said he did not expect Macron's visit to have an impact on fuel prices.

"The Arab countries of the Gulf are very eager to supply the world, and the French market, but it is difficult for them to make firm commitments until the region has been stabilised," he said.

Macron will hold talks with Gulf leaders including the UAE's president and Qatar's emir on ways to "secure" maritime shipments and find "alternative and bypass routes" for energy exports, the presidency said.

France and Britain have assembled an international mission to help reopen the Strait of Hormuz, mainly through demining operations, once the United States and Iran reach agreement on the waterway.

However, the two sides remain at an impasse, eight months since the start of hostilities.

The French president will also hold talks on defence cooperation, after the Gulf countries were targeted by thousands of Iranian missiles and drones.

France deployed its aircraft carrier Charles de Gaulle in the spring, along with Rafale fighter jets, a frigate and air defence assets.

Macron also sent French soldiers to protect Yanbu, an oil terminal on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast that has become a vital conduit for exports.

body_text:
France's Foreign Minister has underlined the need for a “new international framework” to support Lebanese security forces after the mandate of the UN peacekeeping mission in south Lebanon (Unifil) expires at the end of the year.

Jean-Noel Barrot, who was accompanied on a weekend visit to Beirut by Alice Rufo, the French Armed Forces Minister, said a “security vacuum” must not develop when Unifil ends its mission after nearly five decades.

Post-Unifil international presence and support is still to be defined but French diplomatic sources said ahead of the visit that any security vacuum in south Lebanon would be “extremely dangerous”.

Macron arrives in Kuwait as part of Gulf tour

Mr Barrot and Ms Rufo held meetings with senior Lebanese officials during their visit, including President Joseph Aoun, Prime Minister Nawaf Salam, Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri and army commander Gen Rodolphe Haykal.

While Mr Aoun would prefer to extend Unifil's mandate, he said if that were not possible, Beirut would welcome “any formula that ensures an international presence in the south”.

The US and Israel pressured the UN to end Unifil's mandate, saying the force was partly to blame for the failure to prevent repeated conflicts across the Blue Line, the UN-demarcated border that separates southern Lebanon and Israel.

The French ministers stressed the need to support the underfunded and under-equipped Lebanese Armed Forces as it continues with the uphill task of bringing all weapons under state control. This would mean disarming Hezbollah, which the Iran-backed Lebanese armed group and political party has so far resisted.

Israel's military currently occupies about 65 towns and villages in southern Lebanon, where it has declared a security zone along the border after the latest round of fighting with Hezbollah broke out in early March.

Last week, the European Union announced the establishment of a support mission for the Lebanese Armed Forces, with an initial mandate of three years.

The mission will work to strengthen the capacity of the Lebanese Armed Forces and the Internal Security Forces, as well as supporting maritime security, although EU leaders have stressed it is not intended as a replacement for Unifil.

India has strongly rejected the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation’s (OIC) resolution on the situation in Jammu and Kashmir, saying the grouping has allowed itself to be “misused” by Pakistan for its “bigoted agenda”.

A day after the resolution was passed during the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Baghdad, Iraq, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said on Monday, “The references to India are malicious, biased and false, and have been orchestrated by Pakistan. We are disappointed that the OIC has once again allowed itself to be misused by Pakistan for its bigoted agenda.”

New Delhi also emphasised that the OIC has “no locus standi whatsoever” to comment on matters strictly internal to India.

‘Stark contrast’ to situation in PoK

“The Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh are integral and inalienable parts of India. Politically motivated propaganda can never alter this reality,” the MEA said in its statement, adding, “Over the past years since the abrogation of Art 370, Jammu and Kashmir has seen significant economic growth and benefits accruing directly to its people through infrastructure development, tourism and connectivity.”

This, the MEA said, is in “stark contrast” to the situation in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir where Islamabad has “unleashed violence, repression and brutality on civilian protesters, killing scores of them, including women and children.”

The MEA said that “no amount of media blackout has been able to hide these grave violations of human rights”.

“The only issues related to Jammu and Kashmir that remain to be addressed are Pakistan vacating areas under its illegal and forcible occupation and ceasing its continued support to cross-border terrorism,” it added.

The MEA described other “fabricated and hostile references against India in the OIC resolutions including insinuations related to Islamophobia” as nothing but a “desperate attempt by Pakistan to divert international attention from its own appalling record of minority persecution and sectarian violence”.

The 57-member bloc has repeatedly issued statements and adopted resolutions regarding Jammu and Kashmir following the abrogation of Article 370 of the Constitution, which granted special status to the erstwhile state.

The most recent resolution comes just weeks after the joint communiqué issued by the OIC Contact Group on Jammu and Kashmir on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York in September 2026.

On this, the MEA said, ”The OIC’s repeated endorsement of patently malicious propaganda and narratives peddled by Pakistan raises serious questions about its credibility and integrity. We hope its members will do better and reform this organisation.”

headline: Russian, Iranian foreign ministers hold talks in Tehran
summary: Sergey Lavrov, Abbas Araghchi begin diplomatic consultations as Moscow, Tehran seek to follow up on bilateral agreements
body_text:
Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov met his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi in Tehran on Monday, with diplomatic delegations from both countries beginning talks immediately afterward, Iran’s state broadcaster IRIB reported.

Lavrov arrived in Tehran on Monday for an official visit to hold talks with Iranian officials on bilateral relations and regional and international developments.

The meeting between Lavrov and Araghchi was followed by consultations between the Iranian and Russian diplomatic delegations, according to IRIB.

Lavrov is also expected to meet Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian during the visit, IRIB said, citing Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei.

Baqaei said the visit is part of ongoing bilateral consultations and efforts to follow up on agreements between the two countries.

Iran and Russia have strengthened political, economic and military cooperation in recent years amid Western sanctions imposed on both countries.

In January 2025, Pezeshkian and Russian President Vladimir Putin signed a 20-year Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Treaty in Moscow, covering cooperation in defense, security, energy, trade and transportation.

​​​​​​​The agreement also provides for closer coordination on regional and international issues, although it does not establish a mutual defense obligation.

headline: Iran develops two-year plan to expand cooperation with SCO member states — vice president
summary: Mohammad Reza Aref emphasized that "in addition to economic and trade ties, a key priority for Iran within this organization is expanding cooperation in the fields of advanced technologies and artificial intelligence"
body_text:
RABAT, October 19. /TASS/. The Iranian authorities have developed a two-year plan to strengthen cooperation with the member states of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO), First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref announced.

"The Iranian government has developed a two-year plan aimed at maximizing the SCO's potential in various sectors," the IRNA news agency quoted him as saying. Aref emphasized that "in addition to economic and trade ties, a key priority for Iran within this organization is expanding cooperation in the fields of advanced technologies and artificial intelligence."

According to the first vice president, Iran "is focusing on its domestic potential, particularly in logistics, transportation, and modern technological solutions." Aref stressed that Tehran’s strategy is "to maintain an active and effective presence in the SCO." "Despite differences on certain regional and international political issues, Iran’s goal is to overcome these differences and reach common solutions through dialogue and cooperation," he concluded.

headline: Top 64 concerts and events coming to the UAE, from Mariah Carey to Katy Perry
summary: From pop and rock to stand-up comedy, ballet, opera and musicals, the UAE’s live events season is in full swing, with the months ahead offering a packed line-up across Abu Dhabi, Dubai and Sharjah. Mariah Carey will return to Abu Dhabi with her Christmas-time show in December, while Wasla Festival brings regional acts, including Marcel Khalife, Le Trio Joubran, TootArd and Fatima to Expo City Dubai in November.Najwa Karam will bring her greatest hits to Dubai’s Coca-Cola Arena, while Abu Dhabi Comedy Season has announced shows led by Palestinian-American star Mo Amer and US comic Aries Spears.Elsewhere, Abu Dhabi Festival will bring a strong classical programme including the American Ballet Theatre and Dhafer Youssef. Dubai audiences can also look forward to four shows by superstar comedian Trevor Noah, as well as concerts by Vir Das, Atif Aslam, Hiba Tawaji with Ibrahim Maalouf.Abu Dhabi Grand Prix weekend will add another run of major shows, with The Chainsmokers and The Script closing the after-race concert series at Etihad Live, and Anyma performing at Yas Gateway Park as part of the official concert series.Looking ahead to 2027, Shah Rukh Khan curate the inaugural Unifyd festival at Etihad Live, with Arijit Singh, Karan Aujla and Sonu Nigam among the first artists announced.Here, we round up the concerts and live events still to come in the UAE.1. Gipsy Kings by Andre Reyes: October 22 at Dubai OperaA new twist on the sound of the beloved group has founding member Andre Reyes lead a symphonic version of the Gipsy Kings repertoire, with hits such as Bamboleo, Djobi Djoba, Volare and Un Amor reworked with full orchestral arrangements.Doors open 7.30pm; show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh3952. Nancy Ajram: October 24 at Coca-Cola Arena, DubaiLebanese singer Nancy Ajram returns to Dubai with a catalogue that made her one of the defining Arabic pop stars of the 2000s and beyond. Her songs include Akhasmak Ah, Ah W Noss and Ya Tabtab.Show starts 9pm; tickets from Dh2103. Black Coffee: October 24 at Ushuaia Dubai Harbour ExperienceSouth African DJ and producer Black Coffee returns to Dubai to open the third season of Ushuaia Dubai Harbour Experience. The Grammy winner is known for a deep house sound that draws on soulful rhythms and African percussion, with tracks including Drive.Earlier this year, he became the first African DJ to sell out London's O2 Arena.Doors open 8pm; tickets from Dh2504. Prateek Kuhad: October 24 at Dubai OperaIndian singer-songwriter Prateek Kuhad opens his Full Moon Chamber Tour in Dubai, following the release of his third studio album Full Moon Chamber. The record was written and recorded between New York and Los Angeles, and continues the intimate songwriting heard across tracks including Kasoor, cold/mess and Co2.Show starts 8.30pm; tickets from Dh1955. Blue: October 25 at Dubai Millennium Amphitheatre, Expo City DubaiBritish pop group Blue will celebrate 25 years of hits with a Dubai show built around fan favourites such as All Rise, One Love and Sorry Seems to Be the Hardest Word, alongside newer material from their Reflections album. The four-piece remain one of the UK’s most successful boy bands, with three number one albums and 11 Top 10 singles.Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh2396. Russell Peters: October 25 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiKnown for his rapid-fire delivery, crowd banter and cultural observations, Indian-Canadian comedian Russell Peters built an international following through specials such as Outsourced, Red, White and Brown and Deported. Peters remains one of the highest-grossing comedians globally, with a touring career spanning more than two decades.Show starts 8.30pm; tickets from Dh2757. Shaan: October 25 at Coca-Cola Arena, DubaiIndian playback singer Shaan brings his All of Me Tour to Dubai, looking back on a career spanning more than three decades. The set features romantic ballads, Bollywood favourites and earlier hits including Tanha Dil, Jab Se Tere Naina, Main Hoon Na and Behti Hawa Sa Tha Woh.Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh1508. Titize: A Venetian Dream: October 29 to 31 at Dubai OperaVenice is the inspiration for this show mixing circus, theatre, dance and live music.The 10-member cast use acrobatics, clowning and physical theatre to create a dreamlike version of Venice through its masks, waterways and carnival traditions.Shows at 2pm and 8pm; tickets from Dh2759. Nass: October 30 at The Arts Centre at NYU Abu DhabiFrench-Moroccan choreographer Fouad Boussouf brings together seven male dancers in a work connecting hip-hop movement with the ritual dimensions of North African music. The title takes inspiration from Moroccan group Nass El Ghiwane and draws parallels between their search for identity and the origins of hip-hop.Show starts 7.30pm; tickets from Dh52.5010. Riverdance: October 31 and November 1 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiRiverdance returns to the UAE with a production marking the Irish dance show’s 30th anniversary. The staging retains Bill Whelan’s Grammy Award-winning score while introducing updated choreography, costumes, lighting, projection and motion graphics.Performance times vary; tickets from Dh21511. Benjamin Clementine: November 1 at Dubai OperaBritish singer, pianist and composer Benjamin Clementine performs a programme combining experimental pop, contemporary classical music, jazz and poetry. His debut album, At Least for Now, won the Mercury Prize, while later recordings include I Tell a Fly and And I Have Been.Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh50012. Jony: November 4 at Coca-Cola Arena, DubaiRussian-Azerbaijani singer Jony is a star Russian pop and built a following with songs including Kamin, Kometa and Ty Besposhchadna.Show starts 9pm; tickets from Dh29513. Mo Amer: November 6 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiPalestinian-American comedian Mo Amer performs as part of Abu Dhabi Comedy Season. Born in Kuwait to Palestinian parents and raised in the US, his comedy draws on displacement, immigration and life between cultures.Those experiences also shaped Mo, the semi-autobiographical Netflix series he created with Ramy Youssef, which won a Peabody Award in 2023.Show time and ticket prices to be announced14. Maz Jobrani: November 7 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiIranian-American comedian Maz Jobrani returns to Abu Dhabi with material exploring immigrant experiences, cultural misunderstandings and family expectations. He previously performed at the inaugural Abu Dhabi Comedy Week in 2024 on a shared bill with Bassem Youssef.Show time and ticket prices to be announced15. Ministry of Sound Classical: November 7 at Dubai OperaClub anthems are given an orchestral spin as Ministry of Sound Classical brings dance music into the concert hall.Conducted by David Mahoney, the show combines a full orchestra and vocalists with electronic music, lighting and visuals, drawing on tracks associated with decades of club culture.Show time and ticket prices to be announced16. American Ballet Theatre: November 20 at Emirates Palace, Abu DhabiDubbed one of the world's greatest dance companies, the American Ballet Theatre will perform works including Frederick Ashton’s Birthday Offering, Jiri Kylian’s Nuages, Brady Farrar’s Trio Elegiaque and Paquita, staged by Natalia Makarova after Marius Petipa.Show starts 8pm, tickets from Dh125 17. Aries Spears: November 21 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiAmerican comedian Aries Spears brings more than three decades of stand-up, impressions and crowd work to Etihad Arena. A former Mad TV cast member, he is known for his celebrity impersonations that include Michael Jackson, Eddie Murphy and Shaquille O'Neal.Doors open 9pm; show starts 10pm; tickets from Dh12018. Synthony x Faithless: November 21 at Bla Bla by McGettigan's, DubaiSynthony makes its Middle East debut with a full orchestra reworking electronic dance anthems through live instrumentation, vocals and visual production. The night will also feature Faithless Sound System, led by Sister Bliss, with tracks including Insomnia and We Come 1.Doors open 6pm; tickets from Dh29519. Trevor Noah: November 25-26 and November 28 and 29 at Dubai OperaTrevor Noah brings a new stand-up show to Dubai across four nights. The Emmy Award-winning South African comedian and former host of The Daily Show has released several Netflix specials, hosts the podcast What Now? with Trevor Noah and is the author of Born a Crime and Into the Uncut Grass.Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh29520. Algarabia: November 26 at Emirates Palace, Abu DhabiAlgarabia presents a theatrical production blending flamenco with Arabic poetry, performed by musicians from Spain’s University of Navarra Symphony Orchestra alongside dancers and actors. The work follows the journey of an Arab girl drawn to ancient botanical theory and poetic tradition.Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh10021. Hiba Tawaji and Ibrahim Maalouf: November 27 at Dubai OperaHiba Tawaji and Ibrahim Maalouf will unite for a one-night performance at Dubai Opera, with the programme drawing on French musical heritage through a blend of chanson, jazz and contemporary composition. Tawaji’s emotive vocals and Maalouf’s genre-crossing trumpet work make this one of the more distinctive concert pairings on the calendar.Show starts 8.30pm; tickets from Dh35522. Atif Aslam: November 27 at Coca-Cola Arena, DubaiAtif Aslam returns to Coca-Cola Arena after five consecutive years of sold-out Dubai concerts. The Pakistani singer’s programme will move between Bollywood songs, pop-rock and devotional music, with hits including Tajdar-e-Haram, Jeena Jeena, Pehli Nazar Mein, Dil Diyan Gallan and Aadat.Doors open 9pm; tickets from Dh35023. Tarkan: November 27 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiKnown internationally for the global hit Simarik and a catalogue that has defined Turkish pop for more than two decades, Tarkan is making his Abu Dhabi debut is further proof of Turkish’s pop growing popularity in the region.Show starts 8.30pm; tickets from Dh29524. Wasla Festival: November 28 at Jubilee Park, Expo City DubaiLebanese composer and oud player Marcel Khalife headlines the return of Wasla Festival, alongside Palestinian ensemble Le Trio Joubran, Syrian duo TootArd and British-Sudanese singer Fatima. Starts 6pm; tickets from Dh35025. Ramy Sabry: November 28 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiEgyptian singer Ramy Sabry comes to Abu Dhabi with a catalogue of romantic Arabic pop and ballads. His songs include Lama Bywhashny, alongside a wider repertoire centred on love, memory and heartbreak.Doors open 7.30pm; show starts 9pm; tickets from Dh29526. Artbat Present Upperground: November 28 at Ushuaia Dubai Harbour ExperienceUkrainian electronic duo Artbat bring their Upperground event series to Dubai, joined by Miss Monique, R3hab and Italian DJ and producer 7 Skies. The show follows Artbat’s recent reworking of Gotye's Somebody That I Used to Know with David Guetta.Doors open 8pm; tickets from Dh15027. Verdi’s Opera Gala: November 29 at Emirates Palace, Abu DhabiMarking 125 years since Giuseppe Verdi’s death, this programme is led by soprano Maria Agresta and tenor Giorgio Berrugi, and includes selections from Nabucco, I Vespri Siciliani, Otello and La Traviata, alongside overtures and duets drawn from Verdi’s wider catalogue.Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh12528. Andrea Bocelli: December 2 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiItalian tenor Andrea Bocelli brings his 30th Anniversary Romanza World Tour to Abu Dhabi as part of Yasalam Classics. The concert celebrates Romanza, the album that helped establish him internationally and includes songs such as Con te partiro and Vivo per lei.Doors open 6pm; tickets from Dh29529. The Tsar's Bride by the Bolshoi Theatre: December 2 at Dubai OperaThe Bolshoi Theatre begins its first official UAE tour with Rimsky-Korsakov's The Tsar's Bride.Set during the reign of Ivan the Terrible, the opera centres on Marfa, a young woman whose selection as the tsar's bride sets off jealousy, rivalry and political intrigue.Show time and ticket prices to be announced30. Bolshoi Theatre Orchestra, December 3The Bolshoi Theatre Orchestra takes centre stage for a symphonic concert on the second night of the company’s first official UAE tour.Showtime and ticket prices TBC31. Lewis Capaldi and Zara Larsson: December 3 at Etihad Park, Abu DhabiLewis Capaldi and Zara Larsson will open the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix 2026 after-race concert series with separate sets at Etihad Park. Capaldi returns to the capital following his Saadiyat Nights performance in January, bringing a catalogue that includes Someone You Loved, Before You Go and Forget Me. Larsson joins the bill with pop staples such as Lush Life, Never Forget You and Symphony, offering a high-tempo contrast to Capaldi’s ballad-driven set. The show launches the four-night programme running alongside the race weekend at Yas Marina Circuit.Showtime yet to be announced; access exclusive to Abu Dhabi Grand Prix ticket holders32. Shimza: December 4 at 16/360, Yas Marina Circuit, Abu DhabiSouth African DJ Shimza brings his percussion-heavy Afro-tech sound to 16/360 as Abu Dhabi Grand Prix weekend gets under way. Mont Rouge and Moojo: December 4 at Bagatelle, W Abu Dhabi, Abu DhabiSwiss duo Mont Rouge and French DJ Moojo share the Friday bill at Bagatelle's rooftop pop-up during Abu Dhabi Grand Prix weekend. Mont Rouge are known for their Afro-house version of Voyage Voyage, recorded with Francis Mercier and Coco, as well as their remix of Axwell and Sebastian Ingrosso's More Than You Know.Tables from Dh7,00034. The Nutcracker by the Bolshoi Theatre: December 4 to 6 at Dubai OperaThe Nutcracker has become a Dubai Opera tradition, and this year's production will feature the Bolshoi Theatre, with Tchaikovsky's ballet performed by the company's dancers and orchestra.Yuri Grigorovich's choreography follows Marie from a family Christmas celebration into a fantasy world of toys and magic, set to a score containing some of Tchaikovsky's best-known music.Show times and ticket prices to be announced35. Anyma: December 4 at Yas Gateway Park, Abu DhabiItalian-American DJ and producer Anyma will perform at Yas Gateway Park as part of the official Abu Dhabi Grand Prix after party concert series. Known for large-scale audiovisual shows and melodic techno, he brought his dazzling live production to the Pyramids of Giza in 2025 and has become one of electronic music’s most distinctive live acts through his work as a solo artist and as one half of Tale of Us.Abu Dhabi Grand Prix ticket holder pre-sales begin on September 10, with general sales opening on September 11; show time and ticket prices to be announced36. Imagine Dragons: December 5 at Etihad Live, Abu DhabiImagine Dragons will headline the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix after-race concert series on Saturday night. Fronted by Dan Reynolds, the US band are known for songs including Believer, Radioactive, Demons, Thunder and It’s Time. The group last performed in Abu Dhabi in 2023, when they sold out Etihad Arena.Showtime yet to be announced; access exclusive to Abu Dhabi Grand Prix ticket holders37. CamelPhat: December 5 at 16/360, Yas Marina Circuit, Abu DhabiBritish electronic duo CamelPhat take over the trackside 16/360 venue on the second night of its Grand Prix programme. Dave Whelan and Mike Di Scala broke through internationally with the Grammy-nominated Cola, while their catalogue also includes Panic Room with Au/Ra and Breathe with Cristoph and Jem Cooke.Access exclusive to selected 16/360 Grand Prix hospitality ticket holders; packages from Dh1,25038. Gordo: December 5 at Bagatelle, W Abu Dhabi, Abu DhabiDJ and producer Gordo, formerly known as Carnage, joins Bagatelle's race-weekend programme with his house-focused sound. He contributed to Drake's 2022 album Honestly, Nevermind and released his debut album Diamante in 2024, featuring collaborations with Drake and Maluma.Tables from Dh10,00039. The Chainsmokers and The Script: December 6 at Etihad Live, Abu DhabiThe Chainsmokers and The Script will close the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix after-race concert series with separate sets on race day. Irish band The Script are known for songs including Breakeven, The Man Who Can’t Be Moved, For the First Time and Hall of Fame.US electronic duo The Chainsmokers bring a catalogue that includes Roses, Don’t Let Me Down, Closer, Paris and Something Just Like This.Showtime yet to be announced; access exclusive to Abu Dhabi Grand Prix ticket holders40. Black Coffee: December 6 at 16/360, Yas Marina Circuit, Abu DhabiGrammy-winning South African DJ Black Coffee closes the three-night 16/360 programme on race day with his blend of deep house, African percussion and soulful vocals. His album Subconsciously, featuring collaborations with Pharrell Williams and David Guetta, won the Grammy Award for Best Dance/Electronic Music Album.Access exclusive to selected 16/360 Grand Prix hospitality ticket holders; packages from Dh1,25041. Carl Cox: December 6 at Bagatelle, W Abu Dhabi, Abu DhabiBritish DJ Carl Cox closes Bagatelle's Grand Prix weekend programme. A pioneer of Britain's acid-house movement, he has spent more than four decades playing house and techno and held a 15-year residency at Space Ibiza.His links with motorsport extend beyond the weekend through Carl Cox Motorsport, which he founded in 2013.Tables from Dh10,00042. Enrico Macias: December 10 at Dubai OperaMore than six decades of chanson and Mediterranean music feature in Enrico Macias’s latest Dubai concert. The French-Algerian singer is known for Adieu mon pays, Les filles de mon pays and Enfants de tous pays. The concert is reportedly among his final international appearances.Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh29543. Lisa Batiashvili and Giorgi Gigashvili: December 10 at The Arts Centre at NYU Abu DhabiGeorgian musicians Lisa Batiashvili and Giorgi Gigashvili will perform works by Beethoven, Bartok and Franck, alongside a contemporary piece by composer Josef Bardanashvili.Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh15044. Minsoo Sohn: December 11 at The Arts Centre at NYU Abu DhabiPianist Minsoo Sohn will perform Book One of Bach’s Well-Tempered Clavier, presenting the 24 preludes and fugues that explore every major and minor key. The recital highlights both the intellectual depth and emotional breadth of the landmark work.Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh15045. Guy Manoukian: December 11 at Dubai OperaGuy Manoukian marks Dubai Opera's 10th anniversary by returning for his own milestone 10th performance at the venue, following nine sold-out shows.The Lebanese-Armenian pianist and composer blends original work with Arabic melodies and contemporary arrangements, with his repertoire also drawing on the music of Fairouz and Abdel Halim Hafez.Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh33046. Denis Matsuev: December 16 at Dubai OperaRussian pianist Denis Matsuev moves between classical repertoire and jazz in a concert titled Classics and Jazz.Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh35049. Saint Levant is the first announced artist, with the Palestinian-Algerian performer known for blending Arabic, English and French across songs including Very Few Friends and Deira.The remaining artists are yet to be announced.Doors open 4pm daily; tickets from Dh24551. Dhafer Youssef: December 19 at The Arts Centre at NYU Abu DhabiOud maestro Dhafer Youssef will perform with his quintet, bridging sounds from the East and West through jazz, Arab and North African traditions, as well as European classical and electronic elements. He is expected to perform material from his latest album Shiraz, described as his most personal work to date.Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh150 52. Katy Perry: December 31 at Atlantis, The Palm, DubaiKaty Perry returns to the UAE to headline the New Year's Eve gala at Atlantis The Palm, a year after closing the 2025 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix. The American pop star brings a catalogue including Teenage Dream, Roar, Dark Horse and Firework.The black-tie gala also features a 30-piece live band, entertainment throughout the evening and a midnight fireworks display across Atlantis Dubai on Palm Jumeirah.Doors open 7pm; tickets from Dh6,500 for children and Dh8,500 for adults53. Vessbroz: December 31 at Cavo, Ramee Dream Hotel, DubaiVessbroz headline Cavo’s New Year’s Eve party with a set built around electronic house music and Middle East-inspired sounds. The line-up also includes Bazz Key, Qtee Rue, Taina and Hellfox.Doors open 10pm; tickets from Dh150.54. Tony Ann: January 12, 2027, at Dubai OperaCanadian pianist and composer Tony Ann makes his Dubai debut with a programme blending contemporary piano and classical influences. Known for his viral #playthatword series and the Emotionally Blue, Orange and Red EP trilogy, Ann has also co-written The Chainsmokers tracks Sick Boy and Call You Mine.55. Swan Lake on Ice: January 14 to 17, 2027, at Dubai OperaTchaikovsky’s Swan Lake is reimagined on ice by the Imperial Ice Stars, with 24 skaters bringing together figure skating, ballet, aerial movement and theatrical choreography. The production follows the story of Odette, Prince Siegfried and Rothbart, with snowfall, fog, pyrotechnic effects and elaborate costumes adding to the staging.Show times vary by date; auditorium doors open 30 minutes before each performance; tickets from Dh30056. Buena Vista Social Club Legacy Concert: January 24, 2027 at Dubai OperaCuban music takes over Dubai Opera with a concert featuring Ibrahim Ferrer Jr, son of Buena Vista Social Club singer Ibrahim Ferrer, alongside veteran laud player Barbarito TorresBilled as Una Noche En La Habana, the show draws on son, bolero and other Cuban traditions associated with the musicians who brought Buena Vista Social Club to international audiences in the late 1990s.Show time and ticket prices to be announced57. Tamaas Festival: January 29, 2027, at The Arts Centre at NYU Abu DhabiTamaas Festival returns with three acts moving between traditional forms and club-orientated production. Moroccan-Swiss musician Sami Galbi combines rai and chaabi with electronic music, while Nigerien guitarist Bombino performs Tuareg desert blues and rock.British collective Ibibio Sound Machine close the evening with West African rhythms, post-punk, disco and electronic music.Festival starts 7pm; free pass upon registration58. Harry Potter Film Concert Series: February 5 to 6, 2027, at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiThe UAE National Orchestra accompanies two Harry Potter films across consecutive nights. John Williams’ stirring score for Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban is performed on February 5, followed by Patrick Doyle’s music for Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire on February 6.Doors open 6.30pm; shows start 7.30pm; tickets from Dh12059. Ramadaniyat – The Handover: February 17, 2027, at The Arts Centre at NYU Abu DhabiEgyptian oud player Aly Eissa, Alexandrian violinist Ayman Asfour and Belgian-Norwegian keyboard player Jonas Cambien make their UAE debut as The Handover. The trio bring the ritual and folk music of rural Egypt into contact with free improvisation, psychedelic rock and electronic textures.Show starts 9.30pm; tickets from Dh52.5060. The Phantom of the Opera: March 10 to 28, 2027 at Etihad Arena, Abu DhabiAndrew Lloyd Webber's The Phantom of the Opera makes its Abu Dhabi debut with a three-week run at Etihad Arena. Based on Gaston Leroux's novel, the musical follows the masked phantom who lives beneath the Paris Opera House and becomes obsessed with soprano Christine Daae. The score includes The Music of the Night, All I Ask of You and the title song.The Abu Dhabi run comes during the musical's 40th anniversary year, following its West End premiere in 1986.Runs from March 10 to 28; tickets from Dh24061. Unifyd: March 20, 2027 at Etihad Live, Abu DhabiArijit Singh, Karan Aujla and Sonu Nigam lead the inaugural Unifyd music festival curated by Bollywood star Shah Rukh Khan. The one-day event will feature more than 15 artists across several stages, spanning Hindi film music, Punjabi music and other strands of Indian culture.General sale opens October 20 at 10.30am through the District app; ticket prices to be announced62. Tribute to Ziad Rahbani by Faraj Suleiman: March 26, 2027, at The Arts Centre at NYU Abu DhabiPalestinian composer and pianist Faraj Suleiman returns with a programme dedicated to Lebanese composer, pianist and playwright Ziad Rahbani. Rather than reproducing the original recordings, Suleiman re-orchestrates and re-harmonises the material through contemporary piano, jazz and Arabic composition.Show starts 7.30pm; tickets from Dh78.7563. A1 and Music Travel Love: April 17, 2027, at Coca-Cola Arena, DubaiBritish-Norwegian pop group A1 and Canadian duo Music Travel Love will share the stage for the first time in Dubai. A1 are known for hits including Everytime, Caught in the Middle and Like a Rose, while Music Travel Love, formed by twin brothers Bob and Clint Moffatt, are known for acoustic covers and originals including Nothing’s Gonna Change my Love for You.Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh29564. Richard Marx: June 6, 2027 at Coca-Cola Arena, DubaiAmerican singer-songwriter Richard Marx comes to Dubai with a catalogue spanning more than four decades. His best-known songs include Right Here Waiting, Hazard, Hold On to the Nights and Satisfied, while his song-writing credits include hits recorded by artists such as Luther Vandross, Keith Urban and NSYNC.Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh225

The title takes inspiration from Moroccan group Nass El Ghiwane and draws parallels between their search for identity and the origins of hip-hop.

Riverdance returns to the UAE with a production marking the Irish dance show’s 30th anniversary. The staging retains Bill Whelan’s Grammy Award-winning score while introducing updated choreography, costumes, lighting, projection and motion graphics.

Performance times vary; tickets from Dh215

British singer, pianist and composer Benjamin Clementine performs a programme combining experimental pop, contemporary classical music, jazz and poetry. His debut album, At Least for Now, won the Mercury Prize, while later recordings include I Tell a Fly and And I Have Been.

Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh500

Russian-Azerbaijani singer Jony is a star Russian pop and built a following with songs including Kamin, Kometa and Ty Besposhchadna.

Show starts 9pm; tickets from Dh295

Palestinian-American comedian Mo Amer performs as part of Abu Dhabi Comedy Season. Born in Kuwait to Palestinian parents and raised in the US, his comedy draws on displacement, immigration and life between cultures.

Those experiences also shaped Mo, the semi-autobiographical Netflix series he created with Ramy Youssef, which won a Peabody Award in 2023.

Show time and ticket prices to be announced

Iranian-American comedian Maz Jobrani returns to Abu Dhabi with material exploring immigrant experiences, cultural misunderstandings and family expectations. He previously performed at the inaugural Abu Dhabi Comedy Week in 2024 on a shared bill with Bassem Youssef.

Show time and ticket prices to be announced

Club anthems are given an orchestral spin as Ministry of Sound Classical brings dance music into the concert hall.

Conducted by David Mahoney, the show combines a full orchestra and vocalists with electronic music, lighting and visuals, drawing on tracks associated with decades of club culture.

Show time and ticket prices to be announced

Dubbed one of the world's greatest dance companies, the American Ballet Theatre will perform works including Frederick Ashton’s Birthday Offering, Jiri Kylian’s Nuages, Brady Farrar’s Trio Elegiaque and Paquita, staged by Natalia Makarova after Marius Petipa.

Show starts 8pm, tickets from Dh125

American comedian Aries Spears brings more than three decades of stand-up, impressions and crowd work to Etihad Arena. A former Mad TV cast member, he is known for his celebrity impersonations that include Michael Jackson, Eddie Murphy and Shaquille O'Neal.

Doors open 9pm; show starts 10pm; tickets from Dh120

Synthony makes its Middle East debut with a full orchestra reworking electronic dance anthems through live instrumentation, vocals and visual production. The night will also feature Faithless Sound System, led by Sister Bliss, with tracks including Insomnia and We Come 1.

Doors open 6pm; tickets from Dh295

Trevor Noah brings a new stand-up show to Dubai across four nights. The Emmy Award-winning South African comedian and former host of The Daily Show has released several Netflix specials, hosts the podcast What Now? with Trevor Noah and is the author of Born a Crime and Into the Uncut Grass.

Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh295

Algarabia presents a theatrical production blending flamenco with Arabic poetry, performed by musicians from Spain’s University of Navarra Symphony Orchestra alongside dancers and actors. The work follows the journey of an Arab girl drawn to ancient botanical theory and poetic tradition.

Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh100

Hiba Tawaji and Ibrahim Maalouf will unite for a one-night performance at Dubai Opera, with the programme drawing on French musical heritage through a blend of chanson, jazz and contemporary composition.

Tawaji’s emotive vocals and Maalouf’s genre-crossing trumpet work make this one of the more distinctive concert pairings on the calendar.

Show starts 8.30pm; tickets from Dh355

Atif Aslam returns to Coca-Cola Arena after five consecutive years of sold-out Dubai concerts. The Pakistani singer’s programme will move between Bollywood songs, pop-rock and devotional music, with hits including Tajdar-e-Haram, Jeena Jeena, Pehli Nazar Mein, Dil Diyan Gallan and Aadat.

Doors open 9pm; tickets from Dh350

Known internationally for the global hit Simarik and a catalogue that has defined Turkish pop for more than two decades, Tarkan is making his Abu Dhabi debut is further proof of Turkish’s pop growing popularity in the region.

Show starts 8.30pm; tickets from Dh295

Lebanese composer and oud player Marcel Khalife headlines the return of Wasla Festival, alongside Palestinian ensemble Le Trio Joubran, Syrian duo TootArd and British-Sudanese singer Fatima.

Starts 6pm; tickets from Dh350

Egyptian singer Ramy Sabry comes to Abu Dhabi with a catalogue of romantic Arabic pop and ballads. His songs include Lama Bywhashny, alongside a wider repertoire centred on love, memory and heartbreak.

Doors open 7.30pm; show starts 9pm; tickets from Dh295

Ukrainian electronic duo Artbat bring their Upperground event series to Dubai, joined by Miss Monique, R3hab and Italian DJ and producer 7 Skies. The show follows Artbat’s recent reworking of Gotye's Somebody That I Used to Know with David Guetta.

Doors open 8pm; tickets from Dh150

Marking 125 years since Giuseppe Verdi’s death, this programme is led by soprano Maria Agresta and tenor Giorgio Berrugi, and includes selections from Nabucco, I Vespri Siciliani, Otello and La Traviata, alongside overtures and duets drawn from Verdi’s wider catalogue.

Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh125

Italian tenor Andrea Bocelli brings his 30th Anniversary Romanza World Tour to Abu Dhabi as part of Yasalam Classics. The concert celebrates Romanza, the album that helped establish him internationally and includes songs such as Con te partiro and Vivo per lei.

Doors open 6pm; tickets from Dh295

The Bolshoi Theatre begins its first official UAE tour with Rimsky-Korsakov's The Tsar's Bride.

Set during the reign of Ivan the Terrible, the opera centres on Marfa, a young woman whose selection as the tsar's bride sets off jealousy, rivalry and political intrigue.

Show time and ticket prices to be announced

The Bolshoi Theatre Orchestra takes centre stage for a symphonic concert on the second night of the company’s first official UAE tour.

Showtime and ticket prices TBC

Lewis Capaldi and Zara Larsson will open the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix 2026 after-race concert series with separate sets at Etihad Park.

Capaldi returns to the capital following his Saadiyat Nights performance in January, bringing a catalogue that includes Someone You Loved, Before You Go and Forget Me. Larsson joins the bill with pop staples such as Lush Life, Never Forget You and Symphony, offering a high-tempo contrast to Capaldi’s ballad-driven set. The show launches the four-night programme running alongside the race weekend at Yas Marina Circuit.

Showtime yet to be announced; access exclusive to Abu Dhabi Grand Prix ticket holders

South African DJ Shimza brings his percussion-heavy Afro-tech sound to 16/360 as Abu Dhabi Grand Prix weekend gets under way. Known for extended, hypnotic sets, he has performed across Europe and Africa and collaborated with fellow South African DJ Black Coffee.

Access exclusive to selected 16/360 Grand Prix hospitality ticket holders; packages from Dh1,250

Swiss duo Mont Rouge and French DJ Moojo share the Friday bill at Bagatelle's rooftop pop-up during Abu Dhabi Grand Prix weekend. Mont Rouge are known for their Afro-house version of Voyage Voyage, recorded with Francis Mercier and Coco, as well as their remix of Axwell and Sebastian Ingrosso's More Than You Know.

The Nutcracker has become a Dubai Opera tradition, and this year's production will feature the Bolshoi Theatre, with Tchaikovsky's ballet performed by the company's dancers and orchestra.

Yuri Grigorovich's choreography follows Marie from a family Christmas celebration into a fantasy world of toys and magic, set to a score containing some of Tchaikovsky's best-known music.

Show times and ticket prices to be announced

Italian-American DJ and producer Anyma will perform at Yas Gateway Park as part of the official Abu Dhabi Grand Prix after party concert series. Known for large-scale audiovisual shows and melodic techno, he brought his dazzling live production to the Pyramids of Giza in 2025 and has become one of electronic music’s most distinctive live acts through his work as a solo artist and as one half of Tale of Us.

Abu Dhabi Grand Prix ticket holder pre-sales begin on September 10, with general sales opening on September 11; show time and ticket prices to be announced

Imagine Dragons will headline the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix after-race concert series on Saturday night. Fronted by Dan Reynolds, the US band are known for songs including Believer, Radioactive, Demons, Thunder and It’s Time.

The group last performed in Abu Dhabi in 2023, when they sold out Etihad Arena.

Showtime yet to be announced; access exclusive to Abu Dhabi Grand Prix ticket holders

British electronic duo CamelPhat take over the trackside 16/360 venue on the second night of its Grand Prix programme. Dave Whelan and Mike Di Scala broke through internationally with the Grammy-nominated Cola, while their catalogue also includes Panic Room with Au/Ra and Breathe with Cristoph and Jem Cooke.

Access exclusive to selected 16/360 Grand Prix hospitality ticket holders; packages from Dh1,250

DJ and producer Gordo, formerly known as Carnage, joins Bagatelle's race-weekend programme with his house-focused sound. He contributed to Drake's 2022 album Honestly, Nevermind and released his debut album Diamante in 2024, featuring collaborations with Drake and Maluma.

The Chainsmokers and The Script will close the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix after-race concert series with separate sets on race day. Irish band The Script are known for songs including Breakeven, The Man Who Can’t Be Moved, For the First Time and Hall of Fame.

US electronic duo The Chainsmokers bring a catalogue that includes Roses, Don’t Let Me Down, Closer, Paris and Something Just Like This.

Showtime yet to be announced; access exclusive to Abu Dhabi Grand Prix ticket holders

Grammy-winning South African DJ Black Coffee closes the three-night 16/360 programme on race day with his blend of deep house, African percussion and soulful vocals. His album Subconsciously, featuring collaborations with Pharrell Williams and David Guetta, won the Grammy Award for Best Dance/Electronic Music Album.

Access exclusive to selected 16/360 Grand Prix hospitality ticket holders; packages from Dh1,250

British DJ Carl Cox closes Bagatelle's Grand Prix weekend programme. A pioneer of Britain's acid-house movement, he has spent more than four decades playing house and techno and held a 15-year residency at Space Ibiza.

His links with motorsport extend beyond the weekend through Carl Cox Motorsport, which he founded in 2013.

More than six decades of chanson and Mediterranean music feature in Enrico Macias’s latest Dubai concert. The French-Algerian singer is known for Adieu mon pays, Les filles de mon pays and Enfants de tous pays. The concert is reportedly among his final international appearances.

Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh295

Georgian musicians Lisa Batiashvili and Giorgi Gigashvili will perform works by Beethoven, Bartok and Franck, alongside a contemporary piece by composer Josef Bardanashvili.

Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh150

Pianist Minsoo Sohn will perform Book One of Bach’s Well-Tempered Clavier, presenting the 24 preludes and fugues that explore every major and minor key. The recital highlights both the intellectual depth and emotional breadth of the landmark work.

Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh150

Guy Manoukian marks Dubai Opera's 10th anniversary by returning for his own milestone 10th performance at the venue, following nine sold-out shows.

The Lebanese-Armenian pianist and composer blends original work with Arabic melodies and contemporary arrangements, with his repertoire also drawing on the music of Fairouz and Abdel Halim Hafez.

Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh330

Mariah Carey returns to Abu Dhabi with her Christmastime show, featuring festive songs including All I Want for Christmas Is You, Santa Baby and Christmas (Baby Please Come Home) alongside hits from her wider catalogue.

The concert will be her second Abu Dhabi performance of the year, following her Saadiyat Nights show in February.

Doors open 7pm; tickets from Dh249

The Broadway production of Chicago comes to Coca-Cola Arena for eight performances over five days. Set during the Jazz Age, the musical follows nightclub performer Roxie Hart and vaudeville star Velma Kelly as they compete for public attention while awaiting trial for murder.

The score includes All That Jazz, Cell Block Tango and Razzle Dazzle.

Performance times vary; tickets from Dh49

Russian pianist Denis Matsuev moves between classical repertoire and jazz in a concert titled Classics and Jazz.

Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh350

Gulf theatre comes to Dubai Opera with Abracadabra, an Arabic language suspense comedy about two struggling theatre groups trying to save their careers. Their plan to stage a new show inside an abandoned theatre is disrupted by strange events, unexpected twists and a series of comic situations.

The production runs for about an hour and blends Gulf theatre, suspense and entertainment.

Show times vary; tickets from Dh230.

Dopa World is a three-day festival focused on young Arab music, culture and creative businesses. Saint Levant is the first announced artist, with the Palestinian-Algerian performer known for blending Arabic, English and French across songs including Very Few Friends and Deira.

The remaining artists are yet to be announced.

Doors open 4pm daily; tickets from Dh245

Oud maestro Dhafer Youssef will perform with his quintet, bridging sounds from the East and West through jazz, Arab and North African traditions, as well as European classical and electronic elements. He is expected to perform material from his latest album Shiraz, described as his most personal work to date.

Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh150

Katy Perry returns to the UAE to headline the New Year's Eve gala at Atlantis The Palm, a year after closing the 2025 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix. The American pop star brings a catalogue including Teenage Dream, Roar, Dark Horse and Firework.

The black-tie gala also features a 30-piece live band, entertainment throughout the evening and a midnight fireworks display across Atlantis Dubai on Palm Jumeirah.

Doors open 7pm; tickets from Dh6,500 for children and Dh8,500 for adults

Vessbroz headline Cavo’s New Year’s Eve party with a set built around electronic house music and Middle East-inspired sounds. The line-up also includes Bazz Key, Qtee Rue, Taina and Hellfox.

Doors open 10pm; tickets from Dh150.

Canadian pianist and composer Tony Ann makes his Dubai debut with a programme blending contemporary piano and classical influences. Known for his viral #playthatword series and the Emotionally Blue, Orange and Red EP trilogy, Ann has also co-written The Chainsmokers tracks Sick Boy and Call You Mine.

Tchaikovsky’s Swan Lake is reimagined on ice by the Imperial Ice Stars, with 24 skaters bringing together figure skating, ballet, aerial movement and theatrical choreography. The production follows the story of Odette, Prince Siegfried and Rothbart, with snowfall, fog, pyrotechnic effects and elaborate costumes adding to the staging.

Show times vary by date; auditorium doors open 30 minutes before each performance; tickets from Dh300

Cuban music takes over Dubai Opera with a concert featuring Ibrahim Ferrer Jr, son of Buena Vista Social Club singer Ibrahim Ferrer, alongside veteran laud player Barbarito Torres

Billed as Una Noche En La Habana, the show draws on son, bolero and other Cuban traditions associated with the musicians who brought Buena Vista Social Club to international audiences in the late 1990s.

Show time and ticket prices to be announced

Tamaas Festival returns with three acts moving between traditional forms and club-orientated production. Moroccan-Swiss musician Sami Galbi combines rai and chaabi with electronic music, while Nigerien guitarist Bombino performs Tuareg desert blues and rock.

British collective Ibibio Sound Machine close the evening with West African rhythms, post-punk, disco and electronic music.

Festival starts 7pm; free pass upon registration

The UAE National Orchestra accompanies two Harry Potter films across consecutive nights. John Williams’ stirring score for Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban is performed on February 5, followed by Patrick Doyle’s music for Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire on February 6.

Doors open 6.30pm; shows start 7.30pm; tickets from Dh120

Egyptian oud player Aly Eissa, Alexandrian violinist Ayman Asfour and Belgian-Norwegian keyboard player Jonas Cambien make their UAE debut as The Handover. The trio bring the ritual and folk music of rural Egypt into contact with free improvisation, psychedelic rock and electronic textures.

Show starts 9.30pm; tickets from Dh52.50

Andrew Lloyd Webber's The Phantom of the Opera makes its Abu Dhabi debut with a three-week run at Etihad Arena. Based on Gaston Leroux's novel, the musical follows the masked phantom who lives beneath the Paris Opera House and becomes obsessed with soprano Christine Daae. The score includes The Music of the Night, All I Ask of You and the title song.

The Abu Dhabi run comes during the musical's 40th anniversary year, following its West End premiere in 1986.

Runs from March 10 to 28; tickets from Dh240

Arijit Singh, Karan Aujla and Sonu Nigam lead the inaugural Unifyd music festival curated by Bollywood star Shah Rukh Khan. The one-day event will feature more than 15 artists across several stages, spanning Hindi film music, Punjabi music and other strands of Indian culture.

General sale opens October 20 at 10.30am through the District app; ticket prices to be announced

Palestinian composer and pianist Faraj Suleiman returns with a programme dedicated to Lebanese composer, pianist and playwright Ziad Rahbani. Rather than reproducing the original recordings, Suleiman re-orchestrates and re-harmonises the material through contemporary piano, jazz and Arabic composition.

Show starts 7.30pm; tickets from Dh78.75

British-Norwegian pop group A1 and Canadian duo Music Travel Love will share the stage for the first time in Dubai. A1 are known for hits including Everytime, Caught in the Middle and Like a Rose, while Music Travel Love, formed by twin brothers Bob and Clint Moffatt, are known for acoustic covers and originals including Nothing’s Gonna Change my Love for You.

Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh295

American singer-songwriter Richard Marx comes to Dubai with a catalogue spanning more than four decades. His best-known songs include Right Here Waiting, Hazard, Hold On to the Nights and Satisfied, while his song-writing credits include hits recorded by artists such as Luther Vandross, Keith Urban and NSYNC.

Show starts 8pm; tickets from Dh225

headline: Trade turnover between Georgia, Russia up 16% in three quarters
summary: With Russia being Georgia’s third-biggest trading partner, its share in the republic’s total external trade volume equaled 10.8% in the reporting period
body_text:
TBILISI, October 19. /TASS/. Trade turnover between Georgia and Russia amounted to over $2.2 bln in January-September 2026, which is 16% higher than in the same period last year, according to data released by the National Statistics Service of Georgia.

With Russia being Georgia’s third-biggest trading partner, its share in the republic’s total external trade volume equaled 10.8% in the reporting period. Georgian exports to Russia amounted to more than $560 mln (up by 3% in annual terms) in three quarters of this year, while imports reached over $1.6 bln (up by 21%).

Turkey was Georgia’s biggest trading partner in the period, with mutual trade turnover standing at around $2.6 bln (up by 12% compared with the same period in 2025). China ranked second, with trade turnover amounting to more than $2.3 bln (up by 41%). Among Georgia’s biggest trading partners were also the US (around $1.9 bln), and Azerbaijan (over $1.1 bln).

A growing divide is visible everywhere: in households, in businesses and even in consumer habits. Our correspondents Serge Berberi and Renée Davis report.

headline: Qatar and Singapore strengthen energy ties as PM Wong visits Doha
summary: Qatar and Singapore have agreed to renew an energy cooperation memorandum of understanding, as the two countries seek to deepen ties in investment, energy security and technology during Singaporean Prime…
body_text:
Qatar and Singapore have agreed to renew an energy cooperation memorandum of understanding, as the two countries seek to deepen ties in investment, energy security and technology during Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong’s official visit to Doha.

Qatar’s Amir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani and Singapore’s Prime Minister and Minister for Finance Lawrence Wong held official talks at the Amiri Diwan on Monday, discussing ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation, particularly in the economic and investment sectors.

Wong is visiting Qatar from 18 to 20 October, marking his first official visit to the Middle East as prime minister.

Sheikh Tamim welcomed Wong and his accompanying delegation, expressing hope that the visit would strengthen the partnership between Qatar and Singapore and expand cooperation in ways that serve the interests of both countries.

Wong thanked the Amir for the warm welcome and hospitality, expressing his desire to elevate relations between the two countries.

The talks covered bilateral relations and opportunities to expand cooperation across various fields, as well as regional and international developments of mutual interest. The two leaders also held a separate meeting to exchange views on current developments.

Wong also met Qatar’s Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, to discuss strengthening cooperation in energy security, supply chain resilience, artificial intelligence, and digitalisation.

In a post on X following the meeting, Wong said the discussions covered ways to deepen the partnership, including strengthening energy security and supply chain resilience, as well as exploring new opportunities in areas such as artificial intelligence (AI) and digitalisation.

Wong also expressed appreciation for Qatar’s role in facilitating dialogue and efforts to ease tensions in the Middle East, emphasizing the importance of continued diplomacy to promote regional peace and stability.

Qatar and Singapore renew energy cooperation MoU

Sheikh Tamim and Wong witnessed the signing of the minutes of the ninth Qatar-Singapore High-Level Joint Committee meeting and the exchange of documents announcing the renewal of a memorandum of understanding between QatarEnergy and Singapore’s Ministry of Trade and Industry on liquefied natural gas (LNG) and cooperation in carbon reduction technology.

The renewed MoU reflects the two countries’ continued energy cooperation and their interest in exploring collaboration on carbon reduction technology.

The meeting was attended by Qatar’s Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, Chief of the Amiri Diwan Abdullah bin Mohammed Al Khulaifi, and several other ministers.

Singapore’s delegation included Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan, Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Home Affairs Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim, and other senior officials.

Sheikh Tamim later hosted a luncheon in honour of Wong and his delegation.

Wong visits Qatar Foundation and National Museum of Qatar

During his visit, Wong was also welcomed to Education City by Qatar Foundation Vice Chairperson Sheikha Hind bint Hamad Al Thani.

The delegation was introduced to Qatar Foundation’s ecosystem and its works in education, research, and community development. Sheikha Hind and Wong also discussed approaches to digital technology that promote safety and balance.

Wong also visited the National Museum of Qatar, accompanied by Sheikh Thani bin Hamad Al Thani, where he explored collections documenting Qatar’s geological development, natural environments, archaeological sites and petroglyphs, as well as the lives of Qataris on land and along the coast.

The tour included a digital exhibition, displays of pearls and jewellery design, and galleries tracing Qatar’s modern history following the discovery of oil and gas.

body_text:
For a demonstration of just how badly Britain is blighted by bottlenecks, the loss of a flagship Microsoft data centre deal is Exhibit A.

Just north of London is a piece of waste ground covered with broken concrete. The site, at Loughton in Essex, had been designated as the UK’s flagship entry point into the global data-centre race. Instead, last week it was at the forefront of the markets’ collapsing confidence that the worldwide data-centre boom can ever be delivered.

That market reticence should not let the UK off the hook. There is a particular regulatory and leadership failure in the country that serves as a warning for other nations overly dedicated to a regulatory economy.

When US President Donald Trump made his state visit to the UK just over a year ago, Microsoft announced a $30 billion (Dh110 billion) commitment to the country. Of that, $2 billion was allotted to this patch of London’s suburban fringe for a data centre. A Microsoft blog post read: “This investment will enable us to build the country’s largest supercomputer – with more than 23,000 Nvidia GPUs – in partnership with Nscale.” The good vibes kept on coming with Jensen Huang, the Nvidia boss, saying the UK would be an “AI superpower” with all this investment in the pipeline.

What went wrong was that the failures in the UK’s national electricity grid have come home to roost. Instead of connecting to the electric network next year as had been billed in Nscale’s contracts, now the facility will not have a connection date until the 2030s. Nscale has quietly accepted the blow with a sigh of futility. "This unfortunate London-wide grid issue has no impact on our other contracts," it said. The British technology company’s other projects are in alternative locations outside the UK, such as Norway, Portugal and the US.

The growth blight for the UK as a result of the decline in its electric architecture is only just beginning. The country has the most expensive electricity of any major nation. Large-scale industrial operations based around petrochemicals or refining of oil into products such as diesel have steadily shut down across the country. In the 1980s when the coal mines were shutting down, their names would be tagged in labels across large banners that followed the colliery bands. Now the loss of names such as Grangemouth, which made two thirds of all the refined oil products used by Scotland, are briefly noted inside newspapers.

The idea of Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s government is that the UK can re-industrialise. Contrary to expectations, the country had until recent years done a decent job of maintaining a network of facilities that were supplying its own and export markets. This is now stuck in a vortex of decline that largely centres around the National Grid and its projected shortages. The data centre boom is catching it out in new ways.

The UK has been a trailblazer in harnessing wind from offshore turbines that have been constructed in massive arrays. Yet even this generation is not being exploited in the ways that it could. The National Grid has failed to match its capacity to transmit the energy into its systems. In fact, Britain spends more than £1.5 billion (Dh7.34 billion) a year on “constraint payments” to turn off wind farms and use gas plant generation instead because the electricity grid could become unbalanced.

That is not all. Note the Nscale statement said there was a London-wide problem with the grid. The gas plants have clustered in the middle of the country and so getting their output to the country’s largest economy – London – is problematic.

The country is also being forced to make payments to obtain emergency supplies through interconnectors from foreign nations at an increasing rate. Last week an emergency drawn down from France is believed to have cost almost £40 million alone. The figure for all of September for “balancing payments” ran to £500 million.

This time of year, European countries that use a lot of wind power are often confronted by a lack of wind. Worryingly for the UK, this year there has been good wind availability, yet the country is still facing increasing and steep payments to keep its electric network functioning. That is while charging vast sums for its output to customers. It is also unable to deliver an architecture of future capacity growth that meets the needs of flagship investors.

All the while planners in other parts of the system worry that the UK has failed, like Germany, to upgrade its storage of imported natural gas, a commodity undergoing a supply crunch because of the Iran war and the arrival of El Nino. The figures show that the underground gas storage available to the UK energy suppliers was only 48 per cent full at the start of October, the lowest among its neighbours.

With the rise of the digital economy and the data boom, one would expect electricity to be the greatest priority in the UK’s economic management. Allow me to let you down with some figures.

The National Energy System Operator, which draws that interconnector power to balance the system, says that electricity should represent 70 per cent of the UK’s power mix by 2050. Last year it was just a shade under 20 per cent, with 25 years to go to the deadline.. Last year it was just a shade under 20 per cent, with 25 years ago. Go back 25 years to the year 2000 and the electric part of the power mix was also hovering at 20 per cent.

In a world of rapid advances, the UK is effectively running too hard just to stand still.

headline: NATO air defenses require modern capabilities — general
summary: Lieutenant General Guillaume Thomas emphasized that the challenge is not only technological but also industrial
body_text:
BRUSSELS, October 19. /TASS/. NATO has "quietly shifted" from air policing missions in the Baltic states, Benelux, the Balkans, and Iceland to "a unified 360-degree air defense system," which, however, lacks the necessary capabilities, first and foremost the actual means of detecting and intercepting aerial targets, Deputy Commander of NATO Allied Air Command Lieutenant General Guillaume Thomas said in an interview with the Brussels-based portal Rapporteur.

According to him, since last fall, NATO has been conducting a "single mission that is able to cover a 360-degree approach." He explained that this mission has brought together the disparate "air policing" (air patrol) missions in various NATO regions and the system for countering drones and missiles, placing them under a single command.

However, according to Thomas, apart from the change in the command structure, NATO’s new air defense mission has not received additional military resources or staff capabilities to improve coordination among the various air defense components.

Therefore, Thomas acknowledged that NATO’s air defense is lacking in everything: "We need modern tools for our command and control system. We also need sensors and a high-low mix of effectors for this 360 approach, which is a big, big challenge," Thomas said.

The general emphasized that the challenge is not only technological but also industrial, and called on NATO countries to invest in, develop, and produce more air defense systems.

headline: Explainer-What's behind Egypt's move towards possible military involvement in Saudi-Yemen conflict?
summary: CAIRO, Oct 19 (Reuters) - Egypt's parliament is expected to vote this week on whether toauthorise the armed forces to help defend Saudi Arabia against attacks by Yemen'sHouthis if Riyadh requests its support.The move would bring the Arab world's most populous country closer to direct military involvement in the widening conflicts unleashed by the US-Israeli air assault on Iran in February.
body_text:
CAIRO, Oct 19 (Reuters) - Egypt's parliament is expected to vote this week on whether toauthorise the armed forces to help defend Saudi Arabia against attacks by Yemen'sHouthis if Riyadh requests its support.

The move would bring the Arab world's most populous country closer to direct military involvement in the widening conflicts unleashed by the US-Israeli air assault on Iran in February.

PresidentAbdel Fattah al-Sisi requested the approval in a speech on Saturday, saying Egypt would "never, never forget our brothers in the Gulf" and telling Saudi Arabia's leaders that Cairo would "take any measure to protect you".

Like the Gulf states that have come under attack from Tehran in the Iran war, Egypt is a longstanding partner in the US-led security order that is being tested by the conflict.

WHAT IS EGYPT'S STANCE ON THE IRAN WAR?

Sisi's comments marked a clear escalation from the more measured tone authorities have tended to adopt since the Iran war started. Though Egypt has repeatedly voiced strong support for its Gulf allies, Cairo has stopped short of publicly committing itself to a direct combat role in the conflict.

In May, the presence of EgyptianRafale fighter jets in the United Arab Emirates was disclosed in Emirati state media coverage ofan official visit by Sisi. Egyptian coverage of the visit did not mention the deployment. When Saudi Arabia signed a joint defence agreement with Turkey and Pakistan in August, Egypt did not join, though it said it was considering it.

The tone started to shift after the Houthis stepped up attacks on Saudi oil and other infrastructure. Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman last month visited Egypt, where he discussed the need to ensure freedom and security of navigation in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and the Red Sea, on which both countries have long coastlines.

WHAT'S AT STAKE FOR EGYPT?

Egypt's economic stability has long been tied up with the oil-producing Gulf. Remittances from Egyptian expatriate workers there are an important source of foreign currency and income for families back home at a time of double-digit inflation worsened by surging food and fuel prices.

Saudi Arabia, the UAE and other Gulf countries have been amongSisi's key financial backers, providing tens of billions of dollars of aid, central bank deposits and investments since the army overthrew President Mohamed Morsi, a senior Muslim Brotherhood figure, in 2013.

"We can never forget how our brothers in the Gulf states stood by Egypt during that period," Sisi said in his speech.

Growing security concerns have also pushed Cairo towards a more active stance, analysts say. A drone strike on two gas vessels at the Mediterranean port city ofDamietta in July underscored that Egypt could not expect to keep itself fully isolated from the conflict.

"I think they realise that they can't be on the sidelines about this indefinitely," said H. A. Hellyer, a scholar at the Royal United Services Institute think tank.

For the authorities, the economic and security concerns were "one and the same," he said.

Saudi Arabia and Egypt also have a shared interest in securing shipping through the Red Sea, an outlet for Saudi oil blocked from leaving the Strait of Hormuz. Egypt earns billions of dollars a year from fees on Suez Canal traffic.These overlapping concerns mean "Saudi Arabia's security constitutes a dimension of Egyptian national security," saidSherif Aref, an Egyptian political researcher and journalist.

WHAT SORT OF MILITARY DOES EGYPT BRING TO THE TABLE?

Egypt has one of the Arab world's largest armed forces, with hundreds of thousands of active personnel and large air, land and naval inventories, according to military analysts. Egypt sources equipment from a range of countries, and its air force operates US-made F-16s, French Rafales and Russian-made MiG-29s.

Egypt receives about $1.3 billion a year in USmilitary aid, which helps fund its purchases of American military equipment. Washingtonwaived human rights conditions on a tranche of the funds this year after what it called Cairo's "helpful role" since the Iran war began.

In the years after the 2011 uprising that ousted President Hosni Mubarak, the armed forces fought a counterinsurgency campaign against Islamist militants in the Sinai Peninsula. Egypt also contributed air and naval forces to the Saudi-led coalition that intervened in Yemen in 2015, and conducted airstrikes against Islamic State targets in Libya during that country’s civil war.

Egypt has not undertaken a large-scale foreign ground deployment since the 1991 Gulf War, when its troops joined the US-led coalition to drive Iraqi forces from Kuwait. Nearly three decades earlier, President Gamal Abdel Nasser had sent Egyptian forces into Yemen in a costly intervention later compared to the US involvement in the Vietnam War.

WHAT SORT OF SUPPORT IS LIKELY?

Sisi's speech and subsequent statements have not specified what sort of military forces, if any, Egypt would ultimately intend to send. A deployment of Egyptian troops inside Yemen itself is unlikely, military analysts say.

More likely interventions might include air defence and naval support, said Samir Ragheb, a retired Egyptian military officer who heads the Arab Foundation for Development and Strategic Studies think tank.

"The threats, missiles and drones, require air defence and air forces," he said, adding that the navy could be used for protecting ships, naval operations against piracy and protecting the Saudi coastline.

(Reporting by Alexander Dziadosz, Dina Sakr and Mariam Rizk; Writing by Alexander Dziadosz; Editing by Timothy Heritage)
