headline: Saudi airport closure disrupts life in kingdom's capital
summary: The prolonged closure of Riyadh's airport after a series of fatal attacks has exposed the risks confronting Saudi Arabia's drive to shift its international image, disrupting businesses, airlines and residents more than a week after flights were grounded. Deadly strikes by Yemen's Houthis in recent weeks have dealt a blow to the kingdom, forcing the airport to close until further notice and a slate of events to be postponed or cancelled including its flagship investment forum dubbed "Davos in the desert".
body_text:
The prolonged closure of Riyadh's airport after a series of fatal attacks has exposed the risks confronting Saudi Arabia's drive to shift its international image, disrupting businesses, airlines and residents more than a week after flights were grounded.

Deadly strikes by Yemen's Houthis in recent weeks have dealt a blow to the kingdom, forcing the airport to close until further notice and a slate of events to be postponed or cancelled including its flagship investment forum dubbed "Davos in the desert".

Government agencies in the Saudi capital have also told employees to work from home starting Monday, one worker and two consultants told AFP, as has the 99-storey Kingdom Centre skyscraper in downtown Riyadh housing the regional office of the International Monetary Fund.

"When people start throwing missiles directly at Riyadh airport and any other airport, you can't just continue to operate," said Captain Desmond Ross, an aviation expert based in Dubai and Ireland with decades of experience as a pilot and air traffic controller.

"An attack on an airport is something entirely different from a non-aviation target," he told AFP.

"I think Riyadh has suffered that more dramatically than any other of the Gulf nations or the Arab nations," during the ongoing Middle East war.

Last week, the Saudi-led coalition accused the Houthis of attacking Riyadh's airport 20 times in October alone.

"The Houthis must immediately cease all terrorist operations," said coalition spokesman Turki Al-Malki.

Saudi Arabia has faced Houthi barrages targeting its airports and energy infrastructure in recent weeks, after fighting between the kingdom and the Iran-backed rebels sharply escalated.

The Houthis have remained unrepentant and continued to issue warnings about flying in Saudi airspace.

Saudi officials did not respond to questions from AFP about a possible timeline for the airport's reopening.

According to a regional airline source, their carrier was told by Saudi authorities on Friday the airport would remain closed until further notice, with no further details provided.

A second source from another regional carrier said the airline had been told the airport would remain closed at least until October 24.

With the airport shuttered, Saudi Arabia has been forced to cancel or postpone high-profile events, including a star-studded tennis tournament.

The move came amid other announcements concerning MDLBEAST Soundstorm music festival, Riyadh fashion week and the Red Sea Film Festival.

The kingdom's flagship investment forum the Future Investment Initiative (FII) was also postponed until 2027 on Monday.

It deals another blow to the kingdom's ambitious economic transformation drive.

For nearly a decade, the conference has been a showcase for Saudi Arabia's push to attract global investors, business leaders and heads of state -- and to sell its vision of an economy less dependent on oil.

"Few want to visit a country under persistent deadly missile attacks. And even fewer want to invest in one," wrote Karen Elliott House, author of a recent book about the crown prince, in a Wall Street Journal op-ed.

Domestic airlines have scrambled to find alternative routes for the capital's seven million residents, with recent targeted advertisements highlighting flights from Qassim airport three hours from Riyadh.

Others have bused to airports in Bahrain and Qatar to both exit and enter the kingdom.

A Dubai-based consultant said that "no employee is forced to travel to Saudi Arabia" but if a client relationship was at risk they were "encouraged to make the trip by car via Bahrain".

One Riyadh resident described being re-routed mid-flight during an attack on the airport.

"We decided to land in Jeddah," said the resident on the condition of anonymity. "From Jeddah, thank God, everything worked out, and we were able to catch a flight to Qassim."

With many offices moving to remote work, expatriates in Riyadh who frequently travelled to their home countries on weekends are still weighing their options.

"I can cope with this situation for a month or more, but I cannot imagine it lasting much longer than that," said a resident, who flew home to a Middle Eastern country often before the closure.

Western embassies have also tightened travel advisories, with some warning against travelling to the kingdom.

The moves, and the chatter among expatriates about possibly leaving Saudi Arabia, have stirred resentment among some Saudis who feel well-heeled foreigners have not stuck by their side.

Saudi ministers have instead sought to reassure residents and investors.

As text messages warning of an attack on the capital were sent last week, Human Resources Minister Ahmad bin Sulaiman Al Rajhi looked up from his phone at the Riyadh Economic Forum.

headline: Russia’s BRICS envoy advances Suez Canal industrial zone in talks with Egyptian President
summary: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi and Minister of Foreign Affairs Badr Abdelatty held talks in Cairo on Monday with Maxim Oreshkin, Russia’s Deputy Chief of Staff of the Presidential Executive Office and Special Representative for BRICS Financial and Economic Cooperation, to advance bilateral projects and activate the Russian Industrial Zone. During his meeting with Oreshkin, Sisi requested that his greetings be conveyed to Russian President Vladimir Putin. The Egyptian president affirmed Cairo’s commitment to continuing coordination with Moscow to implement bilateral cooperation projects and strengthen strategic relations across various fields, according to Presidential Spokesman Ambassador Mohamed El-Shenawy. Oreshkin conveyed Putin’s greetings and expressed Russia’s desire to deepen bilateral cooperation, coordinate closely on mutual interests, and advance strategic projects. El-Shennawy noted that the discussions also covered the latest developments within the BRICS bloc and broader regional issues. headline: Kiev’s unreadiness for talks, Iran’s just cause: Lavrov’s statements
summary: Moscow has never targeted Ukrainian infrastructure that is not used for terror attacks on Russia, the foreign minister stressed
body_text:
TEHRAN, October 19. /TASS/. Iran’s struggle against the aggression unleashed upon it is a just cause, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov told a joint news conference after talks with his Iranian counterpart, Abbas Araghchi.

According to the top Russian diplomat, neither Kiev nor its European sponsors are ready for talks. Russia has never targeted Ukrainian infrastructure that is not used for terror attacks on Russia, he stressed.

TASS has summarized the top Russian diplomat’s key statements

Russia has targeted only Ukrainian infrastructure producing goods used to carry out terrorist attacks on Russian territory: "We have never launched attacks on civilian infrastructure in Ukraine, except in cases involving facilities that directly supply the Ukrainian armed forces with the relevant products, which are then used to carry out terrorist attacks against Russian citizens."

"It is clear that neither the Kyiv regime nor its European backers are ready for such talks."

The religious factor is one of the triggers for the crisis in Ukraine: "In Ukraine, this [religious] factor is indeed one of the triggers for the current crisis, because long before the special military operation - back when there was no sign of such a war, which the Europeans instigated against Russia using the Ukrainian Nazi regime - the previous president of Ukraine and his government had already begun a campaign to undermine the canonical Ukrainian Orthodox Church."

Russia continues advocating the rights of Russian-speakers in territories controlled by the Vladimir Zelensky regime: "First and foremost, we are fighting for the rights of our people in all spheres, including religious, but also language, and we are fighting for the rights of Russian people and those of Russian culture, including those who currently remain in the territory controlled by Zelensky, and for their right to be part of Russian history. The regime, however, which is supported by European elites, is aimed precisely at destroying these fundamental, inalienable human rights."

The West would prefer that Ukrainians, in their religious outlook, lean not on traditional Christian values, but rather to the so-called "freethought" currently being actively promoted in Europe: "Western Europe would likely feel more comfortable if Ukrainians, in their religious views, aligned themselves with what is termed 'freethought' - a concept currently being actively imposed across Europe - as an alternative to the traditional Christian values that have endured for centuries, and indeed, for millennia."

Iran’s struggle against the aggression unleashed upon it is a just cause, "people should not have to suffer because of events that occur against their will": "Therefore, I am confident that Iran’s cause - much like Russia’s - is a just cause."

Moscow is ready to help look for ways to settle the conflict between the United States and Iran: "We analyzed the situation that had emerged as a result of an unprovoked US-Israeli aggression against Iran. I once again outlined our country’s readiness to render assistance in searching for mutually acceptable solutions to resolve this artificially created crisis."

"We welcomed Tehran’s efforts focused on using diplomacy to establish durable peace and stability in the region."

"It is important to return to the pre-crisis situation in the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, including measures to restore the freedom of navigation and guarantees against the recurrence of aggression."

"We appreciate the efforts by international mediators who are trying to help reach such a reliable agreement."

Russia managed to prevent attempts to justify aggressive actions by the United States and Israel against Iran at the United Nations: "At the United Nations, we prevented attempts to justify the unlawful, aggressive actions of the United States and Israel against Iran. We provided humanitarian aid to the friendly Iranian people as quickly as possible, delivering the medicines and medical supplies they needed, while food supplies are also being delivered regularly."

Russia is not interested in volatility of prices on international energy markets: "President [of Russia Vladimir] Putin reiterated that we are not interested in price volatility, in prices bouncing up or down. We as a serious country want stability, including stable prices."

The stability of prices is required to plan the long-term development of the country: "The latest budget, which is being reviewed at present, assumes such scenario exactly."

There are attempts to push the issue of establishing a Palestinian state to the background: "With regard to a Middle East settlement, it is crucial to intensify efforts on the Palestinian issue, which some are currently attempting not only to push to the very bottom of the international agenda, but also to emasculate any resolutions regarding the establishment of a Palestinian state."

Russia and Iran insist on strict compliance with the relevant resolutions: "Russia and Iran stand firm for the implementation of relevant resolutions, as well as the UN Security Council resolutions on Lebanon."

Moscow will not abandon its economic agreements with Iran despite the difficult situation: "Despite the challenging situation, which has repeatedly been mentioned, Russia has no intention to abandon the implementation of economic and investment agreements with Iran."

"Russian specialists are gradually returning to the Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant."

Russia expects that President of Iran Masoud Pezeshkian will participate in the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) summit on October 27 in Moscow.

Russia also expects an Iranian delegation to take part in the Minsk Security Conference.

Russia had welcomed the formation of the Mecca Pact: "We proceed from the understanding that the goals declared as the foundation of this association are to achieve stability and promote peace and cooperation."

"Some other countries and regions, including Arab states, have also expressed interest in this ‘trio’ and in joining its work."

Moscow would respect Iran’s decision to join the Mecca Agreement if Tehran concludes that doing so would contribute to peace: "If at some stage the leadership of the Islamic Republic of Iran decides that contacts with this structure could help advance the cause of peace and free development, we will respect the choice of our friends."

It is necessary to resume dialogue on settling the political situation in Yemen and return to the 2023 roadmap offered by Saudi Arabia: "Of course, it is also important to resume dialogue on the situation in and around Yemen. Ideally, we should return to the roadmap developed by Saudi Arabia in 2023, which was acceptable to both the internationally recognized authorities in Aden and the Ansar Allah movement."

headline: Madbouly: Egypt Forum 2026 to set national priorities through dialogue
summary: Egypt’s Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly said Egypt Forum 2026 aims to establish shared national priorities and develop actionable solutions with clearly defined responsibilities and measurable outcomes, as the government seeks to address citizens’ concerns and set its agenda through 2030. Speaking at the opening session of the forum, held under the theme “A Look at Today, a Vision for Tomorrow” in the presence of President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi, Madbouly said the event was designed to facilitate constructive dialogue among the government, civil society, experts, political figures, opposition representatives and citizens. “The government will not speak alone while citizens listen; the opposite is what should happen,” Madbouly said, stressing that the forum would provide an opportunity for citizens to raise questions and for government officials to respond openly. He noted that the forum would review Egypt’s development efforts over the past 12 years, assess achievements and shortcomings, and address public concerns over government policies and national projects. Madbouly added that discussions would also examine the challenges that had prompted changes in some government priorities, with the aim of objectively evaluating past decisions and identifying priorities for the coming years. More than 16,000 proposals submitted The prime minister said preparations for the forum included public opinion surveys, consultation sessions and discussions involving universities, research centres and civil society representatives. During the 15 days following the president’s call to organise the forum, surveys were conducted among citizens, young people, investors and private-sector representatives to identify their main concerns and assess their satisfaction with public services. More than 450 citizens participated in listening sessions at the National Training Academy, submitting around 150 ideas and proposals. Meanwhile, more than 4,000 academics, researchers and experts took part in 30 preparatory sessions held across 28 Egyptian universities. The government also organised approximately 13 preparatory sessions involving 16 think tanks at the Cabinet’s Information and Decision Support Center. Madbouly said the forum’s website had recorded 17 million views and more than 61,000 registered participants, who submitted over 16,000 ideas and proposals. Around 50% of registered participants were aged between 18 and 35, including more than 5,000 students, some of whom were school pupils. The consultations identified more than 42 public questions for discussion during the forum, covering issues including the New Administrative Capital, infrastructure spending priorities, the future of Egypt’s economy after its programme with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), external and regional challenges, and public debt management. Madbouly said the government would respond to citizens’ questions transparently and without withholding information, while presenting the results of its policies and explaining the reasoning behind major decisions. Education, inflation and healthcare top public concerns According to the prime minister, five issues emerged as the leading priorities for approximately 70% of respondents: education, prices and inflation control, improving healthcare services, wages and pensions, and maintaining security and stability. Other concerns included culture and media, strengthening national identity, employment, youth and sports, and information and communications technology. Madbouly said the findings would help shape the forum’s agenda and ensure that discussions reflected citizens’ needs, particularly those of younger generations. The forum’s programme is organised around several main themes, beginning with human development. The first day focuses on education, youth and creativity, culture, and social values, with discussions examining how to improve educational outcomes and expand opportunities for learning, participation and innovation. The second day addresses integrated development and quality of life, including urban development, healthcare and digital government services. Discussions will examine how to maximise the benefits of national projects and improve the accessibility and efficiency of public services through digital transformation. A further theme focuses on social protection and community security, including economic and social pressures on households, social protection programmes, and food and water security. Economic agenda focuses on investment Economic issues will feature prominently in the forum, with sessions dedicated to investment, industry, sustainable employment and the government’s proposed national economic transformation programme for the period following the IMF programme. The agenda will also cover ways to increase foreign currency resources, manage public debt and address energy-related challenges. Madbouly explained that the central objective was to move from economic stability towards more productive and competitive growth led by investment and the private sector, with benefits extending to employment, incomes and living standards. Friday’s sessions will provide citizens with an opportunity to discuss issues of public concern directly, including prices, the settlement of building violations, urban greening, regulation of the real estate market, issues affecting Egyptians abroad and the problem of stray dogs. Government targets measurable action through 2030 Madbouly stressed that the forum’s success would not be measured solely by the publication of recommendations, but by the development of a practical programme with clear responsibilities, implementation timelines and performance indicators. The government aims to establish a national action programme covering the next four years through 2030, with each relevant authority responsible for implementing its assigned measures and monitoring progress against defined targets. He indicated that the broader objective was to improve living conditions while taking into account Egypt’s economic circumstances and the challenges facing the country. The prime minister also acknowledged the burden borne by Egyptian citizens during years of economic and structural reforms, describing them as central to the country’s development journey. Concluding his remarks, Madbouly said national progress required sustained collective effort rather than promises of rapid success, emphasising the importance of commitment and cooperation in achieving long-term development goals.

headline: Egypt’s chemical exports to India surge about 325% to $627m in 8 months
summary: Egypt’s exports of chemicals and fertilisers to India surged 325% year on year to $627m during the first eight months of 2026, up from $147m in the same period last year, according to the Chemical and Fertilisers Export Council. The increase amounted to approximately $480m, making India the third-largest destination for Egyptian chemical and fertiliser exports, after Türkiye and Italy, Khaled Abu El-Makarem, Chairperson of the council and the Egyptian-Indian Business Council, said. The performance came as Egypt’s total chemical and fertiliser exports rose 30% year on year to $8.255bn between January and August 2026. Abu El-Makarem said the growth reflected India’s increasing importance as a destination for Egyptian products and presented opportunities to expand trade, industrial cooperation, and investment between the two countries. He added that India’s extensive industrial base and demand for fertilisers, raw materials, and industrial inputs could create further opportunities for Egyptian companies to expand their market presence. The council is working with the Egyptian-Indian Business Council to strengthen ties between the two countries’ business communities, promote the capabilities of Egyptian manufacturers, and identify opportunities for commercial, industrial, and investment partnerships. Abu El-Makarem said the next phase would focus on translating trade growth into long-term partnerships based on industrial integration, technology exchange, and higher value-added exports. Fertilisers and pesticides dominate exports Fertilisers and pesticides accounted for the largest share of Egypt’s chemical and fertiliser exports to India, reaching approximately $552m during the January-August period, equivalent to around 88% of the total, according to the council. Inorganic chemicals generated approximately $30m in exports, while petrochemical products reached $24m and miscellaneous chemicals totalled $15m. The four product categories collectively accounted for around $621m of exports to India, highlighting the concentration of trade in a limited number of product groups. Abu El-Makarem explained that diversifying the export basket and increasing the contribution of higher value-added products would be important to sustaining growth in the Indian market. He added that the council was working to provide exporters with market intelligence, information on export opportunities and target-market requirements, while supporting promotional activities and business-to-business meetings. Egypt and India prepare new economic event Abu El-Makarem also disclosed that preparations were under way to organise an economic event with Indian counterparts in the coming period. Further details will be announced at a later date. The event is intended to strengthen commercial ties, facilitate direct engagement between Egyptian and Indian companies, and identify opportunities for trade, investment, and industrial cooperation. He said bilateral meetings and economic events could help businesses identify market demand and turn commercial interest into actual contracts and investment projects. According to the council, India accounted for approximately 7.6% of Egypt’s chemical and fertiliser exports during the first eight months of 2026. Exports to the sector’s 10 largest destination markets totalled $4.619bn over the same period, representing around 56% of the sector’s overall exports.

The increase amounted to approximately $480m, making India the third-largest destination for Egyptian chemical and fertiliser exports, after Türkiye and Italy, Khaled Abu El-Makarem, Chairperson of the council and the Egyptian-Indian Business Council, said.

The performance came as Egypt’s total chemical and fertiliser exports rose 30% year on year to $8.255bn between January and August 2026.

Abu El-Makarem said the growth reflected India’s increasing importance as a destination for Egyptian products and presented opportunities to expand trade, industrial cooperation, and investment between the two countries.

He added that India’s extensive industrial base and demand for fertilisers, raw materials, and industrial inputs could create further opportunities for Egyptian companies to expand their market presence.

The council is working with the Egyptian-Indian Business Council to strengthen ties between the two countries’ business communities, promote the capabilities of Egyptian manufacturers, and identify opportunities for commercial, industrial, and investment partnerships.

Abu El-Makarem said the next phase would focus on translating trade growth into long-term partnerships based on industrial integration, technology exchange, and higher value-added exports.

Fertilisers and pesticides accounted for the largest share of Egypt’s chemical and fertiliser exports to India, reaching approximately $552m during the January-August period, equivalent to around 88% of the total, according to the council.

He added that the council was working to provide exporters with market intelligence, information on export opportunities and target-market requirements, while supporting promotional activities and business-to-business meetings.

The event is intended to strengthen commercial ties, facilitate direct engagement between Egyptian and Indian companies, and identify opportunities for trade, investment, and industrial cooperation.

He said bilateral meetings and economic events could help businesses identify market demand and turn commercial interest into actual contracts and investment projects.

headline: Indonesia first foreign country to own property in Saudi Arabia's Mecca
summary: Indonesia's sovereign wealth fund Danantara has received ownership certificates for the 2-billion-riyal ($531.4 million) acquisition of a hotel and 14 adjoining development plots.
body_text:
Indonesia has become the first foreign state to own property in Saudi Arabia’s holy city of Mecca, after sovereign wealth fund Danantara Indonesia received ownership certificates for a 2 billion-riyal ($531.4 million) acquisition.

What happened: The real estate assets were acquired by Danantara Indonesia, through its investment arm, Danantara Investment Management, at Thakher Makkah, a major urban development about 1.2 kilometers north of the Grand Mosque, or Masjid al-Haram.

Thakher Development, the project’s master developer, handed over the ownership documents, completing the acquisition of the 1,461-room Novotel Thakher Makkah Hotel and 14 adjoining development plots, according to a company press release.

“This is a historic moment for Thakher Makkah. Welcoming the first foreign state to own property in our destination reflects international confidence in Thakher Makkah,” Faisal Shaker, CEO of Thakher Development, said in the statement.

headline: Russia, Iran reaffirm mutual interest in intensifying efforts within BRICS, SCO, EUAE
summary: The current bilateral agenda was addressed in the traditionally constructive atmosphere with a focus on strengthening comprehensive strategic partnership in light of agreements reached by Presidents Vladimir Putin of Russia and Masoud Pezeshkian on Iran on the sidelines of the recent events in Kyrgyzstan and Turkmenistan
body_text:
MOSCOW, October 19. /TASS/. Moscow and Tehran reaffirmed their mutual interest in invigorating joint efforts within BRICS, the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO), the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), and the United Nations, the Russian Foreign Ministry said after Minister Sergey Lavrov’s visit to Iran.

During his working visit to Tehran, the top Russian diplomat was received by Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and met with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaei.

"Both sides expressed a mutual interest in intensifying joint efforts in multilateral formats - the United Nations, BRICS, the SCO, and the EAEU," the ministry said.

"The sides noted with satisfaction the intensive nature of the political dialogue and the close cooperation at the governmental and sectoral levels, as well as between parliaments, regions, and the business community," it stated. "Attention was given to issues related to expanding trade, economic, and investment cooperation, including the implementation of joint transport, logistics, and energy projects."

The current bilateral agenda was addressed in the traditionally constructive atmosphere with a focus on strengthening comprehensive strategic partnership in light of agreements reached by Presidents Vladimir Putin of Russia and Masoud Pezeshkian on Iran on the sidelines of the recent events in Kyrgyzstan and Turkmenistan.

"The [Russian minister’s] visit to Tehran marked a continuation of the substantive political dialogue and made it possible to outline practical steps for the further development of bilateral relations and foreign policy cooperation between Russia and Iran," the ministry added.

But all Lebanese officials who spoke to The National expressed low expectations for the talks, describing them as largely technical and an opportunity for Lebanon to repeat its demands for a full Israeli withdrawal from the occupied south.“We don’t expect any major decisions or an expansion of the pilot zones tomorrow and the verification mechanism won't be established,” a military source said. “We will as usual shine a light on the [Israeli] aggression and the ceasefire violations, and demand a full withdrawal from the south – the same demands as always.”Still, Lebanon sees little alternative to continuing with the negotiations, even as officials increasingly question whether they can produce Israeli concessions. body_text:
Lebanon is rejecting US-backed proposals for its troops to co-ordinate directly with the Israeli army, officials said before talks resume in Florida on Tuesday.

They said they expected limited progress before Israel's legislative elections next week.

The latest round of direct talks, bringing together Lebanese and Israeli military delegations in Tampa, follows a decision last month to formally separate the political and military aspects of the negotiations.

The aim is to negotiate an Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanon. The price demanded by Israel is for Hezbollah to be disarmed. However, Lebanon is pushing back against the idea of direct military co-ordination.

“The issue keeps coming up but we always tell them 'no, we will not do that,'” one Lebanese political official close to the discussions said. They added that any future talks must continue to involve American mediation.

“There are Israelis and Lebanese, with the Americans in the middle. That's it and that's how it will remain. Our position has always been that there should be a third party for verification.”

The proposed verification mechanism would oversee the agreements in so-called “pilot zones” – areas of southern Lebanon where Hezbollah would disarm, Israeli forces would withdraw and the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) would assume control.

Progress has stalled for months since the first pilot zones were established in July. The process remains untested, with no agreed mechanism to verify compliance by all sides, while critics point out that the initial zones had no Israeli military presence to begin with.

Israel continues to demand Hezbollah's disarmament as a condition for its withdrawal and has cast doubt on the LAF's ability to carry out the process.

Political uncertainty in Israel has further hampered talks, with legislative elections scheduled for the end of the month leaving Lebanese officials expecting little movement on the more contentious issues until the poll is over.

“There's no real political track between [Lebanon and Israel] because there's a dead end until it's clear what the new government in Israel will be,” a political source told The National. The election of a hard-line Israeli government could lead to more delays.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told Israeli media on Sunday he does not trust the Lebanese government to disarm Hezbollah. “That's why we said that as long as it is not disarmed, we will remain in this zone that changed the situation in the north,” Mr Netanyahu said.

One source acknowledged mounting pressure on Lebanon to “do more to show movement on expanding the authority of the state [by] moving against Hezbollah at least in small steps”.

But all Lebanese officials who spoke to The National expressed low expectations for the talks, describing them as largely technical and an opportunity for Lebanon to repeat its demands for a full Israeli withdrawal from the occupied south.

“We don’t expect any major decisions or an expansion of the pilot zones tomorrow and the verification mechanism won't be established,” a military source said. “We will as usual shine a light on the [Israeli] aggression and the ceasefire violations, and demand a full withdrawal from the south – the same demands as always.”

Still, Lebanon sees little alternative to continuing with the negotiations, even as officials increasingly question whether they can produce Israeli concessions. Lebanon entered direct talks hoping the US would use its leverage over Israel to secure an end to attacks in the south and begin a phased Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory.

Instead, Israeli military operations and demolitions have continued alongside the discussions, including beyond the boundaries of Israel's own declared “security” zone – leaving Lebanese officials in doubt as to what the diplomatic process has achieved so far.

headline: Zelensky says Starshield speed limits slowing down frontline response
summary: Speed limits on a US military grade satellite system are hindering Ukrainian forces' ability to coordinate drone strikes against Russian forces, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Monday. Zelensky said frontline units had reported that the Starshield equipment "stops functioning at speeds of 130-160 kilometres (80-100 miles) per hour in various sectors of the front". Separately, a Ukrainian army brigade has announced the rescue of a wounded soldier from the front line using an aerial drone, describing the evacuation as the first of its kind. The brigade published a video showing the drone lowering itself to the ground, before a man in combat gear fastens himself to a winch onboard and is lifted upwards. FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg reports from Ukraine.

body_text:
Claude developer Anthropic has announced it is committing 5 per cent of its shares to a “public benefit fund” amid growing backlash over artificial intelligence.

And Tesla boss Elon Musk has promised to give a share in his SpaceX company to “every kid in America” next year.

AI start-up Anthropic said in a blog post the fund would be a wholly owned liability company and that it would receive an additional 2 per cent of Anthropic shares at the board's discretion for every 50 per cent increase in the company's value above a to-be-announced baseline.

Abu Dhabi launches TAMM Global to export AI-powered government services worldwide

It said establishing the fund, which would be subject to shareholder approval, will give it more flexibility and scale to make donations “to traditional non-profit or direct distributions to specific populations”.

“Because of the way the fund is structured, the more Anthropic grows, the larger the share of the company that can be dedicated expressly to the public good,” it said on Sunday.

The company is planning one of the biggest IPOs in history as a public benefit corporation, possibly as soon as November. The company said in June it had submitted a confidential filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission for its proposed IPO. Abu Dhabi technology investment firm MGX took part in Anthropic's recent $65 billion funding round.

Anthropic gave the labour market as one area of focus for the fund, with a $200 million commitment to study the issue. Research from the International Monetary Fund estimates about 60 per cent of jobs in advanced economies are exposed to AI. Separate research from Goldman Sachs said recent anecdotes and data suggest AI displacement in the US could be strong among entry-level workers.

Mr Musk responded to Anthropic's announcement on X saying, “I recommend giving the shares directly to the public."

He pledged one share of SpaceX to “every kid in America” next year in a separate post on Monday, without providing further details.

“This will be the first of many,” Mr Musk wrote.

The world's first trillionaire could theoretically use the recently created Trump Accounts programme to donate the shares. The programme allows donors to make contributions without paying a capital gains tax, in some circumstances. The Treasury Department said in a September notice that it was seeking to automatically enrol up to 60 million children in the programme.

With about 73 million people under 18 years of age in the US, the pledge would be valued at about $10.7 billion at the company's Friday close at $146.03 a share. SpaceX was trading 0.78 per cent higher at $147.33 a share as of 2:30pm ET (8pm GST) on Monday.

The pledges from Anthropic and Mr Musk come as Americans grow more concerned about AI. A recent AP-Norc poll found 64 per cent of US adults believe the technology is developing “too fast”, compared to 27 per cent saying development has been “about right” and 8 per cent saying it is moving “too slow”.

Building the massive data centres housing the technology is also leading to rising energy costs. A recent poll from Quinnipiac University said about 73 per cent of US voters oppose the building of data centres in their communities.

AI executives and President Donald Trump have recently adopted a defensive stance amid this growing backlash, with the US leader calling AI anxieties a "hoax".

In September, he hosted chief executives from Nvidia, Meta and other Big Tech firms at the White House, where they signed what was billed as a morally binding agreement to help police AI.

The document encourages companies to "implement robust internal controls" to monitor models during training, empower an internal team to ensure controls are operating as intended, link up with an independent external auditor, and designate an independent committee to oversee and receive reports from the team operating the controls.

Mr Trump has also opposed AI regulations, saying such orders would put the US at a disadvantage against China in the AI race.

headline: Seha Group partners with Chubb Life Egypt to digitize insurance operations
summary: Seha Group has announced a strategic partnership between its technology arm, SehaTech, and Chubb Life Egypt to digitize insurance operations, alongside the launch of SehaAcademy to develop specialized talent in medical insurance and healthcare management. The announcements were made during Seha Group’s first annual event, which brought together around 250 industry leaders, executives, and decision-makers from the insurance and education sectors. Under the partnership, SehaTech will provide integrated technology solutions to support Chubb Life Egypt’s medical and life insurance operations, including the management of insurance groups and beneficiaries, invoicing, reporting, and other operational processes. Eslam Nagah, Country President and Managing Director of Chubb Life Egypt, said the partnership would combine Chubb’s international insurance expertise with SehaTech’s technological capabilities and understanding of the local market to improve operational efficiency and develop solutions tailored to Egypt’s insurance sector. Mohamed El Shabrawy, CEO and co-founder of Seha Group, said the partnership reflects the group’s strategy of expanding collaboration across the insurance industry while investing in technology and professional development. Seha Group also launched SehaAcademy in collaboration with the British University in Egypt (BUE), with GREA UK appointed to manage the academy under an agreement signed with the group. The academy will offer specialised training programmes in medical and life insurance, as well as healthcare management, targeting both existing industry professionals and new entrants to the sector. The initiative builds on the existing collaboration between SehaOne and BUE’s School of Continuing Education to develop professional training programmes and strengthen skills in the healthcare and insurance industries. Mostafa AboElsoud, CEO of GREA UK, said the collaboration would focus on delivering specialised programmes combining academic knowledge and professional training to help prepare qualified personnel for the sector’s evolving requirements. Separately, SehaOne announced the launch of InsureHub and AiDa, an artificial intelligence-powered assistant designed to help insurance companies respond to inquiries from visitors to their websites and improve access to insurance information. The new solutions form part of SehaOne’s efforts to expand its digital services for insurers and advance the electronic administration of medical insurance operations through electronic third-party administration (e-TPA) services. SehaOne’s platform connects insurance companies with healthcare providers and supports the administration of insurance processes, including claims and approvals. The company aims to use digital tools and data analytics to streamline procedures and improve operational efficiency.

headline: Netanyahu basks in Trump endorsement week before election
summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Monday basked in Donald Trump's endorsement days before close-fought elections, airing a call in which the US president predicted he would win and suggested they may again attack Iran together. A day after Trump publicly endorsed Netanyahu for the October 27 vote, Netanyahu put out a video of a telephone call in which the two right-wing leaders lavish praise on each other. "I think you're going to have a tremendous victory, actually," Trump can be heard saying on speakerphone.
body_text:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Monday basked in Donald Trump's endorsement days before close-fought elections, airing a call in which the US president predicted he would win and suggested they may again attack Iran together.

A day after Trump publicly endorsed Netanyahu for the October 27 vote, Netanyahu put out a video of a telephone call in which the two right-wing leaders lavish praise on each other.

"I think you're going to have a tremendous victory, actually," Trump can be heard saying on speakerphone.

"You're the man I want by my side, Bibi," Trump said, referring to Netanyahu by his nickname.

Netanyahu -- while reminding the famously loose-lipped president that they were on an open line -- hailed Trump for joining Israel in attacking Iran in late February.

"Donald, we have a job to finish," a beaming Netanyahu said. "We'll finish it together. We'll finish it, and no one else will do it."

Netanyahu did not elaborate but again described Iran's clerical state, which remains in power nearly eight months after the joint attack, as "the greatest danger".

Netanyahu appeared to be speaking to Trump from an air force base from which he earlier released a video warning that he had been assured of Israel's "capability to strike our enemies the moment it is required".

Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, had waited for years for a US president who would agree to attack Iran. But Trump abruptly switched course in April and reached with Iran a ceasefire that is now in tatters.

Polls showed that Trump's approval rating in Israel dropped sharply afterwards.

David Makovsky, a fellow at the Washington Institute for Near East Policy, said it was unclear that Trump's endorsement would have a "huge impact" on Israelis.

Netanyahu is "a polarising figure. You either love him or hate him," Makovsky said. "How many undecideds are there? Not that many."

Trump went ahead with the endorsement despite open tensions involving top US officials. Vice President JD Vance has issued stinging criticism of Israel over the Iran war, saying it had no friends other than the United States and needs to get in line with US policy.

Makovsky said Trump's move may indicate that he secured an agreement from Netanyahu in return for the endorsement, although it was unclear on what.

The Israel Hayom newspaper -- in a report denied by the US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee -- recently said the Trump administration was pushing Netanyahu to form a government that no longer includes his far-right allies, who have championed settler extremists in the West Bank and urged the expulsion of all of Gaza's Palestinians.

The newspaper said that a more moderate new unity government could then work on normalising Israel's relations with more Arab and Islamic states. Netanyahu in the call to Trump mentioned expanding the so-called Abraham Accords, in which the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Morocco normalised with Israel in 2020.

Netanyahu described Trump as "by far, the greatest friend Israel has ever had".

Since his first term, Trump has taken several major steps to back Israel, including moving the US embassy to Jerusalem, which most countries do not recognise as Israel's capital due to the dispute with the Palestinians.

Netanyahu's top challenger, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, still voiced respect for Trump after the endorsement, while adding, "Only Israelis can choose their leader."

Trump, 80, and Netanyahu, who turns 77 on Wednesday, have forged a close partnership at a time when both are vastly unpopular in public opinion in most democratic nations.

Both have also managed to avoid prosecution while in power, with Netanyahu facing charges of corruption that could land him in prison.

Trump, who remains bitter over cases against him including over his attempts to overturn his 2020 election loss, told Netanyahu in language he often uses about himself, "You're a warrior. You've been treated unfairly by your country and by some others."

Netanyahu faces an arrest warrant by the International Criminal Court over alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity in the relentless Israeli offensive in Gaza in response to the October 7, 2023 Hamas attacks.

Netanyahu has angrily denounced the charges, and the Trump administration has tried to dismantle the court in The Hague through sanctions.

headline: Curfew imposed on Paris’ Place de la Republique amid riots — TV
summary: According to the television channel, the curfew will be in effect from 10:00 p.m. on Monday until 6:00 a.m. on Tuesday and will apply to all citizens
body_text:

headline: Paris to impose overnight curfew around Place de la Republique, Les Halles
summary: Curfew applies to entire population, while demonstrations also banned in some Paris neighborhoods from 8 pm to 6 am
body_text:
After days of mass protests that have sometimes turned violent, French authorities will impose an overnight 10 pm to 6 am curfew around Paris’ Place de la Republique and in streets surrounding the Les Halles area, French broadcaster BFMTV reported Monday.

Authorities clarified that the curfew applies to the entire population, not just minors. It also announced a ban on demonstrations in certain Paris neighborhoods from 8 pm to 6 am.

The restrictions come as authorities around France introduce curfews and other security measures following violence and looting during weekend demonstrations nationwide against the rising cost of living and fuel prices.

French authorities said earlier Monday that overnight curfews would be imposed in four northern communes -- Lille, Douai, Wattignies, and Denain -- for two nights, with the agreement of their respective mayors.

Those restrictions will run from 8 pm to 6 am.

Denain has also introduced a separate nighttime 9 pm to 6 am curfew through Sunday, Oct. 25.

Around 550,000 people took part in 110 demonstrations across France on Saturday, including 110,000 in Paris, while about 400 arrests were recorded nationwide, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said.

Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said Monday that he had asked prefects to introduce localized and partial curfews following the unrest.

He also announced a major judicial operation and partial unemployment measures for businesses affected by the violence.

Authorities have also announced restrictions on gatherings in Marseille.

headline: France riots: AI photos falsely depict elderly couple ‘stripped and robbed’
summary: AI-generated photos falsely claiming to show an elderly couple being “stripped and robbed” during unrest in France have racked up millions of views. Amplified by far-right accounts, the images fuelled inflammatory claims about Muslims, Jews and the riots. The FRANCE 24 Observers traced one image to an AI photo montage published by a pro-Israel account. The images were created using OpenAI tools, and the alleged assault remains unverified, with no official reports confirming the attack.

AI-generated photos falsely claiming to show an elderly couple being “stripped and robbed” during unrest in France have racked up millions of views. Amplified by far-right accounts, the images fuelled inflammatory claims about Muslims, Jews and the riots. The FRANCE 24 Observers traced one image to an AI photo montage published by a pro-Israel account. The images were created using OpenAI tools, and the alleged assault remains unverified, with no official reports confirming the attack.

Two AI-generated photos falsely claiming to show an elderly couple in their 80s being “stripped and robbed” during unrest in France have racked up millions of views online. The images spread widely on X, particularly among far-right accounts. Some users described them as “the most horrific image of October 17th”, while others claimed they showed that “France has fallen” and warned that the rest of Europe and the UK would be next.

Several accounts also claimed the couple were Jewish, accusing French President Emmanuel Macron of failing “the Israeli people” and comparing the alleged attack to a 1941 pogrom in Ukraine.

American far-right conspiracy theorist Alex Jones also shared one of the fake images, blaming the alleged violence on “criminal consortium of Muslims and communists, who are unified by their hatred of the west and white people”.

The images did not only circulate on social media. French digital media outlet Sirenes shared one on Instagram, while Israeli right-wing news channel C14 published it under the headline “Islam Conquers Europe”.

However, both images are AI-generated.

The FRANCE 24 Observers confirmed their artificial origin using SynthID, an invisible digital watermark designed to help identify AI-generated content. Both images were detected as having been created using OpenAI tools.

There are also several visual clues that point to manipulation in one of the photos. The woman’s hand appears to have only four fingers, with an enlarged, deformed thumb. Two masked heads are visible despite there being only one body, while a bollard lying on the ground does not resemble the type typically found in Paris.

With the help of the European Broadcasting Union’s Spotlight network and Belgium’s RTBF fact-checking team, FRANCE 24’s Observers traced the source of the image: a montage published late on October 17 by the pro-Israel account Infos-Israel.news. The montage contained several AI-generated images and was flagged as AI content.

The same white border visible around the image in the original montage also appears in posts circulating on X, indicating that the photo was lifted and re-shared directly from that collection.

But while the images are fake, what about the underlying claim that an elderly couple was assaulted?

The allegation gained traction after French journalist Dominique Rizet said on air on BFM that an elderly couple had been attacked in Paris, citing a police source. His report was subsequently picked up by other media outlets, though no official photos or sources confirmed the alleged assault.

FRANCE 24 contacted Rizet, who said he had received the information from a police source at 8:47 pm on Saturday and that it had been “confirmed”.

However, the fact-checking service CheckNews of French newspaper Libération contacted the Paris prosecutor’s office, which said that, as of Monday - around 48 hours after the alleged incident - there had been no reports to that effect to date.

As of now, other credible sources or official reports have confirmed the alleged attack.

headline: UN food agency cuts Gaza assistance by one-third amid funding shortages
summary: Half a million Palestinians lose access to critical food assistance ahead of winter
body_text:
Anadolu Ajansı © 2026

The UN World Food Program (WFP) announced Monday that funding shortages have forced it to cut food assistance in the Gaza Strip by around one-third, leaving half a million people without critical support as winter approaches.

In a statement, the agency said it is now assisting 1.1 million vulnerable people in Gaza, down from 1.6 million last month, while food rations have been halved.

Families receiving assistance will now get one food parcel instead of two, along with a smaller bag of wheat flour, it said.

The number of daily hot meals has also dropped from 250,000 to 150,000, while families in hard-to-reach areas, including near the Israeli army-controlled "yellow line," will receive meals every other day instead of daily.

The agency has also reduced the value of cash assistance for 75,000 families.

According to WFP, an estimated 1.4 million people, or 67% of Gaza's population, face crisis-level food insecurity or worse, including around 200,000 experiencing emergency conditions requiring immediate food assistance to prevent deaths from hunger.

Only one in five children consumes a sufficiently diverse diet, while unemployment exceeds 80%, leaving many families unable to afford nutritious food.

WFP warned that "modest" improvements in food security since the October 2025 ceasefire remain "fragile" and could quickly be reversed by further reductions in humanitarian assistance.

Funding shortages have also forced the agency to halve its assistance in the occupied West Bank, from 400,000 to 200,000 people.

The agency said it urgently needs $450 million to sustain critical operations across Gaza and the West Bank over the next six months, through March 2027.

Speaking at a UN briefing, WFP Acting Executive Director Carl Skau said the agency would seek to rotate food assistance rather than cut off 500,000 people entirely, prioritizing the most vulnerable.

Skau stressed that the reductions were driven solely by funding shortages, not delivery obstacles or declining needs.

"I want to be clear: this is not because the needs are going down, and it's not because we aren't able to bring in the food. This is only because we have less funding," he said, noting that WFP had recorded only three incidents of interference with aid deliveries throughout the war.

He warned that life in Gaza remained "absolutely brutal," with UN teams recording up to 50 security incidents daily and UNICEF reporting an average of one child killed each day since the ceasefire took effect last year.

Skau also said commercial deliveries had been halted for five days, driving up food prices. He urged the removal of Israeli restrictions on certain so-called "dual-use" materials needed for shelter, water and sanitation.

Turning to the occupied West Bank, he warned that a hunger crisis was emerging even as the Palestinian territory also continues to face a "human rights and protection crisis."

"Primarily, it's still a human rights and protection crisis, but it's now also becoming a hunger crisis because food insecurity has more than doubled in the last three years," Skau said.

"Almost a million Palestinians now need food assistance, and yet also in the West Bank, we are now forced to cut back," he said, adding that attacks by Israeli occupiers over only the first two weeks of the sensitive olive harvest have "already surpassed the whole of last year."

headline: Iran resolved to stregthen strategic ties with Russia
summary: TEHRAN, Oct. 19 (MNA) – Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council (SNSC) Major General Mohsen Rezaei told visiting Russian foreign minister that Tehran is resolved to solidify its strategic relations with Moscow.

TEHRAN, Oct. 19 (MNA) – Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council (SNSC) Major General Mohsen Rezaei told visiting Russian foreign minister that Tehran is resolved to solidify its strategic relations with Moscow.

The representative of the Leader of the Islmaic Revolution and the Secretary of the SNSC emphasized Iran’s determination to strengthen strategic cooperation between Tehran and Moscow in a meeting with Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov.

In the meeting, which took place in Tehran on Monday evening, Major General Rezaei emphasized the strategic impacts of the cooperation between the two countries for intra-regional cooperation to consolidate stability and ensure security in the region and accelerate the development and progress of the countries in the region.

Welcoming Russia’s ideas and initiatives to expand diverse cooperation between the two countries, the SNSC secretary said that joint economic projects between Iran and Russia, such as the completion of strategic corridors, have regional stabilizing impact.

Referring to the new post-war conditions in the region, the Secretary of the SNSC said that the durability and sustainability of regional security and stability depend on multilateral cooperation in the region.

Russian Foreign Minister, fore his part, emphasized his country's support for Iran's initiatives and interests in international bodies, including the UN Security Council and the Board of Governors of the International Atomic Energy Agency, and strongly condemned the illegal military attacks by the United States and the Zionist regime on Iran, including the bombing of nuclear facilities under which had been under the inspection of the Agency, and said that the prospects for cooperation between Iran and Russia are broad and all-out.

headline: Iran summons German ambassador over repeated allegations
summary: TEHRAN, Oct. 20 (MNA) – Iran summoned German Ambassador Axel Dittmann to the Foreign Ministry on Monday in protest over repeated baseless allegations by German officials against Tehran.
body_text:
TEHRAN, Oct. 20 (MNA) – Iran summoned German Ambassador Axel Dittmann to the Foreign Ministry on Monday in protest over repeated baseless allegations by German officials against Tehran.

Dittmann was summoned on October 19, 2026, by Alireza Yousefi, Assistant Foreign Minister and Director General for Western Europe, who conveyed the Islamic Republic’s strong objection to what he described as the inappropriate approach adopted by some German officials toward Iran.

Yousefi stressed that making security-related allegations against Iran had long been a tactic employed by the Israeli regime and some Western countries.

Iran Criticizes German Judiciary The Director General for Western Europe also stated that providing judicial cover for baseless political claims would not lend credibility to such allegations but would instead undermine the credibility of Germany’s judicial system.

Yousefi further assured the German ambassador that German officials’ attempts to implicate Iran were aimed at diverting attention from the German government’s responsibility for supporting and participating in the US-Israeli military aggression against Iran.

He emphasized that such tactics would in no way deter Iran from pursuing Germany’s international responsibility for its participation in war crimes committed during the US and Israeli military aggression against Iran.

The German ambassador said he would convey Iran’s concerns to the relevant authorities in his country.

Separately, Germany’s Foreign Ministry summoned Iran’s ambassador on Monday over allegations of an attempted attack against a leader of one of the country’s Jewish communities.

In a post on the social media platform X, the German Foreign Ministry said it would not tolerate attacks against Jewish residents and strongly condemned what it described as Iran’s actions.

A few days earlier, a court in Germany sentenced two men to prison over alleged plans to attack prominent pro-Israeli figures and spy on Jewish people on behalf of Iran’s intelligence services.

headline: US allowing 'dark fleet' oil tankers to ship crude, Energy Secretary says
summary: US President Donald Trump's administration is allowing oil tanker under sanctions to begin a process to legitimately ship crude, Energy Secretary Chris Wright said on Monday.Mr Wright told a Citadel Securities event in New York that this would involve investors buying and refurbishing idled sanctioned tankers, then using them to transport legal oil.“We’re going to move some of the ships from what I call the ‘bad-guy fleet’ to the ‘good-guy fleet,’” Mr Wright said. “They will not carry sanctioned oil any more.”He said there are about 1,600 tankers in the "dark fleet", and that dozens or hundreds could be added to the legitimate ships.It is the latest attempt by the Trump administration to reduce energy prices, which have soared amid the prolonged closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude, the global benchmark for much of the world's oil, settled 0.48 per cent lower on Monday at $109.3 a barrel. West Texas Intermediate, which tracks US crude, was 0.61 per cent lower at $98.42.Analytics firm Kpler said easing sanctions on the shadow fleet would have little effect on record freight rates. It estimated that only 24 of the about 160 vessels under sanctions from the Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control could return to mainstream trade after taking into account their age and ownership restrictions.“With war risk, rather than vessel availability alone, driving freight costs in the Middle East Gulf, sanctions relief risks delivering limited commercial benefits while weakening geopolitical leverage,” analysts wrote.Mr Wright rejected the idea that the process would be dropping penalties from ships that would carry crude from Russia, Iran or other countries on which the US imposed sanctions. “We are converting dark tankers to legitimate tankers,” he said.

Brent crude, the global benchmark for much of the world's oil, settled 0.48 per cent lower on Monday at $109.3 a barrel. West Texas Intermediate, which tracks US crude, was 0.61 per cent lower at $98.42.

Analytics firm Kpler said easing sanctions on the shadow fleet would have little effect on record freight rates.

It estimated that only 24 of the about 160 vessels under sanctions from the Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control could return to mainstream trade after taking into account their age and ownership restrictions.

“With war risk, rather than vessel availability alone, driving freight costs in the Middle East Gulf, sanctions relief risks delivering limited commercial benefits while weakening geopolitical leverage,” analysts wrote.

Mr Wright rejected the idea that the process would be dropping penalties from ships that would carry crude from Russia, Iran or other countries on which the US imposed sanctions.

“We are converting dark tankers to legitimate tankers,” he said.

The probe was launched aboard an H3 heavy-lift rocket from the Tanegashima Space Center. JAXA is broadcasting the launch live.

The MMX probe’s main mission is to collect soil samples from Phobos. The spacecraft is expected to return to Earth in 2031 and release a capsule containing the samples. By analyzing these samples, Japanese specialists hope to gain insights into the origins of Phobos and Mars itself.

SEOUL, Oct. 20 (Yonhap) -- The education ministers of North Korea and Russia have met in Pyongyang and discussed ways to expand exchanges in the education field, the North's state media reported Tuesday, amid deepening cooperation between the two nations.

North Korean Education Minister Ri Yong-chol and his Russian counterpart, Sergey Kravtsov, held talks the previous day, according to the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA). A Russian delegation, led by Kravtsov, arrived in Pyongyang on Monday.

"At the talks, the successes and experience gained by the two countries in the field of education were shared, and the issues of further boosting bilateral exchange and cooperation were discussed," the KCNA reported, without disclosing other details.

In a separate dispatch, the KCNA said the Russian delegation toured the Pyongyang University of Education No. 2, a major educational institution for training teachers in the North, the previous day.

The two nations signed a "supplementary agreement" to establish and operate a Russian education center in North Korea under a partnership between the Pyongyang university and Russia's Blagoveshchensk State Pedagogical University, according to the KCNA.

North Korea and Russia have been expanding the scope of cooperation in the military, economy and other areas since they signed a mutual defense treaty in June 2024.

headline: French and UAE presidents discuss maritime security and global energy supplies
summary: Emmanuel Macron and Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan also discuss regional and international developments amid French president's Gulf tour
body_text:
French President Emmanuel Macron and his United Arab Emirates counterpart Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan discussed maritime security and global energy supplies in Abu Dhabi on Monday.

The talks came as part of Macron's three-day Gulf tour that started earlier Monday.

They addressed bilateral ties and focused on expanding cooperation in trade, investment, energy, advanced technology and artificial intelligence as well as advancing joint projects in key sectors, the Abu Dhabi Media Office said in a statement.

The two leaders also reviewed regional and international developments, "foremost among them developments in the Middle East and ongoing efforts to address their impact on maritime security and global energy supplies," the office said.

Macron and Sheikh Mohammed reaffirmed their "shared determination to strengthen coordination" to promote regional security, stability and peace.

The meeting was attended by Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Sheikh Mohammed bin Hamad bin Tahnoon Al Nahyan, and several other senior Emirati officials, it added.

The French president began his Gulf tour in Kuwait earlier Monday and is scheduled to visit Bahrain and Qatar after the UAE.

The tour comes amid heightened regional tensions and disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic waterway through which a significant share of global oil supplies passes.

Oil prices fell on Tuesday as markets weighed an executive order from US President Donald Trump that waived some sanctions and tariffs tied to Russian energy exports, while attacks on Saudi Arabia and Yemen kept fears of Middle East supply disruptions in view.

Brent crude futures fell 49 cents, ⁠or ​0.45%, to $109.06 a barrel by 0010 GMT. The US West Texas Intermediate crude (WTI) contract for November delivery, set to expire on Tuesday, eased 0.33% to $103.32. The more-active December contract was down 46 cents, or 0.47%, at $98.08.

International Maritime Organization (IMO) Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez says about 6,000 sailors remain trapped in the Strait of Hormuz since the US-Israel war on Iran began.

“Too many vessels have been attacked, particularly in recent days. Seafarers have continued to perish in these attacks,” he told Fox News Digital. “The message is not to transit the Strait of Hormuz.”

Dominguez said an increase in vessels using fraudulent registration and false flags to move cargo is contributing to the escalation. He accused “irresponsible shipowners” of risking crews’ lives to continue trading.

Yemen’s Houthis said they had carried out several attacks targeting energy facilities, airports and military sites in Saudi Arabia, including an Aramco facility in Yanbu, Reuters reported.

They said they had attacked the Shaybah oilfield, King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Abha Airport, according to a statement by the group.

There was no immediate comment or confirmation from Saudi authorities regarding the reported attacks.

Iran’s High Council for Human Rights says recent US sanctions pose serious risks to people’s access to healthcare services.

The government-run council, which operates under Iran’s judiciary, said the impact of economic restrictions will go beyond patients and vulnerable groups.

“The humanitarian consequences of these restrictions are not limited to the importation of finished medicines,” a statement carried by state-run IRIB said.

14 people were killed and 7 others injured following the collapse of an illegal gold mine in southwestern Colombia, local authorities said on ⁠Monday.

The ​accident took place in the rural Chambero sector of the Santa Barbara de ​Iscuande municipality, ​located in the ⁠province of Nariño.

Search and rescue operations have concluded, ‌Nariño Governor Luis Alfonso Escobar said.

The governor called on the national government, the National Mining Agency, and the Ministry of Mines and ⁠Energy to accelerate ⁠the formalization process for illegal and small-scale miners ⁠to ‌improve working conditions ​and safety standards.

In ‌August, 13 people died in a similar mining ‌accident ​in the town ​of ​Policarpa, also in Nariño.

US Defense Secretary Pete ⁠Hegseth ​met with ​Israeli ​Prime Minister ⁠Benjamin Netanyahu ‌during an unannounced visit ⁠to ⁠Israel ⁠on ‌Monday, ​Axios ‌reported, citing two ‌sources ​with ​knowledge.

More than 45% of flight departures from Saudi Arabian airports have been cancelled since October 8, according to data from aviation analytics company Cirium, Reuters reported.

Brigadier-General Hossein Mohebbi, spokesman for Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC), has threatened communication cables passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

“Seven major undersea cables pass through the Strait of Hormuz, and all of the world’s internet and commercial data depend on them,” Fars news agency quoted Mohebbi as saying.

A day after Trump publicly endorsed Netanyahu in the close-fought October 27 election, the Israeli premier put out a video of the two right-wing leaders lavishing praise on each other by telephone.

body_text:
US prosecutors said on Monday that Abdulrahman Alfozan, a Saudi citizen accused of hiding a recording device at OpenAI's headquarters “presents an ongoing danger” and should not be released from custody.

In a court filing, the US Justice Department responded to a request from Mr Alfozan's lawyer in California that sought to grant his release amid the continuing investigation, which is expected to culminate in a criminal trial.

“The defendant presents an ongoing danger to the community and a serious risk of flight that no set of release conditions can reasonably mitigate,” Craig Missakian, a lawyer for the US Justice Department wrote.

According to the department's memo in support of continuing the suspect's detention, “a member of the Saudi military booked and paid for” a flight for Mr Alfozan's wife and son several days after he was arrested.

“The day before she left the US, the defendant’s wife told the FBI agents who interviewed her that her US visa was expiring and that she and her son were permanently moving back to Saudi Arabia – and that her husband, the defendant, eventually intended to do the same,” US prosecutors wrote.

Mr Alfozan, a Saudi citizen and former OpenAI employee, was arrested on October 8 over accusations he had hidden a recording device at the company's offices in San Francisco.

Investigators said last week that Mr Alfozan planted the device – a Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-S3, manufactured by a company in China – behind a television in a conference room.

The device has a “thumb-sized development board with a detachable camera sensor, digital microphone and micro-SD storage”, the Justice Department said.

Mr Alfozan started working for the OpenAI product team in July last year. He was fired on the same day of his arrest, the company said.

According to the original criminal complaint previous filed by prosecutors, actions taken by Mr Alfozan indicated he planned to depart the US swiftly.

“Indeed, the defendant, his wife and a third family member have booked one-way tickets from San Francisco to Saudi Arabia (via Istanbul) … and defendant has the means and the incentive to flee the US sooner if he learns about this case before he is arrested,” the initial filing reads.

Last week, California lawyer William Pernik told The National he was still waiting to see what other evidence the government has against his client and that he plans on presenting all appropriate defences in court.

“Like countless Americans, Mr Alfozan came to this country years ago as a young person with a dream,” Mr Pernik said in an email. “These allegations appear wholly out of character for him, and we will relentlessly investigate all evidence produced by the government in this case to understand what actually happened, who was responsible and any possible reasons why.”

On Friday, Mr Pernik filed a court request to get Mr Alfozan out of custody on the condition he wears a GPS ankle tag, remains at his home in Millbrae, California and surrenders his passport.

The filing also proposed a “an appearance bond co-signed by sureties from his Bay Area community and supported by the written undertaking of the Consulate General of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia”.

According to his LinkedIn profile, Mr Alfozan has lived in California since 2015 and started working at OpenAI as a lead engineer in 2025. Before his years in California, he was an intern at Meta, Microsoft and SAP.

Mr Alfozan received his undergraduate degree from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in 2016 and then earned a master's degree in 2025 from the University of California-Berkeley.

According to the Justice Department, he was arrested on October 9 and charged with using an electronic, mechanical or other device to intercept oral communications. He is scheduled to appear in court on 19 for a detention hearing.

“If convicted, Alfozan faces a maximum sentence of five years in prison and a $250,000 fine, followed by three years of supervised release,” a press release from the Justice Department read.

OpenAI has faced a barrage of criticism from employees amid allegations it has disregarded the need for regulations when developing AI technology. American AI companies such as OpenAI also face stiff competition from China, as Washington and Beijing vie for dominance in the technology race. Companies have gone to great lengths to protect intellectual property and trade secrets.
